title: 3D Closed‐Loop Navigation of Magnetic Microswimmers Using Vision‐Derived Depth Feedback
abstract: Despite growing interest in autonomous microswimmer navigation, achieving closed‐loop 3D control remains challenging because simple, real‐time depth feedback compatible with standard microscopy is unavailable. This work presents a unified multimodal control framework integrating Model Predictive Control (MPC) with A* path planning for both surface‐bound and free‐swimming locomotion of planar magnetic microswimmers. A propulsion‐only depth regulation strategy uses a signed Fourier‐domain blur metric from a single monocular microscope image to estimate axial position without magnetic gradients or volumetric imaging. This vision‐based method enables real‐time depth estimation and waypoint tracking with minimal computational cost. In experiments, the proposed controller achieved 3D closed‐loop navigation with a median planar error of 12–15 μm and overshoot of 20 ± 5 μm (mean ± SD, n ≥ 20). During fixed‐focus 3D swimming, depth regulation was maintained within an axial working window of approximately 200 μm. For surface locomotion, A*‐guided MPC completed obstacle‐rich routes about 40% faster than reactive MPC while maintaining 100% target‐reach success when a collision‐free path existed. These results demonstrate robust multimode transitions, depth‐aware 3D control, and high‐precision navigation using only propulsion and monocular vision, providing a foundation for future in vitro and ophthalmic applications.
authors: Yasin Cagatay Duygu; Sangwon Lee; Min Jun Kim

title: A 0.5 cm³ Ingestible Capsule Sensor with Synchronized Sensing and Tracking for Active Gastrointestinal Event Identification and Localization
abstract: Characterizing natural gastrointestinal (GI) biochemical and physiological processes at specific anatomical sites and matched time points is a long-sought goal in research on digestive mechanisms and related disorders, which requires capabilities that conventional research modalities cannot provide: non-invasive, real-time sensing and monitoring with precise spatial localization. Here, by leveraging the ionic conductivity of biological tissues to enable intra-body coupled communication and precise spatial localization, we overcome the size and power bottlenecks inherent to conventional ingestible sensors based on resonant antennas and discrete positioning modules. We demonstrate a fully functional ingestible platform integrating centimeter-scale localization, multimodal sensing, onboard computation, and high-speed wireless transmission within a swallow-safe 0.5 cm³ frame-supported membrane architecture. This ultra-miniaturized integrated system enabled long-term, real-time monitoring of key GI biomarkers, such as temperature, peristaltic rhythm, bleeding, and gas distribution, while synchronously tracking their dynamic spatial coordinates throughout GI transit, thereby realizing spatial and temporal mapping of multi-modal GI biomarkers. We demonstrated complete functional validation in freely moving animal models, maintaining full functionality from ingestion to excretion, and established a foundation for spatially resolved GI health monitoring, mapping of dynamic gut microenvironments, and precision therapeutic interventions.
authors: Qingjun Liu; Zijian An; Fengrong Liu; Ang Li; Yuxi Li; Yunrui Cao; Zhenghan Shi; Xin Li; Hao Wen; Rujing Sun

title: A Magnetic Robotic Platform for Enhanced Stem‐Cell‐Based Tendon Repair
abstract: Robotics enables regenerative medicine to be more precise, less invasive, and more targeted. Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy shows great potential for tissue regeneration, but challenges such as low cell survival and limited differentiation ability after in vivo implantation hinder its clinical translation. In this study, we propose a magnetic robotic platform capable of autonomously recognizing and targeting injury sites, as well as delivering noninvasive magnetic stimuli to programmatically regulate MSC functions for tendon repair. This platform integrates 3D-MRI with real-time recognition to enable spatial perception of deep tissues, which is visualized through panoramic simulation. It provides an engineering-precise and intelligent automated magnetic stimulation for the diverse tendon injuries scenarios. We identified pulse electromagnetic field (PEMF) parameters that induced proliferation and tenogenesis of MSCs, respectively, and demonstrated the feasibility of programmed PEMF to sequentially regulate cell behaviors of transplanted MSCs, which contributed to the structure and functional recovery of rat injured tendons. Furthermore, we elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms by which different magnetic stimuli regulate MSC functions, providing insight into PEMF-mediated MSCs responses. Generally, this magnetic robotic system offers a noninvasive, precise, and biosafe strategy to enhance MSC-based therapies, with significant implications for clinical applications and broader regenerative medicine.
authors: Mumin Cao; Renwang Sheng; Yimin Sun; Ying Cao; Xuepeng Lv; Hang Zhang; Hao Wang; Yucheng Gao; Zhengkuan Ou; Hongkang Zhu; Fei Xiong; Gao‐Jun Teng; Qianqian Wang; Yunfeng Rui

title: A Miniaturized Wi-Fi HaLow-Based Wireless Imaging Transfer System for Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Wireless capsule endoscopy is constrained by severe limitations in size, available power, and reliable data transmission through biological tissues. Although recent advances in miniature imaging sensors have improved image quality, the wireless transmission of color images at practical frame rates remains a challenging task under the tight capsule constraints. We present the design and the experimental validation of a miniaturized Wireless Imaging Transfer (WIT) system for capsule endoscopy based on a sub-GHz IEEE 802.11ah (Wi-Fi HaLow) wireless link. In addition, a preliminary in-vivo validation of Wi-Fi HaLow communication is reported, showing that a stable through-body wireless link can be established across biological tissues in a clinically relevant porcine model. These in-vivo results provide direct experimental support for the adoption of sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow for capsule endoscopy applications. Experimental results demonstrate stable wireless image transmission at a resolution of 320x320 pixels, with measured end-to-end data rates above 12 Mbps and a transmission energy efficiency of 20.7 nJ/bit. We also report a detailed power consumption analysis, with a breakdown of the contributions from the imaging sensor, illumination, digital processing, and RF transmission. When all active subsystem contributions are considered, including the camera, digital processing, RF transmission, and illumination at 60% LED brightness, the total power consumption is approximately 477 mW, corresponding to a complete-chain energy consumption of approximately 39.6 nJ/bit. Overall, the measured performance confirms that sub-GHz Wi-Fi HaLow provides a promising trade-off among throughput, robustness, and energy efficiency for wireless imaging in capsule endoscopy.

title: A Mixed-Reality Virtual-Monitor Workspace for Endoscopic Pituitary Surgery: Proof of Concept from Bench to Bedside
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Endoscopic transsphenoidal pituitary surgery requires the management of an increasing amount of information: the surgeon must reconcile spatially separated operative screens-endoscopy, neuronavigation and preoperative imaging-each on its own monitor, away from the operative axis. To our knowledge, no 3-source virtual-monitor workspace has been reported during live endoscopic pituitary surgery. This proof-of-concept study tested the workspace in the anatomy laboratory and in a first clinical case. METHODS: A custom mixed-reality platform was developed to integrate the endoscopic feed, neuronavigation data, and radiological imaging into the HoloLens 2 headset, where information was displayed through voice-controlled virtual monitors within the surgeon's field of view. Ten operators (5 consultants and 5 second-year residents) performed standardized endoscopic endonasal procedures on a cadaveric specimen while wearing the headset. Perceived usability (System Usability Scale [SUS]) and workload (Surgery Task Load Index [SURG-TLX]) were assessed. The platform was used by the lead surgeon during resection of a pituitary microadenoma. RESULTS: Laboratory SUS was 88 ± 6 and SURG-TLX weighted composite 38 ± 17 (0-100). In the clinical case, the workspace was used through the nasal, sphenoidal, and sellar stages without modifying the operative workflow or requiring removal of the headset (SUS, 88; SURG-TLX, 52). Situational stress, temporal demand, and task complexity were rated highest; mental demand, physical demand, and distractions were rated lowest. CONCLUSIONS: A surgeon-centered mixed-reality workspace was feasible and well tolerated in both anatomical and live pituitary surgery. The findings support feasibility; whether workload was reduced was not assessed. Larger controlled studies incorporating objective measures of gaze, posture, and workload are needed.
authors: Carlotta Fontana; Michele Guacci; Francesco Corrivetti; Anna Tortora; Luigi Falchetta; M. Vincenzo; Giuliana Panico; Giuseppe Carpenzano; Giorgio İaconetta; Nicola Cappetti; Matteo de Notaris

title: A Pixel-based Confidence Weighted Transfusion model for Colonoscopy and Colon Capsule Endoscopy image-based Polyp Segmentation
abstract: Polyps one of the most frequently occurring lesions in the human gastrointestinal system and play a critical role in colorectal cancer development, often serving as early indicators or precursors of malignant transformation. Timely and early detection of polyps is critical for lowering the risk of colorectal cancer and increasing survival. Polyp segmentation is crucial in improving computer-aided detection and diagnosis systems, which may support early intervention. CNN-based segmentation models often struggle to capture global contextual information, leading to suboptimal performance. These limitations are further amplified in endoscopic imaging scenarios, where variable resolution in colon capsule endoscopies (CCE) and conventional colonoscopy images—introduces inconsistencies in feature representation and contextual awareness. Therefore, we develop a comprehensive TransFuseNet model that captures local and global receptive fields at the encoder and decoder levels. The pixel-based confidence-weighted fusion combines features from two models, which facilitates knowledge and domain shift features that allows segmentation of low- and high-resolution images. We validated the model's performance on seven diverse optical colonoscopies, CCE, and synthetic datasets. Analysis reveals that our developed model has yielded an intersection over the union of 84.67\%, 89.05\%, 88.91\%, 89.46\%, 89.58\%, 82.07\%, and 86.41\% on the Kvasir, CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB, CVC-ClinicDB, ETIS, CCE CareForColon2015 dataset, and Synthetic datasets, respectively. The external validation also confirms the robustness and effectiveness of our developed model, providing a new pathway for polyp segmentation using optical colonoscopy and CCE images with explainable characteristics and polyp pixel measurement. Thus, our proposed TransFuseNet effectively handles both low- and high-resolution endoscopic images by fusing local and global contextual features. This supports more reliable polyp segmentation across diverse imaging conditions, enhancing diagnostic accuracy in clinical practice.
authors: Khare SK, Braun J, Schelde-Olesen B, Koulaouzidis A, Nadimi ES.

title: A Robotic Tele-Laser System for Remote Visualization and Nd:YAG Laser Triggering: A Preclinical Feasibility Study
abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the technical feasibility and short-term procedural safety of a remotely operated robotic tele-laser platform for anterior-segment neodymium-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (Nd:YAG) laser delivery in rabbit models. Methods: A remotely operated, robotic tele-laser platform integrating a customizable finger robot, stereoscopic visualization, and a Nd:YAG laser device was developed to enable ophthalmologists to remotely perform laser treatments. Twenty-four rabbits were allocated into two predefined experimental cohorts: a posterior capsular opacification (PCO) cohort (n = 12) and a laser peripheral iridotomy (LPI) cohort (n = 12). Within each cohort, animals were assigned into remotely operated and on-site subgroups. Outcome measures included technical completion, laser-delivery duration, laser parameters, engineering performance, and postoperative findings. Results: All 24 procedures were technically completed. For capsulotomy, median laser-delivery duration was 285.0 seconds (interquartile range [IQR], 161.5-793.5) in the remotely operated group and 214.0 seconds (IQR, 173.25-441.0) in the on-site group (P = 0.589). Intraocular lens (IOL) pitting within the central 3-mm optical zone occurred in four of six eyes and in three of six eyes, respectively. For LPI, no statistically significant between-group differences were detected in laser-delivery duration, laser parameters, or change from baseline at postoperative day 1 in intraocular pressure (IOP). Mean targeting errors were 0.0380 ± 0.0174 mm in the remotely operated procedure and 0.0341 ± 0.0230 mm on site (P = 0.053). Mean glass-to-glass video latency and button-to-laser activation latency were 258.6 ± 10.2 ms and 522.7 ± 29.3 ms, respectively. Conclusions: This controlled preclinical study demonstrates the feasibility of a remotely operated robotic tele-laser platform for anterior-segment laser delivery. The platform enabled remote completion of capsulotomy and LPI workflows under controlled experimental conditions and provides a foundation for further engineering and translational validation. Translational Relevance: This study demonstrates the preliminary feasibility of a remotely operated robotic tele-laser platform in a preclinical animal model. This platform enables remote expert participation in laser treatment workflows and provides a foundation for future tele-laser applications. Further engineering optimization, safety validation, and clinical studies are required before translation into human ophthalmic practice.
authors: Andi Xu; Yining Huang; Zhangkai Lian; Naiji Yu; Ruiyang Li; Yangfan Yang; Qiong Ke; Mohammad Ali Nasseri; Qianni Wu; Wenben Chen; Haotian Lin

title: A Survey of Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models: Towards Recursively Self-Improving and Collective Agents
abstract: Reasoning is a fundamental cognitive process underlying inference, problem-solving, and decision-making. While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong reasoning capabilities in closed-world settings, they struggle in open-ended and dynamic environments. Agentic reasoning marks a paradigm shift by reframing LLMs as autonomous agents that plan, act, and learn through continual interaction. In this survey, we organize agentic reasoning along three complementary dimensions. First, we characterize environmental dynamics through three layers: foundational agentic reasoning, which establishes core single-agent capabilities including planning, tool use, and search in stable environments; self-evolving agentic reasoning, which studies how agents refine these capabilities through feedback, memory, and adaptation; and collective multi-agent reasoning, which extends intelligence to collaborative settings involving coordination, knowledge sharing, and shared goals. Across these layers, we distinguish in-context reasoning, which scales test-time interaction through structured orchestration, from post-training reasoning, which optimizes behaviors via reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning. We further review representative agentic reasoning frameworks across real-world applications and benchmarks, including science, robotics, healthcare, autonomous research, and mathematics. This survey synthesizes agentic reasoning methods into a unified roadmap bridging thought and action, and outlines open challenges and future directions, including personalization, long-horizon interaction, world modeling, scalable multi-agent training, and governance for real-world deployment.

title: A Systematic Review of Bias, Validation, and Explainability in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Dental Diagnostics
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To critically evaluate the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in dental diagnosis across multiple dental disciplines, assessing diagnostic performance, methodological quality, risk of bias, validation, explainability, and clinical applicability. DATA AND SOURCES: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD42025639340). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, LILACS, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to December-2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies was assessed using QUADAS-2-tool, evaluating the domains of patient selection, index test, reference standard, flow and timing whilst randomised studies were assessed using Cochrane RoB 2-tool. Reporting quality and transparency of AI-model development and validation were assessed using the selected items from TRIPOD-AI reporting guideline. Methodological quality and risk of bias in AI model development and evaluation were additionally assessed using PROBAST+AI. STUDY SELECTION: Ninety-six studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 90.6% were retrospective. Convolutional neural networks (CNN) were the most frequently used architecture (82.3%). Sixteen studies failed to specify the CNN architecture used. Reported diagnostic accuracy ranged from 81% to 99% across dental specialties, with high performance in implantology (92-99%), orthodontics (88-99%), endodontics (87-99%). Panoramic radiographs and cone-beam computed tomography were the most used imaging modalities. QUADAS-2 analysis indicated that high-risk of bias in 55.2% of studies and most lacked external validation, whilst Assessment using selected TRIPOD+AI items identified important gaps in reporting completeness and transparency, particularly in sample-size justification, missing-data handling, protocol availability, study registration, and data or code availability. CONCLUSIONS: AI demonstrates substantial technical capability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. However, the predominance of retrospective designs, limited external validation, and methodological weaknesses constrain the strength of current evidence. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The use of AI is potentially considered as a decision-support tool rather than replacement for clinical judgement.
authors: Adel Alrayes; Dimitrios Kollias; Aylin Baysan

title: A Transnasal Endoscope for Robotically Assisted Gastroscopy
abstract: A robotic transnasal endoscope (TNE) is developed to improve minimally invasive access to the upper gastrointestinal (GI) tract and support early cancer detection. The device is 4.25 mm in diameter and is designed to be compatible with transnasal access while preserving diagnostic and interventional capability achievable with bigger peroral access devices. The distal segment incorporates permanent magnets that enable precise remote manipulation through externally applied magnetic fields. A tendon‐driven variable stiffness mechanism provides high compliance during navigation and controlled stiffening for enhanced pushability, stability, and shape control. The feasibility of using the TNE for upper GI endoscopy is demonstrated through in vitro and in vivo evaluations. The robotic TNE achieves full navigation of the upper GI tract, including retroflexions, pyloric passage, duodenal access, and tissue biopsy. Robust maneuverability is maintained across stiffness states, confirming reliable control during complex motions. This approach has the potential to increase patient acceptance of routine screening and expand access to minimally invasive GI interventions.
authors: Alexandre Mesot; Michelle Mattille; Sean Lyttle; Shannon Melissa Chan; Philip Wai Yan Chiu; Quentin Boehler; B.J. Nelson

title: A circRNA-microRNA-Pdcd1 axis drives microglial activation and retinal ganglion cell degeneration
abstract: Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration is the primary cause of vision loss, driven by the complicated effects of intrinsic neuronal damage and neuroinflammation. However, current single-target therapies fail to address these dual pathological challenges. CircRNAs, functioning through ceRNA networks, represent a multi-target intervention due to their stability. Here we show that, using whole‑transcriptome sequencing of optic nerve crush (ONC), we bioinformatically predicted nine candidate ceRNA networks. Among these, the network centered on circAgtpbp1 was significantly up-regulated post-injury, independent of its host gene. Mechanistically, circAgtpbp1 functions as a ceRNA by sequestering miR-3098-3p, thereby de-repressing the translation of PD-1 ( Pdcd1 ). In the ONC model, this upregulation of PD-1 protein amplifies microglial activation, creating a pathogenic non-cell-autonomous inflammatory amplification loop that drives RGC degeneration. Our findings not only uncover a novel circRNA-mediated mechanism in neurodegeneration but also identify the circAgtpbp1-miR-3098-3p-Pdcd1-microglia axis as a promising therapeutic target for neuroprotective interventions.
authors: Lanfang Sun; Xiaoyu Ke; Jingjing Yu; Jinfei Wei; Jiayi Gu; Zhou Wanchen; Yixin Cen; Jin Huang; Xiaoling Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Shuo Zhang; Xiaojiang Liu; Yangyang Ji; Wentao Yan; Shaohui Pan; Meng Zhou; Wencan Wu

title: A comparative in vitro study on the accuracy of robotic arm mode versus dynamic navigation mode of an autonomous dental implant robot in the posterior mandibular region
abstract: To investigate the application efficacy of the robotic arm mode versus the navigation mode of an autonomous dental implant robot in posterior mandibular implant surgery. A total of 80 custom-designed resin models were stratified and equally divided into an experimental group (robotic arm mode, n = 40) and a control group (dynamic navigation mode, n = 40). Implants were placed using the respective robotic operating modes. Postoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans were performed to measure the spatial deviations between the actual implant positions and the preoperatively planned positions, comparing accuracy across different unilateral posterior mandibular defect classifications. Data from the 120 placed implants were aggregated to the model level ( N = 80). In the robotic arm mode group, the entry point deviation, endpoint deviation, and angular deviation were 0.68 ± 0.18 mm, 0.75 ± 0.24 mm, and 1.26 ± 0.44°, respectively. In the dynamic navigation mode group, these deviations were 1.01 ± 0.27 mm, 1.12 ± 0.35 mm, and 2.34 ± 0.54°, respectively. (1) Under standardized in vitro conditions, both the robotic arm mode and the dynamic navigation mode achieved clinically acceptable implant accuracy in simulated posterior mandibular defects. (2) However, the accuracy of robotic arm mode-assisted implant placement was significantly superior to that of dynamic navigation mode, suggesting that the robotic arm mode reflects the anticipated precision advantages of automated mechanical execution over manually controlled navigation in a controlled laboratory setting.
authors: Honghong LIU; kunming LIU; mengmeng YOU; yingying ZHANG; Yanqing Wang; Zhihong Zhang

title: A diagnostic pitfall: pediatric eosinophilic enteritis with ileal involvement mimicking Crohn’s disease despite nondiagnostic conventional endoscopy—a case report and literature review
abstract: Eosinophilic enteritis (EoN) is a rare eosinophilic gastrointestinal disorder that can be difficult to diagnose because symptoms and imaging findings are nonspecific and the mucosa may appear grossly normal. We report an 8-year-old boy with recurrent abdominal pain and intermittent vomiting for more than 4 months. Initial upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy was nondiagnostic. Persistently elevated fecal calprotectin and computed tomography enterography showing segmental bowel-wall thickening subsequently raised concern for Crohn’s disease. Peripheral eosinophil counts and serum total immunoglobulin E (IgE) remained within normal ranges. Because symptoms and objective evidence of intestinal inflammation persisted, transanal double-balloon enteroscopy (DBE) with ileal biopsies was performed. Histopathology showed spatially heterogeneous eosinophilic infiltration of the ileal lamina propria, with approximately 20 eosinophils per high-power field (HPF) at 15 cm and 70 eosinophils/HPF at 5 cm proximal to the ileocecal valve; no granulomas or crypt architectural distortion were identified. Secondary causes of intestinal eosinophilia were systematically evaluated, supporting EoN with histologically confirmed ileal involvement. The patient improved clinically after combined dietary, nutritional, and systemic corticosteroid treatment. This case highlights that grossly normal mucosa and patchy histological involvement can make conventional evaluation nondiagnostic. Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms accompanied by objective inflammatory or radiologic abnormalities should prompt repeat small-bowel assessment with adequate histological sampling.
authors: Yingying Lin; Lijun Deng; Yudi Li; Jingtian Xie; Ming Luo; Lingyu Fu; Junbin Hong; Jinghua Yang

title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings.

title: A qualitative systematic literature review of the impact of school‐based experiences on wellbeing: The views of young people with special educational needs and disabilities in mainstream secondary schools
abstract: The objective of this systematic literature review was to synthesise qualitative research exploring how young people with a range of special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) experience mainstream secondary education and how these experiences shape their wellbeing. Searches were conducted in August 2022 and re‐run in February 2024. Of the 7893 studies identified, 36 met the inclusion criteria. The data were synthesised through qualitative meta‐aggregation, an integrative method of synthesis that emphasises the presentation of synthesised findings to inform policy and practice. Four synthesised findings were developed, highlighting aspects of mainstream secondary education that are important for the wellbeing of young people with SEND: (1) peer relationships and social contexts, (2) within classroom experiences, (3) the school environment and SEND support and (4) experiences of academic pressure and examinations. By identifying patterns across young people's experiences, this review provides practical, evidence‐informed recommendations to support the development of more inclusive educational policy and practice. The findings highlight the importance of fostering supportive peer and teacher relationships, creating responsive learning environments, ensuring wellbeing is prioritised alongside academic attainment and providing meaningful opportunities for young people to have their voices heard and to participate in the decision‐making of their learning and support. Context and implications Rationale for this study: The voices of young people with SEND, and their perspectives on how mainstream secondary education shapes wellbeing, remain underrepresented in research and policy development. Why the new findings matter: The findings of this review provide insight into how everyday school experiences shape wellbeing and foreground young people's voices in evidence‐informed recommendations for inclusive policy and practice. Implications for educational researchers and policy makers: For practitioners, the findings emphasise the importance of fostering supportive peer and teacher relationships, creating calm and accessible learning environments, and co‐producing individualised SEND support. For policymakers, the review highlights the need to adequately resource inclusive practice, strengthen SEND training for school staff, and embed wellbeing alongside attainment in accountability frameworks. For researchers, the findings identify key gaps in the representation of primary need and geographical context and reinforce the importance of co‐produced qualitative research that prioritises the voices of young people with SEND.
authors: Megan Cutts; Neil Humphrey; Ola Demkowicz; Margarita Panayiotou

title: A quantum-inspired cross-attention fusion network for multi-class eye disease classification from retinal fundus images
abstract: Automated screening of blinding eye diseases from colour fundus photographs is an active area of medical image analysis, yet many reported systems are validated on a single dataset and offer limited insight into their internal decision process. This study introduces QICAF-Net, a dual-branch deep learning framework that couples a Swin Transformer global-context branch with an EfficientNet local-lesion branch and fuses their representations through a novel Quantum-Inspired Cross-Attention Fusion (QICAF) module. The QICAF module reformulates cross-attention using the mathematical formalism of quantum states: token features are amplitude-encoded as complex unit vectors, transformed by a learnable norm-preserving unitary gate, compared through a fidelity-inspired similarity, normalised by a Born-rule measurement rule, and combined through an entanglement-inspired bilinear interaction. All operations are executed as classical linear algebra on conventional graphics hardware; no physical quantum computer and no quantum speed-up are claimed. The model was trained and evaluated on a balanced four-class retinal dataset of 4,217 fundus images spanning cataract, diabetic retinopathy (DR), glaucoma and normal categories. Under stratified five-fold cross-validation with six-view test-time augmentation (TTA), QICAF-Net attained a macro-F1 of 0.9358 ± 0.0113, an accuracy of 0.9367 ± 0.0112 and a macro one-versus-rest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9914 ± 0.0023; a three-seed evaluation of the full model gave a macro-F1 of 0.9420 ± 0.0071. An 18-run multi-seed component ablation (six fusion configurations × three seeds) confirmed that the quantum-inspired components achieve accuracy statistically indistinguishable from strong classical fusion baselines, and a paired three-seed significance test between QICAF-Net and a matched dual-branch concatenation model returned no statistically significant accuracy difference (paired t-test p = 0.887; Wilcoxon p = 1.000). Against five single-backbone baselines under an identical preprocessing and TTA protocol, QICAF-Net was competitive but did not exceed the strongest backbones (Swin-Tiny 0.9583, ViT-Small 0.9487). The principal contribution of the module is therefore a novel and interpretable formulation rather than a raw accuracy gain. External validation on a heterogeneous independent cohort (N = 3,907) showed heterogeneous cross-dataset transfer - better preserved for cataract and normal and substantially degraded for glaucoma; under an observed external-domain shift the diabetic-retinopathy sensitivity fell to 39.61%, and under colour-constancy correction with six-view TTA the external accuracy was 0.8741 (95% CI 0.8633-0.8841) and the macro-F1 0.7188 (95% CI 0.6969-0.7398). Two complementary explainability methods together with visualisation of the QICAF attention indicated that the model attends to clinically plausible regions, most strongly the optic nerve head for glaucoma. Calibration, quantitative explanation-faithfulness (deletion/insertion) and profiler-based computational analyses were additionally performed. QICAF-Net is thus presented as an interpretable and transparently evaluated framework whose accuracy is on par with established fusion strategies while contributing a new attention formulation to the retinal imaging literature.
authors: P. Abinash; Krishnamoorthy N

title: A rare case of pediatric iron deficiency anemia: Gastric hamartomatous polyp
abstract: Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is the most common hematologic disorder in children and may result from chronic blood loss. Gastrointestinal (GI) sources should be considered, even in the absence of prominent symptoms. We report a previously healthy 6-year-old girl with 2 years of fatigue and intermittent abdominal pain found to have severe microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 4.7 g/dL) and iron deficiency. A heme-positive stool suggested occult GI bleeding. Endoscopy demonstrated a large pedunculated polyp in the gastric body, confirmed on pathology as a hamartomatous gastric polyp with intestinal metaplasia, with no dysplasia. Colonoscopy and capsule endoscopy were normal, and genetic testing for hereditary polyposis syndromes, including STK11 mutation, was negative. Hemoglobin levels improved with iron supplementation. This case highlights a rare cause of severe pediatric IDA and underscores the importance of considering structural GI lesions and endoscopic evaluation in unexplained pediatric IDA.
authors: Sabrina A. Karim; Victor L. Fox; Jared Silverstein; Lori A. Zimmerman; Elana M. Bern

title: A robust lightweight deep learning network with deformable convolutions for efficient segmentation of optical coherence tomography images
abstract: Introduction: Manual segmentation and evaluation of optical coherence tomography (OCT) images are difficult and rely on specialist training, which limits the output in a busy clinic. While automatic segmentation can ease this burden, the deep models that currently lead the field tend to be too heavy for routine deployment on standard clinical hardware. A further obstacle is the unusual geometry of OCT data: instead of compact objects on a background, the structures of interest form long, undulating tissue strata that extend horizontally across the whole frame, and this layout is poorly matched to convolutional kernels designed for ordinary photographs. Methods: We address both issues with LiDeOCTNet, a compact segmentation backbone tailored to the layered nature of OCT. Within a reduced UNet, we introduce learnable sampling offsets so that each kernel can reshape itself locally and trace the curved, irregular interfaces between tissues. To assess the design, we evaluate the network on three OCT collections covering retinal as well as endoscopic acquisitions. Results: Across all three, LiDeOCTNet surpasses a parameter-matched UNet baseline and approaches the accuracy of much heavier benchmarks such as TransUNet, despite using about 750× fewer parameters and running roughly 7.4× faster at inference. Discussion: Together these properties point to LiDeOCTNet as a practical option for real-time OCT analysis pipelines, including embedded and resource-limited devices.
authors: Mehmood Nawaz; Syed Muhammad Tariq Abbasi; Sheheryar Khan; Muhammad Ameer Hamza; Khadija Bibi; Syeda Aimen Abbasi; Muhammad Daud; Muhammad Asim; Wu Yuan

title: A self‐retaining mouth prop for intraoral access during periodontal surgery in rat models: A technical note
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rodent models are widely used in oral health research; however, maintaining stable and effective intraoral retraction in the small oral cavity is challenging. Manual retraction methods often lead to procedural instability, operator fatigue, and increased tissue trauma during rodent oral surgery. METHODS: A stainless-steel wire mouth prop incorporating helices for self-retention and auxiliary lateral soft tissue displacement prongs was fabricated. 32 adult Wistar albino rats were randomly allocated to two groups (n = 16 each). In the experimental group, procedures were performed using a custom mouth prop, and the control group underwent conventional manual retraction. Outcomes included time to achieve adequate retraction, slippage events per procedure, operator fatigue scores, and complication rates. Student's t-test was used for statistical analysis of retraction time, and the Mann-Whitney U test was used for slippage frequency, and fatigue scores. Statistical significance was determined using a Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of p < 0.017. RESULTS: Retraction time was significantly shorter in the experimental group (2.5 ± 0.6 min) than in control group (6.3 ± 1.2 min, p < 0.001). Slippage events per procedure were markedly lower with mouth prop (0.1 vs. 3.4 ± 1.1, p < 0.001). Operator fatigue scores were also reduced (2.4 ± 0.8 vs. 7.2 ± 1.4, p < 0.001). Complication rates were significantly lower in the experimental group (p = 0.024). CONCLUSION: The proposed custom-made mouth prop demonstrated favorable procedural handling characteristics during rat intraoral surgery and may serve as a practical, low-cost refinement tool for improving intraoral access and procedural stabilization in experimental oral research settings.
authors: Saravanan Sampoornam Pape Reddy; Delfin Lovelina Francis; Vivek Kumar Thakur; Balaji Manohar; Shaili Pradhan; Shesh Nath Rai

title: ACCESS2 study: the potential for autonomous AI to mitigate disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening in youth
abstract: Minority and underserved youth are less likely to undergo diabetic retinopathy screening, yet more likely to have diabetic retinopathy. We hypothesize that autonomous artificial intelligence-based diabetic eye exams could mitigate screening disparities in minority youth. This prospective study enrolled 397 White and non-White youth with type 1 (72%) and type 2 (28%) diabetes at diabetes care visits. Participants underwent autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exams and optical coherence tomography imaging. The primary outcome is equivalence in screening completion between White and non-White youth. The secondary outcome is diagnostic accuracy of AI against prognostic standard. At baseline, participants in the White cohort were more likely to have completed a prior diabetic eye exam (79.8% v 61.8%, p < 0.0001). Following the artificial-intelligence intervention, 99.5% in the White cohort and 98% in the non-White cohort completed the autonomous artificial-intelligence diabetic eye exam, demonstrating equivalent screening completion after implementation. When compared to standard grading, AI demonstrated sensitivity of 100% (95% CI: 67.6%, 100%), and specificity of 76% (95% CI: 71.4%, 79.9%) for detecting more than mild diabetic retinopathy. Implementation of autonomous AI at the point of care increases access to and completion of diabetic eye exams, achieving equivalent screening completion among White and non-White youth, suggesting the potential to reduce disparities in diabetic retinopathy screening. Study Registration: NCT05463289.
authors: Risa M. Wolf; Roomasa Channa; T. Y. Alvin Liu; Elizabeth A. Brown; Lee A. Bromberger; Neha Parimi; Anum Zehra; Dhruva Patel; Bernard Pan; Yoohee Claire Kim; ALIYAH SHEHADEH; Harold P. Lehmann; Michael D. Abràmoff

title: AI Revolution in Modern Ophthalmology
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has fundamentally reshaped the clinical landscape of ophthalmology, evolving from isolated image classifiers into an integrated driver of the entire clinical pathway. Given the high degree of standardization in ophthalmic imaging, this field serves as a premier domain for the real-world application of deep learning (DL) and multimodal algorithms. This chapter provides a comprehensive synthesis of functional roles of AI in modern eye care, demonstrating its shift from simple disease detection to sophisticated clinical management. We explore how AI enhances screening and early detection for major retinal diseases such as diabetic retinopathy (DR) and age-related macular degeneration, facilitates precision diagnosis and urgent triage through micron-level image quantification, and enables a transition toward predictive medicine by forecasting treatment responses and individualizing monitoring protocols. Furthermore, the integration of AI into surgical planning, robotic-assisted microsurgery, and teleophthalmology frameworks is discussed as a means to enhance procedural safety and global healthcare accessibility. Finally, we address the critical barriers to large-scale deployment, including algorithmic generalizability, the “black-box” nature of neural networks, and evolving ethical and regulatory landscapes. By consolidating these multifaceted applications, this chapter outlines a roadmap for a future AI-augmented ophthalmic ecosystem that prioritizes precision, efficiency, and patient-centered care.
authors: Yuchi Tian; Temitope Emmanuel Komolafe

title: AI driven oral cancer diagnosis from clinical imaging and computational pathology to precision therapeutics
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a computational approach for analysing the complex and heterogeneous data generated across oral cancer diagnosis and management. This narrative review provides an integrated overview of AI applications from early oral lesion detection, computational pathology, prognostic assessment, and precision therapeutics. It describes how machine learning and deep learning process clinical photographs, digitized histopathological images, whole-slide images, radiological examinations, and molecular or clinical data to generate task-specific outputs. The review covers AI-assisted identification of suspicious oral lesions, histopathological detection of oral epithelial dysplasia and oral squamous cell carcinoma, assessment of tumor differentiation, characterization of disease progression, and prediction of treatment response for therapeutic stratification. Particular attention is given to the relationship between the input data, computational task, and clinically relevant output rather than to model architecture alone. Although several studies report high diagnostic performance, much of the current evidence remains based on retrospective datasets and internal validation, while external, multicentre, and prospective evaluations are comparatively limited. Major challenges include dataset quality and representativeness, domain shift, annotation variability, interpretability, and integration into clinical workflows. Future progress will require patient-level evaluation, multicentre validation, multimodal integration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and prospective assessment of clinical utility. This review outlines the evolving role of AI as a potential decision-support framework across the oral cancer care pathway.
authors: Shreyas Agarwal; Baijnath Das; ShivMohan Singh; Bina Pani Gupta

title: AI-Driven Robotic Systems for Precision Ophthalmic Surgery
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), microscale robotics, and real-time intraoperative imaging are shaping ophthalmic surgery from teleoperated assistance toward tasks-specific robotic autonomy. This chapter provides a systematic review of AI-enabled surgical robotics and intelligent intervention techniques in ophthalmology. It introduces the Closed-Loop Intelligent Ophthalmic Surgery framework (CLIOS), which integrates four functional blocks: Perception, AI Processing, Control, and Execution. Perception uses instrument-tissue interface. AI Processing supports phase recognition, instrument tracking, and interoperative decision-making, while Control converts surgical plans into robotic motion through trajectory generation, tremor suppression, and visual servoing. Execution implements these commands through robotic manipulators, with feedback enabling real-time correction. Based on 62 studies, current evidence shows progress in augmented reality guidance three-dimensional (3D) instrument-tip tracking, and autonomous needle placement. In porcine eye models, autonomous needle placement achieved success rates of 90% under static conditions and 83% under motion. However, clinical translation remains limited, with only two robotic systems reaching first-in-human trials. A substantial gap persists between controlled laboratory performance and the complex conditions of living, bleeding, and moving eyes. High system costs, ranging from approximately USD 500,000 to USD 2.5 million, further constrain adoption. CLIOS is proposed as a conceptual framework to bridge laboratory innovation and clinical translation toward safe autonomous robotic eye surgery.
authors: Mostafa Orban; Mustafa Mahmoud Elsayed; M.G.E. AbdelJawad; Temitope Emmanuel Komolafe; Ahmed Fares; 郭凯; Basem M. Elhalawany

title: AI-assisted curriculum mapping for competency-based dental education: a comparative study
abstract: Curriculum mapping is essential for competency-based dental education but is often time-consuming and dependent on faculty interpretation. As dental schools undergo digital transformation, artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools may enhance curriculum quality assurance and alignment processes. Large language models (LLMs) may support curriculum alignment tasks; however, evidence in dental education remains limited. This study compared the accuracy, quality, efficiency, and faculty acceptance of ChatGPT-assisted versus manual curriculum mapping. A fixed-order, repeated-measures comparative study included 90 dental faculty members from Periodontology, Oral Medicine, and Oral Diagnosis. Participants completed manual mapping followed by ChatGPT-assisted mapping after a seven-day washout period, aligning course-level Intended Learning Outcomes with Program Learning Outcomes. Mapping accuracy against an independent, Delphi-derived reference standard was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included rubric-based mapping quality, task completion time, error patterns, and faculty perceptions assessed using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). The primary comparison used participant-level paired t-tests, with participant-clustered logistic generalized estimating equations used to assess incorrect mapping occurrence. Mapping accuracy was significantly higher with ChatGPT assistance than with manual mapping (78.8% ± 7.9% vs. 74.3% ± 8.2%; mean difference = 4.5% points, 95% CI 2.81–6.19; Cohen’s d_z = 0.56; p < 0.001). A secondary participant-clustered analysis supported this finding, showing lower odds of incorrect mapping (OR = 0.78, 95% CI 0.62–0.98; p = 0.035). ChatGPT-assisted mapping yielded higher rubric-based quality scores (25.67 ± 0.26 vs. 20.96 ± 0.36; p < 0.001) and shorter completion times (14.0 ± 1.5 vs. 27.8 ± 2.9 min; p < 0.001). The participant-clustered analysis found no statistically significant difference in the relative distribution of error types between methods ( p = 0.053). Faculty reported favorable technology acceptance, with all three TAM constructs rated significantly above the neutral midpoint (all p < 0.001). ChatGPT-assisted mapping was associated with significantly higher mapping accuracy, higher rubric-based quality scores, and shorter completion times than manual mapping. However, the fixed-order, non-randomized design precludes attributing these differences exclusively to AI assistance, as practice and familiarity effects may have contributed to the observed results. These findings support further evaluation of LLMs as faculty-supervised decision-support tools for curriculum alignment, particularly through randomized, counterbalanced, multicenter studies.
authors: Fatma E. A. Hassanein; Suliman Alsaeed; Asmaa Abou‐Bakr

title: AI-assisted versus point-based registration for digital planning in CBCT images with metallic artifacts
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate registration between cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images and intraoral scans is fundamental to digital implant planning because registration errors may propagate throughout the digital workflow and affect the accuracy of computer-guided implant surgery. Conventional point-based registration relies on manually selected anatomical landmarks and may be compromised by metallic artifacts that obscure dental structures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted registration has recently emerged as a promising alternative; however, evidence comparing its performance with conventional point-based registration under clinically challenging conditions remains limited. This study aimed to compare the registration accuracy (primary outcome) and registration duration (secondary outcome) of AI-assisted and conventional point-based registration in patients presenting with metallic artifacts on CBCT images. METHODS: This study included 45 eligible patients with corresponding full-arch CBCT datasets and intraoral scans. Registration accuracy was evaluated at the arch level by measuring the mean discrepancy at three predefined anatomical landmarks using Geomagic Control X software. Registration duration was recorded for each workflow. Arches were classified according to artifact burden into mild (> 0-33%), moderate (> 33-66%), and severe (> 66%) categories. Because the data were non-normally distributed, paired comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used as a sensitivity analysis to account for clustering of maxillary and mandibular arches within the same patient. Intra-observer reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). RESULTS: A total of 78 paired arch observations were available for registration accuracy analysis. AI-assisted registration demonstrated significantly lower registration discrepancies than conventional point-based registration (median 0.190 mm [IQR 0.121-0.275] vs. 0.268 mm [IQR 0.200-0.418]; p < 0.001). Registration discrepancy increased with increasing artifact burden for both techniques, although AI-assisted registration consistently demonstrated lower discrepancies across all artifact severity groups. Registration duration was comparable between the two workflows. The GEE sensitivity analysis confirmed the primary findings after accounting for within-patient clustering. Intra-observer reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.985; 95% CI: 0.968-0.993). CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted registration achieved significantly lower registration discrepancies than conventional point-based registration while maintaining comparable registration duration in CBCTs with metallic artifacts on CBCT images. These findings suggest that AI-assisted registration may improve the accuracy and consistency of multimodal image registration within the digital implant planning workflow, particularly in clinically challenging cases. Further prospective multicenter studies involving multiple implant-planning software platforms and broader clinical scenarios are required to confirm these findings.
authors: Nehal Ibrahim Shobair; Zainab H. Abdel Rahman; Mohamed Tolba; Yassin S. Alian

title: AI-driven Innovations in 6G Networks: A Survey
abstract: The Sixth Generation Mobile Communication Technology (6G) is envisioned as a transformative network architecture featuring ultra-high speed, low latency, massive connectivity, and pervasive intelligence to meet the demands of future communication scenarios. To achieve these goals, 6G networks are expected to integrate highly dynamic, heterogeneous, and multi-layered structures. However, this inherent complexity poses significant challenges to traditional rule-based or static network management strategies. In this context, Artificial Intelligence (AI) serves as a foundational technology to enable intelligent, adaptive, and scalable 6G networks. Unfortunately, there is a lack of a panoramic review on AI for the construction of 6G networks. To bridge this gap, this paper presents a thorough survey on AI-driven innovations in 6G networks. We begin with an introduction to 6G networks and the AI techniques commonly employed in 6G networks. Additionally, we propose a set of criteria for evaluating existing AI-driven solutions in 6G networks. We then categorize existing works and conduct a detailed review and analysis on each of them based on our evaluation criteria. Finally, we identify open issues and propose potential directions for future research and development.
authors: Lanzhen Shao; Shufan Fei; Zheng Yan

title: AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood. Here we identify the mitochondrial scaffold protein A‐kinase anchoring protein 1 (AKAP1) as a critical regulator of RGC resilience in glaucoma. AKAP1 expression is reduced in glaucomatous retinas and correlates with disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, oxidative stress, synaptic impairment, and visual decline. AAV2‐mediated restoration of AKAP1 preserves RGC survival and visual function in two independent experimental glaucoma models. These data suggest that retinal AKAP1 promotes mitochondrial fusion, cristae integrity, and bioenergetic capacity in the inner retina and in stressed cultured RGCs, and is accompanied by increased mitochondrial content in presynaptic terminals of the inner plexiform layer. Retinal AKAP1 is further associated with higher PKA abundance, normalized CaMKII and synapsin phosphorylation, preserved synaptophysin, and lower complement C1q and glial activation markers; these associations do not, by themselves, establish causality. These findings identify AKAP1 as a candidate regulator of mitochondrial and synaptic homeostasis and highlight AAV2‐AKAP1 gene therapy as a promising neuroprotective strategy for vision preservation in glaucoma.
authors: Tonking Bastola; Keun-Young Kim; Ziyao Shen; Guy A Perkins; Muna Poudel; Veronica Gomez; Yoonjin Lim; Soo‐Ho Choi; Jae Yon Won; Soo-Ho Choi; Mark H. Ellisman; Robert Neal Weinreb; Won‐Kyu Ju

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AS A DECISION-SUPPORT TOOL FOR MATERIAL SELECTION IN PROSTHODONTICS: AN ANALYTICAL REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
abstract: Background. The rapid development of digital dentistry and artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the range of technologies available for diagnosis, treatment planning, prosthetic design, and outcome prediction. Material selection remains a clinically important component of prosthodontic treatment because the choice of restorative material must account for mechanical, functional, biological, and esthetic requirements. Aim. To analyze recent literature on the application of AI in prosthodontics, with particular attention to its potential role in supporting restorative material selection, integrating clinical and digital parameters, predicting prosthetic outcomes, and personalizing treatment planning. Materials and methods. A narrative analytical review was developed from literature published during seven completed calendar years (January 2019–December 2025). Relevant publications were identified in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and NCBI resources using combinations of terms related to artificial intelligence, machine learning, prosthodontics, dental materials, CAD/CAM, crowns, dental prostheses, occlusion, and treatment outcomes. Publications were thematically analyzed according to AI application, type of prosthodontic task, data source, clinical purpose, reported outcomes, and limitations. Results. The reviewed literature demonstrates that AI is increasingly applied in prosthodontic diagnostics, treatment planning, automated crown design, finish-line detection, occlusal assessment, prediction of prosthetic outcomes, and digital workflows. AI-assisted CAD systems have shown potential to improve design efficiency and, in selected studies, achieve clinically acceptable crown fit. However, the evidence remains heterogeneous with substantial differences in datasets, algorithms, validation procedures, and outcome measures. Direct evidence supporting independently validated AI systems for individualized restorative material selection remains limited. Current evidence therefore supports the use of AI primarily as a clinical decision-support tool rather than as an autonomous system for material selection. Conclusions. AI has considerable potential to support individualized material selection and prosthodontic treatment planning by integrating multiple clinical and digital parameters. At the same time, current evidence does not support treating AI as an autonomous replacement for professional clinical judgment. Direct validation of AI systems specifically designed to select restorative materials remains limited, and many predictive models require stronger external validation and prospective clinical evaluation. The most appropriate current framework is therefore a human-in-the-loop decision-support model in which AI augments, rather than replaces, clinical expertise
authors: Tetiana I. Dzetsiukh

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN DENTISTRY: CURRENT APPLICATIONS, ADVANCEMENTS, CHALLENGES, AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies in modern healthcare and is increasingly influencing contemporary dental practice.Recent advancements in machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, and generative AI have enabled the development of intelligent systems capable of analyzing complex clinical, radiographic, and histopathological datasets with remarkable precision.AI applications have demonstrated substantial benefits across multiple dental specialties, including oral radiology, oral pathology, orthodontics, periodontology, prosthodontics, conservative dentistry and endodontics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, pediatric dentistry, and public health dentistry.These technologies facilitate early disease detection, automated image interpretation, treatment planning, outcome prediction, and workflow optimization.The integration of AI with digital dentistry technologies such as cone-beam computed tomography, intraoral scanners, computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing systems, and electronic health records has accelerated its adoption in clinical settings.Despite these advantages, challenges such as data privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, transparency issues, implementation costs, and regulatory uncertainties continue to limit widespread clinical implementation.Furthermore, ethical considerations regarding patient confidentiality and professional accountability remain important concerns.This review provides a comprehensive overview of current AI applications in dentistry, recent technological advancements, existing limitations, and future opportunities for integrating AI into routine dental practice.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Accuracy of a Sparse-View Smartphone-Based 3D Reconstruction Workflow for Dental Models: A Feasibility Benchmark
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study compared the accuracy of a specific sparse-view, smartphone-based 3D reconstruction workflow for digitising dental models, benchmarking its performance against dedicated dental scanners and assessing its feasibility as an innovative alternative. METHODS: Following the International Organisation for Standardisation protocol (ISO 20896-1:2019), a customised 3D-printed model with three test objects was scanned, using coordinate measuring machine (CMM) measurements as the reference. Data were captured 30 times each with an intraoral scanner (IOS), an extraoral scanner (EOS), and an iPhone 15 Pro. Images from the iPhone were three-dimensionally reconstructed using 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and Neural Surface Reconstruction (NSR), respectively. All outputs were converted to the stereolithography (STL) format and analysed in Geomagic Wrap. Accuracy was reported using the mean, standard deviation (precision), bias (trueness), and the root mean square error (RMSE) for each dimension (height, depth, length, and angle). RESULTS: The IOS achieved the highest accuracy (RMSE < 20 µm), followed by the EOS (RMSE < 80 µm) with systematic negative bias in full‑arch spans. 3DGS and NSR produced substantially larger deviations (approx. 200-250 µm for crown and inlay preparation, and approx. 300 µm for full-arch model). CONCLUSION: Geometry and span affected the accuracy across all methods. IOS consistently displayed the highest accuracy, while 3DGS and NSR with a sparse-view workflow showed substantial errors and surface distortions and were therefore not yet suitable for high-precision prosthodontic restoration. SIGNIFICANCE: Dental scanners remain superior for precision prosthodontics, while the sparse-view 3D reconstruction workflow may hold potential for less demanding clinical and educational contexts.
authors: Shujiang Chen; Jiamin Wu; Ying Liu; Qianhui Li; James Kit Hon Tsoi; Yanning Chen

title: Acoustically driven micro/nanobubbles: from fundamental mechanisms to biomedical applications
abstract: Acoustically driven micro/nanobubbles, as a bridge between macroscopic acoustic fields and microscopic biological machinery, have shown considerable promise due to their non-contact actuation, tunable mechanical responses, and favorable biocompatibility. Recent advances in bubble formulation and acoustic control have further expanded their capabilities, enabling targeted membrane permeabilization, enhanced molecular transport, and precise manipulation at the microscale. In this review, we summarize the fundamental mechanisms linking bubble dynamics to biologically relevant effects under ultrasound and establish quantitative design criteria that govern the coupling between acoustic parameters, bubble behavior, and therapeutic performance. We then organize biomedical applications across scales, spanning single-cell manipulation, tissue-level barrier modulation, and organ-scale imaging and therapeutic interventions. Particular attention is given to how acoustic modes and bubble configurations translate into measurable performance metrics, as well as the limitations that constrain reproducibility and safety in complex biological environments. Finally, we discuss key challenges for practical translation from an engineering perspective and propose strategies for improving controllability, standardization, and system integration. By providing a framework to overcome the inherent randomness of bubble-acoustic interactions in clinical translation, this review outlines a roadmap toward reliable and programmable mechano-bio platforms for closed-loop, patient-adaptive interventions.
authors: Jiaxin Wu; Tatsuo Arai; Chenhao Bai; Changsheng Li; Xingguang Duan; Toshio Fukuda; Xiaoming Liu

title: Action-conditioned latent Kalman filtering for robust spatio-temporal state estimation of deformable object
abstract: Robust spatio-temporal state estimation from noisy observations is a critical challenge in robotic manipulation. Current latent space representations derived from dynamic point clouds often suffer from severe perceptual noise and occlusions, leading to discontinuous trajectories and pronounced temporal jitter. To mitigate these artifacts, we propose an Action-Conditioned Latent Kalman Filter (AC-LKF) framework. Leveraging a hybrid architecture of PointNet++ and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), our method models non-linear temporal dynamics within a low-dimensional latent manifold. Instead of claiming to fully model the physical causality of deformable-object dynamics, AC-LKF incorporates the robot end-effector displacement as a low-dimensional, observable, and task-relevant kinematic prior to condition the latent state transition. Furthermore, a heteroscedastic latent filtering module adaptively estimates process and measurement uncertainties, balancing the action-conditioned prior with degraded visual inputs under noise and occlusion. Evaluations using quantitative temporal metrics and reconstruction errors, supplemented by principal component analysis (PCA) and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations, show that AC-LKF improves latent trajectory smoothness, information retention, and dynamic robustness by reducing abrupt observation-induced state transitions. These results indicate that kinematic action conditioning can improve the temporal consistency and robustness of learned geometric state representations for interactive deformable-object manipulation.
authors: Duan Gao; Majed Melibary; Junlei Hu

title: Active Targeting Across Scales in Medical Robotics
abstract: The diagnosis and treatment of human diseases often involve interventions that target different levels of the body's complex hierarchical organization, from macroscopic organs through microscopic cells, down to nanoscale molecular structures such as proteins. These interventions are hindered by challenges, such as biological barriers and dynamic microenvironments, which necessitate the development of more effective diagnosis, therapy, and microsurgery strategies. Multiscale medical robots are an emerging strategy to address these challenges: advances in micro and nano engineering have enabled the development of sophisticated medical robots with size adaptability and hierarchical navigation for active targeting. Such systems can connect organ-level access and navigation with local action at tissue, cellular, or molecular scales. Here, we discuss advances in micro/nano engineering to design and fabricate multiscale medical robots, with focus on their active targeting capabilities in precision medicine. We provide an overview of the current state of these systems, from accurate diagnosis and targeted therapy to minimally invasive microsurgery across the various scales of the human body, and explore how anatomical, biological, and imaging constraints shape their design. Finally, we discuss the practical challenges of clinical translation, including system-level assessment within the intended clinical workflow and the need for collaboration between engineers and clinicians.
authors: Rujie Sun; Xin Song; Jonathan P. Wojciechowski; Yuyang Zuo; Thomas F. F. Fernandez Debets; Yee Lin Tan; Maggie S. Chen; Nuala Del Piccolo; Yixuan Leng; Kun Zhou; Yiming Ma; Molly M. Stevens

title: Active sensing explains cortical variability and improves visual information
abstract: Active vision is often considered at the scale of saccades, with each fixation treated as a static visual sample. Yet the eyes continue to move during fixation, continually transforming the retinal input. Here we measured these movements at high precision while recording neuronal populations in the foveal primary visual cortex of awake marmosets viewing repeated flashed natural images. Fixational eye movements accounted for most conditional firing-rate variability and nearly all shared variability not explained by the trial-averaged response. An image-computable model captured this modulation largely from gaze-dependent retinal input; explicit eye-position and eye-velocity signals added little predictive power. Under natural viewing, retinal motion redistributed image power across temporal frequencies, and motion effects grew when this power engaged spatiotemporal tuning. In model-derived populations, fixational motion increased the spatial information carried per spike relative to stabilized input, with sharpening growing across successive nonlinear stages. Thus, activity commonly assigned to cortical noise is not just structured visual reafference generated by the movement of the observer, but is beneficial signal which sharpens spatial representations.
authors: Ryan A. Ressmeyer; Declan P Rowley; Tejasvi Kothapalli; Dekel Galor; Ruei-Jr Wu; Rucci Michele; Jude F. Mitchell; Daniel A. Butts; Alexander C. Huk; Jacob L. Yates

title: Adaptive dual-programming magnetic soft robot with lifelike behavior.
abstract: Magnetic soft robots with embodied intelligence of multimodal motions, environmental perception, and functional decoupling depend on ingenious material arrangement and programmable morphing information introduction. While some efforts have been made, achieving lifelike behaviors for soft robots in system-level strategy remains a notable challenge. Here, we present dual-programming hydrogel-based soft robots (DHSRs) that couple magnetic and anisotropic programming through the spatial arrangement of patterned magnetic skeletons into responsive and structural hydrogel bodies. These DHSRs exhibit programmable exquisite and multicurved structures in three-dimensional (3D) space, environment-adaptive deformation behaviors proved by switching from random jumping on land to regular swimming in water of a fish-like soft robot, and further locomotion-function decoupling capabilities of region-selective cargo delivery in an integrated "locomotion-perception-action" workflow. Our strategy in biomedical potential is exemplified by a ring-like pH-responsive DHSR for gastric ulcer therapy, which integrates multimodal locomotion (rolling, tumbling, and rotating), adaptive matching, and microneedle-mediated penetration. By collaborating with a capsule endoscopy system, we explore the possibility of a wireless and painless diagnostic-therapeutic platform in a pig model. This strategy endows the robot with perception and multitask execution capabilities, highlighting a promising route for the intelligent evolution of soft robots across diverse application domains.
authors: Yanchen Ye; Can Xu; Sen Wang; Weijia Li; RongYe Wu; Hao Wu; Neng Xia; TianYe Yang; Shuang Song; Li Zhang; Yue Dong; Bing Li

title: Advanced Diagnosis and Surgical Management of Temporomandibular Joint Disorders: Imaging, Digital Innovation and Procedure Selection
abstract: Temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) comprise heterogeneous pain and dysfunction conditions involving the masticatory muscles, temporomandibular joints (TMJs), and associated structures. Reliable care begins with standardized clinical diagnosis, assessment of psychosocial and functional contributors, and imaging selected to answer a defined clinical question. This chapter reviews functional anatomy, contemporary classification, the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMDs), and the complementary roles of magnetic resonance imaging and cone-beam computed tomography. It then develops a diagnosis-driven pathway from education, self-management, rehabilitation, and behavioral care to arthrocentesis, arthroscopy, open-joint surgery, ankylosis release, and alloplastic total joint replacement. Evidence is strongest for conservative multimodal care in chronic pain-related TMD; procedural evidence is more heterogeneous and often comes from observational series. Accordingly, escalation should be based on concordant symptoms, examination, imaging, functional impairment, prior treatment, and shared decision-making. Digital planning and patient-specific reconstruction are increasingly useful in complex structural diseases. In contrast, biomarkers, wearable phenotyping, and artificial intelligence remain investigational until standardized methods, external validation, and evidence of clinical benefit are established.
authors: Vikranth Ravipati; Anjan Kumar Thyagaraajen; Maha Rizvi; Qasim Khalid; Junad Khan

title: Advanced Medical Optics & Surgical Robotics: Applications of Jana's Invariant Lens Equations in Orthopedics, Neurosurgery, Ophthalmology, and Dentistry
abstract: This paper establishes a high-precision computational paradigm for biomedical optics, robotic surgery, and advanced diagnostic imaging by extending Jana’s Invariant Lens Governing Equations—specifically the dif- ferential velocity profile (dv/du + (v/u) 2 = 0), the cubic spatial matrix (Equation C), and the radical symmetry boundary (Equation K). Traditional surgical microscopes, intra-oral scanners, and autonomous robotic cutting arrays experience processing latencies when adapting to micro-scale tissue variations and localized movement-driven focal shifts. By hardcoding Jana’s non-linear spatial transformations directly into optical tracking firmware, this model eliminates computational tracking lag by roughly 65%. We de- tail direct engineering frameworks to achieve absolute focus stabilization in orthopedic bone cutting, deep micro-vascular neurosurgery, LASIK ophthalmic tracking, and intra-oral 3D dental mapping.
authors: Suryakanta Jana
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Advances in Dental Imaging and the Integration of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Diagnostic imaging of the oral and maxillofacial region is of paramount importance in clinical diagnosis, treatment planning, and follow-up procedures in dentistry. Periapical radiographic examinations and various panoramic imaging systems are routinely employed in clinical dental practice. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has become a widely used and currently preferred imaging modality in dental implantology, endodontics, maxillofacial surgery, periodontology, temporomandibular joint disorders, orthodontics, airway assessment, sleep disorders, and forensic dentistry. However, relatively high radiation doses, prolonged scanning times, and high costs limit its routine clinical use. Ultrasound imaging is also among the recommended techniques in dental practice, as it provides real-time imaging using an ionizing radiation-free, cost-effective, rapid, and user-friendly technique. Ultrasonography can be utilized in the dentomaxillofacial region for various diagnostic purposes, including the examination of the salivary glands and superficial tissues. More recently, dedicated dental magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been introduced, incorporating specialized software, hardware, imaging sequences, and fields of view tailored to the anatomical characteristics of the dentomaxillofacial region. Another important topic in dental and maxillofacial radiology is artificial intelligence (AI). Artificial intelligence is a field of computer science dedicated to developing systems or machines capable of performing tasks that have traditionally been associated with human intelligence. Further research and investigation in the field of dental and maxillofacial radiology are expected to make substantial contributions to diagnostic imaging across various dental specialties. This article provides insights into current applications and emerging trends in the field of diagnostic imaging in dentistry.
authors: Nebiha Hilal Bilge

title: Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care
abstract: Background and Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision loss. Staging based on colour fundus photography captures only part of a disease that involves the whole neurovascular unit and the retinal periphery. This narrative review summarizes the structural (optical coherence tomography, OCT), vascular (OCT angiography and ultra-widefield imaging) and functional (microperimetry, electrophysiology) biomarkers of DR, grades the evidence supporting each of them, and examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing screening, prognostication and treatment selection. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for publications from January 2000 to May 2026, giving priority to randomized trials, prospective multicentre cohorts, systematic reviews and externally validated algorithms. Results: Among imaging biomarkers, disorganization of the retinal inner layers, outer retinal integrity and ultra-widefield angiographic non-perfusion have the most consistent prognostic evidence, whereas OCT angiography metrics remain device-dependent. AI has progressed from research classifiers to autonomous systems with regulatory authorization in the United States and the European Union, to prospectively evaluated deployments in national programmes and low-resource settings, and to time-to-event progression models and foundation models. Image-based prediction improves discrimination over clinical risk factors by modest margins, and biomarker-guided treatment of diabetic macular oedema still rests largely on retrospective series. Cross-device standardization of quantitative metrics, representative datasets, prospective outcome trials and health-economic evidence remain the main gaps. Conclusions: Individualized screening intervals are the application closest to routine practice, whereas phenotype-driven therapy and precision monitoring remain promising but unproven.
authors: Feliciana Menna; Alessandro Meduri; Stefano Lupo; Laura De Luca; Antonio Baldascino; Enzo Maria Vingolo

title: Advances in technologies across the marine plastic value chain in Europe: A critical review
abstract: Marine Plastic Pollution (MPP) is widely recognised as a significant global challenge, driven by unsustainable plastic production, ineffective waste management, and the long-term persistence of plastics in marine environments. MPP has become increasingly widespread across oceans, along coastlines and on the seafloor, resulting in an urgent need for the development of technologies capable of advancing a Circular Economy (CE) for marine-derived products. Advances in cleaner production technologies, including satellite and drone-based remote sensing, autonomous robotic platforms, and machine-vision systems, have improved the efficiency of plastic debris identification, classification, and recovery in complex marine environments. Similarly, innovations in downstream sorting, such as electrostatic separation, selective dissolution, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven classification, are enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of processing MPP. The review evaluates mechanical recycling methods with particular emphasis on recent advances in extrusion, moulding technologies, and additive manufacturing for converting MPP into high-value secondary materials in a CE framework in Europe. These technological developments demonstrate the potential for establishing viable and scalable valorisation routes. Overall, the review outlines key opportunities to strengthen a sustainable CE and guide future research and industrial adoption.
