title: Etiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnosis and management tactics for patients with hepatic portal hypertension depending on the anatomical features of the portal vein and its tributaries
abstract: Portal hypertension (PH) syndrome remains one of the most challenging issues in modern hepatobiliary surgery. The clinical significance of the hepatic form of PH is determined not only by the risk of fatal hemorrhagic complications but also by systemic metabolic disorders. This review systematizes current data on the etiology, pathogenesis, classification, diagnosis, and surgical treatment of hepatic portal hypertension. A literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, eLibrary, and Google Scholar databases for the period from 2010 to 2025 in both Russian and English. Original studies and systematic reviews relevant to the topic were included. Data analysis emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis, a comprehensive approach to treatment, and multidisciplinary collaboration among specialists to improve clinical outcomes and enhance the quality of life for patients with PH.
authors: Igor V. Makarov; I.V. Kolesnik; A. S. Efimova; V.D. Aksenova

title: Evaluating Synthetic Skin Lesion Images for Classifier Training: A Safety-Aware Algorithm
abstract: Skin cancer classifiers need large sets of annotated images, which are scarce, especially for rare lesion types. AI-generated images can fill the gap, but a generator produces images of widely varying quality, so selecting which images to retain is important. That choice usually rests on a single quality score, most often the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), which has not been tested against what a classifier needs and cannot tell whether the generator memorizes its training photographs. We test that practice with a tournament of 16 quality metrics. Each metric alone selects a training subset from a pool of 275,472 images generated by a diffusion model (EDM2), and a classifier trained on each subset scores the metric per class. The tournament shows that no single metric serves every class: FID computed on Inception features gives the best classifier for one lesion type and no measurable advantage over random sampling for another, and the generation setting it prefers is also the one closest to the training images. We turn these per-class measurements into a safety-aware evaluation algorithm that weights each metric by its measured value in each class and removes images too close to a real training image. On the held-out ISIC-2018 test set, the algorithm improves Macro-$F_2$, a recall-weighted measure of classification performance, over the FID baseline for a Swin-B classifier by +0.0136 to +0.0164 across four safety thresholds (Bonferroni-corrected $p < 0.02$) and over random sampling by about +0.03, though not for ResNet-50. Tightening the threshold improves a memorization-safety score with no measurable change in utility, but every curated set remains less safe than random sampling. The results show a modest but statistically significant gain on the primary classifier, and offer a practical, safety-aware procedure for evaluating and using synthetic data.
authors: Amindu Kumarasinghe; Vinh Bui; Reza Ghanbarzadeh

title: Evaluating Wi-Fi HaLow for Next-Generation Capsule Endoscopy
abstract: Capsule endoscopy is limited by its wireless link: insufficient throughput restricts image resolution and frame rate, whereas high-rate radios typically use higher carrier frequencies that experience greater attenuation through tissue. This work evaluates Wi-Fi HaLow (IEEE 802.11ah), a sub-GHz Wi-Fi standard, as an image link for capsule endoscopy. Across all tested combinations of modulation and coding scheme and bandwidth, the saturation TCP throughput reached 15.55 Mbps, and the fastest configuration also achieved the lowest energy per bit. Through power optimization strategies, the combined power consumption of the HaLow module and microcontroller at 1 frame per second (FPS) was reduced from 101.70 to 14.00 mW, which is comparable to that of Bluetooth Low Energy systems. In a simulated in vivo setting, the default rate control selected the highest tested MCS and bandwidth, indicating sufficient link quality; this configuration also had the lowest measured power in both the 1 FPS mode (13.59 mW) and the 30 FPS mode (174.21 mW). The capsule-to-receiver latency was 20.68 ms for a 24 KB frame, while the receiver-to-capsule latency was 4.77 ms for a command; this low-latency bidirectional communication supports real-time detection and manipulation for next-generation capsule endoscopy.
authors: Ziyao Zhou; Chen Shen; Tiancheng Cao; Hen-Wei Huang

title: Evaluation of Personas and Daily Activity Maps to Inform Clinical Care and Socially Assistive Robot Training and Design for Persons With Dementia: Mixed Methods Study
abstract: Background: Over 55 million people worldwide are living with dementia, resulting in significant caregiving demands and caregiver burden. Socially assistive robots (SARs) are increasingly being explored to reduce caregiving workload and improve the quality of life for persons with dementia; however, their effectiveness depends on person-centered design grounded in a comprehensive understanding of the target population. Personas and their corresponding daily activity maps (DAMs) are user-centered design tools that provide a holistic understanding of the personal, medical, emotional, and life trajectory of persons with dementia, enabling SARs to engage in contextually relevant and empathetic interactions. Despite their potential, these tools have not been formally evaluated for dementia care and digital health technology development. Objective: This mixed methods study aimed to explore the perspectives of professional and family caregivers, health care providers, and robot designers on the quality and use of personas and DAMs in clinical practice and digital health design. Methods: Using purposive sampling, 15 stakeholders involved in dementia care or digital health design were interviewed via Zoom (Zoom Communications, Inc) between March and April 2025 to evaluate a subset of persona-DAM pairs using a modified 12-item version of the Persona Perception Scale (PPS), adapted for dementia care contexts, across 5 domains: Credibility, Completeness, Clarity, Willingness to Use, and Empathy. Participants subsequently provided qualitative perspectives through semistructured interviews, reflecting on their ratings and offering suggestions for improvement. Results: Fifteen participants with a median of 9 (IQR 4-15) years of experience in dementia care evaluated 9 persona-DAM pairs. Overall evaluation-level median PPS scores were 4.79 (IQR 4.45, 4.91) for personas and 4.76 (IQR 4.45, 4.94) for DAMs. For both personas and DAMs, the highest-rated domains were Clarity, Credibility, and Willingness to Use (all median 5.00), suggesting stakeholders perceived the tools favorably and were willing to use them. Empathy scores (personas: median 4.67, IQR 4.25-5; DAMs: median 4.83, IQR 4.33-5) highlighted the need for greater cultural, ethnic, and religious representation to foster culturally sensitive interventions. Completeness was the lowest-scoring domain (personas: median 4.50, IQR 3.94-5; DAMs: median 4.38, IQR 4-5), representing the most quantitative improvement suggestions. Qualitative analysis revealed 3 major themes: (1) improving human-robot interaction training through greater knowledge of the personal context of persons with dementia; (2) comprehensive assessment of clinical history and functional capacities as essential for the provision of safe and effective interaction; and (3) perceived design utility: translating person-centered knowledge into actionable tools. Conclusions: This study provides early-stage exploratory evidence that personas and DAMs are perceived as clinically and technically relevant tools for dementia care, complementing existing clinical documentation through a holistic, person-centered view, and serving as human-centered design tools for developing personalized digital health solutions.
authors: Adeline Nyamathi; Mahkameh Rasouli; Choong-Pyo Jeong; Sabine Brunswicker; Elena Agapie; Jocelyn Ludlow; Riyam Jawad; Chet Khay; Audrey Zhixin Lu; Jessica Ding Liao; Saba Azizabadi Farahani; Jung‐Ah Lee; Nikil D. Dutt; Amir M. Rahmani; Erik Krogh

title: EviGround-CT: Sentence-to-Volume Grounding for Verifying LLM-Generated Chest CT Reports
abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) reports generated by large language models (LLMs) can describe positive findings that lack localized evidence in the scan. We propose EviGround-CT to verify these findings after report generation. A deterministic extractor identifies positive finding sentences, and a 3D grounding model predicts an evidence mask for each sentence. Using the full sentence retains anatomical location, laterality, and descriptive modifiers in the grounding query. We evaluate report generation on CT-RATE, and grounding and verification on a held-out 100-case ReXGroundingCT subset. Using the available annotations, sentence-grounded verification raises evidence-supported precision (ESP) from 0.263 to 0.365 across 137 extracted in-scope positives, compared with category conditioning. The corresponding unsupported positive finding rate falls from 0.737 to 0.635. The paired case-level bootstrap ESP difference is +0.102 (95% confidence interval: [0.028, 0.181]). The predicted masks associate individual report statements with spatial evidence that can be inspected alongside the CT.
authors: Ziyuan Li; Juncheng Ni; Feng Li

title: Examination of YouTube Videos on Lamina Preparation Techniques Using the DISCERN Scale
abstract: Objective: This study assesses the quality of information about lamina preparation processes found in YouTube videos.Methods: In February 2023, it was posted on the social media site YouTube. A search was conducted using the term "lamina preparation." The top 100 videos with the most views were listed as a result of this search. After that, 60 videos were examined using the predetermined standards. After seeing the videos, two impartial researchers assessed and graded them using the DISCERN scale and additional standards. The collected data were statistically analyzed using descriptive and frequency analyses and the Mann-Whitney U, Kruskal-Wallis, and Fischer exact tests.Results: Mann-Whitney U test results showed statistically significant differences in the scores made by the two researchers in the DISCERN scale evaluations (P<.001). Kruskal-Wallis analyses according to the content quality of the videos, total number of views, viewing rates, and DISCERN scale scores revealed significant differences between the variables (P<.05).Conclusion: Professionals should use caution when evaluating the informational value of YouTube videos.Keywords: DISCERN, lamina, YouTube.
authors: Tuba Şenocak; Alper ÖZDOĞAN; Furkan Karataş

title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
abstract: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.
authors: DM BAPPY; Eunsu Kim; Hanjoo Lee; Sung Hak Lee; Sangjeong Ahn

title: F2D-RetinaNet: a feature-to-decision dual-path network with fractional operators for retinal disease detection and grading
abstract: Visible pathological abnormalities and vascular integrity help diagnose retinal diseases. This paper introduces a unified feature-to-decision framework that first extracts vasculature and enhances lesions. First, this study proposes the fractional anisotropic diffusion–based hybrid enhancement (FADHE) method that selectively amplifies lesion contrast and vessel visibility in the green channel using long-memory fractional diffusion dynamics. Second, this study introduces a fractional Hessian-based attention U-Net (FHAU-Net), a multi-scale vessel segmentation model that leverages fractional Hessian responses across eight fractional orders and attention-guided skip connections to capture fine vessel structures. Finally, this work designs a dual-branch disease grading model, F2D-RetinaNet, which jointly processes the enhanced image and vessel map to learn lesion-related and vascular feature representations for the recognition and grading of retinal diseases. The FHAU-Net model achieved a Dice coefficient of 0.8987, a sensitivity of 0.9084, an accuracy of 0.9804, and a specificity of 0.9876 across the unified test set, which contains variations in resolution, acquisition site, camera type, and imaging conditions. The F2D-RetinaNet is evaluated for Diabetic retinopathy (DR) detection, DR grading, and multiclass retinal disease classification tasks. Extensive testing and comparisons to the baseline procedures support the reliability of the proposed methodology on the datasets evaluated here.
authors: Mukesh Delu; Priyanka Harjule; Rajesh Kumar; Kushal Gajjar; Pilani Nkomozepi

title: FDI World Dental Congress 2026 in Prague: key trends and implications for Ukraine
abstract: This review analyses the scientific programme and key events of the FDI World Dental Congress held in Prague, Czech Republic, on 4–7 September 2026. The authors aimed to summarise the main scientific, clinical and organisational themes of the congress, to compare them with current evidence and to assess their relevance for the Ukrainian dental community. The sources included congress materials, WHO and FDI documents, and publications retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and The Cochrane Library, mainly for 2018–2026. The transformation of the profession by artificial intelligence, robotics and new biomaterials ran through the whole congress; however, the literature shows that the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence systems varies widely and that their implementation requires standardised evaluation. The clinical programme covered molar incisor hypomineralisation, vital pulp therapy and the preservation of natural teeth. The FDI World Dental Parliament discussed the implementation of the WHO Global Oral Health Action Plan, preparations for the 2030 UN High-Level Meeting on Universal Health Coverage and the global phase-out of dental amalgam by 2034. A joint FDI and WHO session addressed electronic cigarettes, heated tobacco products and nicotine pouches; current evidence does not support their safety for oral tissues, while brief interventions based on the 5A and 5R models remain an accessible tool for the dental team. FDI launched the online FDI Young Dentists Community platform during the congress. Ukrainian researchers prepared oral and poster presentations. The findings support the participation of dental departments of Ukrainian medical universities and the NGO “Ukrainian Dental Association” in the FDI Tobacco Cessation project and a wider involvement of young researchers in FDI programmes.
authors: Bohdan Kravchenko; O.A. Kopchak; D.O. Yerofeieva

title: Fast Feature Field (F 3 ): A general predictive representation of events for robot perception
abstract: This paper develops a mathematical argument and algorithms for building representations of data from event-based cameras that we call Fast Feature Field (F 3 ). We learned this representation by predicting future events from past events and show that it preserves scene structure and motion information. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and is robust to noise and variations in event rates. It can be computed efficiently using ideas from multiresolution hash encoding and deep sets, achieving 120 hertz at high-definition (HD) resolution and 440 hertz at video graphics array (VGA) resolution. F 3 represents events in a contiguous spatiotemporal volume as a multichannel image, enabling a range of downstream tasks. We obtained state-of-the-art performance on optical flow estimation, semantic segmentation, and monocular metric depth estimation, on data from three robotic platforms (a car, a quadruped robot, and a flying platform) and across different lighting conditions (daytime and nighttime), environments (indoors, outdoors, urban, and off-road), and dynamic vision sensors (resolutions and event rates). Our implementations can predict these tasks at 25 to 75 hertz at HD resolution.
authors: Richeek Das; Kostas Daniilidis; Pratik Chaudhari

title: Feasibility of Augmented Reality-Guided Robotic Ultrasound with Cone-Beam CT Integration for Spine Procedures
abstract: Needle placement in spine interventions is critical for effective pain management, yet it depends on reliable identification of anatomical landmarks and careful trajectory planning. Conventional imaging guidance often relies on both computed tomography (CT) and X-ray fluoroscopy, exposing patients and staff to high doses of radiation while providing limited real-time 3D feedback. The choice of visualization may also affect operator performance and cognitive workload. We present an optical see-through augmented reality (OST-AR)–guided robotic system for spine procedures that provides in situ visualization of spinal structures to support needle trajectory planning. We integrate a cone-beam CT (CBCT)-derived 3D spine model, which is co-registered with live ultrasound, enabling users to combine global anatomical context with local, real-time imaging. We evaluated the system in a phantom user study involving two representative spine procedures: facet joint injection and lumbar puncture. Sixteen participants performed insertions under two visualization conditions: conventional screen vs. AR. Results show that AR significantly reduces execution time and across-task placement error, while also improving usability, trust, and spatial understanding, and lowering cognitive workload. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of AR-guided robotic ultrasound for spine interventions, highlighting its potential to enhance accuracy, efficiency, and user experience in image-guided procedures.

title: Feasibility, Reliability, and Acceptability of a Haptically Enabled Robot for Teleoperated Echocardiography.
abstract: Haptically enabled robotic teleoperated echocardiography (HERTEC) could improve access to skilled sonographers for patients in rural and remote areas. We sought to determine the feasibility, measurement accuracy, and participant responses to the performance of a robotic echocardiogram performed by a sonographer at a distance. In this cross-sectional study, 41 asymptomatic adults without known cardiac disease underwent focused echocardiography studies using a handheld ultrasound (HHU) device and robot. This device employed a collaborative robotic arm, force-torque sensors, and remote haptic control. Image quality was assessed using the 5-point American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP) scale from 1 (no recognizable structures) to 5 (excellent quality fully supporting diagnosis). A 5-point Likert scale questionnaire assessing participant feedback on safety was obtained posttest. American College of Emergency Physicians scores of the HERTEC system indicated 95% adequate quality (≥3) for parasternal long-axis, 91% for aortic valve-level parasternal short-axis, and 93% for apical 4-chamber views but lower rates for apical 2- and 3-chamber views (71%), with significant differences across windows. All HHU images reached adequate quality for each view. Structural measures demonstrated minor differences between robotic and HHU for left ventricular diastolic dimension (HHU 4.6 vs HERTEC 4.4 cm, P < .001) and left ventricular mass (HHU 126 vs HERTEC 115 g, P = .002). Quality scores were significantly different between methods for the mitral valve short-axis (P = .008), papillary muscle (P = .008), apical 2-chamber (P < .001), and apical long-axis (P < .001) views. The time to complete the study was the most significant difference between the HHU and HERTEC (5.2 ± 1.8 vs 25.2 ± 8.1 minutes, P < .001). Participants felt safe and informed and were willing to repeat robotic scans, with confidence in control features and diagnostic ability. Compared to traditional ultrasounds, 16% were less comfortable with robotic pressure and 10% expressed less overall comfort with the procedure. HERTEC consistently produced lower-quality images than a standard HHU but achieved echocardiography measurements comparable to HHU in most views, with excellent participant safety perceptions and high acceptability despite minor comfort differences. These findings indicate that robotic teleoperated heart ultrasound may have future potential, but technical advances to improve image quality and speed are required before clinical application.
authors: Leah Wright; Edgar M Hidalgo; Mariadas Roshan; Mats Isaksson; Thomas H Marwick

title: FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning (FL) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks-classification, detection, and segmentation. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation-compliant deployment in real-world gastroendoscopy practice.
authors: Alina Devkota; Annahita Amireskandari; Joel R. Palko; Soban A. Maan; Shyam J Thakkar; Tapan Khan; Xiajun Jiang; Donald Adjeroh; Binod Bhattarai; Prashnna Gyawali

title: Force-torque classification of reference-profile–defined drilling states during robot-assisted dental implant osteotomy
abstract: To evaluate whether force-torque features can classify three predefined, reference-profile-defined operational drilling states during robot-assisted implant osteotomy under specimen-level separation. Thirty porcine hemimandibular specimens underwent 180 robot-controlled osteotomies under three drilling conditions. Axial force (Fz) and drilling torque (Mz) were sampled at 1000 Hz, segmented into 100 ms windows with a 50 ms step, and represented by 42 time-, frequency-, and wavelet-domain features; 23 features were selected using training-only ANOVA ranking and correlation pruning. Specimens were separated into training, validation, and held-out test sets (18/6/6). Linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF), and XGBoost were evaluated against predefined depth-indexed operational reference profiles; a same-acquisition CBCT rule served as an imaging comparator. The dataset contained 92 675 overlapping windows. On six held-out specimens (36 osteotomies; 18 496 windows), XGBoost achieved 93.0% accuracy (specimen-clustered 95% CI, 92.0%-94.0%), 82.9% balanced accuracy, and 85.6% macro-F1. RF and SVM accuracies were 90.5% and 88.8%, respectively. The CBCT rule achieved 92.3% accuracy but lower balanced accuracy (80.1%) and transitional recall (51.1%). XGBoost transitional recall was 59.6%, increasing to 73.0% in a weighted sensitivity configuration at the cost of lower overall accuracy. Accuracy decreased from 94.1% away from class boundaries to 75.6% in boundary-adjacent windows. Force-torque features differentiated the three predefined reference-profile-defined drilling states under specimen-separated evaluation. XGBoost achieved the highest classification performance, with errors concentrated primarily in transitional and boundary-adjacent windows.
authors: Jiaqiang Li; Yao Wang; Min Shao; Yangdong Wu

title: ForceU-VLA: A Force-Aware Vision–Language–Action Model for Embodied Ultrasound Scanning
abstract: Embodied intelligent ultrasound scanning enables the automation and standardization of the ultrasound examination process by integrating perception, decision-making, and execution capabilities. However, existing methods suffer from loosely coupled modeling between force and ultrasound modalities and lack awareness of scanning stages, which limits their ability to capture dynamic probe–tissue interactions. To address these issues, we propose ForceU-VLA, a force-aware Vision–Language–Action model for autonomous embodied ultrasound scanning, which leverages force signals and ultrasound image feedback throughout the scanning process to enable accurate and high-quality ultrasound acquisition. Firstly, we propose a Force-Ultrasound Synergistic Fusion Module (FUSFM) that synergistically fuses ultrasound visual and force-feedback information to provide stable, reliable guidance for probe motion. Secondly, a Stage-Adaptive Modulation Mechanism (SAMM) is proposed to accommodate the task requirements across different scanning stages by adaptively modulating multimodal features to enhance their representation quality. Additionally, we introduce ForceU-VLA-Data, a real-world, force-aware embodied ultrasound dataset that integrates visual, force, and action signals, including data from two organs across five representative clinical scanning views, and comprising 450 expert-collected trajectories with approximately 100,000 synchronized multimodal frames. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that ForceU-VLA significantly improves contact stability and probe pressure regulation in embodied ultrasound scanning, thereby effectively enhancing task execution quality and overall system reliability. The source code is available at https://github.com/VMVLab/ForceU-VLA.
authors: Xingzheng Wu; Cheng Zhang; Gu Yan; Xifeng Hu; Zhi Liu; Qing Cai

title: From Engraftment to Vision: Defining Evidence of Functional Success in Retinal Cell Replacement Therapy
abstract: Retinal graft survival and post-treatment visual improvement do not, alone or together, demonstrate functional cell replacement. Apparent benefit may reflect material transfer, trophic rescue, residual host function or procedural and measurement effects. This critical narrative review uses a structured PubMed search covering January 2020 to August 2026, supplemented by seminal studies, to assess retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), photoreceptor, retinal sheet or organoid, and retinal ganglion cell (RGC) transplantation. We separate mechanistic attainment, downstream outcomes and claim-specific causal confidence. Authentic RPE replacement requires donor epithelial function across the host interface, without new synapses. Photoreceptor replacement requires donor phototransduction and transmission to host retinal circuitry; composite grafts additionally require identification of the active donor components. RGC replacement requires both retinal afferent integration and functional reconnection with appropriate central targets. Selected photoreceptor studies demonstrate persuasive local physiological coupling, but durability, donor necessity and generalisability remain incompletely established. Human evidence principally supports feasibility, safety and graft-associated anatomy, rather than convincingly donor-mediated visual restoration. We propose a non-linear evidence framework in which outcomes cannot substitute for secure donor provenance, cell-specific function or host-graft coupling. Spatial concordance, durability, controls, disease-model relevance and experimental unit should qualify every claim.
authors: Georgios D. Panos; Theo Empeslidis; Eleftherios Chatzimichail; Lorenzo Motta; Z Gatzioufas; Winfried M. K. Amoaku

title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework
abstract: Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies. Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation. The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning. A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration. A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively. Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback. End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.

title: From Repetition to Reform: Confronting Academic Redundancy in Dental Education
abstract: Introduction: Why This Conversation Matters NowModern dental education was built on a vision of continual improvement.Nearly over a century ago the great visionary William J. Gies said, What we want is a better class of better dentists, because the world is, I believe, suffering from a lack of good dental service more than from any bodily ailment of which we have any knowledge .This insightful vision has helped shape the foundations of modern dental education; the profession faces a different but related challenge: How to preserve educational rigor and institutional memory while ensuring that accumulated curricular and organizational structures remain responsive to contemporary learners and professional needs.Calls for transformation in dental education are not new.The American Dental Education Association (ADEA) Commission on Change and Innovation in Dental Education identified the need to reconsider traditional educational approaches and promote deliberate change in response to evolving societal, professional, and educational demands [ 1,2 ].The Commission's work also highlighted concerns about curricular complexity and educational environments that may be expensive and dissatisfying for learners [ 2 ].Yet curricular renewal remains challenging.New knowledge, technologies, expectations, and educational priorities are often added to existing structures, while fewer mechanisms exist for systematically determining what should be integrated, reduced, or retired.
authors: Manish Kumar Bhagania; Richard D’Innocenzo; Gail McCausland; Cataldo W. Leone

title: From algorithm performance to clinical value in AI-assisted skin cancer diagnostics
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated high diagnostic performance in skin cancer detection and is increasingly being integrated into clinical workflows. However, whether these advances translate into meaningful patient-relevant and healthcare system outcomes remains unclear. Evidence on value-oriented outcomes has not been systematically synthesized. Methods: We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of studies published between January 2015 and October 2025 identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science. Studies evaluating AI-based technologies for skin cancer diagnosis, triage, risk stratification, or management were included if they reported outcomes beyond technical performance metrics. Reported outcomes were mapped to three value-oriented domains: clinical and prognostic, process and experiential, and system-level and economic outcomes. Results: Of 4,021 records identified, 33 studies met the inclusion criteria, whereas 389 publications were excluded because they reported only technical performance metrics without value-oriented outcomes. Reported outcomes were predominantly process and experiential (28/33 studies), including diagnostic confidence, workflow efficiency, and user acceptance. Clinical and prognostic outcomes were reported in only five studies, with four studies focussing on prognostic utility and one study focussing on patient management, while system-level and economic outcomes were identified in three studies. Most evaluations were conducted in controlled experimental settings, whereas prospective real-world implementation studies were less common. Overall, the available evidence predominantly focused on process-level benefits, with limited evidence for clinical and prognostic or system-level and economic outcomes. Discussion: Current evaluation strategies for AI-based skin cancer diagnostics remain predominantly performance-oriented and are largely focused on process and experiential outcomes. From a value-based healthcare perspective, current evidence remains largely confined to intermediate stages of the diagnostic value chain: although AI-assisted systems may improve diagnostic workflows, clinician confidence, and clinical decision making, few studies have evaluated their impact on downstream patient-relevant clinical and prognostic, or system-level and economic outcomes. Future research should prioritize prospective real-world studies, outcome-driven evaluation frameworks, and economic assessments that examine the impact of AI-supported decision-making on clinical outcomes and healthcare systems. Conclusion: Despite promising effects on diagnostic processes, evidence for the clinical and system-level value of AI-based skin cancer diagnostics remains limited. Outcome-driven evaluation frameworks are needed to bridge the gap between algorithmic performance and meaningful healthcare impact.
authors: Lennart Ocker; Elisabeth Livingstone; Georg Christian Lodde; Eggert Stockfleth; Nessr Abu Rached; Dirk Schadendorf; Stephan Nüesch

title: From biomechanical data to robotic execution: design and control of an intelligent Tuina system
abstract: Introduction: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) Tuina (massage) relies heavily on practitioners' physical stamina and subjective experience, leading to operational variability that hinders therapeutic standardization and scalable rehabilitation service delivery. To address this limitation, this study proposes an intelligent TCM Tuina robotic system integrating biomechanical data-driven design and hybrid control strategies. Methods: A 6-DOF manipulator equipped with a biomimetic end-effector is developed, and a CMPGA-Corr neural network (Convolutional Multi-branch Prototype-Guided Architecture with a Channel-Correlation Branch) is constructed to decouple the spatiotemporal features of nine Tuina manipulations from 25-channel tactile data. Robotic execution is implemented within a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2)-based control framework. The framework combines RRT-Connect path planning, S-curve speed profiling, and RBF-compensated admittance control. PID, conventional Admittance, and RBF controllers were compared in complete-process simulations using five repetitions per manipulation. Results: The RBF controller produced the lowest mean RMSE and MAE for all six evaluated manipulations. Physical experiments on a silicone back phantom further demonstrated bounded and repeatable force-tracking behavior under the tested conditions. Discussion: The proposed framework bridges TCM practice with modern robotic engineering and provides a scalable and standardized solution for precision rehabilitation robotics.
authors: Yuhui Zhou; Enna Chen; Jiale Lu; Xuan Qiao; Liu‐Jie Ren; Yi Yu; Zouqin Huang; Wei Yao

title: From macroscopic screening to microscopic characterization: AI and CLE in small bowel disorders
abstract: Background Small bowel diseases have long posed a diagnostic challenge in gastroenterology due to their deep anatomical location, tortuous configuration, and nonspecific clinical presentation. Capsule endoscopy (CE) and device-assisted enteroscopy (DAE) have improved small bowel visualization, yet CE reading burden and DAE procedural complexity remain core limitations. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy and confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) have emerged as promising solutions. Methods This review narratively synthesizes the current evidence on AI-assisted capsule endoscopy (AI-CE) and AI-assisted device-assisted enteroscopy (AI-DAE) in the diagnosis of small bowel disorders. A critical appraisal approach was adopted to evaluate methodological quality, lesion type coverage, and standardization across studies. A literature search of PubMed was performed up to September 1, 2026, and reference lists of key reviews were screened to identify additional relevant articles. Results AI-CE has accumulated substantial evidence for Tier 1–2 (lesion detection and macroscopic classification), yet its capability does not extend to Tier 3 (microscopic characterization). AI applications in DAE are in early stages, facing challenges of data scarcity and cross-device generalization. CLE enables real-time “optical biopsy” but is constrained by the pharmacological limitation that fluorescein sodium does not stain cell nuclei and the absence of small bowel-specific diagnostic criteria. While AI + CLE has achieved notable progress in other parts of the gastrointestinal tract, the small bowel remains nearly blank. Conclusion The current core bottleneck lies not in technical feasibility but in the uneven distribution of research effort. This review proposes a four-step integrated framework—CE macroscopic screening → AI-CE reading → DAE-guided CLE targeted characterization → AI-CLE image analysis—to bridge the gap between macroscopic screening and microscopic characterization. This framework remains conceptual and requires prospective validation.
authors: Lianting Zhang; Wei Zhang

title: From task-specific networks to foundation models in diabetes care: a critical review of opportunities, evaluation gaps, and safety frontiers
abstract: Artificial intelligence in diabetes care has historically relied on task-specific supervised learning, such as bespoke networks for retinopathy grading, kidney disease prediction, and glucose forecasting. The emergence of foundation models (FMs: large models pretrained on broad data, typically with self-supervision, and adapted to many downstream tasks) is displacing this paradigm across diabetes-relevant modalities: ophthalmic models such as RETFound, pretrained on 1.6 million retinal photographs, have been reported to outperform task-specific networks on retinopathy grading and systemic disease prediction, especially when labeled data are scarce; transformer-based time-series models are replacing long short-term memory (LSTM) pipelines for continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) forecasting; clinical large language models (LLMs) such as Med-PaLM and GPT-4 attain expert-level scores on medical question-answering benchmarks; and generative models supply synthetic CGM and electronic health record (EHR) data. This review provides a critical, modality-organized synthesis of this transition. We (i) formalize a three-era taxonomy: rule-based risk scores (era I), task-specific deep learning (era II, 2016-2020), and foundation models (era III, from 2021), and map the diabetes literature onto it; (ii) survey foundation-model architectures, pretraining objectives, and adaptation strategies across retinal imaging, CGM, longitudinal EHR, and multimodal data; (iii) expose an evaluation crisis: benchmark contamination of LLM medical evaluations, a near-universal absence in the literature we reviewed of external and prospective validation for retinal and CGM foundation models, miscalibration under dataset shift, and, to our knowledge and within the reviewed literature (January 2016-December 2025; negative findings are time-sensitive), the absence of any randomized evaluation of a foundation model in a diabetes workflow; and (iv) analyze safety risks: hallucinated insulin-dosing advice, automation bias, inherited algorithmic inequity, and privacy exposure during adaptation. We conclude that the decisive open problem is no longer representation learning but grounded, calibrated, causally informed deployment, requiring contamination-resistant evaluation, prospective trials, and hybrid architectures coupling foundation-model representations with treatment-effect estimation.
authors: M. Nanda Kishore; C. Navaneethan

title: Fundic Heterotopic Pancreas: Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection of a Subepithelial Lesion
abstract: Gastric subepithelial lesions (SELs) encompass a wide range of pathologies, including lipomas, gastrointestinal stromal tumours (GISTs) and heterotopic pancreas, and can be challenging to diagnose on endoscopy and endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) alone. We report a woman in her 50s who presented with abdominal discomfort and was found to have a subepithelial lesion in the gastric fundus, initially considered to represent a GIST. Despite repeated EUS and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) over four years of surveillance, tissue diagnosis remained elusive. She ultimately underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), with histology confirming pancreatic heterotopia. Follow-up endoscopy demonstrated complete healing, and she was discharged from surveillance. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty of heterotopic pancreas presenting with atypical features often masquerading as a GIST. It demonstrates ESD as a safe, minimally invasive, diagnostic and therapeutic option when diagnosis cannot be achieved by conventional means.
authors: Apoorva Hegde; Parth Paskaran

title: Fundus torsion in strabismus: Measurement, clinical interpretation, and emerging imaging approaches.
abstract: Fundus torsion is an important but underused anatomical marker in strabismus evaluation, particularly for cyclovertical disorders. Unlike subjective cyclodeviation testing, fundus-based assessment provides an objective reference based on retinal landmarks, though it remains influenced by image acquisition, head position, ocular anatomy, and measurement conventions. We synthesize the anatomical basis of ocular and fundus torsion, contemporary qualitative and quantitative assessment methods, and disease-specific evidence across superior oblique palsy, pattern strabismus, pediatric and adult strabismus, and surgical follow-up. The review emphasizes 3 clinically important issues: the frequent dissociation between objective fundus torsion and subjective cyclodeviation, the need for method-specific interpretation using reproducibility and minimal-detectable-change data, and the importance of avoiding isolated treatment decisions based on anatomical torsion alone. Recent optical coherence tomography-based and artificial intelligence-assisted approaches may improve measurement consistency and scalability, but current evidence supports their use as adjunctive tools rather than autonomous decision systems. Fundus torsion should therefore be interpreted within a multimodal clinical framework that integrates motility findings, sensory status, age, chronicity, fixation behavior, and surgical history. Treatment options include observation and symptom relief in selected patients, inferior oblique weakening for associated overaction, and torsion-directed surgery for persistent symptomatic excyclotorsion; comparative evidence remains limited. Prospective comparative treatment studies are a clinical research priority. Standardized acquisition protocols, explicit reporting conventions, age- and population-specific normative data, externally validated automated methods, and prospective studies linking torsional change to symptoms and functional outcomes are needed to strengthen the clinical utility of fundus torsion assessment.
authors: Kai Jin; Chee Chew Yip; Stephen P Christiansen; Andrzej Grzybowski; Jingjing Jiang

title: Generative Active Learning for Label-Efficient Pan-Organ Ultrasound Diagnosis
abstract: Medical ultrasound (US) enables real-time, non-invasive diagnosis, yet building US-based AI systems is limited by data scarcity, costly expert annotation, and limited cross-center generalizability. Privacy constraints and instance-level reporting hinder the collection of diverse abnormal cases and frame-level labels, while repeated retraining for new centers increases computational cost. We introduce EvoDiff, a generative active learning framework that integrates diffusion modelling with information-theoretic objectives, evolutionary search, and curriculum-based sampling to select informative samples across heterogeneous US datasets. EvoDiff formulates sample selection as a generate-to-retrieve process, in which diffusion-based optimization in feature space guided by information gain produces synthetic probes, and only the real unlabeled samples retrieved by these probes are annotated and used for downstream training. Across six benchmarks covering fifteen datasets and 16,696 images, we evaluate EvoDiff on convolutional network and transformer-based foundation model. EvoDiff approaches fully supervised performance with substantially fewer labels, outperforms active learning baselines, and improves foundation model generalization under cross-domain external validation on unseen cohorts. A reader study with six radiologists indicates the potential to support clinical annotation workflows, with a model-based estimated 24% to 84% reduction in annotation workload at matched downstream performance.
authors: Yaofei Duan; Yuhao Huang; Yuan Gao; Ruixiang Qi; Tianyu Zhang; Yanlin Geng; Yue Sun; Sio-Kei Im; Dong Ni; Dong Xu; Ritse Mann; Tao Tan

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Dentistry: Clinical Applications, Evidence, Limitations, Ethical Considerations, and a Framework for Responsible Implementation
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), including large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models, is increasingly being used in dentistry, dental education, and scientific research. Unlike conventional predictive AI, which is generally developed for defined classification or prediction tasks, GenAI can produce new text, images, summaries, and other outputs from user prompts. In dentistry, potential applications include patient communication, clinical documentation, education, literature synthesis, and selected forms of decision support. These applications are accompanied by important risks, including hallucinated information, bias, privacy breaches, fabricated references, and automation bias. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence on GenAI in dentistry, with emphasis on the distinction between assistive use and autonomous clinical decision-making. Recent systematic, scoping, and narrative reviews describe applications in dental education, oral and maxillofacial surgery, implant dentistry, endodontics, and other areas, but the available evidence remains heterogeneous and prospective clinical validation is limited. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) may improve evidence alignment by linking language models to curated external sources, although dental-specific evidence remains early. Based on the reviewed literature, responsible implementation should be task-specific and should include data minimization, verification of outputs, human accountability, documentation, and ongoing monitoring. A seven-stage framework is proposed: define the task, assess risk, protect data, verify output, retain human decision-making, document relevant AI use, and monitor performance. At present, GenAI is best regarded as an assistive technology that can support, but should not replace, professional dental judgment.

title: Giant Brunner's gland hamartoma: the surgical management of complex cases.
abstract: Brunner's gland hamartoma (BGH) is a rare, benign tumour composed of mucin-secreting glands within the duodenal submucosa. Lesions typically range from 0.5 to 1.0cm and are usually managed endoscopically, with larger tumours occurring infrequently. This case involves a 74-year-old woman presenting with syncope. Diagnostic investigations revealed a massive BGH with a 10cm pedicle, accompanied by significant iron deficiency anaemia and intussusception. Although there are no formal, universally established guidelines, literature favours endoscopic removal because of reduced bleeding, a shorter hospital stay and lower cost. However, open surgical resection proved more appropriate owing to the lesion's size and complexity. This case highlights the challenges of managing giant BGHs and supports open surgical intervention when standard methods are unsuccessful.
