title: Haptic Probing for Subsurface-Aware Force Distribution on Layered Soft Tissue
abstract: Force-regulated contact with layered soft tissue fails most often where the subsurface composition changes: controllers infer the substrate from the loading signal alone, so the estimate guiding them lags the change---more acutely, we argue, over compliant than over bone-backed tissue. We remove that lag with a separate haptic channel. Under a light preload, a brief low-amplitude excitation lets the local dynamic admittance discriminate muscle from bone-backed tissue relative to a per-subject baseline, before task force is applied---active haptic sensing used to commit a control decision rather than to characterise tissue. A force- and tactile-driven distribution law then consumes that regime throughout execution: an instantaneous allocation equalises pressure across the engaged fingertips, while the regime sets the admissible pressure and hence the area the hand must recruit to deliver the target force---making patch area a controlled variable rather than a by-product. Probing, switches and recruitment are priced in a partitioned passivity budget, so safety monitoring cannot suppress the probe and a refused recruitment forfeits force tracking rather than the pressure bound. We report force tracking and pressure uniformity over curved, migrating contact on three human subjects, with regime labels from anatomical landmarks.
authors: Lei Shi; Xiaoyu Wang; Cheng Zhou; Yongjian Liu; Jing Wang; Dongsheng Zhang; Yonghui Zhu; Xiong Li

title: Hiding in plain sight: case report of congenital simplehamartoma of the retinal pigment epithelium
abstract: Congenital simple hamartoma of the retinal pigment epithelium (CSHRPE) is an extremely rare benign intraocular tumor, originating from the retinal pigment epithelium. The exact prevalence of CSHRPE is unknown, but very few cases have been reported in the literature to date. It is typically asymptomatic, discovered mostly incidentally during routine eye examination, and it can mimic other pigmented retinal lesions, posing diagnostic challenges. We present a case of a 53-year-old woman referred for ophthalmological evaluation due to recurrent, non-specific headaches. Fundus examination revealed a juxtafoveal, hyperpigmented lesion of the left eye with associated drusen around the lesion. Multimodal imaging, including fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and fluorescein angiography (FA), confirmed the diagnosis of CSHRPE. OCT showed a well-demarcated, elevated, hyperreflective lesion causing optical shadowing of deeper retinal layers. FAF demonstrated a complete lack of autofluorescence at the lesion site, while FA revealed hypofluorescence throughout all phases without autonomous circulation. Unlike prior reports describing complications such as macular edema, epiretinal membrane, or macular hole, no such changes were observed in this patient. The lesion was stable over five years of follow-up, and visual acuity remained unaffected. In the absence of complications or progression, no treatment was necessary, but periodic monitoring is recommended.
authors: Ivana Ljubić Zeljko; Irena Sesar; Ivan Zeljko; Renato Pejic

title: High Accuracy Fingerprint Recognition on FPGA Using a Dual Path Lightweight CNN
abstract: This paper addresses the increasing demand for reliable identity verification in various applications and highlights the importance of biometric features such as fingerprints due to the limitations and potential distrust of identification cards. Given the strong performance of neural network-based methods, this work focuses on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for fingerprint image classification and identification, with an emphasis on efficient hardware implementation on field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs). A lightweight CNN architecture is proposed that achieves higher accuracy compared to prior approaches while operating directly on raw images without pre-processing. The proposed model is evaluated under two data augmentation scenarios, achieving accuracies of 70.3% and 63.1%, respectively, outperforming previous studies. The network response time per sample is 77.9 ms on GPU and requires approximately 483 KB of memory for parameter storage. The architecture is implemented on a Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA using VHDL, utilizing 70% of available resources. The FPGA implementation consumes 28.72 W of power and operates at a maximum frequency of 108.6 MHz.
authors: Abdolah Amirany; Belal Jahannia; HAMED Dalir

title: High-Precision RCM Motion for Ophthalmic Robotics via Hierarchical QP Control and Authority-Guided Recovery Planning
abstract: General-purpose manipulators can position ophthalmic instruments under a software Remote Centre of Motion (RCM). However, at some reachable configurations that are nonsingular for the tip task alone, the RCM and tip-tracking objectives conflict and the servo oscillates. We formalise this failure as a constraint-induced task singularity: the RCM-projected tip Jacobian loses rank while the unprojected tip Jacobian stays well conditioned. Thus, the effective tip authority collapses although the target remains reachable. We present a high-precision RCM servo architecture with built-in singularity recovery: for each commanded target, an authority-guided planner selects a well-conditioned arm configuration that reaches it and plans an RCM-consistent route, executed by a fixed hierarchical-QP controller. On a 200-scenario kinematic benchmark, the complete nominal-and-recovery protocol reaches 128/128 near-singular targets and 71/72 near-joint-limit targets (100% and 99%, respectively), with the software-RCM residual below 0.142 mm. On a physical 6-DOF arm it executes across four RCM entry points, with a worst-case kinematically reconstructed RCM residual of 178 μm and a median tip-regulation error of 32μm, within the 200μm control requirement adopted for the ophthalmic task.
authors: Huanyu Tian; Adriana Namour; Lingyun Zeng; Zicong Wu; Sébastien Ourselin; Lyndon da Cruz; Christos Bergeles

title: High-Speed Widefield Hyperspectral Imaging
abstract: Fourier-transform hyperspectral imaging is an emerging technology that combines widefield acquisition with flexible spectral resolution. Yet, it typically requires the acquisition of dense sequences of full-field interferograms during optical-path scanning, which ultimately reduces the final throughput. To circumvent this limitation, this manuscript introduces an event-based Fourier-transform hyperspectral microscopy technique that exploits the coupling of a neuromorphic event camera with a common-path birefringent interferometer operated under continuous scanning. Specifically, two complementary acquisition strategies are investigated, one with steady broadband illumination where the event stream corresponds to a derivative-like interferogram, and another with a temporal modulation of a broadband LED, which produces an intensity-like event response. Both approaches are able to retrieve the principal spectral profiles of photographic filters, showing a good qualitative match with both frame-based and spectrometer references. Compared against the typical 15-minute acquisition time for step-scan reference configuration, both methods represent a speedup larger than 3 orders of magnitude, entering real-time acquisition speeds: the derivative-based method acquires the useful interferometric range in approximately 200 ms, corresponding to an effective rate of approximately 5 hyperspectral cubes per second, whereas the modulation-assisted method achieves an experimentally measured spectral resolution of 17.9 nm at an effective acquisition rate of 2.5 datacubes per second. Finally, reflection-mode imaging and motion-compensated reconstruction of moving particles further demonstrate spatially resolved spectral recovery beyond static transmission measurements, establishing the solution as a promising technology for continuous, wide-field hyperspectral imaging.
authors: Joana M. Teixeira; Tomás Lopes; Tiago D. Ferreira; Catarina Sofia Bento Monteiro; Pedro A. S. Jorge; Nuno A. Silva

title: Household beverage consumption patterns and their influence on dental erosion risk
abstract: Dental erosion is a growing oral health concern characterized by the irreversible loss of dental hard tissues through chemical processes involving acids of non-bacterial origin. Frequent consumption of acidic beverages, including carbonated soft drinks, fruit juices, energy drinks, and sports drinks, contributes to enamel demineralization and increases the risk of erosive tooth wear. Household beverage consumption patterns play a significant role in shaping dietary behaviors, particularly among children and adolescents who develop their preferences through family interactions and shared routines. Parental drinking habits, purchasing decisions, and the availability of acidic beverages at home influence the frequency and duration of dietary acid exposure. Children often adopt beverage preferences observed in their parents, potentially establishing consumption patterns that persist into adulthood. The relationship between shared beverage habits and dental erosion is influenced by several factors, including beverage acidity, consumption frequency, drinking methods, salivary protection, and individual susceptibility. Prolonged sipping and repeated consumption between meals may extend acid contact with dental surfaces, increasing the likelihood of enamel damage. Socioeconomic circumstances, cultural preferences, and parental awareness also contribute to differences in household beverage choices and associated oral health risks. Family-based preventive strategies emphasize reducing acidic beverage availability, encouraging water consumption, and promoting healthier drinking routines. Parental involvement in dietary education can support behavioral modifications and improve children's understanding of beverage-related oral health consequences. Regular dental examinations, early identification of erosive changes, and individualized dietary counseling remain essential for managing erosive tooth wear. Although household members may share similar drinking habits, differences in biological characteristics and oral protective mechanisms can produce varying clinical outcomes. Addressing beverage consumption within the family environment provides opportunities to reduce repeated acid exposure, strengthen preventive practices, and promote sustainable oral health behaviors across different age groups and generations while supporting broader efforts to prevent diet-related dental erosion throughout childhood and later life.
authors: Abdulaziz Fareed Meeralsulaimani; Abdulrahman Hamed Aljohani; Azam Tariq Abushal; Mazen Abdulaziz Alfaruqi; Salem Abdulrahman Albalawi; Arwa Saeed Alqahtani; Wesam Yousef Alibrahim; Sheikha Ibrahim Alfayez; Noura Salem Alqahtani; Jawaher Salem Alzahrani
venue: International Journal of Community Medicine and Public Health

title: How does hard magnetic soft matter deform?
abstract: Hard magnetic soft materials, i.e. elastomers seeded with hard magnetic particles, convert magnetic energy into complex motion and have become central to the design of untethered soft robots, biomedical devices, and, in general, for enabling fast, wireless actuation. Their behavior depends critically on how the surrounding soft matrix deforms and transmits torque to each magnetized inclusion, yet there is no consensus on the correct mapping between macroscopic strain and microscopic motion. Competing models predict conflicting particle rotations and magnetic responses under identical loads. Here, we construct counterexamples that show the key shortcomings in these models, and then establish a first-principles framework that leads to an optimal deformation mapping. The resulting closed-form law unifies conflicting models and shows that they are, in fact, simply different limits of our general approach. Our work permits the rational design of magnetically actuated soft devices and a unified view of deformation in magnetic soft matter, and broadly, in similar architectured materials.
authors: Daniel Katusele; Carmel Majidi; Liping Liu; Pradeep Sharma; Kaushik Dayal

title: Human-Centered Robotics for Surgery
abstract: Surgical ergonomics is influenced by many aspects associated with posture, vision, hand motion, and haptic feedback. Specific ergonomics aspects can induce long-term effects in the surgeon directly affecting the performance. One of the major disadvantages of Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) remains the non-ergonomic design of the entire surgical environment. This condition results in a significant reduction in the quality of interventions and discomfort for the medical operator. Modern teleoperated surgical robots offer an optimized console, in which the surgeon can operate in a seated position with specific arm support and a 3D view of the operating site. The da Vinci surgical console offers ergonomic improvements over standard endoscopic surgery. Modern robotic platforms stand beyond the da Vinci System, offering more advanced ergonomic solutions in terms of haptic feedback and visual perception. Due to the introduction of more advanced technology, surgery has changed, resulting in increased system complexity at the technical, human and organizational levels, which may lead to higher variability of patient outcomes due to new error pathways. Adopting a proactive approach enables the prior identification of critical factors and the design of safer socio-technical systems, thanks to a multi-level perspective. This chapter addresses the fundamental elements of surgical ergonomics, considering the factors that affect performance and healthiness during traditional procedures, with specific reference to MIS and microsurgery. This baseline is then compared to the use of surgical robots by evaluating the effect of design decisions on operator ergonomics. In addition, studies propose proactive methodologies that assess the personal and organizational factors of surgical performance in this complex socio-technical system.
authors: Rocco Moccia; Raffaella Mancino; Emanuele Ruffaldi; Massimiliano Simi; Rossella Onofrio; Fanny Ficuciello

title: Hybrid deep feature fusion framework with maximum entropy based selection for accurate diabetic foot ulcer diagnosis from enhanced and segmented medical images
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) pose significant risks, including delayed wound healing, infection, and, in severe cases, amputation. Early diagnosis is critical to mitigate these risks and enhance patient outcomes. Manual assessment may be affected by inter-observer variability and workflow delays, which motivates the investigation of AI-assisted methods for DFU image classification. In this study, several hybrid artificial neural network (ANN) strategies were developed incorporating features from various convolutional neural network (CNN) models for diabetic ulcer image diagnosis. The use of feature selection algorithms, specifically principal component analysis (PCA) and maximum entropy score based selection (MESbS), enhanced the discriminatory power of the models. Image quality was improved by using fused filters - average and Laplacian - to enhance the images and highlight the features of the diabetic ulcer and highlight the boundaries of the lesion. The geometric active contour (GAC) algorithm facilitated isolation of damaged areas from healthy areas. AlexNet, MobileNetV2 and VGG16 models processed these regions and extracted deep feature maps. These maps are later combined to create global feature vectors, namely, AlexNet-MobileNetV2, MobileNetV2-VGG16, AlexNet-VGG16, and AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16. The fusion of features from multiple CNN models gives rise to high-dimensional vectors, prompting the application of PCA and MESbS for feature selection. The proposed hybrid strategies demonstrated strong diagnostic performance on the evaluated dataset. Among the evaluated configurations, the AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16-ANN model with MESbS achieved the highest performance, reaching an AUC of 99%, sensitivity of 99.7%, accuracy of 99.5%, precision of 99.5%, and specificity of 99.75%. These findings suggest that combining complementary CNN feature representations with feature selection may improve DFU classification under the evaluated experimental conditions.
authors: Elham Ali; Ebrahim Mohammed Senan; Narmine El Hakim; M. Attique Khan; Ibrahim Abdulrab Ahmed; Omaia Mohammed Al-Omari; Suliman Mohamed Fati

title: INTELLIGENT DENTAL DISEASE DIAGNOSIS AND PERSONALIZED TREATMENT RECOMMENDATION USING MOBILENETV3
abstract: Many dental problems go unnoticed until they cause pain or visible damage, which makes easy-to-reach screening and prompt professional follow-up valuable.In this paper we describe a web-based decision-support system that pairs deep-learning image analysis with visual explanation, patient-friendly guidance, and a dentist's review.The users upload an intraoral picture or dental x-ray, which is then fed into a MobileNetV3 classifier dedicated to that particular modality.There are seven classes for each classifier.The pictures are categorized according to the following classes: calculus, caries, gingivitis, healthy, hypodontia, oral ulcer, and tooth discoloration, whereas x-rays are classified in the following order: dental caries, dental infection, endoperio lesion, impacted tooth, periapical lesion, periodontal bone loss, and root fracture.The application presents the user with a Grad-CAM heatmap showing the part of the image that made the AI give a particular diagnosis.In addition, it gives the confidence score, indicative severity, and corresponding home care recommendations.Prior to giving the final diagnosis to the patient, the dentist can approve, deny, or modify the prediction of the AI.The application is developed using React.js,FastAPI, and PostgreSQL technologies and offers a prediction history, PDF reports, and a chatbot powered by Llama 3.3 model hosted on Groq.We present our work as a prototype of clinical decision support rather than fully autonomous diagnostic software since its accuracy and practical use require further validation on independent test sets and in prospective studies with clinicians.
venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science

title: ISG15+ Müller glial subtype contributes to early blood–retinal barrier breakdown in diabetic retinopathy
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy features early glial stress and neurovascular dysfunction, yet Müller glial programs linking inflammatory cues to oxidative injury remain unclear. We identify a spatially clustered interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15)+ Müller glial subtype expanded in streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice. High glucose alone did not increase basal free ISG15 or detectable ISGylation (ISG15-dependent protein modification) in primary Müller glia, whereas conditioned medium from high glucose-exposed microglia induced both, recapitulated by IFN-β and attenuated by type I interferon receptor 1 inhibition. In vivo, Ifnb1 RNAscope signals were associated with microglia, retinal Ifnb1 expression increased in diabetic retinas, and microglial depletion reduced Ifnb1 expression and limited the expansion of ISG15+ Müller glia. Müller glia-specific Isg15 deletion preserved blood-retinal barrier integrity, reduced acellular capillaries and Evans blue leakage, and mitigated oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and glutathione redox imbalance. Loss of ISG15 or disruption of ISGylation blunted interferon-driven oxidative stress in Müller glia and reduced Müller glia-conditioned medium-dependent endothelial migration and tube formation. Mechanistically, IFN-β promoted peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6) ISGylation and proteasome-dependent degradation without altering Prdx6 transcripts. Thus, microglial IFN-β promotes an ISG15+ Müller glial subtype that compromises antioxidant defense and promotes early barrier injury in diabetic retinopathy.
authors: Tian Niu; Yan Jiang; Xindan Xing; Qian Zhu; Xinyi Liu; Kangjia Lv; Junwei Fang; Kun Liu

title: Imaging biological tissue at extended depth using swept-source visible-light OCT
abstract: We present a swept-source visible-light optical coherence tomography (SS-vis-OCT) system with twice the imaging depth of prior SS-vis-OCT and improved sensitivity for imaging biological samples, achieving shot-noise-limited operation. Because second-harmonic generation is limited by the booster optical amplifier’s output power, the visible-light SS power is capped at 450 µW. Increasing it further would require a more powerful, but costlier, amplifier. Instead, we reduce the receiver noise floor by selecting a balanced detector with NEP approaching the thermal (Johnson–Nyquist) limit. Real-time numerical k-linearization increases the effective number of linear-in-wavenumber samples per sweep, further improving SNR and extending the imaging range. Together, these improvements yield a sensitivity of 89 dB and an imaging depth of 9 mm in air or 6.5 mm in tissue, enabling full anterior-segment imaging of ex vivo porcine eyes.
authors: Weijia Fan; Roman V. Kuranov; Menglin Shi; Fengyuanshan Xu; Junfang Zhang; Hao F. Zhang

title: Impact of AI‐Assisted Endoscopy on Secondary Review and Referral Decisions in Gastric Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Real‐World Study
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted endoscopy may support gastric cancer screening, but its impact on structured secondary human review remains unclear. We evaluated secondary review modifications and referral decisions before and after AI implementation. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 5013 screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy examinations performed before (n = 2021) and after (n = 2992) AI implementation. The primary outcome was secondary review modifications. Secondary outcomes included referral for further diagnostic evaluation. Multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, Helicobacter pylori eradication status, prior-year endoscopy, and endoscopist experience were performed. Interaction analyses according to endoscopist experience and inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses were conducted. No external reference standard was available to verify secondary-review modifications or referral decisions. RESULTS: Secondary review modifications increased from 1.2% in the pre-AI period to 3.7% in the AI period (p < 0.01). A significant interaction was observed between AI implementation and endoscopist experience (p for interaction < 0.01), with increased modifications primarily among nonexpert endoscopists. Cancer-related modifications remained uncommon but increased after AI implementation (0.6% vs. 0.2%, p = 0.04). Referral rates decreased from 4.9% to 2.8% (p < 0.01), and AI implementation was independently associated with lower odds of referral (adjusted OR = 0.53; 95% confidence interval = 0.36-0.77). CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted endoscopy was associated with lower referral rates; however, secondary review modifications persisted after AI implementation, particularly among nonexpert endoscopists. These findings describe workflow changes and do not establish the clinical validity of the modifications or the appropriateness of referral decisions.
authors: Sachiyo Onishi; Seiji Adachi; Masahito Shimizu

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Radiographic Caries Detection on Clinical Decision-Making and Patient Outcomes: A Systematic Review
abstract: Dental caries remains a major global health problem, with approximately 2.24 billion people worldwide affected by untreated caries in permanent teeth in 2021. This persistent burden highlights the importance of accurate detection and appropriate management of carious lesions. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly investigated for caries detection on dental radiographs, yet improved diagnostic performance does not necessarily translate into appropriate treatment decisions or better patient outcomes. This systematic review evaluated evidence linking AI-assisted radiographic caries assessment with treatment decisions, treatment intensity, clinical consequences, and economic outcomes. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by PRISMA 2020, with searches carried out in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and SpringerLink. Eligible primary studies applied AI to dental radiographs and linked caries assessment to treatment decisions, treatment recommendations, treatment intensity or appropriateness, clinical consequences, or economic outcomes. Eleven studies were included from 998 records, comprising one cluster-randomized crossover trial, four economic/modeling evaluations, two diagnostic or ex vivo decision studies, and four treatment-planning or decision-support studies. AI assistance improved sensitivity and AUC but also altered treatment decisions, including increased invasive treatment for some lesions. Economic models generally favored AI when early lesions received non-restorative management, whereas trial-derived decisions showed no economic advantage. Treatment-recommendation systems demonstrated technical feasibility but lacked evidence of improved clinical appropriateness or patient outcomes. Overall, AI may influence treatment pathways, but clinical utility evidence remains less mature than diagnostic evidence. Future studies should evaluate AI using prospective designs, independent validation, lesion-specific management pathways, and patient-important outcomes.
authors: Fitri Yustika Sya’bani; Titiek Berniyanti; Dina Izzatul Mila Azka

title: Improved AlexNet–Bi-LSTM Model-Based Gastrointestinal Cancer Classification with Shape and Texture Feature Set
abstract: Background: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancer classification is the process of identifying and categorizing cancers that occur in the GI tract based on their morphological, histopathological, and molecular characteristics. Existing GI cancer classification systems often struggle with low interpretability and limited generalizability across diverse datasets. This study aims to improve the accuracy of classifying cancer. Methods: The Improved AlexNet–Bi-LSTM model-based Gastrointestinal Cancer Classification (IAB-GCC) with a shape andtexture feature set is proposed to improve diagnostic accuracy. The input images are from a dataset consisting of 411,890 unique image patches generated from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) diagnostic slides. Then, the proposed IAB-GCC process begins with input images, which are preprocessed using an Adaptive Weighted Gaussian Filtering (AWGF) technique to reduce noise and enhance image quality. Key features including Weighted Shannon Entropy (WSE)-based features, texture features using Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM), shape, and morphological features are then extracted and fed into the Alex–-Bi-LSTM network, where the extracted features are passed into an Improved AlexNet (IANet) model to train the features, and then the learned feature maps of IANet are subjected to a Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) model for classification. Results: The combination of IANet and Bi-LSTM enables the system to classify cancer cases as stable or unstable, which provides precise and reliable diagnostic results. The proposed IAB-GCC model achieves a higher precision 97% and an accuracy score of 96% in the classification process of GI cancers. Conclusion: The proposed hybrid IAB-GCC provides accurate, reliable, and interpretable GI cancer classification, demonstrating potential for clinical diagnostic applications.
authors: Vanishree Abhay; Achyutha Prasad N; Sathish Babu N; Rekha V S
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Technology

title: Improving the active Crohn’s disease reference standard: comparative evaluation of latent class analysis and panel consensus
abstract: Active Crohn’s disease manifests as bowel inflammation, culminating in chronic damage. Its reference standard must combine evidence from multiple tests, each with suboptimal accuracy alone, to first classify Crohn’s presence and then activity. Panel consensus combines such evidence but is time-consuming, resource-intensive, and vulnerable to group biases. Latent class analysis offers a promising statistical alternative; however, the absence of comparisons against panel consensus limits wider use. We therefore performed the first comparative evaluation of latent class analysis and panel consensus as the reference standard for a diagnostic test accuracy trial. We retrospectively analysed 284 patients with a new Crohn’s diagnosis or suspected relapse. We focused on terminal ileal Crohn’s (TICD), where evidence of activity was most abundant. Panels classified activity using all available clinical, imaging, endoscopic, histopathological, and biochemical evidence collected within six months of recruitment. We developed and estimated a Bayesian random effects latent class model, combining classifications from seven tests (magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, endoscopy, histopathology, C-reactive protein, faecal calprotectin, and Harvey-Bradshaw index). We evaluated agreement between model and panel classifications of active TICD, explored potential reasons for disagreement, and compared the approximate time and resources required for each reference standard. Positive agreement between model and panel classifications of active TICD was 87% (95% CI: 83, 91), and negative agreement was 70% (95% CI: 65, 75). Disagreement probably arose because the model combined classifications from MRI and ultrasound, weighting them heavily, while panels could not use evidence from these tests. Approximately, latent class analysis required one statistician and 14 working days, whereas panel consensus required the equivalent of one panellist and 25 working days, at a considerably higher cost. Latent class analysis may be an efficient and viable reference standard for active TICD, relative to panel consensus. More comparative evaluations are necessary to encourage wider use.
authors: Tom Parry; Nandini Dendukuri; Steve Halligan; Stuart Andrew Taylor; Susan Mallett

title: Influence of deprivation and rurality on colon capsule endoscopy outcomes: a retrospective analysis of the ScotCap registry
abstract: Objective To evaluate the influence of socioeconomic deprivation and rurality on colon capsule endoscopy (CCE) performance and downstream management in a remote National Health Service (NHS) population.Methods We performed a secondary analysis of 2480 patients undergoing CCE within NHS Highland between 2019 and 2024 using data from the ScotCap registry. Primary outcomes were bowel preparation adequacy and CCE completion. The secondary outcome was follow-up pathway (endoscopic vs non-endoscopic). Predictor variables included age, sex, Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation (SIMD) quintile and Urban–Rural Classification (URC). Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate ORs with 95% CIs.Results The mean age was 59.3 years (SD 12.4) and 1379/2480 (55.6%) patients were female. Adequate bowel preparation was achieved in 1787/2480 (72.1%) patients, CCE was completed in 1669/2480 (67.3%), and endoscopic follow-up occurred in 1421/2480 (57.3%). Neither SIMD nor URC was associated with bowel preparation adequacy, CCE completion or follow-up pathway (all p>0.05). Female sex was independently associated with inadequate bowel preparation (OR 1.70, 95% CI 1.42 to 2.04; p<0.001) and CCE incompletion (OR 1.62, 95% CI 1.36 to 1.93; p<0.001). Increasing age was associated with reduced odds of non-endoscopic follow-up (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.00; p=0.01). Inadequate bowel preparation was strongly associated with subsequent endoscopic investigation (OR 0.18, 95% CI 0.12 to 0.27; p<0.001).Conclusions This is the largest study evaluating socioeconomic deprivation and rurality in CCE. Neither influenced CCE performance or downstream management. Instead, patient factors, including sex, age and bowel preparation quality, were the primary determinants of outcomes. These findings support CCE as an equitable diagnostic modality across diverse populations and support the expansion of community and home-based services.
authors: Alishah Haider; Ruari J Jardine; Jemma Hudson; Angus J. M. Watson

title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System
abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) magnetic tracking offers a promising alternative to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based localization for medical robotic guidance. However, scalar field measurements and field-aligned marker moments constrain position and orientation tracking, requiring careful configuration design. We present a unified information-based framework that uses local covariance analysis to evaluate receiver geometry, marker separation, and external source configuration in on/off-board NMR tracking. Numerical evaluation shows that planar-array precision depends jointly on receiver count and geometry, with triangular lattice arrays achieving the lowest best-case position uncertainty among the evaluated layouts for 9--20 receivers. Two spatially separated, field-aligned markers enable device-axis tracking, with predicted angular uncertainty below $2^\circ$ at the evaluated workspace center for suitable marker separations. We further establish point-dipole source--receiver duality, unifying the analysis of on/off-board NMR tracking. These
authors: Seçkin Eren Yetim; Mehmet Efe Tiryaki

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Perioperative Medicine: Current Advances and Future Directions
abstract: Perioperative medicine is undergoing a fundamental transformation from empiric surgery, which relied heavily on individual clinical experience, to image-based precision surgery and, more recently, to data-driven intelligent surgery. Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the entire perioperative continuum, encompassing the preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative phases, by leveraging multimodal data to overcome the uncertainty and subjectivity of traditional management models. This review systematically summarizes cutting-edge applications of AI in the perioperative setting. Preoperatively, AI enables precise lesion detection, staging, and individualized surgical planning through multimodal data fusion. Intraoperatively, computer vision and augmented reality technologies endow navigation systems with dynamic perceptual guidance. Notably, clinical trials demonstrate that AI-based navigation and robotic platforms can substantially improve patient outcomes, such as significantly reducing positive surgical margin rates, decreasing blood loss, and shortening hospital stays. Furthermore, intelligent closed-loop anesthesia and early-warning systems enhance physiological stability, with evidence showing a reduction in the duration of intraoperative hypotension. Postoperatively, AI-based predictive models facilitate the early warning and targeted intervention of complications. Real-world clinical implementations of these models have successfully reduced overall postoperative composite complication rates and 90-day readmission rates, while also achieving per-patient cost savings. However, the broad clinical translation of AI remains constrained by multiple challenges, including data and algorithmic bias, “black box” decision-making, ethical and regulatory concerns, and difficulties in clinical integration. Finally, this review outlines clear research directions to overcome these obstacles, emphasizing the need for high-quality prospective clinical trials, the development of interpretable models, the establishment of flexible regulatory frameworks, and the exploration of optimal modes of human–AI collaboration, with the ultimate goal of harnessing AI to sustainably reduce perioperative mortality, minimize complication rates, and comprehensively improve the quality of surgical care.
authors: Yue Zhao; Huanzuo Yang; Zhidan Wang; Hancong Li; Gongshuang Zhang; Xinyue Fu; Peiheng Li; Puxing He; Shuang Wu; Xiang Gao; Cheng Lu; Han Luo

title: Integrating Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Robotics for Intelligent Information Management and Decision Support
abstract: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Robotics are revolutionizing the landscape of intelligent information management and decision support, connecting data processing, predictive analysis, and autonomous action. This review discusses the conceptual background, technological architectures, and application areas of integrated intelligent systems. It brings together the latest advances in machine learning, deep learning, robotic perception, autonomous control, reinforcement learning, digital twins, edge AI, federated learning and human-in-the-loop decision support. The review also compares the machine learning, deep learning, robotics, and integrated approaches in terms of accuracy, scalability, adaptability, computational efficiency, explainability, and real-time decision making. These technologies are increasingly becoming relevant in the healthcare sector, in manufacturing, in supply chains, in the finance sector, in cybersecurity, in smart cities, in agriculture, and in environmental monitoring. While significant strides have been made, there are still numerous challenges to address, such as data quality, privacy, security, interoperability, computational complexity, transparency, and trust. Multimodal intelligence, foundation models, Distributed learning, and Self-learning robotics are expected to become increasingly common in future intelligent systems. In summary, learning, reasoning, and robotic execution, when integrated, provide a strong basis for trustworthy, adaptive, explainable and human-centric decision support in real-world complex environments and retain the effectiveness of human involvement in the decision process and the responsibility of system governance.
authors: B. Nagarajan; Vipulkumar Kishorbhai Patel; Gurunadham R; G. Naga Chandrika; Bansari Thakkar; Ei Thandar Soe

title: Inteligência artificial no rastreamento da retinopatia diabética
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy can lead to vision loss even when early retinal changes cause no symptoms. Artificial intelligence has therefore been investigated as a means of expanding retinal image screening. This article reviews eight scientific publications on diagnostic accuracy, implementation in healthcare services, and practical limitations. The findings indicate good performance for certain algorithms and higher screening completion when results are available during the visit. However, performance differs across systems, and detecting abnormalities does not in itself ensure access to specialized care. Artificial intelligence may strengthen screening when image quality is assessed and referral pathways are clearly established.
authors: Maria Eduarda Santana Bruneto; João Victor Santana Bruneto

title: Intelligent System for Celiac Disease Detection Based on Deep Learning
abstract: In this study authors explore the application of deep learning techniques for the early detection of celiac disease through the analysis of medical imaging and clinical data. We used the convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed model exhibits promising accuracy in identifying patterns indicative of celiac disease from diverse images of a big database. The integration of deep learning in celiac disease diagnosis holds the potential for enhancing early intervention and improving patient outcomes, marking a significant advancement in medical diagnostics. The proposed approach elucidates the intricacies of celiac disease and implements a robust Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model for accurate image classification. Achieving an average accuracy of 96%, this method promises enhanced diagnosis and management, paving the way for personalized healthcare interventions with significant improvements in patient outcomes and quality of life.
authors: Souhir Sghaier; Nasser Alsharif

title: Internal Validation of a YOLOv8 Model for Classifying Temporomandibular Joint Disc Displacement With Versus Without Reduction on Open‐Mouth Proton‐Density‐Weighted MRI
abstract: BACKGROUND: The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disc plays an important role in maintaining normal joint function. However, disc displacement is a common condition that can lead to pain, restricted jaw movement and chronic TMJ dysfunction. OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate a deep learning model capable of autonomously localizing the TMJ region from magnetic resonance (MR) images during mouth opening using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) v8 framework, and to discriminate between TMJ disc displacement with reduction (DDwR) and disc displacement without reduction (DDwoR). METHODS: This study included 237 patients (48 males, 189 females; age range, 19-83 [mean, 44.73 ± 18.3] years) who underwent MRI examination at our hospital for suspected TMJ disorders and were diagnosed with disc displacement based on imaging findings. After exclusion, 439 proton density-weighted MR images during mouth opening were preprocessed and divided on a patient basis into training (280 images), validation (71 images) and test (88 images) datasets. The TMJ region was manually annotated using LabelImg, including the condyles, articular disc and articular tubercle. The YOLOv8 deep learning model was trained for 200 epochs to localize the TMJ region and classify DDwR or DDwoR. RESULTS: The YOLOv8 model achieved promising results for the detection and classification of TMJ disc displacements. The performance metrics were a precision, recall and F1 score of 0.983, 0.988 and 0.987, respectively, indicating a high accuracy in detecting and identifying disc displacement patterns. CONCLUSION: The YOLOv8 deep learning model demonstrated promising performance in automatically localizing and classifying TMJ disc displacement from MR images.
authors: Kotaro Ito; Hirotaka Muraoka; Satoshi Tokunaga; Kohei Otsuka; Tomohiro Komatsu; Yuta Kohinata; Shoya Hirohata

title: Interpretable video-derived markers of surgical experience during robotic suturing: a proof-of-concept study in an ex vivo porcine model
abstract: BACKGROUND: We present LUMICS (Multi-Level Understanding of Minimally Invasive Colon Suturing) and examine whether routine surgical video yields interpretable markers of general surgical experience in a standardized ex vivo porcine model. METHODS: This observational proof-of-concept study analysed 15 endoscopic recordings from 14 operators. Predictions were converted into action distribution, step duration, and adapted log dimensionless jerk (ALDLJ). Experience classification used 14 procedures from 13 surgeons in four Random Forest configurations with leave-one-surgeon-out evaluation. Because the workflow extractor was trained on procedures represented in the classifier cohort, AUCs are internal estimates and may be optimistic. RESULTS: Experienced surgeons had higher mean ALDLJ (Cliff's delta 0.67, 95% CI 0.14-1.00) and AUC 0.83 (0.55-1.00). Adding ALDLJ to actions increased grouped AUC from 0.52 to 0.62, reproduced by nested cross-validation (0.48 to 0.64) and procedure-level analysis (0.49 to 0.67). Actions plus duration yielded AUC 0.64 and all features 0.54; duration and ALDLJ were strongly inversely associated (Spearman rho = -0.98). CONCLUSIONS: Routine endoscopic video yielded clinically interpretable, sensor-free markers of efficiency and motion smoothness. ALDLJ showed a consistent experience-related signal beyond action distribution, while its overlap with duration suggests convergent information. These findings support ALDLJ's further development as a formative feedback marker pending external validation.
authors: Andrea Borgno; Matteo Pescio; Pietro Leoncini; Roberto Spagnulo; Giovanni Distefano; Federica Barontini; Federica Corso; Lorenzo Revello; Luigi Muratore; Francesca Paola Maenza; Carlo Alberto Ammirati; Giulio Dagnino; Alberto Arezzo; Francesco Marzola

title: Intestinal Diseases in Men and Women: Etiology, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Approaches
abstract: Background/Objectives: Intestinal diseases constitute a significant global public health issue and encompass a broad spectrum of inflammatory, functional, and infectious disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis) and irritable bowel syndrome. In recent years, increasing attention has been paid to sex-related differences in epidemiology, clinical course, diagnosis, and treatment outcomes. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases to identify publications addressing sex-related differences in the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. The aim of the study was to examine sex-based differences in the etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of intestinal diseases. Results: The development of intestinal diseases is determined by the interaction of genetic, immunological, hormonal, microbial, and environmental factors. Sex-related differences were identified in disease prevalence, clinical course, and progression and are associated with hormonal regulation, immune response characteristics, and gut microbiota composition. Diagnosis of intestinal diseases is based on a combination of laboratory biomarkers, endoscopic, and imaging techniques, and diagnostic accuracy may vary according to biological sex. Video capsule endoscopy, balloon-assisted enteroscopy, and advanced imaging methods, including computed tomography colonography, improve the evaluation of small bowel diseases, whereas chromoendoscopy, colonoscopy, and cross-sectional imaging play important roles in the assessment of colonic disorders. Treatment includes pharmacological, dietary, microbiota-based, endoscopic, and surgical approaches. Current evidence suggests that biological sex may influence treatment response, adverse event profiles, and clinical outcomes; however, the available evidence remains limited or inconsistent for several therapeutic strategies, highlighting the need for further sex-specific clinical research. Conclusions: Sex-related differences should be considered to improve diagnostic accuracy, optimize treatment strategies, and support individualized clinical management. Although evidence remains limited in several areas, current findings support the integration of biological sex into clinical decision-making. Further research is needed to establish sex-specific diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
authors: Erik Shorabaev; Amankeldi K. Sadanov; Saltanat Orazymbet; И.А. Ратникова; Baiken B. Baimakhanova; Алтынай Мамбаева; Mira Azhakhmetova; Yelena Shorina; Gulzakira Xetayeva; Maimakova Akmaral; Aziza Assylbekkyzy Kudaibergen; Aknur Turgumbayeva

title: Intestinal ultrasound in the UK: current challenges and future perspectives
abstract: Optimal inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) management increasingly relies on treat-to-target strategies incorporating assessment of transmural inflammation. Intestinal ultrasound (IUS) is an accurate, non-invasive, repeatable and patient-centred imaging modality that enables real-time assessment of disease activity and timely therapeutic decision-making. Supported by a robust evidence base and international guideline endorsement, IUS demonstrates diagnostic performance comparable to magnetic resonance enterography (MRE) while offering advantages including rapid access, excellent patient acceptability, lower cost and integration into routine clinical encounters. Despite the UK’s early contribution to IUS development and a growing evidence base, adoption remains limited and concentrated within a small number of specialist centres. This review examines the current status of IUS in the UK, including the evidence base, patient experience, service delivery models, training, governance and practical considerations for implementation. Successful integration requires multidisciplinary collaboration between radiologists, gastroenterologists, IBD nurses and sonographers, supported by defined clinical indications, standardised scanning and reporting, competency-based training, supervised case acquisition, quality assurance and regular audit. Hybrid models combining point-of-care assessment within gastroenterology clinics with dedicated radiology-led or sonographer-led pathways may optimise capacity and clinical efficiency. Implementation requires investment in equipment, digital infrastructure and workforce development, supported by robust business cases recognising the potential for reduced reliance on MRE and endoscopy. With coordinated national efforts and multidisciplinary engagement, IUS has the potential to become an integral part of IBD care across the NHS.
authors: Khalil ElGendy; William Blad; Gregory Sebepos‐Rogers; Susanna Meade; Polychronis Pavlidis; Natasha Stock; Gauraang Bhatnagar; N.D. Grunshaw

title: Intracellular accumulation of AAV6 genomes governs microglia reactivity and the inflammatory response in retinal gene therapy
abstract: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors possess immense potential for gene therapy applications. However, microglia can mount an immune response against AAV vectors. Yet, microglia are therapeutic targets since they play a driving role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, it is critical to understand the cellular processes driving the microglia-mediated immune response against AAV vectors. To this end, we modelled AAV6 induced inflammation upon retinal gene therapy in minipigs. Upon AAV6 administration, the IBA1+ cells demonstrated a morphological transition to the amoeboid form, indicating microglial reactivity. We also observed the invasion of peripheral immune cells in the retina. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, we transduced human iPSC derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) in vitro with AAV6 and AAV8 respectively. Only AAV6 transduced iMGLs exhibited morphological features and a transcriptomic signature of microglial reactivity. The magnitude of intracellular AAV6 viral genomes was significantly higher as compared to the AAV8 condition. The elevated levels of intracellular AAV6 genomes induced a DNA damage response in AAV6-transduced iMGLs, which is a key feature of neuroinflammation-linked microglial reactivity. Thus, our work highlights the impact of intracellular viral genome accumulation on microglial reactivity and its implications for retinal gene therapy associated inflammation.

title: Intraoperative navigation in robot-assisted kidney surgery: Literature review
abstract: Background. Partial nephrectomy is the treatment of choice for localized renal cell carcinoma, and robot-assisted approach makes it feasible for tumors of high anatomical complexity. While robotic platform deprives a surgeon of tactile feedback, this flaw is compensated through integration of data from an ultrasound probe and fluorescent camera allowing 3D models to be displayed directly on the surgeon console. Aim. To summarize literature data on intraoperative navigation techniques in robot-assisted kidney surgery and to assess their capabilities and limitations, as well as level of evidence. Source search methodology. Literature search was performed in the PubMed, eLIBRARY.ru and Google Scholar databases. The review included studies in which all interventions or one of them was performed using robot-assisted approach. Controlled trials, systematic reviews and comparative studies were prioritized. Results. Studies of navigation in robot-assisted partial nephrectomy, radical nephrectomy and pyeloplasty were analyzed. Intraoperative ultrasound with a robotic drop-in probe remains the basic technique: it defines the margins of endophytic tumors, the extent of tumor venous thrombus and, with contrast enhancement, the ischemic zone. Integrated near-infrared fluorescence with indocyanine green is used to visualize vessels, confirm selective clamping, mark the tumor, and assess ureteral perfusion. Meta-analyses show that use of a fluorescent camera provides modest reduction in warm ischemia time whereas the randomized EMERALD trial found no long-term renal function benefit of superselective clamping. Threedimensional models increase the rates of selective ischemia and enucleation; in a randomized trial, 3D planning reduced operative time, blood loss and clamp time, and a meta-analysis showed that 3D visualization is associated with fewer collecting system dissections and conversions to radical nephrectomy. Use of augmented reality is limited by possibility of organ deformation and the need for manual registration; computer vision methods for automatic registration are being developed. Promising directions include targeted fluorescence, force feedback in new-generation robotic systems and artificial intelligence. Conclusion. Instrumental navigation widens capabilities of robot-assisted kidney surgery, especially in organ-saving surgeries for highly anatomically complex tumors. Intraoperative ultrasound remains the main technique, fluorescent navigation is the most accessible addition, while 3D modeling and augmented reality are being actively developed. Navigation improves surrogate outcomes, but its effect on long-term renal function and oncological results has not been proven. Therefore, randomized trials with clinically meaningful endpoints are needed.
authors: M.B. Zingerenko; A.G. Ivanov; I. O. Avanesyan

title: Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells: Context-Dependent resilience and vulnerability
abstract: Retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) exhibit marked heterogeneity in their susceptibility to injury and disease. Intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs), a small subset of melanopsin-expressing RGCs involved in non-image-forming visual functions, have emerged as a particularly informative example. In multiple experimental models, ipRGCs show relative resistance to acute insults such as optic nerve injury, excitotoxicity, and mitochondrial dysfuinction. In contrast, functional alterations and degeneration have been reported in aging and in neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease. This apparent discrepancy suggests that ipRGC survival may depend on the nature and duration of the underlying stress. In this review, we summarize current evidence on ipRGC resilience and vulnerability across a range of experimental and pathological contexts. We discuss candidate mechanisms that may contribute to these responses, including sustained activity, calcium handling, metabolic specialization, neurochemical interactions, and gene expression programs. We also consider the role of subtype-specific diversity within the ipRGC population in shaping these outcomes. Finally, we examine the potential of ipRGCs as biomarkers of disease and as a source of insight for neuroprotective strategies. Together, these observations support the view that ipRGC behaviour reflects an interaction between intrinsic cellular properties and the context in which they are engaged.
authors: Arianna Cella; Ludovic S. Mure
venue: Neurobiology of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms

title: Investigation of gear design parameters for soft-gear-driven self-propelled colonoscopy robot.
abstract:
Purpose

Colonoscopy is the most effective method for colorectal cancer screening; however, successful insertion requires a high level of operator skill and may cause patient discomfort or injury. To address these challenges, self-propelled colonoscopy robots that generate propulsion at the distal tip have been actively investigated. In our previous work, we developed a self-propelled colonoscopy robot using a worm-gear mechanism; however, the use of rigid gears posed a potential risk of excessive contact force on the colonic wall.

Methods

In this study, we propose a self-propelled colonoscopy robot enabled by soft gears that combine compliant contact with gear-based power transmission. By reinterpreting the crawler-based propulsion concept as a soft spur gear driven by a worm-gear mechanism, the proposed design allows elastic deformation of the gear teeth under load, providing adaptive traction through compliant deformation of the gear teeth. Gear parameters were optimized using gear-design software, and four soft-gear configurations were fabricated to investigate their propulsion characteristics.

Results

The prototypes were fabricated using stereolithography 3D printing and evaluated using a colonoscopy training model. The robot achieved a maximum propulsive speed of 9.6 mm/s and a propulsive force of 1.5 N in straight sections. Gears with larger modules produced higher propulsion performance. In addition, the proposed coaxial double-worm-gear architecture enabled traversal of curved sections of the colon model under manual steering.

Conclusion

These results demonstrate the mechanical feasibility of using soft gears as a propulsion mechanism for self-propelled colonoscopy robots. Although the evaluation was limited to a colonoscopy training model, the proposed design demonstrated stable propulsion in a colonoscopy training model while maintaining compliant contact with the intestinal wall. The simple and compact mechanical structure provides a promising proof of concept for future minimally invasive robotic endoscopy, although further ex vivo and in vivo validation will be required.
authors: Osawa K, Duan K, Ueda A, Nakadate R, Arata J, Nagao Y, Akahoshi T, Eto M, Tanaka E.

title: Just‐In‐Time Modelling of Real‐Time Tissue Deformation in Ultrasound‐Guided Percutaneous Surgery
abstract: Simulators for training ultrasound-guided percutaneous surgery (usPS) demand rapid updates of tissue and image deformation, yet high-fidelity physics models exceed real-time budgets on standard hardware. This paper presents a Just-in-Time (JIT) modelling framework that predicts ultrasound image deformation from needle insertions in real-time. First, an offline historical database of needle locations and resulting image deformations is created using a simulation engine. For each new query, the model selects a local neighbourhood and computes weights that minimize a mean-square error. The resulting weighted prediction of the full nodal deformation is reshaped for direct simulation or visualization. The framework is evaluated against mesh deformations calculated using thin plate spline (TPS), five mesh resolutions and multiple database sizes. On the finest mesh, the mean relative error is 0.2% while the median per-query runtime is 1.1 ms, providing a speedup of 31,900 times over the simulation engine used to generate the offline database. These results indicate that JIT closely reproduces the TPS reference deformation while satisfying stringent real-time requirements. The proposed framework is suitable for real-time, embedded and portable usPS training simulators.
authors: Kian Zalzalah; Carlos Rossa

title: KASID Guidelines for Diagnosis and Monitoring of Inflammatory Bowel Disease: 2026
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by heterogeneous disease presentations and clinical courses. Accurate diagnosis and appropriate disease monitoring play an important role in improving long-term outcomes by preventing misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment; enabling early detection of disease progression, treatment failure, and disease-related complications; and facilitating timely adjustment of treatment strategies. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) developed guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD in adults, reflecting the Korean clinical setting, to support clinical decision-making and improve the quality of patient care. To develop these guidelines, existing international clinical practice guidelines and expert consensus statements were comprehensively reviewed, along with updated evidence relevant to each clinical topic. Final recommendations were established through expert consensus using a modified Delphi process. These guidelines address major clinical areas in the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD, including initial diagnosis and baseline assessment, assessment of disease extent and activity, disease monitoring in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, nutritional assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. These guidelines are intended to support individualized clinical judgment and should be applied flexibly, taking into account not only individual patient characteristics and clinical circumstances but also available resources, access to diagnostic and monitoring modalities, regulatory requirements, and reimbursement policies.

title: KFS$^4$LAM: Adaptive KeyFrame Selection with Structure-Aware Mapping for Endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM
abstract: Gaussian-splatting Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) augments conventional SLAM with a dense, renderable 3D scene representation, enabling high-quality reconstruction and novel-view synthesis. However, its localization, reconstruction, and rendering performance depends strongly on which observations are retained for mapping. Existing systems commonly rely on fixed temporal intervals or simple pose- and overlap-based criteria for keyframe selection. In colonoscopy, non-uniform camera motion, repetitive anatomy, specularities, and visual artifacts can make these criteria unreliable, leading to either redundant keyframes or missed informative viewpoints. We present KFS$^4$LAM (KeyFrame Selection with Structure-aware mapping for endoscopic Gaussian Splatting SLAM), which couples motion-guided adaptive keyframe selection with structurally supervised mapping and restricted temporal deformation. Accumulated motion guides adaptive keyframe selection, with complementary cues suppressing redundant or unreliable candidates. Density-aware mapping with anatomical contour supervision (colon folds) emphasizes structurally informative regions, while restricted temporal deformation accommodates local tissue dynamics without unconstrained geometric drift. We evaluate KFS$^4$LAM against Gaussian-SLAM baselines on C3VD and C3VD-v2, together with cross-backbone and component ablations. KFS$^4$LAM achieves strong overall performance across trajectory, rendering, and depth metrics, with pronounced gains on more challenging C3VD-v2 dataset. In the matched comparison with SplaTAM on C3VD-v2, it reduces rotational relative pose error by 20.3% and depth RMSE by 38.4%, while improving PSNR by 0.78 dB. Cross-backbone experiments further show that the framework is not tied to a single underlying SLAM architecture. Code and visualization results are available at https://xinweiju.github.io/KFSLAM/.
authors: Xinwei Ju; Zhehua Mao; Tianyi Song; Danail V. Stoyanov; Sophia Bano; Francisco Vasconcelos

title: LAVIA-MXID: A New Annotated X-Ray Medical Image Dataset
abstract: X-ray medical imaging datasets are crucial for accurate diagnosis and driving innovation in medical imaging technologies. The LAVIA-MXID extended dataset, curated by the Laboratory of Vision and Artificial Intelligence (LAVIA), addresses limitations of its predecessor, the MXID dataset. It offers increased diversity, nearly 10,000 annotated images, and features tailored for advanced medical imaging applications. This study presents a handcrafted machine learning and deep learning approach for medical image compression, focusing on recognizing peculiarities and problems in medical imaging pattern recognition, such as data set quality, labeling errors, and data imbalance. The LAVIA-MXID dataset, an enhanced version of the MXID dataset, features 9989 images managed by radiologists and medical experts. It is meticulously labeled, categorized into training, validation, and test subsets, and isolated and eliminated for high-quality annotation standards. It supports various image analysis tasks but does not include annotations for specific pathological conditions. The study analyzed 9,989 medical images from the LAVIA-MXID dataset using machine learning and deep learning methods. The results showed marginal improvements in the extended dataset (version 2), but enhanced image quality with reduced reconstruction artifacts. The four models - Autoencoder (AE), Deep Convolutional Autoencoder (DCAE), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Variational Autoencoder (VAE), showed improvement in performance metrics like MSE, PSNR, and MS-SSIM. The proposed dataset and methods improve X-ray medical imaging diagnostic accuracy by training machine learning algorithms, addressing issues like dataset size, quality, labeling errors, and data imbalance. The LAVIA-MXID dataset, developed by LAVIA, offers advanced medical image analysis using machine learning and deep learning paradigms, enhancing compression quality.

title: Laparoscopy in Paediatric Obscure Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Case of Meckel’s Diverticulum and Literature Review
abstract: Obscure gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB) in children presents a diagnostic challenge, often requiring a multimodal approach when standard imaging fails. We report the case of a 13-year-old boy with severe anaemia and recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding, in whom repeated endoscopic and scintigraphic investigations were inconclusive. Abdominal ultrasound suggested a mass in the right lower quadrant, raising suspicion of Meckel’s diverticulum. Diagnostic laparoscopy confirmed the presence of a Meckel’s diverticulum, which was successfully resected extracorporeally. Histopathology revealed ectopic gastric mucosa. A literature review highlights the diagnostic limitations of technetium-99m scans and underscores the increasing role of laparoscopy in both diagnosis and treatment. Emerging techniques, such as capsule endoscopy and the evaluation of the predictive value of haemoglobin levels may support early surgical referral. Laparoscopy offers a safe, minimally invasive, and definitive solution, particularly when imaging is inconclusive. Keywords: Intestinal bleeding, Meckel’s diverticulum, Laparoscopy, Childhood

title: Large-area reflection suppression for structured-light three-dimensional reconstruction of specular surfaces
abstract: The inherent physical constraints of polishing tools lead to positioning and repeatability errors in industrial robots, which compromise polishing accuracy by deviating the actual dwell time from its theoretical value. A structured light detection technology, as a high-precision non-contact measurement technology, provides a promising solution for the on-machine positioning of polished workpieces. Nevertheless, the strong specular reflection of metal workpieces tends to cause large area overexposure in the captured fringe images, thereby inducing the loss of three-dimensional point cloud data. An algorithm combining the improved Retinal-cortex theory (Retinex) and mask-aware transformer (MAT) deep learning is proposed to suppress the influence of large area surface reflection on measurement to address this issue in this study. The process involves adaptive aperture adjustment to obtain images within an optimal grayscale range, followed by Retinex-based strong-light suppression and MAT-based inpainting to recover missing fringe information in overexposed areas. Validation experiments are conducted on high-reflective aluminum alloy plates based on a structured light measurement system calibrated with an accuracy of 0.01 mm. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can effectively recover missing surface-data holes in the point cloud with an average growth rate of 3.92%, eliminate overexposed regions and compensate for underexposed areas, providing a novel solution for the on-machine inspection and localization of polished workpieces. It is of great significance for improving the deterministic polishing accuracy of robots.
authors: Shaojie Zheng; Ying Liu; Ziqi Han; Haihong Ai; Kun Wang; Zhanshan Wang

title: Laser‐Assisted Transoral Robotic Supraglottic Laryngectomy
abstract: Objective To describe the operative setup, safety principles, and stepwise technique for laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy using a flexible CO 2 laser system. Methods This operative video demonstrates laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy performed with the da Vinci SP platform. Key technical steps include laser‐safe airway management, transoral exposure with a Feyh–Kastenbauer retractor, robotic docking, flexible CO 2 laser fiber placement through a distal drop‐in guide, aiming‐beam confirmation, noncontact laser dissection, coordinated bedside suction and bipolar hemostasis, and en bloc specimen delivery. Results The technique allows controlled transoral access to the supraglottic larynx with three‐dimensional visualization, precise noncontact laser incision, and preservation of uninvolved glottic and subglottic structures. A deliberate sequence of inferior, lateral, and superior release facilitates exposure of the pre‐epiglottic space, specimen mobilization, and margin‐oriented en bloc resection. Conclusion Laser‐assisted transoral robotic supraglottic laryngectomy combines the precision of CO 2 laser surgery with the visualization and dexterity of single‐port robotic surgery. With appropriate patient selection, strict laser safety, and a standardized team‐based workflow, this technique can support precise en bloc resection, reliable margin assessment, and preservation of uninvolved laryngeal structures.
authors: Nir Tsur; Andrea Costantino; Jeffery Scott Magnuson

title: Learning-Enhanced Observer for Sensorless Task-Null-Space Compliant Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). In pHRI tasks, robots are expected to perform task-space motions robustly while remaining compliance with human disturbance, which proposes distinct control objectives. Most existing approaches focus mainly on either robustness or compliance and rely on force sensors for real-time tracking. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. Firstly, a neural network (NN) is trained to improve the observer performance by compensating for system friction and unmodeled dynamics. Secondly, a task-null-space decomposition is applied to separate the joint velocity and reduce the effect of the human disturbance on the observer. Finally, a hybrid pose and force controller is introduced to achieve the end-effector pose and force tracking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides robust and accurate wrench estimation while maintaining reliable pose and force tracking performance. The proposed approach offers an effective solution and framework for pHRI without the need of force/torque sensor measurements which can be applied to many robotic manipulator platforms which do not have force/torque sensors.

title: LogicEye: Agent Driven Multimodal Dataset for Interpretable Ophthalmic Diagnosis
abstract: Clinical adoption of ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence remains limited by low interpretability and a lack of finely annotated multimodal data. Most existing datasets provide only coarse disease labels without the granular pathological findings required for differential diagnosis. We present LogicEye$^{Agent}$, a dual-pool inference and verification agent that emulates clinical reasoning by jointly verifying positive inclusion signs and negative exclusion criteria. Using LogicEye$^{Agent}$, we curate LogicEye$^{Data}$, a large-scale multimodal dataset of 804,461 fundus and OCT images paired with structured pathological reports spanning 38 diseases and 29 subtypes, with quality assured through joint verification by multimodal large language models and clinical experts. Building on this dataset, we further develop LogicEye$^{Bench}$, which incorporates a category-constrained loss for hierarchical disease recognition and report generation. Grounding coarse labels into verified visual findings effectively curtails diagnostic hallucinations and establishes a solid foundation for interpretable vision-language modeling in ophthalmology. The code is available at:https://github.com/Eden35/LogicEye-Agent-Driven-Multimodal-Dataset-for-Interpretable-Ophthalmic-Diagnosis.
