title: Recent Advances in Gallium‐Based Nanorobotic‐Nanosystems for Molecular Imaging and Targeted Cancer Therapy
abstract: Gallium (Ga)‐based nanorobotics and nanosystems (NR‐NS) have shown preclinical potential for precision oncology, offering strategies to address the limitations of conventional cancer therapies. Ga exhibits biologically relevant physicochemical and anticancer properties, including disruption of iron metabolism, inhibition of DNA synthesis, and induction of cell‐death pathways. However, the safety and therapeutic efficacy of Ga‐containing nanoplatforms depend on their chemical form, dose, formulation, biodistribution, and duration of exposure. Recent studies have investigated tumour targeting using functionalised nanosystems, externally controlled propulsion, and stimulus‐responsive drug‐release strategies, while artificial intelligence (AI)‐assisted navigation remains an emerging concept. Ga‐based platforms may also integrate therapeutic and diagnostic functions, supporting the development of theranostic applications and tumour monitoring. This review critically examines recent developments in Ga‐based nanorobotic and nanoscale systems for cancer therapy, molecular imaging, targeted drug delivery, and theranostics, with particular emphasis on studies published from 2021 onwards. Key mechanistic insights, nanofabrication strategies, targeting approaches, and emerging biomedical applications are discussed. Current challenges, including biocompatibility, immune interactions, manufacturing scalability, and clinical translation, are also highlighted. Overall, Ga‐based NR‐NS may offer promising opportunities for precision oncology, although their clinical applicability, therapeutic benefits, and long‐term safety require further investigation.
authors: Sourajyoti Goswami; Sanjeev Kumar Patel; Shouvik Kumar Nandy; Akhilesh Kumar Tiwari

title: Recent Advances in Modeling, Control and Motion Planning for AI-Driven Soft Robotic Systems
abstract: Due to their high compliance, environmental adaptability, and inherent safety in human-robot interaction, soft robots have demonstrated considerable potential, including medical rehabilitation, compliant grasping, and operations in complex environments. Unlike conventional robots relying on rigid structures and discrete joint motions, soft robots use flexible materials such as elastomers and hydrogels to achieve motion and functionality through continuous deformation. Despite providing excellent adaptability, these compliant materials also introduce complex behaviors, including continuous morphological changes, material nonlinearities, time-varying properties, and environmental coupling, posing substantial challenges to modeling, control, and motion planning. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI), through nonlinear representation, data-driven learning, adaptive optimization, and autonomous decision-making, has provided new technical pathways for addressing these challenges. Unlike previous reviews organized primarily by AI algorithm type, this work narratively reviews 39 studies and organizes AI-driven approaches according to the soft robotic system implementation process, encompassing modeling, control, and motion planning. Specifically, in modeling, neural networks, Koopman representations, and physics-data fusion methods have enhanced the representation of complex dynamical relationships. In control, learning-augmented control and reinforcement learning have reduced reliance on accurate system models and improved adaptability under uncertainty. In motion planning, learning from demonstration, reinforcement learning, and intelligent optimization methods have strengthened the capability for autonomous motion generation under complex constraints. Finally, this paper summarizes the current state of the field and discusses future trends in AI-driven soft robotics, emphasizing stronger coordination across functional modules. Closed-loop integration of prediction, decision-making, control, and feedback updates may further advance soft robots from stage-specific intelligence toward system-level autonomy.
authors: Lingli Tang; Wenguang Yang; Wenyuan Chen; Jie Yang

title: Recent Advances in Prosthodontics: Integrating Digital Dentistry, Artificial Intelligence, Advanced Biomaterials, and Personalized Rehabilitation
abstract: Background: Prosthodontics is undergoing a substantial transformation through the convergence of digital dentistry, computeraided design and computer-aided manufacturing (CAD/CAM), additive manufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI), advanced restorative materials, implant dentistry, and patient-specific computational modeling. These developments are changing diagnostic procedures, treatment planning, prosthesis fabrication, clinical communication, and long-term maintenance.Objective: This narrative review critically examines recent advances in prosthodontics, evaluates their clinical relevance and limitations, and identifies research priorities for translating emerging technologies into predictable, evidence-based patient care.Methods: A focused narrative literature search was undertaken using PubMed/MEDLINE-indexed literature and supplementary bibliographic searches, prioritizing systematic reviews, meta-analyses, clinical investigations, and relevant foundational studies published between 2015 and October 2026. Literature concerning intraoral scanning, CAD/CAM, virtual patients, digital smile design, AI, additive manufacturing, removable and fixed prosthodontics, implant-supported rehabilitation, biomaterials, robotics, and sustainability was considered. Evidence was synthesized thematically, with emphasis on clinical applicability, technical performance, patient-reported outcomes, and methodological limitations. This review was not designed as a systematic review, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment or quantitative meta-analysis was performed.Discussion: Major advances include increasingly integrated digital workflows, improved intraoral scanning, virtual articulation, facially driven treatment planning, AI-assisted diagnosis and prosthetic design, digitally manufactured complete dentures, and expanded applications of additive manufacturing. Digital implant workflows have improved data exchange and prosthetically driven planning, although full-arch implant accuracy remains technique dependent. Contemporary zirconia, lithium disilicate, high-performance polymers, and CAD/CAM resin-based materials have expanded restorative options. AI offers promising capabilities in image interpretation, segmentation, prosthesis design, and predictive modeling, but much of the evidence remains derived from retrospective datasets, laboratory experiments, and controlled testing. Emerging concepts such as digital twins, sensor-enabled prostheses, robotic assistance, and generative design may further personalize treatment, although their routine clinical value requires validation.Conclusion: Contemporary prosthodontics is progressing toward integrated, patient-specific, and data-driven rehabilitation. Digital technologies can improve efficiency, visualization, reproducibility, and communication, but their clinical value depends on appropriate case selection, material selection, biological understanding, operator competence, and long-term outcome assessment. The most defensible future model is an evidence-based hybrid approach that combines conventional clinical expertise with validated digital technologies.

title: Recent advances in dentistry
abstract: Dentistry has entered a transformative era, driven by rapid technological innovation, interdisciplinary research, and a growing emphasis on patient-centered care. The past decade has witnessed remarkable progress across diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive domains, reshaping both clinical practice and academic inquiry. This book, Recent Advances in Dentistry, seeks to capture these developments in a structured and comprehensive manner, offering readers a panoramic view of the evolving landscape of dental science. The chapters assembled herein highlight the convergence of digital technologies, biomaterials, nanoscience, and regenerative medicine with traditional dental practice. From the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into diagnostic workflows, to the revolution brought by CAD/CAM systems and 3D printing, dentistry is increasingly defined by precision, personalization, and efficiency. Advances in smart biomaterials and nanotechnology promise enhanced durability and biocompatibility, while innovations in orthodontics, pediatric dentistry, and caries management continue to refine patient outcomes across age groups. Equally compelling are the strides made in endodontics and periodontology, where regenerative approaches and novel instrumentation are expanding therapeutic possibilities. The domain of implantology and esthetic dentistry has been reshaped by digital planning, guided surgery, and minimally invasive techniques, ensuring both functional and aesthetic excellence. Emerging modalities such as laser therapy, photobiomodulation, robotics, and augmented reality further underscore the dynamic future of dental practice.
authors: Kumar Tathagat Singh; Ahemer Arif Shaikh; Sumit Bhatt; Venkatesh Kulkarni; Vivek Chaudhary

title: Recurrent Bleeding Due to Ileal Angiodysplasia: Clinical Case
abstract: Small bowel bleeding is a rare clinical condition that remains difficult to diagnose and manage. Due to its recurrent nature and limited accessibility, identifying the bleeding source may require complementary diagnostic investigations [1,2]. This study aimed to present a challenging case of recurrent small bowel bleeding and highlight the role of repeated multimodal diagnostic evaluation. A literature review using the PubMed database and analysis of a clinical case were performed. We included English-language articles published in the last decade. A 72-year-old woman with recurrent severe anaemia and suspected gastrointestinal bleeding underwent repeated endoscopic, radiological, and surgical investigations. Capsule endoscopy and SPECT/CT indicated a possible bleeding site in the ileum, however, angiography and diagnostic laparotomy failed to identify the source. A loop ileostomy was created to facilitate further localization and endoscopic access in case of recurrent bleeding. When bleeding recurred, enteroscopy via the ileostomy identified a bleeding ileal angiodysplasia, and successful endoscopic haemostasis was achieved with clips. In conclusion, recurrent small bowel bleeding may remain undetected despite repeated diagnostic investigations. When clinical suspicion persists or bleeding recurs, repeated and multimodal evaluation is necessary [3,4]. In this case, enteroscopy through the ileostomy enabled identification and treatment of the previously unconfirmed bleeding source.

title: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Shaving With a Blade During Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy
abstract: This video demonstrates blade-based recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) shaving during transoral robotic thyroidectomy in four patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma and tumor adherence to a functioning RLN. Controlled sharp dissection along the tumor-nerve interface enabled anatomical nerve preservation in all four cases, with normal vocal fold mobility at 3 months.

title: Registration accuracy, time, and outcomes across four strategies for task-autonomous robotic maxillofacial osteotomy.
abstract:
Objectives

To compare four registration strategies for task-autonomous robotic maxillofacial osteotomy.

Methods

A maxillofacial model was constructed from imaging data. The maxilla and mandible were registered separately using splint-based landmark registration (SL), dental-landmark registration (DL), dental-surface registration (DS), and bone-surface registration (BS). The target-registration error (TRE) was measured in three osteotomy regions, and registration time was recorded. Osteotomies were then performed using a task-autonomous robotic system. The actual and planned osteotomy surfaces were compared using the root mean square (RMS) deviation, mean signed deviation, and angular deviation.

Results

All four strategies achieved mean TREs of <0.8 mm. In the Le Fort I region, TRE was lower for BS than for SL (0.398 ± 0.126 vs. 0.580 ± 0.098 mm; P = 0.0045). Mandibular TREs showed a significant strategy-by-region interaction (P = 0.0031); in the genioplasty region, DS and BS yielded lower TREs than SL and DL. In the mandibular angle region, DS yielded lower TREs than SL and DL, and BS yielded lower TREs than DL. SL had the shortest registration time for both jaws. In the genioplasty region, DL resulted in greater RMS and angular deviations than the other strategies, whereas in the mandibular angle region, DS resulted in lower angular deviation than SL and DL.

Conclusions

Registration strategy significantly influenced TRE, registration time, and mandibular osteotomy accuracy outcomes. All four strategies achieved submillimetric TREs. Overall, surface-based registration (BS and DS) yielded TREs that were lower than or comparable to those of landmark-based registration (SL and DL) and showed favorable performance for selected mandibular osteotomy accuracy outcomes. However, no consistent difference in accuracy was identified between DS and BS.

Clinical significance

Surface-based registration may support accurate robot-assisted osteotomy when adequate dentition or bony surfaces are accessible.
authors: Song S, Liu H, Liu C, Yan X, Liu Y, Shi Y, Bai S, Zhao Y.

title: Reinforcement learning enables autonomous microrobot navigation and intervention in simulated blood capillaries
abstract: Autonomous microrobots navigating biological vasculature could enable targeted drug delivery and thrombolysis, yet training control policies for physiologically complex environments remains an open challenge. Prior reinforcement learning (RL) studies of microrobotic navigation have largely used idealized geometries lacking realistic flow in confined branching, and dense cellular obstacles. Here, we develop a physically grounded, deliberately idealized two-dimensional capillary simulation, with resolved flow fields, explicit red blood cell dynamics, and schematic-derived branching geometry, training RL agents via an advection-dominated concentration field driven by physiological flow speeds. Mapping success across robot size and swimming speed, we show via zero-shot transfer that most training failures reflect optimization limits, not physical ones. A policy transferred from a more demanding condition succeeds far beyond where per-combination training converges. Its eventual collapse offers a tentative lower bound on what is physically achievable. Successful agents converge on Run-and-Rotate strategies. The transferred policy, a variant of this family, shows a distinctive profile, that we believe is responsible for its exceptional transfer success. Without retraining, these agents perform targeted blocking and unblocking of individual vessel branches, restoring red blood cell passage toward baseline levels and suggesting RL as a viable framework for microrobotic intervention in biological networks.
authors: Jannik Drotleff; Paul Hohenberger; Samuel Tovey; Christoph Lohrmann; Julian Hoßbach; Konstantin Nikolaou; Christian Holm

title: Reliability of AI-Based Occlusal Adjustment Recommendations in Full Mouth Rehabilitation Cases
abstract: Full mouth rehabilitation (FMR) is a complex prosthodontic procedure that aims to restore oral function, occlusal stability, aesthetics, and biological health in patients presenting with extensive tooth wear, multiple missing teeth, altered occlusal relationships, and compromised dentition. Occlusal adjustment is an important component of FMR because premature contacts, occlusal interferences, discrepancies in centric relation and maximum intercuspation, and inappropriate distribution of occlusal forces may compromise the longevity and function of definitive restorations. Conventional occlusal adjustment is largely dependent on clinical examination, articulating paper, shimstock, mounted diagnostic casts, intraoral evaluation, and the experience of the treating clinician. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into digital dentistry has introduced new possibilities for automated occlusal analysis and treatment planning. AI-based systems can process intraoral scans, digital articulations, occlusal contact maps, three-dimensional dental models, jaw-tracking information, and other digital records to identify potentially abnormal contacts and generate recommendations for occlusal adjustment. Recent evidence indicates that AI and digital occlusal technologies may improve efficiency and reproducibility; however, their reliability varies according to the data source, scanner, software, clinical situation, and complexity of the occlusal problem. This article discusses the principles of occlusion in full mouth rehabilitation, conventional methods of occlusal adjustment, digital occlusal analysis, applications of AI in occlusal assessment, AI-based occlusal adjustment recommendations, parameters used to assess reliability, clinician–AI agreement, advantages and limitations, and future perspectives. Particular emphasis is placed on the distinction between contact detection and clinical occlusal diagnosis, as these should not be considered equivalent. Current evidence suggests that AI-based recommendations may serve as a useful decision-support tool, but final occlusal adjustment should remain under clinician supervision.
authors: Manjinder Singh; Amanat Kaur Randhawa; Vritti Aggarwal; Alok Suman; Milind Rajan; Y. SHAH

title: Remote Monitoring or Autonomous Triage: Can Artificial Intelligence Safely Decide When Orthodontic Patients Need In-Person Care?
abstract: Aim and objectives: To examine the diagnostic scope, accuracy and limitations of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based remote orthodontic monitoring for automated triage and to assess whether such systems can safely decide when orthodontic patients need in-person care. Methods: Narrative review of PubMed literature on AI-driven remote monitoring and tele-orthodontics, focusing on diagnostic performance, triage applications and the limitations relevant to distinguishing routine virtual review from urgent in-person care. Results: AI reliably detects visually obvious conditions with high specificity, but sensitivity is variable and often low for periodontal changes and precise tooth-level tracking. GO/NO-GO outputs can be inconsistent, radiographic complications such as root resorption cannot be assessed from photographs and single-center models lose accuracy when applied elsewhere. Early triage trials show faster screening yet still require clinician review for borderline cases. Conclusion: Current evidence indicates that AI is not yet safely autonomous for orthodontic triage. Clinician oversight, standardized triage thresholds, external validation and clear medico-legal frameworks remain essential.

title: ResNet-GA: genetic algorithm-driven optimization of ResNet for automated dental caries detection in medical imaging
abstract: Dental caries is one of the most prevalent oral diseases worldwide and remains a major public health concern because delayed or inaccurate diagnosis can lead to irreversible tooth destruction, pain, infection, and more invasive treatment. Early and reliable detection from dental images is therefore essential for improving preventive care and supporting clinical decision-making. However, manual interpretation of dental radiographs is time-consuming, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Although deep learning has shown strong potential for automated caries detection, its performance often depends on manually selected hyperparameters and may be affected by image variability, low contrast, artifacts, and class imbalance. To address these limitations, we propose ResNet-GA, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines deep convolutional feature learning with a genetic algorithm to automatically optimize selected convolutional configurations, particularly the number of filters and kernel sizes in three convolutional blocks. The proposed framework was evaluated on a publicly available dental caries dataset obtained from Kaggle, comprising caries and non-caries images. Images were resized, normalized, and divided into training and validation subsets, with class balancing applied to reduce bias toward the majority class. The genetic algorithm iteratively evolved candidate convolutional configurations using classification accuracy as the fitness criterion. The optimized model achieved high diagnostic performance, with a mean test accuracy of 87.89% ± 1.41% (macro precision 89.74% ± 0.95%, macro recall 80.38% ± 3.04%, macro F1-score 83.32% ± 2.58%) across five independent runs on an independent test set. These results indicate that evolutionary optimization of convolutional configurations can improve robustness and classification performance for automated dental caries detection. By reducing dependence on manual architectural tuning and improving diagnostic consistency, the proposed framework offers a promising computer-aided decision-support approach for dental image analysis.

title: Research on Aided Reading System of Digital Library Based on Text Image Features and Edge Computing
abstract: With the rapid development of library informatization, traditional text information retrieval service methods have been unable to meet the needs of users. Therefore, personalized assisted reading technology has attracted wider attention, as it can discover hidden associations by mining user information, book information, and user operation logs, and recommend the acquired knowledge to users. In order to improve the service quality and experiences of users, this paper presents a digital library assisted reading system that combines text image features and edge computing. Firstly, the digital library reading assistance system framework is proposed based on edge computing technology, which will improve the service quality and information transmission level of the digital library. The auxiliary reading model of the digital library is presented based on text image features and an RBF neural network. Detailed simulation results verify the applicability and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

title: Research progress on optical coherence tomography image analysis for gastrointestinal tumors: From conventional methods to artificial intelligence
abstract: ABSTRACT Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is increasingly recognized as a high-resolution, real-time modality for imaging and characterization of gastrointestinal (GI) tumors. This review summarizes OCT imaging and the artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methods used in GI oncology, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer models. We review recent advances in preprocessing pipelines, feature extraction, segmentation, and automated tissue classification, tracing developments in classical ML and deep learning architectures. We also discuss emerging AI-assisted OCT approaches to tumor-margin assessment, tissue recognition, and quantitative analysis, together with the validation needed before clinical deployment. We further discuss multimodal imaging fusion strategies that integrate OCT with complementary modalities and AI algorithms to enhance diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision support. Major challenges, such as data standardization, domain generalization, and the need for clinically deployable explainable AI are highlighted. Finally, we outline key future directions, advocating for large-scale multicenter collaborations, robust validation frameworks, and regulatory pathways to advance the safe clinical translation of AI-powered OCT systems in GI tumor management.
authors: Zijing Zhang; Tao Chen; Yutang Ren; Xiaoying Tang; Hongen Liao; Yingwei Fan

title: Restorative Dentistry and Prosthodontics: Caries Detection, Shade Matching and AI-Designed Restorations
abstract: Restorative dentistry has embraced artificial intelligence (AI) across several distinct tasks: caries detection, assessment of existing restorations and tooth-surface loss, tooth-shade determination, computer-aided design of restorations and, increasingly, regenerative-dentistry applications. A comprehensive review of 63 studies published between 2020 and January 2025 reported diagnostic accuracies of up to 95% for AI-based caries detection, together with improvements in treatment-planning efficiency and reduced chair time attributable to AI-assisted workflows. Predictive analytics are beginning to support personalised restorative planning, and emerging trends, including AI-powered robotic systems, virtual assistants and multimodal data integration, point toward deeper integration of AI across restorative and prosthodontic care. This chapter reviews these applications, from the detection of caries on photographs and radiographs to the automatic design of crowns, and discusses the barriers identified in the literature: data-privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, limited interpretability and the absence of standardised AI training for dental professionals. It also examines the management dimension, since digital workflow and AI change documentation, productivity and costs. The chapter concludes that AI can make restorative care more preventive, precise and efficient if early detection is matched by minimally invasive management

title: RetiDual-Select: Reliability-Aware Specialist-Generalist Routing for Retinal OCT under Image-Quality Shift
abstract: Adaptive fusion can repair a static ensemble's errors, but can also overturn correct decisions. RetiDual-Select combines retinal specialist RETFound with the image encoder of the medical vision-language model MedSigLIP, separating candidate fusion, routing safety and predictive review. Calibrated product-of-experts (PoE) fusion is the static reference, a small gate proposes an alternative for each image, a validation-frozen harm guard decides whether that candidate may replace the reference, and a separate score prioritizes review. Static PoE reached the highest or joint-highest clean accuracy on all three datasets. At a clean 2% accepted-error target the review policy accepted 94.3% of Kermany-4 images at 99.89% selective accuracy, and 92.4% of OCT-C8 at 98.65%. Both branches were correct on 95.0% and 91.8% of clean images; only 4.4% and 6.2% had exactly one correct branch. Across 15 prespecified synthetic conditions, adaptive gains were concentrated in severe contrast reduction, where this routing opportunity widened roughly ninefold; percentile rescaling largely removed the effect, linking it to compressed dynamic range. In post-hoc validation-only analyses, gain was higher when the gate followed the more reliable branch, and a frozen guard cut the worst-condition OCT-C8 loss from 1.39 to 0.36 percentage points. Adaptive routing was useful when image quality created a reliability opportunity and the gate followed it; otherwise the system retained Static PoE or deferred for review. The findings are bounded by the synthetic perturbations evaluated and do not establish robustness to natural acquisition or scanner shift.
authors: Zihao Han; Philippe De Wilde

title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
abstract: Ophthalmic clinical decision support requires fast, accurate, and privacy-preserving inference, yet autoregressive large language models (LLMs) incur substantial latency and computational overhead for decisions among predefined actions. We therefore investigate a decision-oriented alternative to generative reasoning. Specifically, we first introduce RetiJev-Data, a source-grounded ophthalmology corpus comprising 78,158 clinical-decision and diagnosis questions derived from articles in PubMed Central and a MeSH vocabulary covering 531 eye diseases, and 50,074 guideline-grading questions spanning 11 grading systems, along with a 24,662-question evaluation benchmark. Based on this, we develop RetiJev, a family of 0.8B-9B decision models that directly score candidate answers without autoregressive decoding. Across all model sizes, RetiJev outperforms both a 27B LLM and the commercial Jev 1.13 decision model on guideline grading by 10.4-23.0 points. RetiJev-9B further achieves the highest accuracy on clinical decisions, improving over both baselines by 5.4-6.5 points while matching them on diagnosis. It answers a case in 158 ms on one GPU, 3.5x faster than LLM generation and 470x faster than reasoning. Models are released at https://github.com/Awenbocc/RetiJev.
authors: Bo Liu; Lianyu Wang; Meng Wang; Ching-Yu Cheng; Huazhu Fu

title: RetinaGuard: Risk-Controlled Agentic Triage for Multi-Disease Retinal Screening
abstract: Retinal screening programmes need to know which automated decisions can be accepted without review. This paper presents RetinaGuard, an agentic triage framework in which quality, diagnostic, uncertainty, verification and explanation agents gather evidence for each fundus photograph, a learned failure predictor estimates the probability that the decision is unsafe, auxiliary tools are invoked only when their expected value of information exceeds their cost, and the acceptance threshold is certified by conformal risk control. On the RFMiD test split, RetinaGuard was compared with confidence and calibrated-uncertainty referral at matched referral budgets and equal certified safety, using two RETFound primary models of different strength. With the weaker model (macro-AUROC 0.896), verifier disagreement added significant information, RetinaGuard captured 119 of 280 unsafe decisions at a 20% budget against 88 for lowest-confidence referral, and at a nominal 5% unsafe level it accepted 37.0% of cases against 10.3%. With the stronger model (0.925) the verifier added nothing beyond uncertainty and the advantage shrank to a few percentage points. In both settings its coverage at the nominal 5% level stayed near 37.7%, gating cut computation by about 30%, and a quality agent reduced unsafe acceptances under most image corruptions. The benefit of agentic evidence gathering thus depends on how much the primary model's own uncertainty already reveals about its errors.
authors: Sohaib Sulman; Muhammad Atif Saeed; Akhtar Jamıl; Alaa Ali Hameed; Roland Can Aydin

title: RetinaSC: Retinal Semantic Communication Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight semantic com- munication framework for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading from fundus images pertaining specifically to the APTOS2019 dataset. The framework includes semantic encoder designed using ResNet34, U-Net, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures. Further, the trained models are used to train the same framework for IDRiD dataset using transfer learning approach. Such a framework will enable the telemedicine sector in the early detection of DR and prevent total blindness. The results reveal that for APTOS, task-oriented semantic systems can achieve satisfactory robust performance (more than 0.8 weighted F1 score for ResNet34 and EfficientNet-B0) across different channels. In particular, considering the trade-off between complexity, latency, throughput, and F1 score, MobileNetV2 is the best model with weighted F1 score of 0.76-0.78 for both task and reconstruction- oriented modules and end-to-end latency of only 8.162 ms.
authors: Avani Shinod; Rangineni Rushitha; Asqeem Nas; Anirban Bhowal; Shikha Baghel

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: <0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. authors: Le Cao; Chen Yaqi; Hang Wang; William Robert Kwapong; Shijia Zhou; Tianxiang Lan; Ruishan Liu; Ruosu Pan; Yuying Yan; Wendan Tao; Guina Liu; Yitian Zhao; Bo Wu
venue: Journal of the American Heart Association

title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas
abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference −1.29 percentage points, 95% CI −3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = −2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = −3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.
authors: Selin Şimşek Alkan; Aslı Vural; Vildan Gürses Beşli; Sibel Zırtıloğlu; Seda Karslı; Seda Turgut; Didem Acarer; Naim Pamuk; Hamide Pişkinpaşa; Sema Çiftçi

title: Retinal Vessel Density Loss Without Structural Thinning in Early Multiple Sclerosis: An Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography Study
abstract: Retinal microvascular and structural changes both occur in multiple sclerosis (MS), but their relationship in early disease remains unclear. We conducted a prospective observational study of 15 participants with early relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS; mean disease duration 1.1 years) and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC), using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) to compare retinal vessel density and structural thickness. MS eyes were stratified by optic neuritis (ON) history. MS eyes without ON history (MS-NON) showed a significant (all standardized β < −1, p < 0.001) reduction in vessel density as compared to HC in macular superficial vascular complex (SVC) and ganglion cell layer plexus (GCLP), as well as peripapillary nerve fiber layer plexus (NFLP), despite relatively preserved macular ganglion cell inner plexiform layer (GCIPL β = −0.26) and ganglion cell complex thickness (GCC β = −0.17; both non-significant). In contrast, MS eyes with ON history (MS-ON) showed tightly coupled structural thinning and reduced vessel density. Structure-vascular correlations in MS-NON eyes were weak for superficial compartments (GCLP, SVC) but strong for NFLP. These findings indicate that microvascular dysfunction can occur in the absence of detectable structural loss in early MS, and raise the possibility that, in eyes without optic neuritis, vascular changes may precede detectable neuronal loss. OCTA-derived vascular biomarkers may complement structural OCT in early MS monitoring.
authors: Elizabeth Silbermann; Ou Tan; Jie Wang; Andrea Hildebrand; Lindsey Wooliscroft; Emma Young; Yali Jia; Po‐Han Yeh; Rebecca Spain; DENNIS N. BOURDETTE; David Huang

title: Retinal foundation-model versus ImageNet pretraining for deep learning grading of diabetic retinopathy: an external validation study
abstract: Purpose To determine whether retinal foundation-model pretraining reduces the loss of diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading agreement on external fundus-photograph datasets compared with ImageNet-pretrained convolutional networks. Methods RETFound (linear probe and full fine-tuning), EfficientNet-B3 and ResNet-50 were developed on APTOS 2019 (3,662 images) and tested unchanged on Messidor-2 (1,744 images, adjudicated grades) and IDRiD (516 images). The prespecified primary outcome was the difference in internal-to-external quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) drop relative to EfficientNet-B3 for one training run per model; a post hoc analysis averaged three or four runs per model. Results Internal QWK was 0.879 (EfficientNet-B3) and 0.888 (RETFound). In the prespecified analysis, RETFound’s excess drop was + 0.020 (95% CI − 0.024 to + 0.064) on Messidor-2 and + 0.033 (− 0.023 to + 0.091) on IDRiD; averaged over runs, it was + 0.068 (+ 0.003 to + 0.134; Holm p = 0.074) and + 0.020 (− 0.041 to + 0.080). On Messidor-2, referable-DR sensitivity was 36–43% with specificity 90–98%, and EfficientNet-B3 graded 259 of 270 mild-DR images as no DR. Matching case mix and merging grades 0 and 1 reduced the Messidor-2 drop by 63–69%. Label smoothing reproduced RETFound’s lower external calibration error. Conclusion Retinal foundation-model pretraining did not reduce external performance loss. Similar internal agreement did not establish robustness across image sources and reference standards, and no model was suitable for autonomous screening at these operating points.
authors: Pravinraj Ethiraj

title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
abstract: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study. It combines measurements of data relationships with two comparisons: changing the evaluation population while holding predictions fixed, and changing training data while holding evaluation fixed. Byte-identical files cross the public training-validation boundary, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings that contribute frames occur in both partitions. Shared source recordings establish cross-split overlap; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent counting unique shared patients. Across ten paired seeds, removing all training rows attributed to Kvasir-Capsule, plus five rows from other sources flagged as near-matches to it, lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%. Evaluating the same fitted models on the validation rows of the other sources reverses the comparison: removal improves balanced accuracy by 1.38 percentage points. The public-validation drop measures sensitivity to source removal, not an amount of leakage-induced inflation. Matched controls show that sample size and class counts alone do not explain the observed score differences. An exploratory experiment removes the training neighbors of validation frames that have close training matches, or equally many distant training rows, and yields a difference-in-differences estimate, relative to matched unflagged frames, of -0.355 percentage points in true-class probability; the paired-t interval for accuracy spans zero. The resulting procedure distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity and specifies the population, class support and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.
authors: Eunseob Choi; Kyeonghun Kim; Hyuk‐Jae Lee; Nam-Joon Kim

title: Reviewer #3 (Public review): Glia regulate local retinoic acid levels to specify neuronal specialisation for high-acuity vision
abstract: This important study investigates how retinoic acid signaling and retinal support cells called Müller glia might contribute to regional differences in the morphology and function of cone photoreceptors -light-sensitive neurons in the zebrafish retina -and may have broader implications for understanding how non-neuronal cells such as glia shape neuronal cell specialization in other regions of the nervous system.Despite well-executed imaging and pharmacological experiments, the evidence remains incomplete because the proposed mechanism is not established as specific to Müller glia, and broader effects on retinal development, cell growth, maturation, and/or differentiation could explain the observed shortening of light-sensitive structures.The work will interest researchers studying vision, nervous system development, and interactions between neurons and their supporting cells.

title: Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment: A Contemporary Review of Repair Techniques, Common Complications, Advances in Imaging and Access to Care.
abstract: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) is a vision-threatening ophthalmic emergency with a rising global incidence driven by aging populations and the worldwide myopia epidemic. Despite modern surgical techniques achieving anatomic reattachment in over 90% of cases, as many as 40% of successfully reattached eyes fail to recover functional vision, underscoring a persistent and clinically important gap between anatomic and visual outcomes. We synthesize contemporary evidence across a wide clinical spectrum of RRD. We examine the pathophysiologic cascade initiated by posterior vitreous detachment, the classification and clinical significance of types of retinal breaks, and the epidemiologic burden of established risk factors including high myopia, pseudophakia, and hereditary vitreoretinal disorders. The historical evolution of repair techniques is reviewed. Evidence based rationale for personalized surgical selection in phakic, pseudophakic, and giant retinal tear-associated detachments is then discussed. The most common complications of surgical repair are addressed, with particular emphasis on proliferative vitreoretinopathy as the dominant cause of surgical failure and the most pressing unmet therapeutic need. We further examine how neighborhood-level social determinants of health independently shape presentation severity and visual recovery, underscoring that equitable access to timely care can be as fundamental to influencing outcomes as surgical technique itself. Finally, emerging pharmacologic strategies, intraoperative optical coherence tomography, robotic surgical assistance, and imaging prognostic tools, with and without the use of artificial intelligence are evaluated as future directions. Advancing outcomes in RRD will require the integration of surgical refinement, emerging pharmacology, imaging-based prognostication, and an unwavering commitment to equitable access across all patient populations.
authors: Ranveer Palia; Kameron Downs; Sally S Ong

title: Risk factors for inadequate bowel preparation and quality improvement strategies in colonoscopy: a narrative review
abstract: Colonoscopy is the gold-standard screening test for colorectal cancer, yet its diagnostic yield relies heavily on adequate bowel preparation. Despite standard protocols, 20%-30% of procedures still have inadequate cleansing, which lowers adenoma detection, prolongs procedures, increases repeat examinations, and wastes resources. Preparation quality is influenced by multiple interacting factors: patient characteristics (age, comorbidities, medication use, adherence), regimen features (purgative type, dose, split-dose scheduling), and healthcare delivery (education quality, appointment timing). Most previous studies have examined these factors in isolation, leaving a gap in integrated, evidence-based guidance. This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on determinants of preparation quality, with emphasis on emerging strategies such as risk-stratified protocols, low-volume purgatives, digital health tools (mobile apps, SMS reminders), and AI-based real-time assessment. We aim to provide a practical framework for individualized preparation, thereby improving both the efficiency and quality of colonoscopy-based screening.
authors: Shanshan Ma; Xinyu Zhou

title: Robot social anxiety as a distinct psychological construct: Relations to human social anxiety and development of the multidimensional social robot anxiety scale
abstract: Anxiety toward social robots is becoming increasingly relevant as they enter everyday environments; however, the psychological structure of this anxiety and its relation to interpersonal social anxiety remain unclear. This study developed and validated the Multidimensional Social Robot Anxiety Scale (MSRAS) and examined whether robot social anxiety (RSA) constituted a distinct psychological construct via two large-scale surveys (N 1 = 1,957; N 2 = 2,393). Based on Dennett’s framework, factor-analytic results identified four dimensions: Physical Danger, Social Cognitive Ability, Information Security, and Social Anxiety toward Robots. These were supported by a bifactor structure in which RSA retained substantial unique variance, indicating that it was conceptually and empirically distinct from other robot-related anxieties. Furthermore, structural equation modeling revealed that general human social anxiety significantly predicted RSA, suggesting that RSA and human social anxiety (HSA) share certain psychological characteristics. However, RSA diverged from HSA in its socio-emotional correlates: it had markedly weaker associations with self-perceived social skills and perceived social support. The association between RSA and need to belong was weaker than that with social phobia but comparable to that with social interaction anxiety, providing only partial support for the predicted attenuation of belongingness-related concerns. These findings suggest that RSA and HSA share certain characteristics while exhibiting systematic differences, potentially reflecting the perceived limitations of robots' social-evaluative and emotional capacities. Furthermore, the MSRAS is a psychometrically robust tool for examining individual differences in robot-related anxiety and advancing theoretical models of anxiety in human–robot interactions.
authors: Te-Chi Huang; Ritsuko Iwai; Takatsune Kumada
venue: Computers in Human Behavior Artificial Humans

title: Robot-Pet and Virtual Reality Distraction During Fissure Sealant Treatment in Children: A Three-Arm Randomized Clinical Trial
abstract: Innovative distraction approaches are increasingly being explored in pediatric dentistry. This three-arm randomized controlled trial aimed to compare Robot-Pet and virtual reality (VR) distraction with Tell-Show-Do (TSD) during children's first dental treatment involving fissure sealant placement. Of the 78 randomized children aged 6-10 years, 72 completed treatment and were analyzed (24/group). Dental anxiety(DA) levels were assessed using the Children's Fear Survey Schedule-Dental Subscale (CFSS-DS) and Facial Image Scale (FIS), and behavior using the Frankl Behavior Rating Scale (FBRS), pre- and post-treatment. Intraoperative behavior was evaluated using the Modified Houpt Scale (MHS) during treatment, while heart rate and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) were measured before, during, and after treatment. Post-treatment perceptions were assessed by questionnaire. Analyses used Chi-square/Fisher’s exact, Kruskal-Wallis, and Brunner-Langer models with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (p<0.05). CFSS-DS and FIS scores decreased post-treatment in all groups (p<0.05), with no between-group differences (p>0.05). VR had lower MHS-Movement scores than Robot-Pet and Control (p<0.05). Heart rate and oxygen saturation did not differ between groups (p>0.05); heart rate increased during washing compared with pre-treatment across groups (p<0.05). Children and parents positively evaluated Robot-Pet and VR. DA scores decreased post-treatment in all groups without between-group differences. Robot-Pet offers tactile distraction, whereas VR provides audiovisual distraction and was associated with less movement during treatment. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov ( NCT06243705), registered on 25 January 2024 (retrospectively registered).
authors: RANA BİLİCİ KÖSE; Bahar Melis Akyıldız Çelik

title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with intraoperative ultrasound guidance
abstract: Background. Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy is one of the main nephron-sparing surgical approaches for localized renal tumors. However, the lack of full tactile feedback during robotic surgery may complicate identification of the true tumor margins, particularly in endophytic, sinus, and anatomically complex tumors. In this setting, intraoperative ultrasound can be regarded as a surgical navigation tool that enables more accurate assessment of tumor localization, depth, and relationship to the collecting system. Aim. To analyze the authors’ experience with robot-assisted partial nephrectomy using intraoperative ultrasound guidance. Materials and methods. From 2024 to the present, 34 robot-assisted partial nephrectomies with intraoperative ultrasound navigation were performed at the University Urology Clinic of the Moscow Multidisciplinary Clinical Centre “Kommunarka”. Clinical and anatomical characteristics of the patients and tumors, perioperative parameters, complication rates, pathological outcomes, surgical margin status, and early renal functional dynamics were assessed. Results. Men and women were equally represented: 17 patients each (50.0 %). Median age was 62 [48.2; 67] years. Median tumor size was 3.0 [2.6; 3.8] cm. cT1a tumors were diagnosed in 27 (79.4 %) patients, cT1b tumors in 5 (14.7 %), and cT2a tumors in 2 (5.9 %). Complexity of intervention depending on anatomical characteristics of the tumors was intermediate (7–9 points per the RENAL score) in 11 (32.4 %) patients, and highly complex (10–12 points) in 23 (67.6 %). Median operative time was 147.5 [121.2; 175] min, and median estimated blood loss was 50 [22.5; 50] mL. Temporary vessel clamping (warm ischemia) was used in 29 (85.3 %) patients, with a median duration of 20 [17; 28] min. Collecting system entry occurred in 5 (14.7 %) patients. Postoperative complications were recorded in 4 (11.8 %) patients, including Clavien–Dindo grade III–IV complications in 2 (5.9 %). Positive surgical margin was identified in 2 (5.8 %) patients. Acute kidney injury occurred in 8 (23.5 %) patients; none required renal replacement therapy. Conclusion. Intraoperative ultrasound navigation is an important stage of robot-assisted partial nephrectomy, particularly in endophytic, sinus, anatomically complex, and poorly visualized tumors. This technique allows more precise assessment of tumor margins, depth of tumor location, and its relationship to the collecting system, thereby facilitating determination of the resection line and improving technical safety of nephronsparing surgery.
authors: D. V. Tyzyo; Кобзев Д. С.; Renat I. Guspanov; Igor V. Meshchankin; A. A. Nemenov; A. G. Pavlenko; G. A. Pirozhenko; A. S. Maksimova; Sergey Vladislavovich Kotov

title: Robotic ultrasound scanning platform with autonomous control, multimodal human-machine interface and real-time image analysis.
abstract: Autonomous robots can streamline repetitive and time-consuming surgical tasks like ultrasound scanning. AI can provide the necessary intelligence, but for clinical acceptance, systems must move predictably, offer intuitive interaction, and maintain low latency on medical-grade hardware. We present an integral robotic platform for autonomous ultrasound scanning. The platform allows to perform scanning on either manual or autonomous mode. The autonomous control combines AI-driven ultrasound target segmentation with geometric motion algorithms designed to focus the probe on the segmented target. We optimized the image processing models for specialized hardware to ensure real-time performance with constrained resources. Users can control the platform via natural language voice commands processed by a Large Language Model (LLM) and visualize the procedure through a synchronized 3D Digital Twin and an augmented reality (AR) environment. We tested the platform in hepatic tumor localization in a synthetic phantom. Autonomous tumor localization showed a success rate of 84% with an average execution time of 5.75 s. Our system successfully automates ultrasound tasks, allowing the user to control the process through an intuitive, multimodal interface. By pairing optimized AI with specialized hardware, we achieved low-latency, real-time adaptability with minimal hardware resources. In the future we plan to adapt this platform for more complex neurosurgical and urological procedures.

title: Robotic ultrasound-guided biopsy, ablation, and access: a bibliometric analysis and validation-evidence map : Original Article.
abstract:
Background

Robotic assistance is increasingly used in ultrasound-guided biopsy, ablation, and percutaneous access, but the extent of experimental and human evaluation varies across these procedures.

Methods

We combined bibliometric analysis with a publication-level assessment of procedural application and the highest reported validation setting in studies published during 2000-2025.

Results

Searches of PubMed and the Web of Science Core Collection returned 1,198 records corresponding to 857 unique publications. The Technology corpus included 197 focused Master publications and 210 adjacent Edge publications (n = 407). Of the Master publications, 184 reported direct evaluation: V0 (bench, phantom, simulation, or in vitro; n = 55), V1 (ex vivo or cadaver; n = 32), V2 (live animal; n = 27), and V3 (human; n = 70). These concerned biopsy (n = 51), ablation (n = 57), access (n = 74), or other procedures (n = 2). Human-stage evaluation was reported in 40/51 biopsy publications (78.4%), 23/57 ablation publications (40.4%), and 7/74 access publications (9.5%). Among 70 V3 reports, 68 described interventions in patients and two described non-interventional evaluation. Fifty-four of the 57 ablation reports could be assigned to five predefined pathways.

Conclusions

Human evaluation was most common in biopsy, whereas ablation and especially access included more preclinical work. These counts characterize the reported settings of evaluation and cannot establish clinical effectiveness, independent patient cohorts, or the maturity of individual technologies.

title: SIGHT: A Methodological Appraisal Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in Ophthalmology
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly evaluated across ophthalmic tasks, yet the methodological quality of these evaluations has received little attention. Most studies report accuracy while overlooking design features required for valid and clinically meaningful inference. We critically reviewed published ophthalmic LLM evaluation studies covering knowledge assessment, patient education, diagnostic reasoning, triage, clinical documentation, multimodal image interpretation, and uncertainty estimation. We used the methodological weaknesses that recurred across study designs to develop the SIGHT framework, which has five domains: Sample and item provenance, Independence and blinding, Ground truth and comparator fairness, Handling of paired and repeated-measures data, and Transparency and trustworthiness. Current evaluations rely heavily on benchmark accuracy, synthetic clinical vignettes, and curated datasets, and real-world clinical validation remains rare. Common limitations include potential training-data contamination, inadequate handling of paired data, limited assessment of inter-rater reliability, inconsistent reference standards, insufficient evaluation of calibration and uncertainty, and frequent overinterpretation of benchmark performance as evidence of clinical readiness. SIGHT provides twenty structured appraisal items to evaluate internal validity, interpretability, and applicability across diverse ophthalmic LLM study designs. It offers a practical way to appraise ophthalmic LLM studies and may improve the methodological quality, interpretability, and clinical relevance of future evaluations.
authors: Hadi Vahedi; Fatemeh Razmjooei; Farbod Semnani; Parviz Vahedi; Roohallah Alizadehsani; Ali Jafarizadeh

title: Safeguards, residual failures, and human oversight in clinical agentic and related artificial intelligence workflows: a systematic scoping review
abstract: Background Clinical agentic artificial intelligence (AI) can alter its actions during a clinical task, creating failure pathways that conventional performance metrics may not capture. Whether safeguards interrupt these pathways remains uncertain. Aim To map safeguard effects, residual failures, human recovery, and resource consequences in clinical agentic and related AI workflows. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and IEEE Xplore, for English-language, peer-reviewed empirical journal reports. This scoping review used independent screening, duplicate extraction, narrative synthesis, and result-specific critical appraisal. Results The 111 reports comprised 56 functionally agentic, 29 related non-agentic, 22 architecture-uncertain, and four human-factors reports; 38 of the 56 agentic reports explicitly documented model-directed subsequent-action selection. Among the 111 selected appraisal results, none both isolated a specified safeguard’s effect and demonstrated reduced measured patient harm. Configurations incorporating safeguards improved selected outcomes, but gains coexisted with omissions, reduced sensitivity, false reassurance, delay, or transferred review burden. Concurrent changes in models, prompts, evidence access, and workflow frequently prevented attribution to individual controls. Some patient-randomised trials reported patient or process benefits, but evaluated bundled interventions rather than the contribution of a safeguard. Human authority was more often documented than successful error detection and recovery; requiring clinician approval did not establish that residual errors were recognised and corrected. Performance varied across models, settings, and information conditions, limiting transfer of favourable findings. Reported efficiency gains depended on measurement boundaries and did not consistently account for review, correction, escalation, and downstream work. Discussion The evidence exposes a gap between local error control and safety across a complete clinical episode. A safeguard can reduce a targeted error while shifting risk to later decisions or human reviewers. We propose a post hoc , non-ordinal evidence profile addressing mechanism fidelity, residual and introduced failures, robustness, joint human–AI performance, and clinical consequences. The profile requires validation; heterogeneous designs and retrospective methodological refinements constrain inference. Conclusion Clinical safety should be evaluated across the complete care pathway, tracing safeguard effects through residual error, human recovery, and patient-relevant outcomes. Selective autonomy requires joint assessment of residual risk and the capacity for timely human review.
authors: Rabie Adel El Arab; Wesam Taher Almagharbeh; Sameer A. Alkubati; Mudassir Imran Mustafa

title: Safety and Usability of a Novel, Robotic Assistance System for Echocardiographic Examination.
abstract:
Background

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is essential for modern cardiac diagnostics, yet it is difficult to access in remote areas. Remotely operated robotic-assisted ultrasound may enable access to services in rural and remote locations, while also improving ergonomics for the sonographer. This study evaluated the safety, usability and patient satisfaction of a novel robotic ultrasound assistance tool (RUAT).

Methods

This open-label, single-site, single-arm clinical trial enrolled adult participants who had recently completed a standard manual echocardiogram. A trained sonographer performed a robot-assisted TTE from a dedicated workstation in the same room as the patient. Endpoints included safety measured by adverse events, technical and clinical usability, and patient satisfaction using surveys about the participants' experience.

Results

The trial cohort (n=30; mean age 62.9 ± 17.5 years; 70% men) all successfully completed the robot-assisted TTE and the patient satisfaction survey. There were no adverse events or adverse device effects. The functional verification checklist supporting technical usability demonstrated an average usability rate of 96.9% (95% CI [98.9-100.0]), with a 100% rate across 10 of 12 metrics. The sonographer's review of the acquired robotic images measured the clinical usability and 29 of 30 examinations met acceptable diagnostic standards (96.7%; 95% CI [88.1-100.0]). The mean participant satisfaction score was 8.3 out of 10, with 96.7% scoring ≥6.

Conclusion

The RUAT demonstrated high technical and clinical usability, as well as high acceptance by participants. These findings indicate that robot-assisted TTE is a viable strategy to enhance remote access to TTE services.
authors: West C, Guppy-Coles K, Armstrong JW, Johnstone M, Scott A, Atherton JJ.

title: Scalable Thermoset Informatics Integrated with Autonomous Experimentation for On-Demand Discovery
abstract: As photopolymer additive manufacturing matures, there is an increasing need for on-demand, application-specific materials. A major bottleneck is the limited exploration of the vast design space for new thermoset polymer formulations, which must satisfy both material property requirements and processing constraints. This challenge arises from the combinatorial complexity of formulations and the high cost of experimental evaluation. In this work, we present an end-to-end pipeline that integrates a partial self-driving laboratory (p-SDL) with informatics-driven optimization to discover and validate thermoset acrylate formulations. The pipeline begins with a thermoset acrylate database that consolidates multiple data sources, including in-house experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and literature data. These data sets are used to train single-task and multitask predictive models, which interface directly with the p-SDL to guide experiments and measure mechanical and processing-related properties. Each component is validated independently and then deployed together to optimize a target elastomeric material with over 90% reduction in human effort. The complete optimization required only ∼40 h of active experimental time, demonstrating rapid identification of formulations that satisfy multiple target properties without exhaustive screening. This work establishes a scalable framework for embedding multifidelity machine learning within laboratory workflows, enabling autonomous, data-driven thermoset formulation discovery.
authors: Marcus R. Fratarcangeli; Ayush Jain; Farzad Gholami; Jiaqi Nie; Anagha Savit; Hang Jerry Qi; Rampi Ramprasad

title: Seeing the Small: Deformable Duality Mamba for Retinal Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) lesions vary widely in shape, and microaneurysms (MAs) span only a few pixels. We hypothesize that modeling the spatial organization of lesion regions, with global context and shape-adaptive scanning, improves the segmentation of such small and irregular lesions. To test this, we propose D$^2$Mamba, which couples non-causal state space duality with deformable Mamba scanning. We evaluate it with five-fold cross-validation on the DDR dataset, comparing against representative segmentation baselines under an identical training protocol, and conduct ablations on each component. D$^2$Mamba achieved the best overall performance, with 33.87% mIoU, 2.99 percentage points above the strongest baseline. The largest gain appeared on MAs, the smallest and most easily missed lesions, where Dice improved by 10.06 percentage points. These results confirm our hypothesis that spatially adaptive state space modeling benefits tiny-lesion segmentation. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/PUREPANEL1/D2Mamba.
authors: Chang Yu; Siqing Li; Yuanchen Liu; Zhenyu Bu; Luming Yang; Alper Yilmaz

title: Segmental jejunal “watermelon-like” vascular ectasia in portal hypertensive enteropathy: rationale for medical therapy over argon plasma coagulation
