title: USB Gym: A Gymnasium Testbed for Closed-Loop Ultrasound View Matching
abstract: Background and Objective: Our main goal is ultrasound guidance: moving a probe until its image matches a target view. Published methods for each part of a guide are evaluated in separate simulators. We asked whether these methods, combined into one guide, are good enough. Methods: We built USB Gym, a testbed whose standard engine simulates ultrasound from public patient CT, with a network drawing organ textures from CT labels. Its guide has three replaceable parts (slots), an organ segmenter, a controller and a reward, which received 20 published methods, each run on the same 60 episodes of six held-out patients. In each slot, a published method replaced ours only if detectably better on these patients. The better of this combination and our original guide on 20 new CTs is the benchmark baseline. A pose oracle, reading the exact probe pose available only in simulation, set the reference. The results below are exploratory. Results: On these CTs, the probe started on average 16.0 mm from the target view; the pose oracle brought it to 1.5 mm. Of the results known when the combination was fixed, only an image-similarity reward (SSIM) was slightly but detectably better, so the combination was our guide with that reward. This combination was the benchmark baseline, ending at 13.7 mm (16% of the oracle's progress). Conclusions: Combining untuned published methods with ours did not guide the probe near the target view; the task remains under-explored. The testbed accepts new methods; no guide was tested on hardware.
authors: Thanapong Intharah; Zhichao Gao; Yiliang Liu; Hao Dong

title: Ultralow‐Bias‐Switchable Dual‐Mode Retinomorphic Device for Adaptive Extreme‐Exposure Image Restoration and Event‐Driven Light Source Positioning
abstract: Safe operation of autonomous driving vision systems requires integrated photodetection and processing capabilities. However, existing vision systems remain constrained by separated architectures and limited adaptability to complex lighting environments. Here, we report a TiO 2 /ZnIn 2 S 4 heterostructure dual‐mode optoelectronic device, enabling on‐demand switching between photodetection and optoelectronic synaptic functions under an ultralow bias of 1 mV. The type‐I heterojunction integrates highly ordered TiO 2 nanotube arrays for directional carrier transport, oxygen vacancies for carrier trapping, and layered ZnIn 2 S 4 nanosheets for enhanced light harvesting and interfacial carrier transfer, enabling bias‐dependent carrier separation and release. As a result, the device exhibits efficient photodetection and tunable synaptic dynamics, enabling adaptive exposure compensation and dynamic image restoration for both overexposed and underexposed visual scenes. When configured into bioinspired spheroidal vision arrays, it further supports wide‐field detection, targeted localization, and early warning of potential hazards. This device highlights a promising approach for adaptive machine vision toward intelligent perception in autonomous driving scenarios.
authors: Linglong Wu; Ruotao Yu; Jiaxin Chen; Wentao Xu

title: Ultrasonography in disaster medicine: a narrative review
abstract: This narrative review aimed to critically appraise the diagnostic accuracy, clinical impact, and operational feasibility of ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography (POCUS) across the four domains of disaster medicine. A literature search was conducted following the SANRA and PRISMA-trAIce guidelines. Records were identified through an AI-assisted literature-discovery tool (the Undermind Deep-Search platform, interrogating the Semantic Scholar corpus) run on 15 June 2025, rather than through an independent structured multi-database search. Candidate references were screened manually against pre-specified eligibility criteria by a single reviewer, with the search parameters independently verified by the senior author. Of 71 records identified, 63 met the inclusion criteria. The included studies comprised 32 original studies, 10 systematic or scoping reviews, 20 narrative or operational papers, and one guideline. In CBRN scenarios, lung ultrasound demonstrated sensitivities of 90-97% for COVID-19 pneumonia versus 60-69% for chest radiography while minimizing healthcare worker exposure. For blast and ballistic injuries, FAST showed a pooled sensitivity of 92.1% (95% CI: 87.8-95.6) and specificity of 98.7% (95% CI: 96.0-99.9) for intra-abdominal hemorrhage. In natural disasters, ultrasound altered management in up to 44% of patients. Post-disaster applications included vascular access, tube confirmation, and complication monitoring. Ultraportable POCUS demonstrates diagnostic utility and operational feasibility across multiple disaster domains. However, evidence quality varies significantly, and standardized protocols remain lacking. Prospective studies linking ultrasound deployment to improved patient outcomes are needed. KEY POINTS: Question When disasters disable conventional imaging, how does ultraportable point-of-care ultrasonography perform for diagnosis, triage, and procedural guidance across the four domains of disaster medicine? Findings Across 63 studies, FAST reached 92.1% pooled sensitivity for hemoperitoneum, lung ultrasound 90-97% versus 60-69% for radiography; management changed in up to 44%. Critical relevance statement This review critically appraises ultraportable ultrasound across all four disaster domains, showing that radiation-free bedside imaging accelerates triage, conserves scarce CT capacity, and extends radiological expertise through tele-guidance, while exposing an evidence base still lacking prospective outcome data.
authors: F. Amiot; Karim Tazarourte; G. Gorincour; Axel Benhamed

title: Ultrasound‐Guided Model Predictive Control for Robot‐Assisted Needle Steering in Muscle‐Contained Double‐Layered Tissue
abstract: BACKGROUND: Needle insertion accuracy in robot-assisted percutaneous puncture is critical for clinical outcomes, especially when traversing multi-layered tissues like muscle and organs. METHODS: This study proposes a novel ultrasound-guided model predictive control method for needle steering. It incorporates a mechanics-based model that accounts for muscle anisotropy and tissue heterogeneity, integrated with ultrasound-based trajectory reconstruction to predict needle deflection. The control strategy is designed to minimise insertion error, the number of rotations, and rotation depth. RESULTS: mm error) for given tasks while minimising tissue trauma. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed method significantly enhances the insertion accuracy and reduces tissue damage, as indicated by the reduced number and depth of needle rotations, for robot-assisted percutaneous in anisotropic, heterogeneous tissue. These results provide a validated foundation for future clinical translation of the proposed control framework.

title: Unclear source of gastrointestinal bleeding: Utilizing small bowel capsule to detect an enteric duplication cyst, a case report
abstract: Enteric duplication cysts (EDCs) are rare congenital malformations that form during embryonic development of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.Symptoms may include vomiting, abdominal distension, a palpable abdominal mass, or bleeding, but they can vary depending on the lesion's location.1 We present the case of a 9-year-old male with recurrent hematochezia and abnormal findings on small bowel capsule endoscopy (SBCE), ultimately diagnosed as an EDC on exploratory laparoscopy.
authors: Victoria Sarata; Kathryn Clarkston; Kirby Lampe

title: Unified image preprocessing and attention-enhanced deep learning framework for cross-device multi-stage retinopathy of prematurity classification
abstract: Background Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is an important retinal disorder in premature infants and a major cause of preventable childhood blindness. Neonatal fundus images exhibit substantial variation across imaging systems, complicating automated analysis. Methods This study presents a unified multi-source framework for five-class ROP image classification combining preprocessing, attention-enhanced deep learning, and Grad-CAM visualization. An initial dataset of 1,151 images was divided into training, validation, and testing subsets, followed by independent offline class-wise augmentation. The pipeline combines adaptive gamma correction, PCAR-CLAHE enhancement, glare suppression, resizing, and normalization. DenseNet201 with CBAM was used for classification. Results On the 300-image augmented test subset, the model achieved an accuracy of 85%, sensitivity of 85%, specificity of 96.25%, and AUROC of 0.9587. Conclusion The framework provides a unified approach for heterogeneous neonatal fundus images with qualitative visual explanations. Findings support further investigation of cross-device generalization and prospective clinical validation.
authors: A. Anny Leema; K. Sowmiya; R Haritha; K. S. Prasanna Kumar; P. A. Balakrishnan

title: Unilateral Anesthesia Mumps After Robotic Gynecologic Surgery: A Case Report.
abstract:
Background

Anesthesia mumps is a rare, benign postoperative complication following anesthesia.

Case

A 63-year-old woman developed unilateral, nontender parotid swelling following robotic-assisted hysterectomy in the Trendelenburg position with shoulder restraints. She had no systemic symptoms, an unremarkable intraoral examination, and a patent airway. No imaging, serology, or amylase testing was performed. Supportive management with hydration, head elevation, and analgesics led to resolution within 24 h.

Conclusions

Unilateral anesthesia mumps likely resulted from dehydration and salivary duct obstruction associated with Trendelenburg positioning. Prompt recognition enabled conservative management, avoiding unnecessary investigations or treatment. As robotic surgery becomes increasingly common, requiring Trendelenburg positioning, anesthesiologists should recognize this complication.
authors: Vlahos F, Panagodimou EK, Sgouta E, Giannakikou I.

title: Use of artificial intelligence as an adjunctive tool in the diagnosis of oral potentially malignant disorders: A literature review
abstract: Objective: To analyze the available scientific evidence regarding the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as an adjunctive tool for clinical evaluation in the diagnosis and screening of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), thoroughly assessing its diagnostic reliability, technical limitations, and relevant ethical aspects. Methodology: This study is a literature review in which structured searches for articles published between 2011 and 2026 were conducted in the PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and Google Scholar electronic databases, using controlled descriptors and Boolean operators related to AI and oral pathology. Results: The scientific literature consistently demonstrates that Deep Learning models, trained primarily on conventional intraoral clinical photographs, achieve high sensitivity and accuracy rates in the detection of OPMDs. However, significant challenges remain, such as high methodological heterogeneity among studies, reliance on well-standardized training data, and the need for more diverse population representation. Conclusion: Artificial Intelligence emerges as a highly promising adjunctive technology for screening and clinical decision support. Nevertheless, its application must remain strictly complementary, in no way replacing the clinical judgment of the dental professional or the histopathological gold standard obtained through tissue biopsy.

title: Using AI-generated ultra-widefield-like fundus images to assist colour fundus photography in screening for chronic kidney disease: a multicentre cross-sectional study
abstract: Objective To develop a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model that derives ultra-widefield-like (UWF-like) fundus images from conventional colour fundus photographs (CFP) and to assess whether these images improve chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening.Methods and analysis This multicentre cross-sectional diagnostic study included 3776 fundus images from 2056 patients at four centres in China and Japan between 2023 and 2024. The generative model was developed and validated using 1865 images from 1049 patients. CKD screening models were developed using 1750 UWF images and their corresponding UWF-derived CFP-like central crops from 909 patients at Ruijin Hospital with patient-level fivefold cross-validation and externally validated using 161 native CFP images from 98 patients at Jiading Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and specificity at fixed sensitivity of 0.80.Results In internal validation, AUCs were 0.911 for real UWF images, 0.773 for AI-generated UWF-like images and 0.689 for UWF-derived CFP-like central crops. At fixed sensitivity of 0.80, specificities were 0.879, 0.573 and 0.459, respectively. In external validation, AI-generated UWF-like images outperformed native CFP images, with an AUC of 0.707 versus 0.609 and specificity of 0.458 versus 0.344. Retinal vascular features from AI-generated UWF-like images remained associated with renal function indicators.Conclusion AI-generated UWF-like images improved CKD screening performance compared with CFP alone. This approach may extend retinal imaging-based CKD screening where UWF imaging is unavailable, but prospective real-world validation is needed before clinical implementation.
authors: Renkai Wu; Huiping Yao; Shanshan Wang; Yan Chen; Linbi Yu; Jingjing Li; Yonghua Kang; Xin Chen; Zhixin Jiang; Yuanlin Mo; Ruiming Fang; Hongen Liao; Guochen Ning; Fang Chen; Qing Chang

title: Utility of the CapsoCam Plus for Overt Gastrointestinal Bleeding After Negative Gastroscopy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
Introduction

Patients with upper gastrointestinal bleeding have a nondiagnostic gastroscopy if bleeding is distal to the duodenum. Capsule endoscopy can localise bleeding to anywhere in the gastrointestinal tract; yield is highest when performed as soon as possible, although impaired motility in unwell patients reduces complete examination rate. The CapsoCam Plus operates without external support equipment, and has a long battery life, theoretically improving completion rate and diagnostic yield.

Objectives

The objectives were to determine the examination completion rate (to the caecum), diagnostic yield and impact on management of the CapsoCam Plus in patients with suspected acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding and nondiagnostic gastroscopy.

Methods

This was an observational retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent gastroscopy within 24 hours of admission to Sheffield Teaching Hospitals, with suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Capsule endoscopy using the CapsoCam Plus was performed in those in whom gastroscopy was normal or identified lesions of uncertain significance. A single expert video reader identified and localised blood, pathological lesions, completeness of small bowel examination and duration of examination. Data were collected retrospectively, including the nature of bleeding, type and timing of investigations, management and diagnosis.

Results

A median of 9 days (IQR 5-14 days) after bleeding, 113 capsule endoscopies were performed in 106 patients (62 M, median age 72 (IQR 63-79) years). Examination was complete to the caecum in 96.5% of cases. Capsule endoscopy identified pathology, blood (in the upper gastrointestinal tract [5.6%], small bowel [68.4%], colon [24.1%] or throughout [1.9%]) or both in 54 (47.8%) examinations, guiding further investigation in 30 (55.6%) of these cases. Of the total number of examinations, capsule endoscopy alone or following guided investigation led to new diagnoses in 21 (18.6%, mostly in the small bowel) and therapeutic intervention in 18 (15.9%).

Conclusions

CapsoCam capsule endoscopy had a high completion rate, making new diagnoses in 18.6% of patients and altering management in the majority of this subgroup.
authors: Johnson CM, Shivakumar V, McKenzie SW, Sidhu R, McAlindon ME.

title: VLM-Based Mesh Segmentation Framework for DDH Robotic Ultrasound.
abstract: For robotic ultrasound targeting developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), reconstructed infant body-surface meshes should preserve the target surface while excluding bed, support, and background geometry. This study proposes a structured vision-language model (VLM)-based multi-view segmentation method for infant phantom mesh cleanup. Text-guided 2D masks provide foreground and background evidence; mask-quality statistics and structured VLM assessments generate view-specific foreground-support weights that undergo deterministic risk suppression before target/non-target classification of 3D vertices. Hard voting and Rule-weighted voting were baselines under identical projection and post-processing settings. We evaluated one physical infant phantom across 150 separate acquisition-reconstruction trials under controlled conditions, each comprising 40 voting views and 10 held-out evaluation views, yielding 1500 manually annotated reference masks. Structured VLM voting achieved a Balanced score (intersection over union minus the 2-pixel tolerant leakage rate) of 0.804 ± 0.085, versus 0.801 ± 0.084 and 0.793 ± 0.086 for Rule-weighted and Hard voting. This leakage rate was 0.087 ± 0.043, versus 0.089 ± 0.042 and 0.092 ± 0.043; mean Coverage remained similar (0.992-0.993). The Balanced-score gain and leakage-rate reduction relative to Rule-weighted voting remained significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.029 and p = 0.033, respectively). Validation using real-infant data, 3D reference standards, and closed-loop robotic scanning is still required.

title: Velocity Optimization via Thermal Imaging Enhances Autonomous Tumor Resection
abstract: Objective: To demonstrate and evaluate THERMO, a thermal-velocity optimization algorithm for autonomous electrosurgery, in ex vivo porcine tissue using the UR10e-based ASTR system. Methods: Thermography for Electrosurgical Rate Modulation via Optimization (ThERMO), a closed-loop algorithm that uses real-time thermal imaging data to minimize thermal injury while ensuring accurate cut margins, was tested on ex vivo porcine tissue. Histological analysis was performed to detect thermal injury extent at a cellular level, and 3D photogrammetric measurement was used to verify margin accuracy. ThERMO's performance was compared against two previously used fixed velocity methods. Results: ThERMO outperformed both fixed velocity comparison methods without requiring data-driven training or iterative tuning, reducing thermal injury by up to 52%, improving cut accuracy by up to 59%, and maintaining task completion speed. Conclusions: Closed-loop thermal feedback via ThERMO improves autonomous robotic electrosurgery by simultaneously reducing thermal injury and improving margin accuracy, reinforcing its value over fixed velocity approaches for tumor resection applications. Significance: This work advances autonomous robotic tumor resection by demonstrating that real-time closed-loop thermal feedback control can substantially reduce collateral tissue damage and improve surgical margin accuracy.
authors: Naveed D. Riaziat; Jiawei Ge; Ethan Kilmer; Michael W. Mikula; Paul Maria Scheikl; Michael Kam; Leila Jean Mady; Axel Krieger; Jeremy D. Brown

title: VesselRegNet: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network for Multi-Modal Joint Retinal Vessel Segmentation and Registration
abstract: Multimodal retinal image registration remains challenging due to nonlinear intensity discrepancies and insufficient feature representation across modalities. To address these limitations, we propose VesselRegNet, a joint retinal vessel segmentation and registration framework based on multi-scale feature fusion. The model integrates a multi-scale semantic feature extraction module with a shared prediction head and rotation-equivariant constraints to enhance feature consistency. Unlike conventional approaches relying on binary segmentation masks, the proposed method utilizes dense semantic features to directly guide deformable registration. Experimental results demonstrate that VesselRegNet achieves an average Dice coefficient of 0.664 and SSIM of 0.645, achieving a relative improvement of 4.1% in Dice and 2.5% in SSIM over the strongest baseline (RetinaRegNet), and up to 11.9% improvement over general unsupervised registration frameworks. The proposed multi-scale fusion and joint learning strategy improves registration accuracy under complex retinal deformations.
authors: Anyu Cao; Maosong Jiang; Qinghong Gao; Xuelian Yang; Caiye Fan; Shu’an Liu; Zuoping Tan; Yuanyuan Wang

title: Video capsule endoscopy in patients with altered proximal small-bowel anatomy: longer transit time and more frequent suboptimal visualization - a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Video capsule endoscopy (VCE) is an effective, noninvasive modality for small bowel (SB) visualization. Comparative data on the technical performance and diagnostic yield of VCE in patients with surgically altered proximal SB anatomy remain limited. Our aim was to compare diagnostic yield, visualization quality, completion and safety, and transit times among patients with surgically altered SB anatomy, other SB resections and non-surgical controls. We retrospectively analyzed prospectively documented data from standardized electronic VCE intake forms and examination reports. All consecutive VCEs of patients aged ≥ 18 years (03/2018-02/2022) were included. Patients with altered SB anatomy (e.g., gastric bypass, one-anastomosis gastric bypass, pancreaticoduodenectomy and Billroth II gastrojejunostomy) were compared to surgical and non-surgical controls. We compared 21 patients with altered SB anatomy (altered-anatomy) to 51 surgical and 932 non-surgical controls. Clinically significant VCE findings were detected in 5/21 (23.8%) altered-anatomy examinations, compared with 30/50 (60.0%) surgical controls ( p = 0.009) and 357/926 (38.6%) non-surgical controls ( p = 0.255). Inadequate SB visualization was observed in 11/21 (52.4%) altered-anatomy examinations, compared with 13/50 (26.0%) surgical controls ( p = 0.053) and 215/926 (23.2%) non-surgical controls ( p = 0.004). Completion rates were 20/21 (95.2%), 47/51 (92.2%), and 912/932 (97.9%), respectively. Median SB transit time was longer in the altered-anatomy group (338 min [IQR 210.3-391.3] vs. 247 min [IQR 187.0-334.0, p = 0.053] in surgical and 241 min [IQR 193.0-290.0, p = 0.013] in non-surgical controls). VCE completion was high in this small altered-anatomy cohort, with no observed adverse events. More frequent inadequate visualization and longer observed SB transit times warrant further investigation, accounting for surgical anatomy and capsule delivery method.
authors: Tamar Thurm; Nimrod Akerman; Shai Meron Eldar; Mati Shnell; Oren Shibolet; Liat Deutsch

title: Vulvar Crohn's disease in children: Diagnostic challenges and therapeutic implications from a literature review
abstract: Vulvar Crohn's disease (CD) is a rare and frequently under-recognised extraintestinal manifestation in children and may precede gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to significant diagnostic delays. We report the case of a 13-year-old girl with a 3-year history of chronic vulvar swelling, erythema, and fissures, initially misdiagnosed despite extensive investigations. Vulvar biopsy ultimately revealed non-caseating granulomatous dermatitis consistent with metastatic CD, and a subsequent endoscopic evaluation confirmed colonic CD. Due to severe and refractory vulvar involvement, treatment with anti-tumour necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) therapy was required, with dose intensification necessary to achieve disease control. Furthermore, we performed a narrative review of the literature and identified 56 paediatric cases of vulvar CD. In most patients, vulvar manifestations preceded the diagnosis of intestinal disease and were frequently independent of gastrointestinal disease activity. Vulvar swelling was the most common presentation, often painless and isolated. Diagnosis was based on a combination of clinical, endoscopic, radiological, and histological findings. Gastrointestinal evaluation played a central role, while pelvic magnetic resonance imaging was essential to exclude contiguous fistulising disease. Vulvar biopsy was performed in most cases but may not be required when CD is confirmed endoscopically and alternative diagnoses have been excluded. Reported treatment ranged from topical therapies and antibiotics to systemic immunomodulators and biologics, with frequent need for escalation to anti-TNF-α therapy in refractory cases. Early recognition and a multidisciplinary approach are essential to prevent irreversible tissue damage and optimise long-term outcomes in affected children.
authors: Silvana Ancona; Matilde Tagliabue; Rosaria Celano; Francesca Laura Boggio; Veronica Boero; Francesca Musto; Giulia Naspi Catassi; Giulia D’Arcangelo; Marina Aloi
venue: Journal of Pediatric Gastroenterology and Nutrition

title: Waveguided, Self‐Sensing Sheath–Core Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fiber Actuators
abstract: Soft actuators capable of operating in confined and hard-to-access environments, while providing integrated self-sensing capabilities, are highly desired for next-generation robotic systems. Here we report a waveguided sheath-core optical fiber actuator consisting of a liquid crystal elastomer core encased in a conductive sheath of carbon nanotubes/carbon black. Near-infrared light guided through the fiber actuator drives reversible contractions of up to 38% and enables a load-bearing capacity of up to 320 times the actuator's own weight. Arrays of these fibers enable independent optical addressing of individual actuators, allowing programmable multimodal gripping in confined environments. The conductive sheath simultaneously serves as a strain sensor, providing real-time monitoring of actuation states via changes in resistance. By integrating photothermal actuation and self-sensing into a single fiber architecture, this work establishes a multifunctional platform for soft robotic systems operating in spatially confined environments.
authors: Hailong Wei; Cheng Zhou; Zhoutao Li; Zhixin Wang; 高福廷; Yuwei Tian; S.H. Chon; Hyun Kim; Ye Xiao; Guanggui Cheng; Zhongqiang Zhang; Xinghao Hu

title: When Every Test Fails: Multifocal Grade 1 Ileal Neuroendocrine Tumors Causing Transfusion-Dependent Obscure Overt Gastrointestinal Bleeding.
abstract: Small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) rarely present as obscure overt gastrointestinal bleeding (OGIB), causing significant diagnostic challenges. We report a 56-year-old man who presented with OGIB that required approximately 50 units of packed red blood cells during a 6-week hospitalization. Multimodal evaluation, including computed tomography angiography, tagged red blood cell scan, video capsule endoscopy, computed tomography enterography, provocative mesenteric angiography, balloon enteroscopy, and octreotide scan, failed to identify a source. Exploratory laparotomy identified 3 mid-ileal nodules with histopathology revealing well-differentiated grade 1 neuroendocrine tumors. Bleeding resolved following resection. This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic role of surgical exploration in refractory OGIB.
authors: James Mo; Suraj Suresh

title: When dentists explain with AI: an exploratory study on patients’ attitudes after clinician-mediated AI-assisted panoramic radiograph communication
abstract: Objectives To evaluate patients’ immediate attitudes after dentist-mediated communication of AI-assisted panoramic radiographic findings, including their willingness to accept an AI-only diagnosis. Materials and Methods In this exploratory observational study, adult patients (≥18 years) who required dental treatment planning were first informed of their diagnosis using panoramic radiographs as part of the conventional explanation. Afterward, the same radiographic findings and treatment plan were explained with the assistance of AI-based segmentation and diagnostic support software. Participants were then surveyed using a 12-item Likert-type questionnaire developed to assess their immediate attitudes and concerns following the AI-assisted explanation. Descriptive statistics were calculated, and exploratory associations with age, sex, and educational level were examined using Spearman correlation coefficients (α = 0.05). Results Fifty-two patients participated. Items related to perceived understanding, confidence, quality of care, and speed of care received high scores (medians 10). Most participants were unwilling to accept an AI-only diagnosis without the involvement of a qualified professional (median 1). Concern about potential increases in treatment costs was substantial (median 10), whereas concerns about data privacy were comparatively low in this immediate clinical context (median 1). No statistically significant correlations were found between survey responses and age, sex, or educational level. Conclusions After experiencing a clinician-mediated AI-assisted panoramic radiograph explanation, patients were generally favorable toward AI as a supportive tool. The main perceived benefits were better communication, confidence, and perceived quality of care. Participants rejected AI-only decision-making and expressed concern about the potential financial impact of AI use in dental care. Clinical significance These preliminary findings are relevant for a patient-centered, clinician-supervised implementation of AI in dental imaging communication, emphasizing potential communication benefits, human oversight, transparency, and careful management of financial implications in dental practice.
authors: Julio Ruiz Marrara; Thais Cristina da Cunha Vitareli; João Donato Bauman; Marcelo José Palma‐Fernandes; Hugo Gaêta‐Araujo; Paulo Melo; Alessandra Alaniz Macedo; Camila Tirapelli

title: When endoscopy is not required: reducing low value care for more sustainable endoscopy - European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) Position Statement Update 2026 recycling ESGE published guidelines and position statements.
abstract:
Background

The European Society of Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ESGE) published its first Position Statement on digestive conditions that do not require endoscopy in 2020. Since then, multiple ESGE guidelines have expanded recommendations that promote appropriate indications, de-escalation of surveillance, and evidence-based avoidance of low value procedures. In parallel, avoiding unnecessary endoscopy has emerged as a major strategy for reducing the environmental burden of gastrointestinal endoscopy. This updated Position Statement consolidates such ESGE recommendations into a practical framework defining when endoscopy is not required.

Methods

This Position Statement is based exclusively on recommendations developed or endorsed by ESGE. Recommendations from ESGE Guidelines and Position Statements published in Endoscopy were systematically reviewed and synthesized. Positive recommendations advocating alternative management strategies were reformulated, where appropriate, into explicit "do not perform endoscopy" statements without modifying the underlying evidence or recommendation strength. The resulting document provides a clinically oriented synthesis rather than new guideline recommendations.

Results

Recommendations covering upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy, endoscopic ultrasound, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, capsule endoscopy, and therapeutic endoscopy were identified. Across these modalities, four overarching scenarios emerged in which endoscopy is not required: screening when endoscopy does not meaningfully prevent disease incidence or improve relevant outcomes; surveillance when repeat endoscopy provides no additional benefit beyond an adequate index examination or when expected benefit is limited by age, co-morbidity, or life expectancy; diagnostic endoscopy when validated noninvasive strategies provide sufficient information or when endoscopic findings are unlikely to change management; and therapeutic endoscopy when intervention does not improve clinically relevant outcomes compared with conservative or alternative management. Additional principles include avoiding redundant investigations and unnecessary repetition of adequately performed procedures. Together, these recommendations provide a framework for reducing low value endoscopy while limiting patient burden, healthcare resource use, and environmental impact.

Conclusions

An appropriate indication is the cornerstone of high quality endoscopy and the primary driver of sustainable endoscopic practice. Endoscopy should be avoided when it does not provide meaningful additional benefit in screening, surveillance, diagnosis, or therapy. Applying these principles can improve patient safety, optimize healthcare resources, and reduce the environmental footprint of endoscopy. This updated ESGE Position Statement provides an evidence-based framework for high value, patient-centered, and sustainable endoscopic practice.

title: When the Gut Speaks, the Liver Listens: Pathogenesis, Diagnostic Spectrum, and Artificial Intelligence Guided Interventions in Colitis-Driven Hepatopathies
abstract: About 5% of people with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) eventually develop clinically severe, chronic liver disease, even though up to 50% of patients have temporary hepatobiliary alterations, and up to 30% have abnormal liver biochemistries.Colitis-associated liver disorders (CALD) range from transitory rises in liver enzymes to serious, life-threatening conditions such as primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).Currently available diagnostic criteria for gut-associated liver disorders are limited due to the complexity and bidirectional nature of the gut-liver axis.Large-duct PSC is primarily diagnosed by magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP), but liver biopsy is especially recommended to confirm potential PSC-autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) overlap syndromes and diagnosis of small-duct variations in the context of a normal MRCP.These methods contain sampling errors, lack interobserver variability, and have limited sensitivity to pre-symptomatic changes.Thus, the standard of care available to date is primarily palliative rather than curative.Modern biologic treatments are effective for colonic inflammation, but they don't always alter the course of liver disease.The prevailing treatments for the above-mentioned disorders (e.g., ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), immunosuppressants, or metabolic stabilizers) are often ineffective against fibrotic progression.This review evaluates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in tackling these challenges.Highly effective AI-enhanced diagnostics and therapeutic pipeline, focusing on computational models and multi-omic integration, has also been discussed.
authors: Roobee Garla; Tanvi Sharma; Monika Sharma; Naveen Kaushal

title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
abstract: Coding agents built to repair software now write, test, and repair programs for robots, laboratories, and industrial controllers. Unlike in software engineering, no test suite comes with the code. Whether a program works must be established by running it on a robot, in a physics simulator, or through the policies it helps to train, and such evidence is costly to obtain and can itself be wrong. As these agents take on more physical tasks, how their programs are judged matters as much as how they are written. This paper examines this emerging area, agentic intelligence for the physical world, by treating the world as the program's test suite. We organize the discussion around three questions: how agents write programs for the physical world, how these programs are tested, and how agents learn from the results. We first trace how language models for robots and software engineering agents came together, ask which software testing practices carry over to physical tests, and describe each program by where it sits relative to the actuator and by what judges it. For writing, we cover programs that act as robot policies and programs that support policy learning by producing rewards, tasks, and training worlds. For testing, we examine what physical trials cost, what traces, learned judges, simulators, and formal checks can establish in their place, and what safety requires beyond task success. For learning, we discuss how tested programs are retained as experience, in skill libraries and in model weights. Finally, we turn to benchmarks and evaluation practice and outline open challenges. Writing programs is becoming cheap, while trustworthy evidence about what they do remains costly. Progress will therefore depend on a physical counterpart of continuous integration: verification cheap enough to run often, reliable enough to trust under search, and maintained alongside the experience it validates.
authors: Kaixin Li; Meng Luo; Yanlin Li; Yuchen Tian; Xiang Liu; Xiangru Jian; Yan Yang; Zhiheng Xi; Yang Zhang; Ziyang Luo; Mingfei Cheng; Hongzhan Lin

title: Where to Predict in Retinal OCT? Anatomy-Guided Target Selection for I-JEPA
abstract: Self-supervised learning aims to learn meaningful representations from unlabeled data, potentially allowing models to capture subtle anatomical variations across patients and reduce the amount of labeled data needed. Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA) learns by predicting target-region representations from visible context rather than reconstructing pixels. However, its uniform target placement does not account for the anatomical structure of retinal OCT, where retinal tissue occupies only part of each B-scan. We investigate anatomy-guided target selection using image intensity and predicted retinal segmentation while retaining the I-JEPA architecture and latent prediction objective. We compare anatomy-guided rectangular targets, anatomy-shaped targets and coverage-constrained placement with uniform masking, and evaluate the learned representations using linear probing for glaucoma classification on FairVision. We found that rectangular targets guided by image intensity achieved the highest linear-probe AUC in our comparisons. We show that anatomically meaningful target selection is promising for retinal OCT representation learning, while greater anatomical specificity did not consistently improve performance.
authors: Yunchu Feng; Wai Tak Lau; Kaveri A. Thakoor

title: sqrtVINS-Based 360 Visual-Inertial SLAM Systems: Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 Entry
abstract: This report describes our submission to the 2026 Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge. The system is a 360-camera visual-inertial pipeline that uses only the provided dual-fisheye image streams and IMU measurements. First, raw images are preprocessed with low-light enhancement and static/dynamic masking, and then fed into a $\sqrt{\text{VINS}}$ frontend as the local odometry, with deep learning-based SuperPoint features, ELSED line segments, and LightGlue matching. The resulting trajectory is refined using a GTSAM-based backend that performs tightly-coupled factor graph optimization with SALAD global descriptor and visual bundle adjustment (BA). The backend performs local-to-global structureless BA, tightly regularized intrinsic and extrinsic refinement, and global scale adjustment supported by the known inter-camera baseline and cross-view constraints. The design targets long indoor sequences with dark regions, repetitive corridors, dynamic objects, and limited geometric parallax, while keeping the pipeline reproducible in the provided ROS2 workspace. Fig. 1 demonstrates that our proposed method aligns well with the floorplan across several indoor sequences.
authors: Jungwoo Lee; Hogyun Kim; Jiwon Choi; Jinyong Jeong; Younggun Cho

title: “Integration of Embedded AI and Medical Heat Pipes in Robotic Neurosurgery: A Novel Framework Based on Elmas’s Thermodynamic Theory”
abstract: Objective: This study presents an interdisciplinary framework that autonomizes the thermal management of high-temperature laser ablation and ultra-low-temperature cryoprobe applications, which represent opposing thermal poles in robotic neurosurgery operations. The thermal sensitivity of neural tissues and the risk of permanent neuron damage developing at temperatures above 43°C necessitate a micron-level stable thermal control. Accordingly, the study aims to optimize surgical robots both in terms of hardware and software. Method: The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the principles of “ELMAS’s Thermodynamic Theory”, the “5th Law of Thermodynamics”, and “Bio-Robotic Resonance” developed by Asst. Prof. Dr. Emin Taner Elmas. In the hardware layer, dual-phase medical heat pipes integrated into the tip of the robotic arm (end-effector), having a diameter of 0.8 mm, flexible, and containing sintered copper powder micro-capillaries with water-graphene nano-fluid, were utilized. In the software layer, an embedded artificial intelligence (AI) engine supported by machine learning models was developed, capable of real-time data processing from micro-sensors on the heat pipe and performing digital twin-based live thermal mapping (HUD). The validation of the system was designed with a 5-step validation protocol encompassing computerized thermal modeling, synthetic gel tests, ex-vivo organ tests, in-vivo animal experiments, and preclinical human simulation. Findings: The integration of the micro-heat pipe provided passive cooling without requiring an external energy source, thereby suppressing peripheral heat dissipation (thermal dissipation) during laser operations and maintaining healthy neural tissues within a stable range of 37°C - 38°C. In cryoprobe applications, it acted as a passive heat barrier, creating reverse thermal gradients along the probe shaft, protecting healthy tissues along the entry path while performing instantaneous shock freezing cycles (freeze-thaw) at the target tumor site. The predictive algorithms of the AI engine predicted the thermal saturation at the tissue border milliseconds in advance and successfully activated the haptic lock (fail-safe) mechanism that applies resistance to the surgeon’s master control arms at critical thresholds. Conclusion: The developed autonomous thermal management architecture elevates surgical robots beyond being merely devices that produce mechanical motion into intelligent protective shields that thermally sense the tissue. The integration of Dr. Elmas’s medical thermodynamics equations into robotic software demonstrates at a preclinical level that a micron-level precise, autonomous, and thermally safe hybrid surgical platform can be established for brain tumor resections. [1-111]
authors: Emin Taner ELMAS
venue: Biomedical Journal of Scientific & Technical Research

title: 3D just-in-time modelling of real-time volumetric tissue deformation for ultrasound-guided percutaneous surgery
abstract: Real-time prediction of tissue deformation is essential for interactive ultrasound-guided percutaneous surgery simulation, but high-fidelity physics-based models often exceed practical online computational limits. This paper presents a 3D Just-in-Time (JIT) modelling framework for real-time prediction of volumetric tissue deformation during ultrasound-guided percutaneous procedures. An offline historical database of needle insertion poses and corresponding volumetric deformation fields is generated using a simulation engine. During runtime, the proposed method retrieves a gated neighbourhood of geometrically similar insertions, computes curvature-aware constrained interpolation weights, and predicts the deformation field in a reduced output space obtained through principal component analysis (PCA). The full volumetric displacement field is then reconstructed and used to deform a baseline ultrasound volume for slice extraction. Across the tested grid resolutions, the proposed PCA-JIT framework achieved millisecond-scale prediction times and is up to 90 times faster than the simulation engine used to generate the database. Prediction errors remained low across all tested mesh resolutions, and the predicted fields enabled deformation-consistent B-mode slice rendering from arbitrarily posed imaging planes. The proposed framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient surrogate for volumetric tissue deformation prediction and is well suited for interactive surgical simulation, ultrasound-based training, and future image-guided intervention systems.
authors: Kian Zalzalah; Carlos Rossa

title: A COMPLEX MÜLLERIAN ANOMALY MISDIAGNOSED AS FIBROID UTERUS: A CASE REPORT
abstract: We report a 47-year-old woman who had never been pregnant and had suffered from primary infertility. She also had chronic pelvic pain and irregular menstrual periods. She had several uterine abnormalities, including a complete septate uterus, a duplicated cervix, and a longitudinal vaginal septum, with primary infertility. Her diagnosis included a large endometrial polyp and submucosal fibroids in the uterine cavity. This has been reported in only a few cases. The ultrasound diagnosis revealed a single uterine body with a single endometrial cavity and uterine fibroids but missed other diagnoses of two separate cervical canals, a double cervix, or separate vaginal canals, and a large endometrial polyp. The patient opted for definitive treatment and declined fertility preservation, leading to a total abdominal hysterectomy and removal of the uterine corpus, both cervices, and the vaginal septum. She was discharged five days after surgery and recovered. There are three clinical aspects to this case. First, imaging techniques (ultrasonography and MRI) should be used to diagnose and classify atypical Müllerian duct anomalies (MDAs) before applying a classification system. Second, in hysteroscopic septal resection, treatment should be individualized based on age, disease severity, and reproductive status. For younger women who wish to conceive, hysteroscopic septal resection is generally the most appropriate option, and hysterectomy is usually the last resort for suitable candidates. Finally, a multidisciplinary approach is necessary to deal with congenital anomalies that are complicated by acquired uterine pathologies. The diagnostic and surgical plan is required for such a patient to achieve optimal outcomes.
authors: Dil Sahi Roka; Priyanka Gharti Magar; Krishna Kumar Sah; Sandeep Shrestha; Lijing Liu

title: A Decade After the Trauma: An Incarcerated Chronic Post-traumatic Diaphragmatic Hernia as a Cause of Acute Abdomen
abstract: Traumatic diaphragmatic hernia is an infrequent complication of thoracoabdominal trauma, and its diagnosis is often delayed because of the absence of specific signs in the acute phase. We report a 44-year-old man with a history of penetrating chest trauma from a stab wound 10 years earlier, managed with bilateral chest tube placement, who presented with severe colicky left hypochondrial pain of eight hours’ duration radiating to the back. Abdominal ultrasound suggested non-obstructive left nephrolithiasis, and urological evaluation led to a non-contrast CT of the urinary tract (pyelo-CT protocol), which instead showed a simple left renal cyst and, as an incidental finding, a left diaphragmatic hernia with protrusion of the splenic flexure of the colon and omental fat through a 22-mm defect. With suspected incarceration and risk of strangulation, urgent left posterolateral thoracotomy was performed 22 hours after symptom onset. Firm adhesions of the hernial sac to the pleura and lung were released, but the contents could not be reduced even after enlarging the defect with a 2-cm longitudinal phrenotomy (final defect 4 cm); the sac was opened and a partial omentectomy was performed, which allowed reduction and confirmed incarceration. The colonic segment was viable, so no bowel resection was required. The sac was resected, and the diaphragm was repaired by primary two-layer closure reinforced with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) pledgets. The patient recovered without complications, was discharged on hospital day five, and showed no recurrence on a chest radiograph at one year. This case shows that delayed traumatic diaphragmatic hernia should remain in the differential diagnosis of acute abdominal pain in patients with a history of penetrating thoracoabdominal trauma, however remote, and that timely surgery can preserve bowel viability.
authors: Alexa Maria Castro Mendoza; Julio Alexandru Zapata Vega

title: A European algorithm and strategy for management of chronic postoperative inguinal pain (EurA-CPIP)
abstract: Background: Chronic postoperative inguinal pain (CPIP) is a disabling complication affecting 8%-17% of all patients after inguinal hernia repair. It is a complex pain condition with several pathophysiological mechanisms involved, including neuropathic pain, inflammation, and mechanical effects (e.g., mesh or scar tissue). Management remains inconsistent, probably due to limited high-quality evidence, heterogeneous approach, and insufficient standardisation of outcomes. This study aimed to develop EurA-CPIP, a multidisciplinary treatment algorithm and prospective data-collection platform designed to support consistent phenotyping, step-up management, and standardised outcomes across centres, creating an iterative platform for future hypothesis-driven research and multicentre trials. Methods: An international multidisciplinary working group from European tertiary referral centres developed the European Algorithm and Strategy for Management of Chronic Postoperative Inguinal Pain (EurA-CPIP). Development was informed by the evidence synthesis underpinning the updated international HerniaSurge guidelines and a critical appraisal of previously published CPIP algorithms. A pragmatic step-up algorithm was designed, integrating pharmacological, interventional, surgical and supportive treatments, with prospective outcome registration and planned data-driven revision on a regular basis. Results: EurA-CPIP provides a multidisciplinary algorithm with entry at multiple levels depending on prior treatment attempts. The concept is to begin and, if needed, advance from conservative measures such as systemic medication and topical therapy, to more invasive treatments such as trigger point injections, and ultrasound-guided nerve blocks; predefined investigational add-ons (radiofrequency, cryoneurolysis, botulinum toxin A) are embedded after documented block response. Multidisciplinary team review precedes escalation to more invasive interventions such as surgery. A supportive and rehabilitative coping trajectory is integrated early on. Standardised outcomes include patient-reported pain outcomes, functional impairment, psychological factors, analgesic use, and patient global impression of improvement. Conclusion: EurA-CPIP is a pragmatic consensus-based strategy intended to harmonise and improve specialised CPIP care while utilising existing and developing emerging therapies. Future research should investigate pathophysiology and intervention effects within this step-up algorithm.
authors: K. G. Andersen; T. W. K. van der Meer; Nadine van Veenendaal; N. B. Foss; M. J. A. Loos; M. Miserez; M. Pawlak; R. M. H. Roumen; T. Naddaf; M. Togsverd-Bo; M. W. Stadeager; E. K. Aasvang; Willem A. R. Zwaans

title: A Multi‐Axis Plantar Load Measurement Platform for the Assessment of Foot Disorders: Comparison of Patients With Psoriatic Arthritis to a Healthy Control Cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate assessment of plantar loading, including shear forces, is crucial for understanding foot pathologies such as dactylitis in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Existing devices predominantly measure plantar pressures, neglecting important shear stresses which may initiate dactylitis. This study presents a novel multi-axis plantar load measurement platform to address this gap. METHODS: The study utilised a newly developed plantar load measurement system, comprising a Hall-effect-based magnetic sensing array, custom data logging electronics, and tailored data processing software. The system's efficacy was evaluated in a pilot feasibility study involving patients with PsA with no, current, or previous dactylitis, and healthy controls. Participants walked barefoot on the platform, capturing plantar shear and pressure data. FINDINGS: Shear stresses were notably higher in the second to fourth rays compared to other regions, particularly in the left foot, aligning with the hypothesis that repetitive local trauma might initiate dactylitis in PsA. However, no consistent differences in stresses were observed between diagnostic groups, likely due to small sample sizes and gait alterations associated with pain. A marked asymmetry was observed between the right and left feet, suggesting dominant-foot placement effects. INTERPRETATION: The new platform demonstrates potential clinical utility in capturing comprehensive foot-loading profiles, including critical shear stresses previously under-assessed. Although the current pilot study was limited in number, the results support the theory that local mechanical stresses may contribute to PsA-related dactylitis. Future larger-scale studies are needed to clarify these findings and overcome limitations related to altered gait patterns due to foot pain.
authors: D. A. Jones; Lefan Wang; Max Houghton; Jennifer Jones; Richard A. Wilkins; Heidi J. Siddle; Graham Chapman; Ali Alazmani; Peter Culmer; Philip Helliwell
venue: Journal of Foot and Ankle Research

title: A Performance Comparison of Forcemyography and Electromyography in Muscle Force Estimation for Human–Machine Interfaces
abstract: The recording of muscle force can be used to control Human–Machine Interfaces (HMIs). A commonly used estimator of muscle force is the envelope of Electromyography (EMG) signals, which requires proper EMG processing. A potentially more convenient alternative is offered by Forcemyography (FMG), which records muscle mechanical activity and inherently provides a signal that is a good estimator of muscle force, without specific processing. This study aimed to compare the performances of EMG and FMG in muscle force estimation aimed at HMI control. Ten healthy subjects performed 15 gradual and 15 rapid isometric biceps brachii contractions at approximately 90° elbow flexion. Force measured at wrist by a load cell, and FMG and EMG signals were recorded simultaneously. Causal root-mean-square EMG envelopes (EMG-RMS) were computed offline using windows of 100, 250, 500, and 1000 ms. For each participant and contraction type, subject-specific sigmoidal regression models were fitted using normalized signals from the first 10 contractions and evaluated on the remaining five held-out contractions. Performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R2), root mean squared error (RMSE), and maximum absolute error (MaAE), with paired Wilcoxon tests and Bonferroni correction. Cross-correlation quantified temporal alignment with the reference force. FMG achieved higher mean R2 and lower mean RMSE and MaAE across all tested configurations. Statistical analyses on the errors revealed that FMG achieved performance comparable to that of EMG-RMS in gradual muscle contractions and significantly superior performance in rapid muscle contractions. These findings support FMG-based external force estimation with simpler pre-processing and provide preliminary evidence for future implementation and validation in muscle-controlled HMIs, assistive exoskeletons, and rehabilitation devices.
authors: Jessica Centracchio; Salvatore J. Parlato; Emilio Andreozzi; Eliana Cinotti; Paolo Bifulco; Gaetano Dario Gargiulo; Daniele Esposito

title: A Standardized Chewable Conductive Hydrogel Sensor for Direct Monitoring of Masticatory Dynamics
abstract: Chewing is a fundamental orofacial function closely related to nutrition, digestion, and quality of life, yet current assessment methods generally rely on indirect signals or endpoint measurements and provide limited process‐level information. Here, a hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC)/polyacrylamide (PAM) conductive hydrogel is developed as a standardized chewable sensor that integrates the test substrate with force‐to‐electrical signal transduction, enabling direct monitoring of masticatory dynamics. The sensor captures chewing frequency, relative force response, chewing duration, relative force response variability, and rhythm variability during standardized tests. Using predefined chewing‐state labels, these features were integrated into a classification framework, with KNN achieving 98.0% accuracy in recording‐level cross‐validation and 76.7% in nested leave‐one‐participant‐out validation, providing an initial assessment of generalizability to unseen participants. The hydrogel exhibits a compressive strength of 2.3 MPa, toughness of 287 kJ m − 3 , a response time of 150 ms, recovery within 173 ms, and less than 3% signal attenuation over 150 cycles. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) encapsulation supports stable intraoral operation and biocompatibility. This work establishes a proof‐of‐concept platform for standardized acquisition and analysis of process‐resolved chewing data, offering a route toward objective, data‐driven assessment of masticatory function and, with larger population datasets, personalized oral rehabilitation and healthcare decision‐making.
authors: Xiaoxuan Xue; Zhan Gao; Jun Wang; Yizhang Yang; Kewei Zhang; Chao Yang

title: A Unique Case of PPP1R12A ‐Related Urogenital and Brain Malformation Syndrome Phenotypically Overlapping With VACTERL Association, With Additional Literature Review of Previously Described Phenotypes
abstract: PPP1R12A-related urogenital and brain malformation syndrome (UBMS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in PPP1R12A, which encodes a regulatory subunit of myosin phosphatase. We report a 46,XY male with a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant in PPP1R12A, c.2629del (p.S877Pfs*38). He presented with features consistent with UBMS, including bilateral cryptorchidism, Müllerian duct remnants, tracheoesophageal fistula, anal atresia, and global developmental delay. Notably, he exhibited cardiac anomalies and hepatic cirrhosis not previously reported in individuals with PPP1R12A-related UBMS, including bilateral pulmonary artery hypoplasia and mitral valve prolapse; however, a causal relationship between these findings and the PPP1R12A variant has not been established. His presentation also has significant overlap with VACTERL association. This case reinforces the association between PPP1R12A dysfunction and complex urogenital and gastrointestinal malformations while expanding the phenotypic spectrum to include novel cardiac and hepatic findings. Collectively, these findings raise the possibility of an expanded phenotypic spectrum associated with PPP1R12A-related disease, though additional data is needed to determine whether all associated features are attributable to the variant.
authors: Elliot Horn; Michał Kołodziejski; Evangelia Kalaitzoglou; Amanda F Buchanan; Douglas Schneider; Juliann Paige Matheny
venue: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A

title: A handheld tool for Young’s modulus characterization of soft materials: towards point-of-care tissue assessment
abstract: Palpation is a rapid and widely used physical examination technique for assessing tissue characteristics and guiding decisions about further imaging procedures. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on clinician experience, making standardized interpretation difficult. This paper presents SensoPal, a portable palpation-based system for quantitative non-invasive tissue stiffness assessment through measurement of the temporal and spatial Young’s modulus of soft materials. SensoPal integrates a handheld device with a miniature load cell and magnetometer, alongside a low-cost camera for position tracking, enabling the generation of spatial stiffness maps. User studies demonstrated Young’s modulus measurement accuracy of approximately ~ 87% (±4%) and repeatability of approximately ~ 86% (±4%). In localization tasks with flat silicone phantoms containing rigid nodules, stiffness maps identified deep-seated nodules undetectable through touch alone. Experiments on curved biofidelic phantoms with soft nodules demonstrated the system’s ability to capture spatial stiffness variations under realistic low-contrast conditions. SensoPal also distinguished compliant nodules embedded beyond depths of 8 mm, where manual detection became increasingly difficult. These findings establish SensoPal as a reliable, low-cost platform for quantitative tissue characterization in point-of-care diagnostics, telemedicine, and patient self-assessment.
authors: Saitarun Nadipineni; Mohamed A. Thaha; Kaspar A. Althoefer; Thilina Dulantha Lalitharatne

title: A responsivity theory of call timing patterns in bat echolocation.
abstract:
Background

The temporal patterning of bat echolocation is extensively characterised, but a general mathematical account linking call timing to acoustic propagation, relative motion, and behaviourally selected information remains incomplete.

Results

We present the responsivity framework, which represents each call event as a delayed active-sensing cycle comprising an acoustic acquisition interval and a subsequent behavioural interval. Their proportional relation is described by the responsivity coefficient, kr , connecting call timing to effective anchor distance, relative velocity, call duration, and the selected echo window. Analytical derivation, call-by-call simulation, internal validation, and comparison with field recordings show how the framework generates hyperbolic call-rate-distance relationships, shifts approach timing with echo-window selection, and places the terminal buzz at the near-target limit of the same timing process. Responsivity and kinematics have separable terminal effects: kr constrains terminal update density and attainable call rate, whereas closing velocity determines the time available within the terminal region. A buzz-readiness state precedes the complete expression of buzz, and transient sonar strobe groups emerge under multi-target anchor allocation without an explicit grouping rule. Field recordings show broad correspondence with simulations in the organisation of movement, call timing and call duration, and illustrate conditional evaluation of acquisition-window and anchor assumptions.

Conclusions

Responsivity theory provides a process-based descriptor of echolocation timing and a diagnostic framework for hypothesis generation and empirical testing. The framework identifies the measurements needed to test how selected acoustic information governs subsequent call timing.
authors: Umadi R, Firzlaff U.

title: AI-Powered Personal Tutors as a Scalable Solution to the 2-Sigma Problem in Pharmacy Education
abstract: Background: The “2 Sigma Problem”, where individualized tutoring outperforms conventional instruction by two standard deviations, remains a persistent challenge in large-enrollment pharmacy courses. Generative AI tutors, constrained to instructor-verified content, offer a scalable, equitable approximation of personalized support. Methods: Four course-specific AI tutors were deployed across first-year (P1; n = 108–119/cohort) and third-year (P3; n = 98–108/cohort) Doctor of Pharmacy cohorts (Fall 2024–Spring 2026) using ChatGPT-4o and PlayLab with retrieval-augmented generation. Effectiveness was evaluated through longitudinal grade analysis, American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy proficiency outcomes, satisfaction surveys, and anonymized interaction log analysis. Results: Engagement was heterogeneous across curricular formats: 15-week P1 courses supported sustained weekly usage for foundational concept reinforcement, whereas 4-week P3 modules exhibited lower, targeted utilization focused on rapid self-assessment. In P1 Biochemistry, tutor integration was associated with longitudinal cohort exam improvements. The overall targeted metabolism exam mean rose from 74.0% (Fall 2023, no AI) to 81.4% (Fall 2024, AI tutor) and 83.6% (Fall 2025, AI tutor), with active users (n = 16, 85%, Fall 2024) outperforming non-users (n = 16, 79.3%, Fall 2024) by 5.7 percentage points, and with higher mean scores observed across progressively higher usage tiers. AACP proficiency means increased from 77.9% to 82.1%, exceeding the 80% benchmark. In P1 Physiology and P3 modules, cohort performance remained consistently high (83.7–88.2%), maintaining AACP benchmark proficiency across all observation cycles. Student perceptions were positive regarding conceptual clarification and adaptive explanations. Conclusions: Curriculum-aligned AI tutors represent a viable strategy for approximating individualized instruction in pharmacy courses. Course-specific AI tutors demonstrate feasibility across PharmD curricula, functioning as continuous retrieval-practice tools in foundational sciences and as targeted self-assessment aids in accelerated modules. Educational benefits and adoption dynamics are moderated by curricular pace, subject complexity, and assessment structures, highlighting key considerations for broader health sciences implementation.
authors: Maria Victoria Tejada-Simon

title: Abnormal behavior perception in elderly care scenarios based on multimodal generative adversarial networks
abstract: In view of the limitations of the existing elderly care anomaly perception methods, which mostly rely on single visual mode and shallow stitching multi-source sensing features, such as insufficient accuracy of long-time progressive anomaly recognition, easy mode collapse of multimodal training, and insufficient utilization of non visual sensing information, this paper proposes a multimodal wgan GP anomaly perception method combining CNN-LSTM spatio-temporal double branch coding. The framework integrates five kinds of heterogeneous sensor data, including vision, inertial IMU, bed pressure, physiological signs and environmental audio, and adaptively allocates the weight of each mode to complete the cross modal feature alignment based on the dual attention of space and time; The shared generator based on the fusion of spatial and temporal two-way sub generators only learns the distribution of normal behavior, and uses multimodal attention discriminator to distinguish the true and false features; Wgan GP gradient penalty and modal imbalance correction item were introduced to stabilize the confrontation training, and the weighted reconstruction error and discriminant confidence were fused to construct a joint abnormal score. Four core abnormalities, including falling, falling out of bed, long-term wandering and physiological index disorder, were identified by dynamic threshold. The experimental results show that the AUC roc of the complete model in this paper can reach 0.978 ± 0.003, the F1 score is 95.64 ± 0.47%, the false positive rate is 2.13 ± 0.24%, and the false negative rate is 3.05 ± 0.30%; Ablation experiments showed that F1 score decreased significantly after removing inertia, bed pressure or audio modes, which confirmed that such non visual modes had complementary contributions to information, and the complete model had stronger scene adaptability and engineering landing value.
authors: Xinbo Zhao

title: Accelerator-based BNCT as a drug–device regimen: system engineering, clinical evidence, and regulatory considerations
abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is a binary, tumor-selective radiotherapy modality that combines preferential delivery of boron-10 to tumor tissue with neutron irradiation to generate high-linear energy transfer particles in situ . The field has undergone a defining transition from reactor-based neutron sources to accelerator-based BNCT (AB-BNCT), enabling hospital-based deployment, broader clinical translation, and renewed global interest in indications with substantial unmet needs, particularly recurrent head and neck cancers and gliomas. However, AB-BNCT is intrinsically a drug–device regimen, requiring coordinated evaluation of the boron agent, neutron irradiation system, and dedicated treatment planning software, supported by end-to-end quality management, commissioning and routine quality assurance, and postmarket surveillance. This review summarizes the system-engineering foundations and current global landscape of AB-BNCT. We outline the therapeutic principle and key subsystems, including accelerator neutron sources, beam shaping assembly, patient positioning and setup, beam/dose monitoring, treatment control, and Monte Carlo–based BNCT treatment planning. We synthesize clinical evidence from reactor-era feasibility studies, accelerator-era registration programs, and emerging real-world evidence, including the Japanese Phase II registration study reporting an objective response rate of 71.4% in patients with unresectable recurrent or locally advanced head and neck cancer and subsequent nationwide postmarketing evidence. We also compare regulatory classification and approval pathways across the European Union, United States, Japan, and China. Finally, we discuss regulatory considerations relevant to the evaluation of BNCT devices in China. Continued advances in boron agents, accelerator engineering, and standardization, together with accumulated regulatory experience, may support broader clinical implementation of AB-BNCT. Further accumulation of evidence integrating beam physics, dosimetry, and clinical outcomes may facilitate cross-jurisdictional understanding and the continued clinical development of AB-BNCT.
authors: Zehua Wang; Yue Wang; Yan Jiang; Qing Zhang; Xiaofang Gu; Lu Liu

title: Acupuncture Needle-Based Biosensors: Interface Engineering, Sensing Strategies, and Applications
abstract: Acupuncture needles, conventionally employed as therapeutic tools in Chinese medicine, have emerged as compelling substrates for constructing minimally invasive sensing platforms. Acupuncture needles' unique attributes, including small size, sharp tip geometry, mechanical robustness, biocompatibility, and ease of insertion into tissue, render them attractive for in vivo, real-time monitoring applications. This review provides an overview of the recent advances in acupuncture needle-based biosensors (ANBSs), focusing on three interconnected aspects: interface engineering approaches, sensing strategies, and representative applications. We demonstrate electrochemical and surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS)-based platforms as two principal classes of acupuncture needle-based biosensors, and survey their applications in neurotransmitter monitoring, disease biomarker detection, therapeutic drug monitoring, metabolite profiling, acupoint initiation investigation, as well as environmental contaminant screening and food safety assessment. Finally, we also discuss current challenges, including long-term instability, inadequate active sites, biofouling, signal drift, and insufficient reproducibility, while offering perspectives on future directions such as optimization of materials, miniaturization and multifunction, intelligent sensing strategies and clinical translation proposal. By bridging traditional acupuncture needles and advanced analytical science, this review not only provides a coherent framework for researchers in biosensors but also inspires the next generation of minimally invasive point-of-care diagnostic tools.

title: Adaptive and bioresponsive peptide-functionalized lipid-based nanocarriers for precision nanomedicine
abstract: Lipid-based nanocarriers have emerged as clinically validated platforms for the delivery of drugs, nucleic acids, and proteins, yet their therapeutic performance remains limited by suboptimal biodistribution, cellular uptake, cargo release, and inefficient cytosolic delivery. Peptide functionalization provides versatile strategies to overcome these limitations by combining the structural adaptability of lipid nanocarriers with the programmable functionality of peptides. This review discusses how bioresponsive peptides transform lipid-based nanocarriers from passive drug reservoirs into adaptive therapeutic systems that sense and respond to pathological cues, including dysregulated protease activity, redox imbalance, local or transient pH changes, and disease-associated receptors. We summarize established and emerging strategies for peptide integration, including post-insertion, surface conjugation, and non-covalent peptide–membrane interactions, and discuss how peptide design enables active targeting, receptor recognition, charge switching, conformational activation, and protease-triggered "stealth-to-active" transitions, with particular emphasis on protease-responsive systems. We further highlight peptide-controlled cargo release, multifunctional combination therapies, theranostic platforms, and peptide-enabled strategies to overcome the major bottleneck of endosomal escape through pH-responsive, redox-responsive, enzymatically activated, fusogenic, and coacervate-based mechanisms. Finally, we discuss key translational challenges, including peptide stability, immunogenicity, ligand-density control, scalable manufacturing, colloidal stability, and the need for predictive structure-function relationships. Collectively, peptide-functionalized lipid-based nanocarriers represent a rapidly evolving class of adaptive nanomedicines with broad potential for precision therapeutic delivery.

title: Adductor Longus Tendon Repair and Lengthening for the Treatment of Core Muscle Injury: A Step‐by‐Step Surgical Technique
abstract: Core muscle injury is an increasingly recognized condition that causes groin pain, most commonly in young, active adults. Multiple surgical interventions have been described, including rectus abdominis repair and/or adductor longus lengthening, generally reserved for recalcitrant cases. This article presents a step-by-step guide to an open adductor longus repair and lengthening. By performing an anatomic tendon repair combined with controlled lengthening at the musculotendinous junction, this approach aims to minimize recurrence while providing sustained pain relief.

title: Adsorption-assisted plasmonic enhancement of flutamide detection using AuNPs@rGOPANI nanocomposite films
abstract: Sensitive detection of flutamide (FLT) in aqueous samples remains important for pharmaceutical and environmental monitoring. Here, we developed a label-free surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor based on gold nanoparticles integrated with a reduced graphene oxide–polyaniline film (AuNPs@rGOPANI). The rGOPANI layer provides a chemically diverse interface that can retain FLT through aromatic and polar interactions, while the AuNP-containing structure may strengthen the optical response to changes in the near-surface dielectric environment. FE-SEM analysis of 232 distinguishable nanoparticle features gave an apparent mean diameter of 24.20 ± 3.07 nm. The sensor showed a concentration-dependent, nonlinear resonance-angle shift over the investigated interval of 0.02–200 μM, with a practical detection threshold of 0.02 μM (20 nM) under the tested conditions. Eight mean calibration responses were fitted to Langmuir, Sips, and Freundlich models. The Sips equation provided the lowest root mean square error (0.03047°) and highest coefficient of determination (R 2 = 0.99090), whereas the Freundlich model was favored by the corrected Akaike information criterion, indicating that no single adsorption model could be selected unambiguously from the available data. The sensor responded more strongly to FLT than to the tested inorganic ions, carbohydrates, and beclamide as a structurally related pharmaceutical interferent, retained approximately 78% of its initial response after 30 days, and showed promising performance in river-water spike-recovery experiments. These findings support the potential of AuNPs@rGOPANI as an adsorption-assisted SPR interface for FLT sensing, while emphasizing the need for further replicate-based validation of quantitative performance across the full concentration interval.
