title: Charge‐Transfer‐Engineered Organic/2D Hybrid Interface for Programmable SERS and Emerging Biosensing Applications
abstract: Surface‐enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) enables label‐free molecular fingerprinting with ultra‐high sensitivity and chemical specificity. Yet traditional plasmonic substrates suffer from instability, poor reproducibility, weak molecular selectivity, and limited biocompatibility. Organic/two‐dimensional (2D) hybrid SERS substrates offer a transformative solution in which the tunable energy levels and dipole moments of organic molecules can be systematically matched to the exceptional electronic and excitonic landscape of 2D materials such as TMDCs. This first‐of‐its‐kind systematic framework focuses on how energy‐level alignment, interfacial molecular orientation, and fluorescence quenching govern SERS enhancement. We hierarchically dissect the enhancement mechanisms, identifying interfacial charge transfer and the exciton resonance as the primary drivers, while critically evaluating the secondary roles of molecular dipoles and defect‐induced electromagnetic effects. Key engineering strategies, including heterojunction design, precise thickness control, and functionalization, modulate these pathways to achieve sensitivities that rival plasmonic systems in optimized cases, yet with superior signal uniformity. These mechanistic insights translate into biosensing, where surface wettability, functional groups, and biocompatibility mitigate nonspecific adsorption. We outline the integration of metasurface architecture and machine learning‐assisted analysis for enhancing reproducibility and quantitative reliability. Finally, identifying critical challenges and future perspectives provides a roadmap for translating organic/2D hybrids into point‐of‐care diagnostic platforms and environmental monitoring.
authors: Abdur Rahim; Habib Ullah; Ali Bahadar; Alamgir; Esha Maqbool; Muhammad Saleem; Irfan Ullah; Abdul Samad; Mei Liu; Ningtao Cheng; De‐man Han; Sailing He

title: Chronic pelvic pain associated with synthetic mesh implants following surgery for pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence
abstract: Introduction. Chronic pelvic pain is one of the most challenging complications of pelvic floor reconstructive surgery involving mesh implants for the treatment of pelvic organ prolapse and stress urinary incontinence. Despite the widespread use of mesh-based techniques, the pathogenesis of this condition remains poorly understood, and the lack of standardized diagnostic criteria and validated pain assessment tools significantly limits comparability between clinical studies. Objective. To summarize current evidence on the epidemiology, clinical phenotypes, pathophysiological mechanisms, diagnostic approaches, and treatment strategies for chronic pelvic pain associated with mesh implants. Materials & methods. A structured narrative literature review was performed. Publications were found through searches of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using keywords related to “pelvic mesh implants”, “chronic pelvic pain”, “pelvic organ prolapse”, “stress urinary incontinence”, and “complications of pelvic floor reconstructive surgery”. Original clinical studies, observational studies, systematic reviews, and case series addressing meshassociated pain and related complications were included. Data were synthesized using qualitative analytical methods. Results. The reported prevalence of chronic pelvic pain after mesh implantation varies widely, ranging from 0% to 30%, largely reflecting differences in terminology, diagnostic criteria, and outcome measures. The longterm prevalence of persistent pain is estimated at approximately 4 – 7%. Mesh-associated pain encompasses several clinical phenotypes, including mechanical pain syndromes, neuropathic pain, myofascial dysfunction, and complex forms of chronic pelvic pain. Proposed pathophysiological mechanisms include nerve entrapment, fibrotic tissue remodeling, mesh contraction, chronic foreign-body inflammatory response, and mechanisms of peripheral and central sensitization. Diagnosis remains challenging because routine imaging and physical examination often fail to identify the source of symptoms. Management typically follows a stepwise, phenotypeoriented approach that includes conservative therapy, pelvic floor rehabilitation, and, in selected cases, surgical revision or mesh removal. Conclusions. Chronic pelvic pain associated with mesh implants represents a multifactorial syndrome resulting from the interaction of biomechanical, inflammatory, and neurophysiological mechanisms. Improving the diagnosis and treatment of this condition requires standardized terminology, development of condition-specific pain assessment tools, and well-designed prospective clinical studies.
authors: T.T. Nomovir; O.A. Plekhanova; Dina Manasherova; George R. Kasyan; Pushkar' DIu

title: Clinical Tasks Explain AI Readiness Across Medical Specialties
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming clinical work, yet its potential impact is often considered at the level of medical specialties rather than their constituent clinical tasks. We developed a clinical task-based framework, medical specialty AI readiness (MSAIR), for evaluating AI readiness across 22 medical specialties, scoring 330 representative clinical tasks across six dimensions. We found AI-readiness scores varied more widely across clinical task categories than across specialties. Clinical documentation and diagnostic interpretation had the highest task-category scores, whereas emergency decision-making and medical procedures had the lowest. Clinical task explained 71.6% of the variation in AI readiness, compared with only 6.4% explained by medical specialty. These findings suggest that AI readiness is more strongly associated with the nature of clinical work than with medical specialty. The MSAIR framework is useful for planning and anticipating how AI may reshape medical practice.
authors: Bertalan Meskó; Gellért Katonai; Shangchu Chen; Bin Sheng; Tien Yin Wong; Eric Topol

title: Clinicopathological profile and surgical outcome of choledochal cysts: a prospective observational study from Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Choledochal cysts are uncommon congenital abnormalities of the biliary tract characterized by cystic dilatation of the extrahepatic and/or intrahepatic bile ducts. This study evaluated the clinicopathological characteristics, diagnostic profile, cyst morphology and surgical outcomes of patients with choledochal cysts treated at a tertiary surgical center in Bangladesh. Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Surgery, Bangladesh Medical University, Dhaka, from January 2013 to December 2014. Forty-two patients with choledochal cysts were included. Demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, associated hepatobiliary conditions, laboratory findings, imaging investigations, Todani classification, operative procedures, histopathological findings and postoperative complications were evaluated. Descriptive statistical analysis was performed. Results: Among 42 patients, 27 (64.3%) were female and 15 (35.7%) were male. Thirty-two patients (76.2%) were older than 20 years. Abdominal pain was the most frequent presenting symptom, occurring in 34 (81.0%) patients, followed by jaundice in 19 (45.2%). Todani type I was the predominant cyst type, identified in 20 (47.6%) patients, followed by type IV in 13 (31.0%). Type II, III and V cysts were present in 3 (7.1%), 1 (2.4%) and 5 (11.9%) patients, respectively. Ultrasonography was performed in all patients, while MRCP was performed in 38 (90.5%). Complete cyst excision was achieved in 34 (81.0%) patients, with Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy being the predominant reconstructive procedure. Seven patients (16.7%) developed postoperative complications. One postoperative death occurred. Conclusions: Choledochal cysts in this series predominantly affected females and were frequently diagnosed during adulthood. Todani type I was the commonest anatomical subtype. Ultrasonography followed by MRCP provided the principal diagnostic pathway. Complete cyst excision with biliary reconstruction was the predominant definitive treatment. Early diagnosis and appropriate anatomical delineation may facilitate definitive surgery and reduce complications associated with delayed presentation.
authors: Mahmud Hasan; M. Ashraful Islam; Z. M. Raihan Kabir; Shaffat Sabbir Khan; Sharmin Akhter; M. Tafazzul Hossain Bhuiyan

title: Cloud-Robust Information-Seeking Agents for Adaptive Earth-Observation Acquisition and Surface Forecasting
abstract: Earth-environment monitoring increasingly has to deliver a decision inside a time window: an inundation map before a crest, a vegetation-condition field before an irrigation window, a damage map while a response team is still deployed. The observations that feed those products are neither free nor always available. Optical revisit is blocked by cloud, acquisitions compete for downlink and ground-station quotas, and synthetic-aperture radar (SAR) and in-situ stations carry different costs. Existing pipelines fix the acquisition policy in advance and spend their capacity on prediction, while recent language-model agents for Earth observation treat acquisition tools as cost-free black boxes and keep no auditable record of what each observation actually covers. We present CRISP, a cloud-robust information-seeking agent that decides what to acquire and then forecasts. A grounding ledger turns every observation into a typed entry with verifiable spatial, temporal, and quality fields and lets all downstream conclusions point back to it. A verbalized value-ofinformation critic converts the language model’s written reasons for a candidate acquisition into calibrated scores, which define a submodular cloud-gap coverage objective; a cost-normalized greedy rule then attains the usual (1 − 1/e) guarantee on a fixed budget and represents complementarity between optical and SAR acquisition. A physics-consistency self-critique recomputes advection, phenology, and radiation residuals, verbalizes the largest ones, and rewrites only the flagged time steps. On the EarthNet2021 surface-forecasting protocol CRISP reaches ENS 0.3075 on the out-of-distribution split and 0.2555 on the extreme split, improving the strongest official baseline by 7.7% and 8.1%; on SEN12MS-CR it reaches PSNR 25.62 and FID 86.2; on the flood-mapping and post-disaster protocols it reaches flood IoU 0.787 and mIoU 83.42. Under an equal acquisition budget it covers 0.78 of the cloud gap against 0.51 for an entropy criterion, and in an agentic protocol it raises task success from 62.4% to 78.6% while cutting invalid tool calls from 21.7% to 6.1%.
authors: Dina Khalil; Mostafa Elhadi; Kareem Nassar; Hossam Fahmy; Yassin Abdelrahman

title: Comparing Outcomes after Core Muscle Repair by Repair Technique: A Systematic Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Core muscle injuries (CMIs) are a common cause of chronic groin pain in athletes. Numerous surgical techniques have been described, ranging from abdominal wall reinforcement to direct muscle and tendon repair; nonetheless, the optimal surgical strategy remains unclear. We aimed to systematically review and compare clinical outcomes associated with different surgical techniques used for CMIs. METHODS: A search was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis (PRISMA) guidelines. Included studies evaluated surgical interventions and reported one or more clinical outcome: return-to-sport (RTS), patient-reported outcome measures, pain scores, and/or complications. Surgical techniques were grouped into predefined repair categories based on repair construct and use of adductor longus (AL) tenotomy. RESULTS: Twenty-seven studies (1803 patients) met inclusion criteria. In total, seven general repair categories were reported. Among 21 studies (1433 patients) reporting RTS, 95.7% returned to sport at final follow-up. The RTS rate was 97.5% after laparoscopic approaches and 94.7% after open procedures. Mesh-based repairs demonstrated 83.9% to 99.3% RTS (n = 12 studies), while rectus abdominis repair with AL tenotomy demonstrated 90.2% to 96.5% RTS (n = 3 studies), often with longer rehabilitation time lines. Overall complication rates were low (5.2%), although higher with mesh or primary tissue repair plus AL tenotomy (16.7%). High heterogeneity was observed in reporting methods of measures of pain/satisfaction/function, limiting comparisons to RTS and complications only. CONCLUSION: Many surgical techniques for CMIs yield high RTS and low complication rates. Treating CMIs as either a hernia-type structural deficiency or a muscle/tendinous injury seems effective when tailored to the underlying pathology.
authors: Ameya Vinayak Belamkar; Manuel Angel Romero‐Padron; Nicholas Ryan Kossoff; Nicholas James Lanzetta; Joshua Scott Everhart

title: Comparison of clinical efficacy between surgical and non-surgical treatments for thoracolumbar type B fractures associated with ankylosing spondylitis
abstract: Background: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) combined with thoracolumbar type B fractures usually presents as unstable injuries, with fractures involving all three columns. Surgical treatment is regarded as the preferred treatment option for this type of fracture. Nevertheless, approximately one-third of patients still opt for non-surgical treatment. Currently, there is a lack of research data comparing different treatment methods for AS patients with thoracolumbar fractures. Methods: Clinical data were collected from patients with AS complicated by thoracolumbar type B fractures who were treated with either surgical or non-surgical methods at our institution between January 2018 and October 2023. The general data of the two groups were compared, and clinical efficacy-related indicators were recorded, including fracture healing time, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) scores, and the incidence of complications. VAS and ODI scores of the two groups were compared at admission, at 3 months, at 12 months, and at the final follow-up. Results: There were 37 patients in the surgical group and 33 patients in the non-surgical group. No significant differences were observed in baseline demographic or clinical characteristics between the two groups. The median VAS scores in the surgical group and the non-surgical group at 3 months were 2 (2, 2) and 3 (3, 4), respectively. The median ODI scores in the surgical group and the non-surgical group at 3 months were 20 (18, 22)% and 40 (36, 44)%, respectively. Comparison of the VAS and ODI scores between the two groups revealed that the differences were statistically significant at 3 months. The median fracture healing time was 7 (6, 8) months in the surgical group and 13 (12, 14) months in the non-surgical group. This difference was statistically significant. The complication rate in the surgical group was 18.9%, which was significantly lower than the 57.6% observed in the non-surgical group. Conclusions: Surgical treatment has obvious advantages in fracture healing, complication rates, and early clinical efficacy, and can promote early rehabilitation of patients. It is the preferred treatment for AS combined with thoracolumbar type B fractures. Clinical trial number: Not applicable.
authors: Zhiyuan Ye; Weikang Zhou; Feng Guo-xin; Xiao-Yu Zhou; Chang-Hua Tang; Zhentao Zhou; Bing-Chen Shan; Xiao-Hui Zhang; Xiao-Zhong Zhou

title: Comparison of three malnutrition assessment criteria for predicting postoperative complications and overall survival in colorectal cancer
abstract: Background Malnutrition is highly prevalent in patients with colorectal cancer and is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes and shortened survival. However, the comparative predictive performance of commonly used nutritional assessment tools—PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM criteria—remains unclear. Methods A total of 1,258 patients who underwent radical resection for colorectal cancer were retrospectively enrolled. Malnutrition was diagnosed simultaneously using the PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM criteria. Agreement among the three tools was evaluated using Cohen’s kappa coefficient. Multivariable logistic regression, an exploratory random forest analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied. For the logistic regression models, ROC curve analysis and pairwise AUC comparisons using DeLong’s test were performed; for the Cox models, bootstrap-based C-index comparisons were conducted. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for the GLIM criterion as a post hoc sensitivity analysis to explore the association between GLIM-defined malnutrition and clinical outcomes. Results The prevalence of malnutrition defined by PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM was 24.7%, 15.7%, and 29.9%, respectively, with pairwise agreements ranging from moderate to substantial. All three criteria were independent risk factors for postoperative complications, with GLIM having the highest odds ratio (OR = 1.869, p < 0.001). AUC comparison further showed that the GLIM-incorporated model achieved the numerically highest AUC (0.781), with a significantly higher AUC than the ESPEN-based model ( p = 0.023), whereas no significant difference was observed between GLIM and PG-SGA ( p = 0.172). For OS, PG-SGA (HR = 1.364, p = 0.014) and GLIM (HR = 1.415, p = 0.004) were independent prognostic factors, whereas ESPEN was not ( p = 0.129). Bootstrap C-index comparisons showed that the GLIM-based model provided modestly better prognostic discrimination than both the PG-SGA- and ESPEN-based models (both p < 0.05), although the absolute C-index improvement was small (approximately 0.015). After PSM balancing baseline characteristics, GLIM-defined malnutrition remained significantly associated with prolonged postoperative hospital stay, higher complication rates, and reduced 5-year overall survival. Conclusion The three malnutrition diagnostic criteria are not interchangeable. For postoperative complications, GLIM demonstrated better discriminative ability than ESPEN but was comparable to PG-SGA. For long-term OS, GLIM provided modestly better prognostic discrimination than both PG-SGA and ESPEN, although the absolute improvement was small. These findings support the potential clinical utility of GLIM for perioperative nutritional risk assessment; however, the clinical relevance of these relatively small performance differences warrants further validation.
authors: Wei Wei; Yangming Li; Guiren Fang; Jinliang Jian; Zhenmeng Lin

title: Condensing patients’ narratives of workplace accidents into standard injury definitions: How the constraints of clinical documentation shape history taking in a prosthetics clinic
abstract: This article examines how what counts as clinically relevant and recordable information is interactionally achieved in the making of medical records. Drawing on ethnomethodology and conversation analysis, we analyze videorecorded first-time consultations with patients seeking prosthetic treatment following workplace injuries, focusing on the “etiology” field of a pre-structured assessment form. We show how the form routinely organizes the clinical interview, shaping what clinicians ask and attend to, and what ultimately enters the record. Patients’ accounts are progressively transformed into brief categorial definitions, which patients confirm or refine. Our analysis demonstrates that relevance is not a given but is interactionally established through situated practices of elicitation, categorization, and negotiation. These findings foreground the interactional work underlying the production of clinical data and raise questions about what may be lost as clinical documentation becomes increasingly automated.
authors: Monica Simone; Renata Galatolo

title: Continual Reinforcement Learning Is an Integration Problem
abstract: This paper presents an opinionated set of ten desiderata intended to inform the design and evaluation of reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually throughout a continuing lifetime. We use these desiderata to examine a representative selection of existing approaches. Progress on individual desiderata is valuable, but the longer-term aim should be to integrate all ten within a single agent. To our knowledge, no published evaluation has yet provided evidence for such an integration. Likewise, the representative benchmarks we review probe different parts of this target, but separate evaluations do not establish that the corresponding properties coexist within one agent throughout a continuing lifetime. As a secondary contribution, we therefore present a compact persistent-world scenario as a playable companion to the desiderata and outline a proposed benchmark that examines a broad range of associated behavioral capabilities together within one such lifetime.
authors: Nis Meinert; Jakob Gawlikowski; Edward Grant; Max Cyprys; Nathan Schurr; Neil Boston; Alfredo Ibias; Milind Tambe; Janusz Marecki

title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Combined With Biopsy for the Preoperative Diagnosis of a Rare Pelvic Schwannoma: A Case Report
abstract: BACKGROUND Primary pelvic schwannomas are rare and often misdiagnosed due to non-specific imaging features. Accurate preoperative evaluation remains a challenge. The clinical utility of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with time-intensity curve (TIC) analysis and targeted biopsy was evaluated for the preoperative diagnosis and management of a pelvic schwannoma. CASE REPORT A 66-year-old man presented with dysuria and lumbago. Imaging revealed a large, mixed cystic-solid pelvic mass. Conventional ultrasound demonstrated a predominantly cystic-solid lesion with limited Doppler flow, whereas CEUS showed progressive dendritic enhancement of the viable solid component from the periphery toward the center, with non-enhancement of cystic or necrotic areas. TIC analysis demonstrated a distinctive "equal-in and slow-out" perfusion pattern, supported by quantitative parameters (rise time, time to peak, fall time, and washout area under the curve). Based on these perfusion characteristics, ultrasound-guided biopsy was directed toward hyperenhanced viable regions while avoiding necrotic zones, thereby improving tissue sampling accuracy. Immunohistochemistry confirmed S-100 and SOX-10 positivity, establishing a definitive diagnosis. Complete surgical resection with bladder defect repair was performed. Postoperatively, urinary function recovered, and no recurrent urinary or pelvic symptoms were reported during outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS Quantitative CEUS-TIC analysis combined with targeted biopsy provides an effective preoperative diagnostic strategy for pelvic schwannomas. The observed CEUS-TIC perfusion pattern may correspond to the heterogeneous microvascular distribution of Antoni A and Antoni B regions; however, this hypothesis requires validation in future imaging-pathology correlation studies.
authors: Jinzhe Wang; Li Wei; Yufei Wang

title: Cryptococcal Meningitis in an Apparently Immunocompetent Patient With a Ventriculoatrial Shunt: Diagnostic Challenges of Negative Serum Cryptococcal Antigen
abstract: BACKGROUND Cryptococcal meningitis usually occurs in people with impaired cellular immunity, but it can also affect patients without a recognized immunodeficiency. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) shunts complicate recognition because symptoms may be subtle and serum studies may be unrevealing. We describe a case of a patient with a longstanding ventriculoatrial (VA) shunt whose CSF findings established the diagnosis despite a negative serum cryptococcal antigen result. CASE REPORT A 60-year-old man with a remote ventriculoperitoneal shunt subsequently converted to a VA shunt developed persistent headache and an episode of seizure-like activity 3 days after robotic cholecystectomy. He had no focal neurological deficit, and electroencephalography showed no epileptiform activity. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed no mass lesion or hydrocephalus. Lumbar puncture revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis (101 cells/μL), CSF protein of 61 mg/dL, and glucose of 44 mg/dL. Serum cryptococcal antigen was negative, whereas CSF cryptococcal antigen was positive at a titer of 1: 40 and CSF culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans . The discordant serum result has an uncertain mechanism because assay-platform details and repeat or dilution testing were unavailable. He received liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine, underwent VA shunt removal and external ventricular drainage, and later had shunt revision. Following clinical and microbiologic improvement, he received fluconazole consolidation and maintenance therapy and remained clinically well at 4-week follow-up. CONCLUSIONS A negative serum cryptococcal antigen result did not exclude meningitis in this patient with a CSF shunt. Persistent unexplained neurological symptoms warrant CSF evaluation when cryptococcosis remains clinically plausible. This case also illustrates the importance of antifungal therapy and coordinated neurosurgical management for suspected shunt-associated infection.
authors: Mustafa Nuaimi; Sara Ubosy; Habib Behjatnia; Patricia Couto; Antonio Crespo; Mario Madruga; Steve J. Carlan

title: Deep Learning for Sequential Decision Making Under Uncertainty: Foundations, Frameworks, and Frontiers
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving beyond prediction toward systems that support decision making in complex, dynamic environments. This shift creates a natural intersection with operations research and management science (OR/MS), which has long provided methodological foundations for sequential decision making under uncertainty. At the same time, deep learning advances, including feedforward neural networks, recurrent architectures, transformers, large language models (LLMs), and deep reinforcement learning, have expanded data-driven modeling for large-scale decisions. This tutorial presents an OR/MS-centered perspective on deep learning for sequential decision making under uncertainty, bridging neural architectures and OR/MS approaches to decision making. Its premise: Deep learning complements optimization rather than replacing it. Deep learning brings adaptability and scalable approximation, whereas OR/MS provides the mathematical rigor to represent constraints, recourse, uncertainty, and decision quality. The tutorial reviews key decision-making foundations, connects them to the major neural architectures in modern AI, and organizes the field around three central themes: predict-then-optimize and decision-aware learning, learning-based decision generation under constraints for continuous and discrete problems with temporal coupling, and deep reinforcement learning for sequential and combinatorial decision making. Impact spans supply chains, service systems, healthcare and epidemic response, agriculture, energy, environmental sustainability, and autonomous operations. This tutorial frames these developments as part of a shift from predictive AI toward decision-capable AI, highlighting OR/MS’s role in shaping the next generation of integrated learning-optimization systems.
authors: İ. Esra Büyüktahtakın

title: Delayed sequential lung, acral cutaneous and brain metastases after radical nephrectomy for clear cell renal cell carcinoma: a case report
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma may recur after nephrextomy. Approximately 25-30% of all RCC patients develop metastases, most commonly involving the lungs, bones and brain. Cutaneous metastases are exceptionally rare (about 3% of all RCC patiens) and are associated with a favorable prognosis. While the surgical interventions remain the cornerstone of the management of RCCs, chemotherapy and biological therapies are also available, therefore a complex approach is a must in order to reach the best possible outcome. This is a case report of a 62-year-old male patient with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking history, who underwent a laparoscopic transperitoneal radical right nephrectomy in 2019. Later the histological examination confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma. During the course of the disease, he developed multiple metastases involving the lungs, the skin and the brain. He received oncological therapies as well as surgeries - involving robot-assisted thoracoscopic surgery and CyberKnife surgery - and tolerated the therapeutic methods well. This case emphasizes that even small acral lesions in patients with prior renal cell carcinoma may represent metastatic disease and demonstrates the value of prolonged surveillance and multidisciplinary treatment in rare delayed metastatic presentations.
authors: Péter Álmos Rajhóczki; Viktor Kardos; Rézan Watti; Marcell Juhász; Magdolna Horváth; Dávid Pócs; Jezdancher Watti

title: Deliberate Vulnerability at the Bedside: Operationalising Failure Rounds in Clinical Teaching
abstract: Bedside rounds frequently devolve into performative clinical demonstrations where cognitive friction, uncertainty and diagnostic hesitations are masked by learners. Inspired by the AMEE 2026 symposium on "Failure Rounds," this perspective translates the pedagogical concept of deliberate vulnerability into front-line bedside clinical teaching. Grounded in psychological safety, productive failure and error-based learning frameworks, deliberate vulnerability repositions uncertainty from a professional deficit into a catalyst for diagnostic reasoning. Front-line faculty discussions highlight practical barriers, including safeguarding patient trust and balancing efficiency with deep pedagogical exploration. We propose three actionable, nonprescriptive pillars for clinical teachers: taking the first turn by acknowledging doubt, decoupling immediate patient care from cognitive debriefing and conducting structured micro-debriefings.
authors: Sara Heydari; Reza Bidaki

title: Design Strategies for Carbon Nanotube-Based Biosensors in Complex Biological Media: From Interfacial Physics to System-Level Translation
abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) biosensors offer sensitive electrical and near-infrared optical readouts, yet performance in defined buffers does not necessarily translate to reliable measurements in complex biological media. Ionic screening, nonspecific adsorption, variable sample composition, and transport limitations can disrupt the relationship between molecular recognition and sensor output. This review examines how interfacial engineering and system-level design address these constraints across serum, plasma, whole blood, saliva, urine, and intracellular or tissue environments. We connect receptor orientation and dimensions, antifouling coatings, and designed corona phases to their effects on analyte accessibility, transduction, and signal stability. We then discuss sample separation, enrichment, and microfluidic delivery as integral parts of the measurement workflow. Electrical CNT architectures and optical single-walled CNT sensors are compared in terms of their operating mechanisms, matrix-dependent limitations, and validation requirements. Particular attention is given to distinguishing direct sensing from CNT-assisted sample preparation, optical visibility from selective analyte measurement, and fortified-sample testing from clinical validation. We also examine data-driven recognition discovery, manufacturing reproducibility, and reporting practices needed for meaningful comparison across platforms. The central design principle is to optimize the complete sample-to-answer process around the dominant limitation in the intended biological environment. Progress toward practical CNT biosensing therefore requires matrix-matched calibration, explicit characterization of sample conditioning, and independent validation across devices, batches, and biological specimens.
authors: Jongwan Lee; Chang-Ho Han; Bon Joon Koo; Minseok Kim

title: Design and Simulation of an Event Driven Sensorless IoT System for Automotive Battery Monitoring and Fault Detection
abstract: In the automobile industry, lead acid battery failure continues to be a major factor in vehicle immobility. In traditional monitoring systems, high inactive current draw, which adds to parasitic drain, or a lack of remote accessibility for real time user notification are common problems. A unique, event driven Internet of Things (IoT) framework for real time vehicle power diagnostics is proposed in this research. The sensorless architecture that uses straightforward resistor divider network to transmit voltage data straight into Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) of the microcontroller, is a significant innovation since it prevents the need for external sensors. Also, this suggested framework makes use of a state machine that alternates between an active sensing mode and a deep sleep period that is only activated by abnormal voltage occurrences. The proposed design validated through an electrical system and supervisory state logic modelled using MATLAB/Simulink, where Python serving as a secondary simulation and communication layer. Five main operating conditions are distinguished by the monitoring algorithm: parked, engine cranking, regular operation, alternator failure, and critical shutdown. The automotive voltage is scaled to an ADC compatible range using a 10 kΩ/2.7 kΩ resistor divider network, and signal filtering is provided by a 0.1 µF capacitor. With voltage settings of 12.60 V during parked operation, 9.80 V during engine cranking, 14.20 V during normal charging, 11.74 V during simulated alternator failure, and 10.30 V at critical shutdown, the simulation replicated the desired vehicle operating sequence. 1000 separate Monte Carlo runs with additive Gaussian measurement noise made up the stochastic validation. Relative mean voltage errors for the statistically assessed parked, alternator failure, and shutdown states were 0.0016%, 0.0009%, and 0.0029%, respectively, whereas the empirical detection success rate under the simulated conditions was 100%. The findings show that the suggested state machine architecture can reduce the need for ongoing high-power monitoring while differentiating between sustained abnormal voltage circumstances and normal beginning transients. As a result, the system offers a useful basis for controlled automotive validation and future ESP32 based physical implementation.
authors: Thushani Mallikarathne; Hashan Abeysinghe
venue: International Journal of Applied Smart Interdisciplinary Technologies

title: Design and optimization of an Ag/Cu–black phosphorus/Franckeite heterostructure for high-sensitivity surface plasmon resonance biosensing
abstract: Introduction Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensors enable label-free, real-time detection, but simultaneously achieving strong field confinement, near-critical coupling, and a high figure of merit (FoM) remains challenging, particularly when low-loss silver must be protected from aqueous media. Methods A CaF 2 /Ag/Cu/black phosphorus (BP)/Franckeite Kretschmann heterostructure was modeled at λ = 633 nm using the frequency-domain Maxwell wave equation and the transfer matrix method under TM-polarized angular and phase interrogation. The Ag and Cu thicknesses were optimized individually and jointly, size-dependent Drude damping corrections were applied, and performance was benchmarked against a Cu-only reference with identical BP/Franckeite overlayers. Fabrication tolerance to BP layer number and Franckeite thickness was also evaluated. Results Joint optimization identified a near-critical-coupling configuration at approximately 31 nm Ag and 7 nm Cu, with a minimum reflectance of 1.1 × 10 −3 within the sensing window. Over 1.328–1.336 RIU, the sensor reached a peak angular sensitivity of 372°/RIU and a FoM of 47.0 RIU −1 at n s = 1.332, approximately 62% and 78% higher than the Cu-only reference. Phase interrogation reached 29,200°/RIU, corresponding to a minimum detectable refractive-index change of approximately 3.4 × 10 −7 RIU. The 1/e evanescent-field penetration depth was 178–201 nm. Size-dependent damping reduced the FoM by approximately 5%, and realistic 2D-layer thickness variations reduced it by no more than approximately 10%. Discussion The Ag/Cu/BP/Franckeite architecture is a promising platform for label-free biosensing, including carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) detection, subject to experimental validation of long-term stability, surface functionalization, and thermally compensated phase readout.
authors: Jacob Wekalao; Tobias Otieno

title: Design strategies and response mechanisms of intelligent dressings and their applications in the repair of diabetic wounds.
abstract: Diabetic wounds result in refractory skin defects due to hyperglycemic toxicity, microcirculatory disorders, and chronic inflammation. Traditional dressings that passively cover wounds have significant limitations. Intelligent dressings offer active sensing, precise responses, and functional integration to break this vicious cycle. This review systematically examines design principles, response mechanisms (endogenous, exogenous, and multi-response synergy), and application progress (infection monitoring, exudate management, regeneration promotion, and closed-loop regulation) of intelligent dressings for diabetic wound repair. Key challenges in technology integration, clinical translation, and individual adaptation are analyzed, and future directions toward precision, personalization, and integration are discussed. This review provides a comprehensive reference for both research and clinical translation in this field.
authors: Chiyu Ma; Yongfeng Ji; Ai Yang; Xinru Li; Wanjun Liu; Chao Zhou; Cunyi Fan

title: Development and internal validation of a multimodal deep learning model for screening-level lower-limb alignment using plantar 3D foot scans
abstract: Lower-limb alignment is a key determinant of musculoskeletal loading and is associated with biomechanical risk pathways for conditions such as knee osteoarthritis and plantar fasciitis. However, routine alignment assessment still relies on radiography or specialist clinical examination, limiting scalability for early screening. Here, we investigated whether plantar foot morphology captured by weight-bearing 3D scanning can serve as a computational screening feature for proximal lower-limb alignment, and we developed a multimodal deep learning framework to support scalable alignment screening. We established a cross-sectional dataset of 167 participants (adults and children aged 6-60 years) with standardised plantar 3D foot scans and clinical labels for arch type, hindfoot alignment, and frontal-plane knee alignment. The proposed model jointly learns from plantar scan images and 16 geometric morphological features, integrated using feature-wise attention to prioritise alignment-relevant cues across modalities. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and AUC on a held-out test set, and interpretability was assessed with class activation mapping (CAM). Ablation studies compared alternative image encoders and fusion variants, including image-only, morphology-only, and fusion without attention. The attention-based multimodal model showed competitive but task-dependent performance, achieving accuracies of 89% for arch type, 81% for hindfoot alignment, and 76% for knee alignment. The image-only ViT achieved the highest accuracy for arch classification, while the ViT without-attention configuration achieved slightly higher accuracy and macro-F1 for knee alignment. These findings indicate that the benefit of multimodal attention fusion varied across alignment tasks. Activation maps consistently highlighted clinically relevant plantar regions associated with alignment patterns, suggesting morphological correlations consistent with a distal-proximal kinetic chain hypothesis. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of plantar 3D scanning combined with multimodal, explainable deep learning as a non-invasive approach for screening alignment-related biomechanical risk factors, warranting further external validation before clinical translation.
authors: Sao Chih Ni; Yaxi Chen; Chenyan Wang; Ding Zhou; Jiaqi Liu; Mo Zhou; Julian Leong; Yipeng Hu; Jie Huang; Jinwu Wang; Chaozong Liu

title: Development of RF Probes and Preamplifiers for MRI at Low Fields
abstract: T) have experienced renewed interest due to the emergence of portable, point-of-care (POC) scanners, and new approaches to mitigating the intrinsically lower signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). The performance of radiofrequency (RF) components is a large factor in determining overall system sensitivity. In contrast to conventional MRI, at higher fields where SNR is typically sample-noise dominated, many low field (LF) systems operate in a coil-noise dominated regime, requiring careful optimization of RF coil design, conductor losses, and receiver electronics. This manuscript surveys RF coil technologies and associated hardware considerations for MRI systems operating below approximately 0.18T, within the range that we designate as low field in this manuscript (0-250 mT). We begin by revisiting early low-field imaging systems and the historical development of RF coil architectures for large-volume imaging. The fundamental noise mechanisms governing low-frequency MR detection are then examined, including Johnson noise in conductors, sample-induced losses, receiver noise figure, and electromagnetic interference (EMI). Design strategies for improving sensitivity are discussed, including conductor optimization (e.g., Litz wire), coil geometry selection such as solenoidal and saddle configurations, and methods for managing coil bandwidth and quality factor. Recent developments in transmit-receive switching, preamplifier design, EMI mitigation, and coil-preamplifier co-design are also reviewed. Finally, we highlight emerging directions for RF hardware development in low-field MRI, including RF coils for encoding, multi-element receive arrays for parallel imaging, and receiver architectures inspired by related modalities such as magnetic particle imaging and ultrasound. Continued advances in RF coil and receiver-chain design will be essential for improving sensitivity and enabling low-field MRI systems for clinical and research applications.
authors: Charlotte R. Sappo; Jonathan B. Martin; Millie A. Barron; Selin Kandemir; Xinqiang Yan; John C. Gore

title: Diagnostic limitations and procedure-related implantation in follicular-patterned thyroid tumors: a focused review with two illustrative cases
abstract: The rapid adoption of thyroid radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and remote-access thyroid surgery has changed the therapeutic landscape for thyroid nodules. These approaches can reduce visible scarring, shorten recovery, and offer alternatives to conventional surgery in appropriately selected patients. However, their expansion has also exposed a persistent diagnostic vulnerability: follicular-patterned thyroid tumors cannot be definitively classified as benign or malignant by cytology alone, because the diagnosis of follicular thyroid carcinoma requires histologic assessment of capsular and/or vascular invasion. This review first summarizes the current clinical context of minimally invasive thyroid intervention, the diagnostic boundaries of fine-needle aspiration and Bethesda reporting in follicular-lineage lesions, the definitions and published evidence for needle-tract or surgical-tunnel implantation, and the molecular context of DICER1-altered follicular-patterned tumors. Two implantation-related cases are used as illustrative clinical scenarios rather than as the primary evidentiary basis. The Discussion then addresses the major controversies, including procedural expansion, the role of benign cytology as a preprocedural gatekeeper, the uncertain role of molecular testing before ablation, terminology, patient selection, surveillance, research gaps, and potential developments. The available literature remains dominated by case reports and small series, and causal inference is limited. Nevertheless, repeated reports of tract- or tunnel-aligned deposits in follicular-lineage tumors suggest that implantation risk should be considered when selecting patients for ablative or remote-access interventions. Molecular alterations such as DICER1 RNase IIIb hotspot mutations may provide biological context, but they should not replace histologic classification. Future progress will require standardized reporting, prospective registries, molecularly annotated cohorts, and preprocedural algorithms that integrate imaging, cytology, molecular testing, procedural anatomy, and patient preference.
authors: Wenjie Zhang; Yuanyuan Chen; Jie Xiao; Ying Liu; Pin Wang; Hong Liu; Jiechao Ren; Jian Wu

title: Diamond and related carbon-based materials for biomedical devices: processing, surface engineering, and functional interfaces
abstract: Diamond and related carbon-based materials are being explored for biomedical devices that require durable contact surfaces, stable electrochemical transduction, or functional optical and biological interfaces. This Review examines crystalline diamond, nanodiamond, nanocrystalline and ultrananocrystalline diamond, boron-doped and fluorescent diamond, diamond-like carbon (DLC), and diamond-containing composites. We discuss how HPHT synthesis, CVD/MPCVD growth, doping, defect engineering, and interfacial modification connect processing with structure, surface behavior, and device function. Representative studies in surgical and dental instruments, orthopedic and cardiovascular technologies, ophthalmology, drug delivery, bioimaging, biosensing, neural interfaces, and regenerative medicine are compared in terms of their methods, reported outcomes, and limitations. Across these areas, we identify opportunities in wear-resistant coatings, conductive diamond electrodes, and functionalized nanodiamond carriers and probes for drug delivery and bioimaging. Surface chemistry, interfacial adhesion, and device architecture emerge as recurring factors governing mechanical durability, electrochemical performance, optical readout, and biological interactions. Particular attention is given to coating failure, wear debris, corrosion, material-dependent biological responses, fouling, signal drift, and device integration. We distinguish direct biomedical findings from manufacturing studies that provide useful but unvalidated engineering principles. Finally, we discuss application-specific comparison metrics, relevant medical-device testing frameworks, and challenges in translating diamond functions into reproducible, safe, and clinically useful technologies.
authors: Lin Jiang; Lijuan Zheng; Chengyong Wang

title: Digital Follow‐Up After Total Knee Arthroplasty: An Interview Study Among Orthopaedic Surgeons
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traditionally, patients who undergo total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are scheduled for an in-person routine follow-up (RFU) regimen. Increasing pressure on orthopaedic services and growing acceptance of digital health technologies urge clinics to adopt more efficient RFU strategies. However, limited insight exists into how RFU after TKA is organised in clinical practice and under which conditions digital follow-up is acceptable to orthopaedic surgeons. This study explored current RFU practices after TKA and examined surgeons' perspectives on digital follow-up. METHODS: A qualitative study using semi-structured interviews was conducted with 21 orthopaedic surgeons from different healthcare institutions. Interviews were conducted digitally, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using qualitative analysis software. Two researchers independently coded the transcripts, after which the codes were compared, refined, and grouped into overarching themes. RESULTS: Four main themes emerged. (1) RFU after TKA was highly fragmented across institutions, with variation in timing, contact modality, responsible healthcare provider, and use of radiographic assessment. (2) Follow-up visits were primarily perceived as a means to confirm uncomplicated recovery and detect complications early. (3) Digital follow-up was viewed not as a replacement for in-person visits but as an additional triage strategy to support decisions on physical consultation. (4) Acceptance of digital follow-up depended on clear patient selection, predefined clinical recovery indicators, and preservation of professional and patient autonomy. CONCLUSION: RFU after TKA is poorly standardized and institution dependent. Digital follow-up is considered acceptable mainly as a triage mechanism if patient safety, professional autonomy, and the surgeon-patient relationship are maintained.
authors: Casper Craamer; Thomas Timmers; Walter van der Weegen; Rudolf Bertijn Kool

title: Digital phenotyping of migraine aura
abstract: Migraine aura is a transient, focal neurological phenomenon, characterized by evolving visual, somatosensory, language, and, to a lesser extent, motor disturbances, among other symptoms that reflect dynamic alterations in brain function, involving not only cortical, but also subcortical structures. Despite advances in understanding its neurobiology, including the role of cortical spreading depolarization, migraine aura remains incompletely characterized. This is most likely because of its unpredictable onset, brief duration, individual and symptom variability, and reliance on retrospective clinical assessment. Consequently, its temporal evolution and biological heterogeneity remain to be fully elucidated. Digital phenotyping has emerged as a framework for characterizing health and disease through continuous real-world data collected using personal digital technologies. Here we examine the rationale for considering the potential application of digital phenotyping to migraine aura. We argue that aura's unique biological and temporal characteristics can make it a suitable choice for continuous multidimensional assessment. Integrating patient-reported symptoms with physiological, behavioral, and environmental data may improve phenotypic resolution. Consequently, it may help advance mechanistic understanding and capture within-person variability. Therefore, we present a conceptual framework alongside the methodological and translational challenges of digital phenotyping, including implementation-related challenges. Rather than replacing established clinical and neurobiological approaches, digital phenotyping is presented as a complementary framework that, if rigorously validated, could potentially advance our understanding of aura and migraine aura research, support the institution and consolidation of precision headache medicine, and facilitate patient care.
authors: Parisa Gazerani; Igor Petrušić; Marcos Fabio Henriques DosSantos

title: Discourse in White Coats: Exploring Linguistic Features in Medical Communication
abstract: The aim of this qualitative descriptive research is to examine both the linguistic and discourse-level features of Medical English. The research employs a two-tiered approach: first, a linguistic analysis focusing on morphology, lexical density, syntax, and semantic evolution; second, a discourse analysis examining text organization, genre conventions, interactional patterns, and communicative practices. From a linguistic standpoint, Medical English is distinguished by its specialized terminology, extensive use of Greek and Latin roots, nominalized structures, passive constructions, and an expanding lexicon shaped by advances in numerous disciplines of Medical Sciences. At the discourse level, Medical English operates across multiple genres including clinical documentation, academic publications, and public health communication, each governed by established frameworks such as SOAP notes, IMRD structures, hedging strategies, and standardized phrasing in Medical research. As a result, Medical English has evolved beyond its traditional boundaries, emerging as dynamic and multifaceted domains of communication.
authors: Jameel Ahmad

title: Doping and Nanostructuring of Spinel Ferrites for Enhanced Gas Sensing: Recent Developments
abstract: Spinel ferrites have emerged as promising materials for gas sensing due to their tunable electronic properties, magnetic characteristics, and thermal stability. This review examines recent developments in doping and nanostructuring strategies for enhancing their gas sensing performance. Strategic incorporation of transition‐metal dopants (Fe 3+ , Co 2+ , Ni 2+ , Mn 2+ , and Zn 2+ ) enables precise control over oxygen‐vacancy concentration, electronic conductivity, and surface reactivity through defect‐chemistry manipulation, while nanostructuring approaches, including hierarchical architectures, hollow spheres, core‐shell configurations, and one‐dimensional structures, substantially increase surface‐to‐volume ratio and gas‐diffusion kinetics. Sensing mechanisms are analyzed through band‐structure engineering, surface catalysis, and charge‐transfer processes, supported by operando characterization that provides direct mechanistic insight. Reported performance gains include sub‐ppb detection limits, response times reduced to seconds, and markedly enhanced selectivity relative to undoped bulk materials, with synthesis‐structure–property relationships established to guide rational design. Persistent challenges include reproducible large‐scale synthesis, long‐term stability, cross‐sensitivity mitigation, and cost‐effective production. Future directions encompass machine‐learning‐guided materials discovery, quantum‐sensing phenomena, bio‐inspired recognition mechanisms, and sustainable synthesis routes, supported by advanced characterization and multi‐scale computational modeling. Convergence with artificial intelligence, IoT platforms, and green chemistry positions doped, nanostructured spinel ferrites to address critical applications in environmental monitoring, industrial safety, healthcare diagnostics, and emerging smart sensing systems.
authors: Avadhesh Kumar Yadav

title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
abstract: Computational drug discovery requires agents to compose scientific operations and adapt to changing evidence and constraints. Here we introduce DrugHarness, an evolvable agent harness coupling composable scientific execution with conditional skill induction. Its environment integrates over 80 scientific operations, biomedical resources and task-specific code, preserving associations among candidates, results and artifacts. From execution trajectories and outcome feedback, DrugHarness induces action hypotheses with observable applicability conditions, recommended actions and supporting evidence. An independent review agent evaluates candidate skills derived from these hypotheses through source verification and, when needed, targeted execution trials. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks and are revised through feedback. Evaluation on MolBench and SMDD-Bench demonstrates capabilities in molecular screening, optimization and constrained design. Without evolution, DrugHarness exceeds reported MolClaw-CC results by 10.8 percentage points in affinity-comparison accuracy and 55% in mean top-three active hits on MolBench. Retrospective evaluation on skill-development tasks shows that evolution increases Qwen's affinity-comparison accuracy from 62.2% to 81.1% and optimization success from 79.5% to 87.2%. In a prospective HPK1 study, DrugHarness achieves a more favorable median docking score than Biomni among system-specific candidates. A synthesized compound achieves a cellular IC50 of 14.19 nM, a 2.64-fold potency improvement over the best input reference, with activity competitive with two selected compounds designed by experienced medicinal chemists. These results support conditional skill evolution for scientific agents and demonstrate a workflow connecting computational drug design with experimental validation.
authors: Chen Yuxing; Zhisheng Zhang; Cheng Tang; Wei Li; Minghui Zhang; ZiYan Huang; Si Wei; Jiawei Chen; Junru Hu; Hongze Zhu; Jianghan Shen; Min Cen; Xinyuan Zhu; Yaxue Zhao; Jubo Wang; Yuqiang Li; Chun-Mei Feng; Zongyuan Ge; Rui Su; Jie Xu; Yirong Chen; Xi Xu; Ming Hu

title: Dual-Valve Infective Endocarditis Caused by Carbapenem-Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii in a Patient with Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Case Report
abstract: Background Infective endocarditis (IE) caused by carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB) is rare and associated with substantial mortality. When it arises on a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), simultaneously involves the aortic and mitral valves, and presents with persistently negative blood cultures, diagnosis and management become exceptionally challenging. Case presentation A 52-year-old man presented with a four-month history of fever and positive rheumatoid factor (RF) and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies, initially raising suspicion of rheumatoid arthritis. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a BAV (right–left cusp fusion), a large mitral anterior leaflet vegetation (1.5 × 1.3 cm), and aortic valve vegetations. Splenic and cerebral infarctions were subsequently identified. Blood cultures remained repeatedly negative in the context of antecedent antimicrobial exposure. He underwent double mechanical valve replacement with vegetation debridement, and intraoperative valve tissue culture grew CRAB, prompting adjustment to a high-dose sulbactam-based regimen. He recovered and was discharged. To our knowledge, this combination of culture-negative CRAB native-valve IE, BAV, dual-valve involvement, and diagnosis solely by intraoperative tissue culture has not previously been reported. This case illustrates a plausible anatomical mechanism linking BAV to concomitant aortic–mitral involvement, highlights the diagnostic value of intraoperative tissue culture and the importance of timely surgical evaluation, and underscores the potential for positive rheumatoid serology to complicate the diagnostic process.
authors: Huangkan Zhao; Shuchun Wang; Di Wu; Zhaolong Cao; Yuhui Zhang

title: Dynamic functional reversibility versus static anatomical burden: a multidimensional prediction model for velopharyngeal surgery outcomes in OSA
abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional static anatomical assessments inadequately predict velopharyngeal surgery outcomes in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). This study aimed to develop and validate a prediction model integrating awake structural burden, sleep-state morphology, and pharmacological reversibility. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 106 consecutive OSA patients (modeling cohort) underwent velopharyngeal surgery following standardized evaluation including the TCM score, polysomnography, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) with dexmedetomidine. Dynamic reversibility was quantified by the proportional change in apnea-hypopnea index following nasopharyngeal tube insertion (ΔAHI-DISE) and oropharyngeal lateral wall collapse patterns. An independent cohort (n = 28) served for temporal validation. Multivariable logistic regression was used to construct a nomogram, with performance assessed by discrimination (AUC), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, Brier score), and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Static anatomical metrics (TCM score) showed modest discrimination (AUC 0.667, 95%CI 0.568-0.765). Dynamic parameters demonstrated superior predictive value: ΔAHI-DISE achieved an AUC of 0.769 (95%CI 0.674-0.864), and oropharyngeal lateral wall response to nasopharyngeal tube insertion remained independently predictive (odds ratio 0.254, 95%CI 0.089-0.688, P = 0.008). The integrated nomogram (TCM + dynamic metrics) achieved robust discrimination (AUC 0.822, 95%CI 0.740-0.904), significantly outperforming TCM alone (DeLong test, Z = 3.42, P < 0.001). Calibration was excellent (intercept 0.000, slope 1.000, Brier score 0.167). Temporal validation showed acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.728, 95% CI 0.535-0.921) but limited calibration (slope 0.524, intercept 0.112), indicating a need for recalibration rather than confirmed transportability; the optimal cutoff shifted from 0.545 to 0.697 in the lower-BMI validation cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic functional reversibility may outperform static anatomical burden in predicting velopharyngeal surgery success. The proposed nomogram may provide preliminary individualized risk stratification, but prospective multicenter validation and recalibration remain warranted.
authors: Jinkun Xu; Zhou Yingqian; Xin Cao; Guoping Yin; Yuhuan Zhang; Yu Sun; Ping Zhang; Jingying Ye

title: Ectopic Prostate Tissue Within the Seminal Vesicle: A Case Report and Literature Review
abstract: IntroductionEctopic prostate tissue confined to the seminal vesicle is an exceptionally rare congenital genitourinary anomaly. Its presentation as a grossly identifiable, mass-forming lesion constitutes an even rarer clinicopathological entity that is almost universally misdiagnosed preoperatively. Given the extreme rarity of this condition, no consistent diagnostic criteria or standardized management protocols have been established.Patient PresentationWe describe a 75-year-old asymptomatic man in whom a pelvic cystic mass was incidentally discovered during a routine health check-up. Preoperative pelvic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) suggested a benign cystic lesion arising from the right seminal vesicle, and the patient subsequently underwent an uncomplicated laparoscopic resection. The gross specimen consisted entirely of a well-circumscribed nodular lesion that had been completely enucleated from the seminal vesicle parenchyma; no adjacent seminal vesicle tissue was submitted for pathological evaluation. Immunohistochemical analysis confirmed the mass as ectopic, hyperplastic prostatic tissue within the right seminal vesicle, with positive staining for prostate-specific antigen (PSA), NKX3.1, and intact basal cell layers, while the seminal vesicle marker PAX8 was negative.ConclusionThis lesion lacks specific clinical and imaging features, and a definitive diagnosis can only be rendered through histopathological evaluation combined with a targeted immunohistochemical panel. Complete surgical excision confers an excellent long-term prognosis. Heightened clinical awareness of this entity is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary intervention.
authors: Xiaojun Pang; Jia Yang; Jiao Peng; Lu Li; Chunlin Li

title: Effects of Osteopathic Manual Therapy on Plantar Pressure Distribution in Adolescents with Functional Lower Limb Postural Deviations: A Pilot Study
abstract: (1) Background: Adolescence is a period of rapid musculoskeletal development during which functional postural deviations may occur without structural deformity. This pilot study investigated changes in the plantar pressure distribution following osteopathic manual therapy (OMT) in adolescents with functional postural deviations. (2) Materials and Methods: Twenty adolescents aged 14–16 years (8 females and 12 males) participated in this study. Functional postural status was characterized using clinical screening and Kineod three-dimensional postural assessment, while plantar pressure outcomes were recorded using the BTS P-WALK platform under static and dynamic conditions. Participants completed 10 individualized OMT sessions over three months, consisting primarily of soft-tissue and muscle-energy techniques. (3) Results: Mediolateral plantar load distribution did not change significantly. Forefoot loading increased from 32.65 ± 12.58% to 39.67 ± 9.29%, with a reciprocal reduction in rearfoot loading from 67.35 ± 12.58% to 60.34 ± 9.29% (Holm-adjusted p = 0.006; Cohen’s dz = 0.842). The right dynamic Arch Index also increased significantly from 13.73 ± 8.86% to 17.37 ± 7.44% (Holm-adjusted p = 0.025; dz = 0.701). Other Arch Index changes were not significant after correction for multiple testing. (4) Conclusions: In this pilot cohort, OMT was followed by measurable changes in the forefoot–rearfoot plantar load distribution and the right dynamic Arch Index. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary functional changes in plantar loading rather than evidence of structural correction or definitive therapeutic efficacy. Larger controlled studies are needed to determine whether these changes are specifically attributable to OMT.
authors: Mihai-Alexandru Citea; Paul Lucaci; Marius Neculăeş

title: Effects of Short‐Term Breathwork on Respiration and Cognitive Performance in a Discrimination Task
abstract: Respiration is a unique physiological process that can operate automatically but can also be deliberately used to modulate the bodily state. Importantly, respiration is deeply intertwined with neural processes, influencing functions from arousal and attention to executive control. Although structured respiration (breathing practice) has been exploited for centuries, the immediate consequences of short periods of structured respiration for sensation and cognition remain poorly understood. The present explorative study examined how brief, 1-min episodes of structured respiration affect respiration and performance in a subsequent sensory-cognitive task. Across two experiments, participants engaged in structured breathing practices that manipulated either respiratory frequency (slow breathing vs. fast breathing) or the inhalation-exhalation ratio (short inspiration-long expiration and long inspiration-short expiration) prior to performing a visual emotion discrimination task. Immediately after breathing practice, participants' respiration deviated from their baseline: Each technique resulted in specific deviations of respiratory frequency, inhalation-exhalation ratio, or the occurrence of atypical respiratory cycles, suggesting technique-specific returns to regular respiration. During the subsequent discrimination task response accuracy and reaction times did not differ between breathing practices. However, we observed transient changes in reaction times immediately following all practices, suggesting a brief facilitation of attentional or sensorimotor responsiveness following conscious breathing. Our findings indicate that even brief, consciously controlled respiration can transiently influence cognitive performance, highlighting the role of voluntary respiratory modulation in shaping brain function and behavior.
authors: Lena Hehemann; Lisa Stetza; Christoph Kayser

title: Embedding far transfer in higher education: A fractal systems model for adaptive expertise and equity in STEM learning
abstract: STEM-focused higher education systems worldwide face increasing pressure to prepare learners for complex, ill-structured challenges, from climate resilience to AI ethics, that demand adaptive expertise and integrative thinking. Yet most higher education environments remain oriented toward near transfer, emphasizing the application of knowledge within familiar boundaries more consistently than flexible reasoning across diverse contexts. This essay advances the Fractal Systems Model (FSM), an equity-centered conceptual framework that integrates cognitive, sociocultural, and systems-theoretical perspectives to examine how higher education systems might be designed to support adaptive expertise. FSM reconceptualizes far transfer as a potentially designable system property shaped by recursively aligned learning processes across educational scales. Drawing on research in cognitive science, situated learning, equity studies, and Discipline-Based Education Research, the model specifies how opportunities for abstraction, integration, and recontextualization can recur across the micro, meso, and macro levels of higher education. FSM further proposes that alignment across these levels may strengthen opportunities for far transfer and adaptive expertise while reducing reliance on isolated courses or selective enrichment experiences. The model offers researchers, practitioners, and policymakers an empirically testable systems framework for examining how equitable learning ecosystems can be designed to support adaptive expertise for the complex challenges of the twenty-first century.
authors: Doug Havard

title: Endocannabinoid-mediated rescue of somatosensory cortex activity, plasticity and related behaviors following an early-life concussion in male mice
abstract: Due to the assumed plasticity of the immature brain, early-life brain alterations are thought to lead to better recoveries in comparison to the mature brain. Despite clinical needs, how neuronal networks and associated behaviors are affected by early-life brain stresses, such as pediatric concussions, have been overlooked. Here we provide first evidence in male mice that a single early-life concussion durably increases neuronal activity in the somatosensory cortex into adulthood, disrupting neuronal integration while the animal is performing sensory-related tasks. This represents a clinically relevant mechanism that was previously unappreciated for understanding impairment of sensory-related behavior performance. We also demonstrate that pharmacological modulation of the endocannabinoid system a year post-concussion is well-suited to rescue neuronal activity and plasticity, and normalizes sensory-related behavioral performance. These findings identify persistent alterations in cortical sensory processing following early-life concussion and demonstrate that neuronal and behavioral deficits remain amenable to pharmacological intervention long after injury.
authors: Jérôme Badaut; Lea Hippauf; M. Malinconi; Brenda P Noarbe; André Obenaus; C. Dubois

title: Engineering Carbon Dots for Cancer Therapy: Active Delivery, Tumor Microenvironment Modulation, and Translational Challenges
abstract: The treatment of solid tumors has long been constrained by two major barriers: inefficient drug delivery and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Carbon dots (CDs) are a class of carbon-based nanomaterials encompassing several subtypes, including graphene quantum dots, carbon quantum dots, carbon nanodots, and carbonized polymer dots. They are evolving from conventional passive delivery carriers into multifunctional platforms that integrate drug delivery, catalysis, and immune modulation. At the delivery level, engineered CDs can facilitate active transport across biological barriers through strategies such as transporter hijacking, receptor-mediated targeting, and biomimetic membrane camouflage. At the therapeutic level, the carbon core structure, surface chemistry, and doped or loaded components can confer diverse therapeutic functions on CD-based systems. Under specific tumor microenvironment (TME) conditions and external stimuli, certain systems can generate reactive oxygen species (ROS), deplete glutathione (GSH), and induce cell death pathways, including apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and necroptosis. At the immunomodulatory level, some CDs can induce immunogenic cell death (ICD), promote dendritic cell maturation, and enhance CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, suggesting their potential to shift the TME from an immune-excluded toward an inflamed phenotype. This review adopts a critical narrative review approach to summarize preclinical advances in the application of CDs for active drug delivery, multimodal therapy, and immune remodeling, and to analyze the key barriers to clinical translation, including the efficacy and biosafety in humans that remain unclear, as well as the in vivo fate and manufacturing consistency that remain to be verified. It aims to provide a reference for the rational design and clinical translation of carbon dot-based nanomedicines. Active delivery is shown as a vertical blood vessel containing multiple red blood cells, with carbon dots near and inside the vessel and an arrow pointing toward an enlarged tumor cell. The section labeled “TME modulation and antitumor immunity” features an enlarged tumor cell containing two vesicles with carbon dots, several cellular organelles, and a reactive oxygen species (ROS) label. An arrow connects the cell to a box listing four cell death pathways: apoptosis, ferroptosis, necroptosis, and ICD. Another arrow leads to a sequence showing an immature dendritic cell, a mature dendritic cell, and CD8⁺ T cells, with arrows connecting each stage. The bottom section compares two tumor microenvironments connected by a rightward arrow. The scene labeled “Immunosuppressive TME” shows a dense cluster of tumor cells interspersed with different immune cell types. The scene labeled “Relatively immune-active TME” shows a similar tumor cell cluster with a different distribution of immune cells.Diagram illustrating carbon dot-mediated active delivery, tumor cell death, and tumor microenvironment modulation associated with antitumor immune activation.
authors: Yalin Wu; Shuang Yang; Zhen Zhang; Sha Tian

title: Engineering a surfactant-free Au@nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dot heterointerface for ultrasensitive electrochemical detection of miR-9
abstract: engineered, surfactant-free Au@nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dot (Au@N-GQD) heterointerface was developed for the sensitive detection of microRNA-9 (miR-9), a clinically relevant biomarker associated with lung cancer progression. The sensing interface was constructed by sequential modification of a fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) electrode with nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots, followed by electrodeposition of gold nanostructures and immobilization of a thiolated DNA capture probe. The synergistic integration of Au nanostructures and N-GQDs provided a highly conductive heterointerface, facilitating electron-transfer kinetics and probe immobilization through Au-S interactions without the need for external labels or enzymatic amplification. The successful fabrication of the sensing interface was confirmed by complementary spectroscopic, microscopic, and electrochemical characterization. Electrochemical measurements using differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), demonstrated a limit of detection of 0.018 aM over a broad investigated concentration range extending from zeptomolar to micromolar levels. The biosensor exhibited high selectivity toward miR-9 in the presence of interfering microRNAs, including miR-21 and miR-223, and enabled reliable detection in spiked human serum samples, demonstrating its potential applicability in complex biological matrices. Overall, the proposed sensing strategy provides a robust, and reproducible platform for sensitive microRNA analysis and shows promise for future applications in lung cancer biomarker detection and point-of-care diagnostics.

title: Engineering organic–inorganic–polymer hybrid electrolytes for transition bimetallic sulfides@MXene nanocomposites toward advanced energy storage and electrochemical sensing

title: Epithelial pSTAT3 Signalling in Crohn’s Disease: Associations with Anti-TNF Response
abstract: Anti-TNF treatment is widely used to treat Crohn’s disease (CD), but some patients do not respond to therapy. Understanding how intestinal epithelial cells respond to inflammatory stimulation and cytokine blockade may help clarify mechanisms underlying differences in treatment response. This study investigated epithelial phospho (p)STAT3 signalling in relation to clinical anti-TNF response using patient-derived colonic organoids. pSTAT3 immunofluorescence staining was optimised in paraffin-embedded organoid sections. Organoids from two non-IBD controls, two anti-TNF responders and one non-responder were treated with butyrate, an inflammatory cytokine mix (CM; TNF, IL-1β and IL-6), and inhibiting antibodies against IFN-I or TNF. Nuclear pSTAT3 positivity was quantified by co-localisation with DAPI. Staining optimisation reduced background fluorescence and improved identification of pSTAT3-positive nuclei. Butyrate combined with CM significantly increased pSTAT3 positivity in all three CD donor organoids compared with untreated organoids (CD1, p = 0.0028; CD2, p = 0.0002; CD3, p = 0.0093). Anti-IFN-I reduced mean pSTAT3 positivity in all five donors, although reductions were not statistically significant in the CD organoids. Addition of anti-TNF reduced mean pSTAT3 positivity in the responder donor CD1 (12.3% to 2.8%) but had little effect in the non-responder donor CD2 (29.0% to 26.5%) or the responder donor CD3 (45.0% to 41.8%). Thus, the two clinical responders showed different pSTAT3 responses to TNF blockade, while the non-responder maintained pSTAT3 positivity. These findings highlight the potential of patient-derived organoids to investigate epithelial pSTAT3 signalling and individual responses to cytokine blockade and anti-TNF response in Crohn’s disease.

title: European Guidelines on Multidisciplinary Management of Obstructed Defecation Syndrome—ESCP, UEG, ESGAR, EAGEN, ESGENA, ESNM and ESPCG
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The goal of this project was to develop a joint European clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis and treatment of obstructed defecation syndrome (ODS), based on the best available evidence. These guidelines are intended to support all healthcare professionals involved in the care of patients with ODS, such as general practitioners, colorectal surgeons, gastroenterologists, gynecologists, radiologists, physiotherapists, and psychologists, as well as to provide accessible information for patients themselves. METHODS: A multidisciplinary Guideline Development Group representing seven European scientific societies and including patient representatives formulated PICO-based clinical questions. Evidence was identified through a systematic literature review and assessed using the GRADE approach. Recommendations were formulated according to the available evidence and, where evidence was insufficient, as expert opinions. RESULTS: The final guideline includes 28 statements (1 moderate grade evidence, 2 low grade evidence, 3 very low grade evidence, 22 expert opinion) covering the diagnosis, conservative and surgical management of ODS, including indications for various imaging modalities, functional tests, and both transanal and transabdominal surgical approaches. Multidisciplinary assessment is recommended throughout the diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. Conservative treatment represents the initial management strategy, with biofeedback recommended before surgery in patients with ODS and dyssynergic defecation who fail dietary and laxative treatment. Surgery should be reserved for selected patients with persistent symptoms after conservative treatment and considered following multidisciplinary pelvic floor evaluation. CONCLUSION: These multidisciplinary European guidelines offer a comprehensive and evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of ODS. They are intended to promote standardized, high-quality care across Europe and to improve outcomes and quality of life for individuals affected by this complex condition. Given the limited quality of evidence supporting many interventions, individualized decision-making within a multidisciplinary setting remains central to ODS management.
