title: Evaluating Perceptions of AI-Simulated Patients as an Adjunct to Peer-Based Clinical Case Practice in Undergraduate Medical Education: A Mixed Methods Survey Study
abstract: AI-simulated patients are an emerging educational tool that may provide learners with accessible opportunities to practise clinical consultations independently. This study explored participants' perceptions of AI-simulated patients compared with traditional peer-based practice, focusing on perceived effectiveness, acceptability, usability, and self-reported confidence. A questionnaire-based study was conducted involving final-year medical students and Foundation Year 1 (FY1) doctors. Participants used AI-simulated patient cases and completed a questionnaire comprising quantitative ratings and qualitative free-text responses about their experiences. Quantitative responses were analysed descriptively, while qualitative responses were examined to identify key themes in participants' perceptions. Participants reported their experiences of the usability and perceived educational value of AI-simulated patients, including their perceived benefits and limitations compared with peer-based practice. Qualitative feedback provided further insight into the perceived advantages of independent practice and immediate feedback, alongside limitations in human interaction and communication. These findings reflect participants' self-reported perceptions rather than objectively measured changes in knowledge or clinical performance. AI-simulated patients may offer a useful adjunct to traditional peer-based practice by providing an accessible and flexible means of practising clinical consultations. Although participants' perceptions suggest potential benefits for self-directed learning and confidence, these outcomes were not objectively assessed. Further research incorporating objective measures of knowledge, clinical performance, and communication skills is required to establish the educational effectiveness of AI-simulated patients.

title: Evaluation of DeepSeek with a RAG-based knowledge base in preoperative assessment for arthroplasty to improve the decision-making accuracy of junior physicians
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing elective joint replacement are mostly elderly individuals with multiple chronic diseases. These patients have a higher risk, so preoperative assessment for joint replacement is vital for surgical safety but remains challenging for junior physicians. This study aimed to evaluate the decision-making performance of different versions of DeepSeek (Chat and R1) and their knowledge base (KB)-enhanced schemes in perioperative risk assessment and their impact on junior physicians' decision-making quality. METHODS: A total of 292 anonymized medical records from joint replacement patients were retrospectively analyzed. A professional knowledge base was constructed using 21 perioperative management guidelines and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology. The performance of four models (DeepSeek-Chat, DeepSeek-Chat + KB, DeepSeek-R1, and DeepSeek-R1 + KB) was compared in ASA scoring, RCRI scoring, surgical tolerance judgment, and risk prediction. These indicators are related to specific decisions in joint replacement surgery, including preoperative optimization before elective TKA/THA, mitigation of infection risk, planning of VTE prophylaxis, and indication for postponing elective arthroplasty, etc. Senior physicians evaluated model performance using a Likert scale. A 5 × 5 balanced Latin square crossover design was used to assess the impact of model assistance on junior physicians' clinical decision-making. RESULTS: No significant difference was found in ASA scoring accuracy (p > 0.05). For RCRI scoring and risk stratification, DeepSeek-R1 models (79.1%-79.7%) outperformed Chat models (56.5%-66.0%, p < 0.05). In surgical tolerance assessment, DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed relatively better performance, with significantly better predictive precision (p = 0.0284) and a lower missed diagnosis rate (p = 0.005) compared to the Chat models. The R1 series also showed higher predictive efficiency (87.2%-86.4% vs. 63.6%-61.8%, p < 0.05). The R1 models showed better performance than Chat models in medical comprehension, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning logic. After adjusting for physician variability and patient case mix, the DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed a statistically significant improvement over independent decision-making (OR = 1.58, p = 0.004), as well as the DeepSeek-R1 and Chat series. CONCLUSION: The DeepSeek-R1 model, with chain-of-thought reasoning, shows a marginal advantage over the Chat version in preoperative assessment for joint replacement. As a cost-effective clinical auxiliary tool, its integration with a professional knowledge base scheme can optimize the decision-making quality of junior physicians, particularly in terms of providing helpful and comprehensive decision support and providing novel insights for individualized assessment in the context of precision medicine.

title: Experience and Operation of Establishing the Korea Biobank Network for Inflammatory Bowel Disease and Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Background: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), is a chronic condition driven by complex interactions among genetic, microbial, immunological, and environmental factors that substantially affect patients’ lives and increase the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). Biobanks support IBD research by providing access to human biospecimens and associated data. This study aimed to describe the workflow and infrastructure of the Kyungpook National University Hospital (KNUH) Biobank, summarize the clinical characteristics of participants and the collection and distribution of biospecimens, and outline future development priorities. Methods: This descriptive report summarizes the collection and distribution activities of the KNUH Biobank from 1 July 2021 to 31 December 2025, including biospecimens collected at Kyungpook National University Chilgok Hospital and incorporated into its collection. Biospecimens and associated clinical and epidemiological data were collected from consenting participants, processed, and stored according to standard operating procedures. Bioresource distribution required formal application and committee approval. Results: The disease-focused collection comprised 1307 participants: 471 with CD (36.0%), 376 with UC (28.8%), 35 with other non-infective gastroenteritis and colitis (2.7%), and 425 with CRC (32.5%). Of these, the mean age at diagnosis was 37.7 years (SD, 23.1), and 849 participants (65.0%) were male. A total of 9577 biospecimen vials were collected from these 1307 participants, excluding the bottom-up collection. Additionally, excluding the bottom-up collection, 2400 vials were distributed through 34 approved applications during the reporting period. Conclusions: This report describes the operational framework and collection and distribution activities of the KNUH Biobank. Future priorities include improving clinical data completeness, establishing systematic longitudinal follow-up, and evaluating resource utilization and operational sustainability.

title: Extensive Pagetoid Spread From Noninvasive Anal Canal Adenocarcinoma Detected by Narrow-Band Imaging: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Dilemma
abstract: A 77-year-old woman presented with a one-year history of erythematous and erosive perianal skin changes. Skin biopsy revealed Paget cells with a cytokeratin 7 (CK7)-negative, cytokeratin 20 (CK20)-positive, caudal-type homeobox 2 (CDX2)-positive, and gross cystic disease fluid protein-15 (GCDFP-15)-negative immunophenotype, supporting colorectal-type secondary pagetoid spread. Conventional colonoscopy showed no distinct anorectal mass; however, narrow-band imaging (NBI) identified a subtle brownish area with irregular microvessels in the anal transitional zone (ATZ). Targeted biopsy confirmed colorectal-type neoplastic cells spreading within the transitional epithelium. Preoperative imaging revealed no definite primary tumor, no evidence of deep tissue invasion, and no metastasis, precluding reliable assignment of a clinical T category. Because extensive epithelial involvement raised concerns about achieving negative margins while preserving anal function, robot-assisted abdominoperineal resection (APR) was performed. Histopathological mapping revealed an approximately 75 × 45 mm lesion composed predominantly of intraepithelial pagetoid spread extending from a small focus of colorectal-type adenocarcinoma in situ located in the rectal-type mucosa of the anal canal adjacent to the ATZ. The neoplastic cells extended continuously through the anal transitional and stratified squamous epithelia to the perianal skin without stromal, submucosal, or lymphovascular invasion. All margins were negative, and no lymph node metastasis was present. The patient remained recurrence-free 30 months postoperatively. This case demonstrates that extensive pagetoid spread may originate from a clinically inconspicuous, noninvasive, anal canal adenocarcinoma. Careful evaluation of the ATZ using image-enhanced endoscopy, targeted biopsy, and immunohistochemistry can help identify the underlying origin. Treatment selection must balance the risk of occult invasion and incomplete excision against the functional consequences of radical surgery.

title: First bite syndrome: A systematic review of clinical features and evidence‐based diagnostic criteria
abstract: BACKGROUND: First bite syndrome (FBS) is a distinct painful condition. Due to limited recognition and the absence of standardized diagnostic criteria, FBS is frequently misdiagnosed. This study systematically reviews the literature on FBS to comprehensively characterize its clinical presentation and propose evidence-based diagnostic criteria using pooled individual patient-level data. METHODS: An exhaustive literature search was conducted in MEDLINE (PubMed), Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL from database inception to March 1, 2026. Peer-reviewed case reports and case series published in English describing patients of FBS were included. Based on critical appraisal of the literature and pooled individual patient-level data, diagnostic criteria for FBS were developed. RESULTS: Seventy-one studies comprising 150 individual cases were included. Of these, 56% (84/150) were male, and the mean age was 50.7 ± 15.7 years. The most common precipitating factor was prior surgical intervention. Pain was typically localized in and around parotid region, triggered by the first bite of a meal, and diminished with subsequent mastication. It was most often unilateral, severe, sharp or electric-shock-like, and lasted for seconds. Approximately two-thirds of patients experienced complete resolution, with a median symptom duration of 360 days (interquartile range [IQR] 90-817.5 days). CONCLUSIONS: FBS exhibits a highly consistent and reproducible clinical phenotype. The proposed diagnostic criteria provide an evidence-based framework and may aid recognition of this distinct pain disorder.

title: Fluorescence-based biosensing with DNA nanostructures and DNA origami: from programmable architectures to quantitative readouts
abstract: DNA nanotechnology and DNA origami have emerged as promising platforms for biosensing by exploiting the programmability of DNA sequences and structural self-assembly. Diverse DNA nanostructures, including three-way junctions (TWJs), dendritic assemblies, hydrogels, and tetrahedral DNA nanostructures (TDNs), provide structurally defined frameworks for the organization of functional components. DNA origami further enables highly programmable and precise spatial positioning by folding long DNA scaffolds with multiple staple strands. Their high biocompatibility and nanoscale spatial addressability allow the controlled organization of fluorophores, quenchers, aptamers, nanoparticles, and other functional components, which is particularly advantageous for fluorescence-based sensing strategies that rely on precise spatial control of these components. In this review, we first introduce the fundamental principles of fluorescence-based biosensing, including Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) and plasmon-enhanced fluorescence (PEF). Then categorize DNA nanostructure-based fluorescence biosensors according to their structural architectures and sensing mechanisms. DNA origami-based platforms are subsequently classified based on their signal transduction strategies. Representative studies are discussed in terms of their design principles and sensing performance. We further critically discuss the remaining challenges, including structural stability, scalability, signal reproducibility, and clinical translation, and provide perspectives on the future development of next-generation fluorescence biosensing platforms enabled by programmable DNA architectures.

title: From Prototype to Sustainable Food Production: Translational Barriers and Design Priorities for Agricultural Biosensing Systems
abstract: Agricultural biosensors could advance sustainable food production by enabling timely detection of crop stress, pathogens, nutrient imbalances, and environmental contaminants. Despite decades of research, however, robust commercial biosensing platforms remain uncommon because analytical performance under controlled conditions does not necessarily translate into dependable field operation or measurable sustainability benefits. Sensors affected by fouling, calibration drift, unstable biorecognition elements, ambiguous biological signals, or frequent replacement may increase cost and material consumption without improving management decisions or reducing agricultural inputs. This perspective article examines the technical, biological, operational, and socioeconomic barriers that limit the transition of agricultural biosensors from laboratory prototypes to resource‐efficient decision‐support systems. It considers performance standards, recognition‐element durability, plant–device biocompatibility, validation practices, user education, and uncertainty communication across open fields, controlled‐environment agriculture, plant wearables, and in vivo platforms. A sustainability‐oriented framework is proposed that connects analytical validity and operational reliability with decision relevance, maintainability, lifecycle considerations, and responsible resource use. Future progress will require biological co‐design, realistic multiscale validation, multimodal data integration, modular and repairable devices, actionable user interfaces, and transparent communication of uncertainty. Agricultural biosensors should ultimately be evaluated not only by their ability to detect target analytes but also by whether they enable reliable interventions that reduce resource consumption, environmental burdens, production risks, and avoidable waste.

title: From pseudo-haptic weight to product meaning: an integrative review of mediated perception, semantic activation, and judgment
abstract: Digital and immersive media increasingly allow people to inspect and manipulate products without receiving the forces that normally accompany physical handling. This creates a psychological problem: how does a digitally generated cue become a felt weight and then an abstract judgment? This integrative review synthesizes a bounded corpus of 56 publications across sensory and consumer psychology, haptic perception, embodied cognition, learned expectancy, semantic activation, and virtual-reality pseudo-haptics. A structured evidence audit separates cue generation, perceived weight, product-specific semantic activation, diagnostic inference, and downstream judgment, while distinguishing direct or near-direct quality evidence from value, preference, comfort, portability, stability, and other outcomes. Within this corpus, direct or near-direct weight-quality evidence is limited to a small subset, so favorable heavy or light effects should not be relabeled automatically as quality effects. The evidence does not support a general heavier-is-better rule. Heaviness can imply solidity, durability, quantity, or premiumness, whereas lightness can imply comfort, portability, user-friendliness, or, in some categories, advanced engineering. Embodied cognition explains why bodily weight experiences can transfer to abstract judgment but is not sufficiently specific to explain category-dependent reversals. Learned expectancy helps explain how prior knowledge can bias perceived heaviness, semantic activation explains how the same percept can make different concepts accessible across product categories, and haptic diagnosticity specifies when weight information is likely to be used. Integrating these accounts, the review uses product-specific weight semantics as an organizing construct for learned category knowledge linking heaviness or lightness to diagnostic attributes; a product-specific weight-quality schema is the narrower case in which those meanings inform perceived quality. Pseudo-haptic methods are theoretically useful because they can vary perceived weight while physical mass is held constant, allowing tests of sensation-to-meaning translation in mediated environments. The review develops a process model and research program that separates manipulation validity, perceived weight, semantic activation, diagnostic attribute inference, and causal effects on judgment.

title: From snoring to obstructive sleep apnea: A narrative review of pathophysiology, clinical implications and multimodal management
abstract: Snoring is a highly prevalent acoustic phenomenon generated by vibration of the upper airway soft tissues during sleep. Long regarded as a benign social nuisance, it is increasingly recognised as a clinically informative manifestation of upper airway dysfunction. In adults it is still defined almost exclusively by subjective report, since standardised objective acoustic criteria remain unestablished; this definitional weakness explains much of the extreme heterogeneity of prevalence estimates, which range from 2% to 83% across studies. Pathophysiologically, snoring reflects an imbalance between a collapsible pharynx and the mechanisms defending its patency. Framing it within the endotypic model developed for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), collapsibility, muscle responsiveness, arousal threshold and loop gain, clarifies why the snoring-upper airway resistance syndrome-OSA continuum holds for many patients but not for all, and why apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) thresholds capture only part of the clinical picture. We argue that so-called "isolated" snoring may be less inert than assumed: respiratory-effort-related microarousals provide a plausible mechanism for insomnia-like symptoms in a subset of symptomatic snorers, while observational and experimental data suggest potential links between snoring, autonomic activation and cardiometabolic risk. These relationships remain incompletely established, particularly in the absence of documented OSA, and should not be interpreted as evidence of causality. Diagnostic assessment should follow a pre-test probability-based, stepwise logic integrating history, upper airway examination, sleep testing and, in selected patients, drug-induced sleep endoscopy and airflow phenotyping, the latter promising but not yet validated for routine use. Management is correspondingly phenotype-driven. We conclude that the field's central task is the transition of snoring from a self-reported symptom to a measurable physiological trait, a prerequisite for precision-based care and for identifying, among snorers, those in whom further physiological and cardiometabolic evaluation may be warranted.

title: Future-Conditioned Representation and Active Sensing in Dynamical Systems
abstract: We show additional future-field predictability in an explicit quadratic expansion of known physical mode amplitudes,and localize forecasting errors by physical component in a controlled Brusselator ensemble. At the critical parameter andhorizon 10, a four-coordinate predictive autoencoder (PRED) gives mean relative L2 field error 0.039 versus 0.152 forthe tested predictive linear references. A quadratic expansion of six physical amplitudes gives lower field error, 0.0229.A nonorthogonal error decomposition resolves the forecasts into critical, fast, uniform and remaining-field components:the quadratic model has smaller uniform and remaining-field squared errors, while PRED predicts the critical amplitudemore accurately. The 27-feature physical expansion uses a larger output-rank allowance and analytical prior, in anexploratory reuse of the original held-out states. Field and linear-coordinate diagnostics support a fast-to-uniform-tocritical interpretation at the sampled horizons in this ensemble. An alanine-dipeptide comparison retains strong linearand torsion-feature references, with a smaller nonlinear margin and an unconfirmed prespecified target-specific crossranking. Separate sensing tests in the Brusselator and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky (KS) systems show favorable, unresolvedor adverse ambiguity-based measurement value, depending on system, horizon and loss.

title: Gate-Tunable Single Ag–rGO FET Platform for Room-Temperature Trigas Detection with a CMOS-Compatible PWM Readout Interface
abstract: Room-temperature gas sensing requires high sensitivity and selectivity, which FET-based architectures achieve through gate-controlled modulation of surface potential and carrier transport, enabling tunable and efficient chemical transduction. In this work, we introduce a smart trigas sensor capable of selectively detecting three target gasesacetone, formaldehyde, and ammonia at room temperature using a single FET by simply tuning the gate voltage. By leveraging gate-induced modulation, this study demonstrates dynamic control over the interaction between gas molecules and the silver-decorated Reduced Graphene Oxide (Ag-rGO) channel-based gas FET sensor, enabling the individual and selective detection of three distinct gases using the single device. Furthermore, the proposed platform demonstrates distinct cross-sensitivity characteristics, wherein gate-bias modulation enables selective discrimination between formaldehyde, acetone, and ammonia under mixed-gas environments. The device exhibits high detection capability with experimentally estimated limits of detection (LOD) of 158 ppb for acetone, 31 ppb for formaldehyde, and 36 ppb for ammonia, highlighting its potential for low-concentration, room-temperature multigas sensing applications. Beyond material and device-level innovation, a TSMC 180 nm 3.3 V CMOS readout circuit is designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso, featuring analogue front-end design for interfacing the proposed gas sensor with a low-power embedded system via PWM signals. The proposed multigas sensor platform and the designed and simulated readout circuit establish a compact and low-power sensing framework, providing a foundation for future studies on breath biomarker analysis and disease-detection applications.

title: GlucoSense: early diabetes risk assessment via fusion of human activity recognition and glucose prediction
abstract: Non-Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Mellitus (NIDDM) is a chronic and progressive metabolic disease characterized by chronically high blood glucose levels. It is a disease with an often asymptomatic onset, which means that a high percentage of affected individuals remain unidentified until quite far in the disease process, thereby underlining the importance of a good, reliable screening instrument for proactive detection. In this paper, GlucoSense is introduced as a single framework for early NIDDM risk stratification by combining Human Activity Recognition (HAR) with continuous blood glucose forecasting using two Graph Attention Network version 2 (GATv2)-based architectures. The first is a HAR module trained with smartphone triaxial accelerometer data that covers 23 activity classes, while the second is a glucose prediction module trained with the OhioT1DM dataset to predict glucose levels for a 30 min horizon. Unlike sequential models, GlucoSense encodes complex dependencies between movement patterns, cardiac activity, nutrition, and glycemic behaviour by modeling relationships in a graph structure. The study was longitudinal, spanning 90 days, with six participants. Three important clinical parameters, mean glucose level, time above hyperglycemic level, and glycemic coefficient of variance were calculated. The system was able to correctly identify metabolically healthy individuals and those with prediabetic patterns. The framework was cross-validated with HbA1c laboratory tests to verify the clinical consistency of the framework. Both modules were benchmarked against sequential, convolutional, attention-based, and graph-based baselines under an identical protocol with five independent runs. The glucose module lowered the root mean squared error from 31.82 mg/dL for an LSTM baseline to 25.60 mg/dL, and the activity module reached 98.50% accuracy, with every difference confirmed by paired significance testing and reported with 95% confidence intervals. Understanding glucose dynamics based on smartphone sensor data and a limited number of physiological markers, GlucoSense offers a non-invasive, scalable and cost-effective alternative to traditional clinical glucose screening. This paper demonstrates the feasibility of smartphone-based longitudinal diabetes risk assessment and motivates future large-scale population studies.

title: Gut-liver axis in liver pre-metastatic niche formation: immune networks, microbial, and metabolic and emerging therapeutic opportunities
abstract: The liver is a leading target for distant metastasis across multiple cancer types, and liver metastasis invariably portends poor prognosis. The formation of pre-metastatic niches (PMNs) within the hepatic microenvironment creates a permissive "soil" for disseminated tumor cells. However, how the gut-liver axis integrates microbial and metabolic signals to remodel the hepatic PMN remains incompletely understood. In this review, we delineate the six hallmark features of PMN assembly, with an emphasis on the complex crosstalk among gut microbiota, their bioactive metabolites, and resident liver cells-including hepatocytes and hepatic immune populations. Notably, these elements engage in a dynamic, reciprocally regulated network characterized by bidirectional feedback loops, rather than a linear signaling cascade. We further survey the emerging landscape of diagnostic biomarkers, including exosomal microRNAs and neutrophil extracellular traps, alongside microbiota-targeted therapeutic interventions. This framework provides testable hypotheses for early interception of liver metastasis and highlights precision medicine opportunities targeting the gut-liver-immune axis.
authors: Leyi Zhao; Qiutong Lin; Danyuan Zhang; Yani Liu; Mingtong Zong; Lingze Xi; Feiyu Xie; Shuyi Song; Peng Xue; Shijie Zhu; Xuelei Chu

title: Handheld enzyme-free photoelectrochemical extended-gate field-effect transistor with a TiS3 photocatalytic interface for urea detection: evaluation in artificial and pretreated human saliva
abstract: Urea is a principal end-product of protein catabolism and a clinically established biomarker of renal function, whose elevation in serum is associated with chronic kidney disease, azotemia, and related conditions. Existing urea biosensors predominantly rely on urease, which entails immobilization and storage constraints and limited long-term reliability. Furthermore, conventional electrochemical and photoelectrochemical sensing platforms generally rely on bulky benchtop instrumentation for signal acquisition and lack an integrated high-gain transduction mechanism, limiting their portability and suitability for compact sensing systems. Here, we report a handheld, enzyme-free titanium trisulfide (TiS 3 )-based photoelectrochemical extended-gate field-effect transistor (PEC-EGFET) that integrates a TiS 3 photoactive catalytic extended gate with a MOSFET transducer for enzyme-free urea quantification. Under illumination, TiS 3 generates electron–hole pairs, and photogenerated holes drive urea oxidation at the TiS 3 /electrolyte interface, modulating the steady-state interfacial photopotential via urea-dependent charge-transfer kinetics. This photopotential is capacitively coupled through the extended-gate connection to the MOSFET gate and converted into an amplified drain-current response. The sensor achieves a 0.5 µM limit of detection (S/N = 3) over a 1 µM–100 mM dynamic range, voltage sensitivity of −18 to −21 mV/dec, and a response time of ∼240 s, with low hysteresis and good reproducibility. Given the clinical relevance of salivary urea as a reliable surrogate marker for blood urea, the platform was further evaluated in artificial saliva and pretreated human saliva as preliminary assessments of its performance in salivary matrices. Spike–recovery experiments in pretreated human saliva yielded recoveries of 94–117%. These results demonstrate the potential of the TiS 3 -based PEC-EGFET as a compact, handheld platform for enzyme-free salivary urea sensing.

title: Head and neck cancer in older adults: biological aging, treatment tolerance, and survivorship
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNC) is increasingly diagnosed in older adults, a population characterized by substantial heterogeneity in physiologic reserve, comorbidity burden, functional status, and social support. Chronological age alone is an inadequate predictor of treatment tolerance and outcomes, yet it continues to influence therapeutic decision-making despite growing evidence supporting individualized assessment. This review summarizes the current evidence on aging and HNC, emphasizing the impact of comorbidities, frailty, comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA), and biological aging on treatment selection, toxicity, and survival. We review validated geriatric assessment tools, including frailty measures and evaluation of cognitive, nutritional, and social domains, which consistently provide prognostic information beyond age and conventional performance status. Emerging data on immunologic aging and other biomarkers of biological aging suggest promising avenues for improving risk stratification, although these approaches remain investigational. We also discuss evidence from contemporary clinical trials, treatment adaptation and de-escalation strategies, implementation science, and the persistent underrepresentation of older adults in oncology research. Survivorship challenges, including late toxicities, functional decline, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary long-term care, are reviewed alongside disparities in access to care that disproportionately affect older patients. Collectively, the available evidence supports a shift from age-based treatment decisions toward individualized care guided by physiologic reserve, geriatric assessment, and patient-centered goals. Future progress will depend on integrating geroscience, validated biomarkers of biological aging, geriatric-informed clinical trial design, and implementation strategies that improve equitable access to evidence-based care for the growing population of older adults with HNC.

title: Hydrogel-Gated Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Wearable and Portable Direct Detection of Aerosol-Borne Viral Antigens
abstract: Direct detection of viral antigens in respiratory aerosols is challenging because affinity-based organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) typically rely on liquid samples. Here, a non-flowing agarose hydrogel replaced the liquid electrolyte to capture aerosols, conduct ions, and support target transport. Before OECT readout, a separate 1-min ring-electrode field-assistance step was applied to facilitate target delivery to the aptamer-functionalized gate. Under the optimized conditions, the device achieved a solution-phase concentration-based limit of detection (LoD) of 1.27 fM and a sample-to-result time of 17 min. The approach was implemented in face-mask and handheld formats with a portable wireless readout system. In nebulization-based tests using SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, the LoDs expressed in terms of the concentrations of the nebulizer source solutions were 6.89 pM and 1.19 pM for the face-mask and handheld configurations, respectively. These results demonstrate that hydrogel-mediated aerosol capture and ionic coupling, ring-electrode field assistance, and OECT transduction can be integrated to enable direct electrical detection of aerosol-borne viral antigens, supporting further development of wearable and portable respiratory screening systems.
authors: Haiyang Yu; Yuhan Lu; Bihan Guo; Jiameng Wang; Ya Zhang; Bingfang Wang; Qiuyu Yang; Lan Shen; Mengtian Shan; Feilong Wang; Daizong Ji; Yin Fang

title: Hydrogel-based delivery of extracellular vesicles for skin wound healing: design strategies, therapeutic mechanisms, and translational perspectives
abstract: Skin wound healing remains a formidable clinical challenge. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have attracted considerable attention as therapeutic candidates for wound repair, given their intrinsic capacities to modulate inflammation, promote angiogenesis, and stimulate tissue regeneration. Hydrogels, with favorable biocompatibility, tunable degradation, and sustained-release properties, serve as candidate EV delivery platforms. This review critically examines the landscape of hydrogel-mediated EV delivery for skin wound repair, progressing from EV sources and engineering strategies, through hydrogel design principles and crosslinking modalities, to the modes of EV-hydrogel integration and the multi-dimensional mechanisms including immunomodulation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cell proliferation that drive the healing process. Recent advances across acute, diabetic chronic, and burn wounds are evaluated, together with stimuli-responsive hydrogels capable of sensing wound microenvironmental cues such as reactive oxygen species, pH, and matrix metalloproteinase activity to enable microenvironment-responsive EV release, representing a transition from passive delivery toward more adaptive and controlled therapeutic strategies. Nevertheless, the current evidence is derived predominantly from in vitro and small-animal studies and is constrained by heterogeneous EV preparations, insufficient standardization of manufacturing and quality control, and limited clinical validation. Finally, critical challenges including production standardization, scalable manufacturing, and regulatory barriers to clinical translation are analyzed, and future directions for advancing hydrogel-EV systems toward clinical translation are discussed, aiming to provide insights and perspectives for further fundamental research and clinical translation of hydrogel-EV systems in skin wound healing.
authors: Yuqiu Jin; Jun Lu; Jingping Wu; Yi Zuo; Huilan Zheng; Fengrui Cheng

title: Hydrothermally Synthesized SnO₂/Reduced Graphene Oxide Nanocomposite as a Solid- Contact Layer for Potentiometric Nitrate Sensing
abstract: A CTAB-assisted hydrothermal method was employed to synthesize SnO 2 and SnO 2 /rGO nanocomposites, which were subsequently characterized to evaluate their structural, morphological, and physicochemical properties. These nanomaterials were then integrated with ion-selective membranes (ISM) to assess their potentiometric performance for nitrate sensing. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the crystalline tetragonal rutile phase of SnO 2 , with a preferential (211) orientation. Incorporation of rGO preserved SnO 2 crystallinity while enhancing interfacial interactions, as evidenced by intensified (110) diffraction and characteristic rGO peaks. Complementary FTIR, Raman, and microscopic analyses validated successful composite formation. Electrochemical studies carried out using cyclic voltammetry in phosphate-buffered solution (PBS) revealed that rGO incorporation significantly enhanced charge storage and redox behavior due to improved conductivity and surface area. Potentiometric performance was assessed through open-circuit potential (OCP) measurements upon successive additions of nitrate (NO 3 ⁻) ions. The ISM–SnO 2 electrode demonstrated a sensitivity of 0.04703 ± 0.00197 V/decade over a concentration range of 1–120 ppm (R 2 = 0.9879), while the ISM–SnO 2 /rGO electrode achieved a higher sensitivity of 0.06379 ± 0.00486 V/decade and an extended detection range up to 240 ppm (R 2 = 0.9718). This enhancement is attributed to the synergistic effect of rGO, which facilitates efficient ion-to-electron transduction and accelerates nitrate reduction. The TDAN-based ISM enabled selective nitrate extraction via electrostatic and hydrogen-bond interactions, followed by electrochemical reduction at the rGO-enhanced SnO 2 interface. These findings highlight the ISM-SnO 2 /rGO platform as a promising candidate for sensitive and selective electrochemical nitrate detection in environmental and biomedical applications.
authors: Percy J. Sephra; Tharini Chandrapragasam

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Modern Healthcare Technology: Applications, Challenges and Future Perspectives
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from being primarily a subject of computational research to becoming an increasingly visible part of modern healthcare. The change has been driven by the rapid growth of digital health records, medical imaging, genomic information, wearable devices and other sources of health-related data. These developments have created opportunities for computational methods to assist with tasks that are difficult to perform efficiently through conventional approaches alone. Machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision and, more recently, generative AI are now being investigated across a broad range of healthcare applications. The influence of AI is particularly evident in medical imaging, disease prediction, clinical decision support, drug discovery, pharmacovigilance, personalized medicine and remote patient monitoring. In pharmaceutical research, machine-learning approaches can be used to explore chemical and biological datasets, predict molecular properties and support the identification and optimization of potential drug candidates. However, the transition from a promising computational result to a clinically useful product is not straightforward. AI systems may perform differently when applied to populations, healthcare environments or datasets that differ from those used during development. Problems related to data quality, bias, interpretability, privacy and cybersecurity therefore remain important. The rapid emergence of generative AI has further broadened the discussion. Large language and multimodal models can summarize information, assist with documentation, support research activities and interact with users through natural language. At the same time, these systems may produce information that is incomplete or factually incorrect, and their apparently confident responses can make such errors difficult to recognize. The World Health Organization has consequently emphasized the importance of human rights, transparency, accountability, safety and appropriate governance in the development and use of AI for health. This review examines the current role of AI in modern healthcare technology, with particular attention to diagnosis, medical imaging, drug discovery, precision medicine, pharmaceutical care, telemedicine, wearable technologies, healthcare management and generative AI. The major limitations and ethical and regulatory concerns are also discussed. Rather than viewing AI as a substitute for healthcare professionals, the review considers a model in which computational systems and healthcare professionals work together, with clinical judgment and patient interests remaining central to healthcare decisions.

title: Impact of Patient Demographics and Platelet‐Rich Plasma (PRP) Composition on Clinical Outcomes Following PRP Injections for Musculoskeletal Conditions: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background and/or Objectives: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) face significant health disparities partly due to inadequate provider training, leading to unmet functional needs.Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) is wellpositioned to address these gaps through functionfocused, patient-centered care; however, IDD remains underrepresented in medical education.Special Olympics MedFest provides a structured service-learning opportunity through pre-participation sports physicals, exposing students to functional assessment and adaptive care.This study evaluated the impact of MedFest on medical students' perceptions of disability, clinical confidence, and understanding of function-based care, as well as its influence on professional identity.Design: Single-group retrospective pre-post mixedmethods study Setting: Community-based Special Olympics MedFest events. Participants: Medical students at a single institution (n=8).Interventions: Students completed supervised preparticipation sports physicals emphasizing functional assessment and adaptive sports participation, followed by retrospective pre-post surveys.Main Outcome Measures: Quantitative data from preand post-MedFest Likert-scale surveys assessed clinical confidence, perceptions of disability, awareness of functional and healthcare access barriers, confidence in performing sports physicals, and applicability of function-based skills to future practice.Qualitative data from narrative responses were analyzed using thematic analysis.Results: MedFest participation significantly improved medical students' confidence in interacting with and providing care for individuals with IDD (p < 0.05).A majority of participants (87.5%) identified gaps in IDD training, and all participants (100%) somewhat or strongly agreed they would apply skills learned at MedFest in future clinical practice.Qualitative analysis identified four themes: (1) increased clinical confidence, tempered by recognition that longitudinal exposure is needed to build preparedness; (2) enhanced communication and adaptive examination skills; (3) recognition of gaps in IDD education and the value of hands-on training; and (4) increased motivation to care for individuals with disabilities.Conclusions: Special Olympics MedFest is a highimpact service-learning model that introduces core PM&R principles of function, adaptability, and participation, while fostering clinical confidence, communication skills, and interest in rehabilitation-focused care.
authors: Jarod M. Carol; Yzen Al-Marrawi; Lindsay Jordan; Joseph Solomon; Aaron Powell; Thomas Nabity

title: Implantable sensors in modern healthcare: advances, clinical applications, and future directions
abstract: Implantable sensors are emerging as powerful tools for continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and biochemical parameters, thus facilitating improved disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and personalized healthcare. Recent advances in microelectronics, materials science, and wireless technologies have accelerated the development of miniaturized implantable devices with enhanced sensitivity, biocompatibility, and long-term operational stability. This review outlines the fundamental principles and major categories of implantable sensors, including biochemical, electrophysiological, pressure, and temperature sensing systems. Particular attention is given to material selection, biointerface engineering, wireless communication, data processing, and integration with biological environments. Current applications in chronic disease management, cardiovascular monitoring, neuroengineering, and precision medicine are highlighted alongside key challenges related to biofouling, immune responses, power supply, device reliability, and data security. Ethical, regulatory, and clinical translation considerations are also examined. Finally, emerging trends in smart materials, self-powered platforms, and intelligent implantable systems are discussed, emphasizing their potential to advance next-generation healthcare technologies.
authors: Ayman Helmy Kamel; Heba M. Hashem

title: Incidence and Distribution of Early Postoperative Fever in Three Hospitals in Al-Muthanna Governorate, Iraq: A Prospective Multicenter Exploratory Study
abstract: Background: Early postoperative fevers are common and are often due to an inflammatory response related to surgical tissue injury rather than infection. However, the frequency rates vary according to patient population, procedure type, definition of fever and intensity of monitoring. In a purpose to estimate the incidence and distribution of fever within the first 48 h after surgery, this study gathered knowledge at three hospitals in southern Iraq. Methods: A multicenter single-arm prospective observational study of 98 patients on elective or emergency surgery was undertaken from 10 December 2021 to 10 April 2022. Body temperature (°C) was measured at least twice daily on postoperative days 1 and 2 with standardized electronic thermometer orally. Fever was defined as any oral temperature of ≥38·0 °C within 48 h. Frequencies, percentages and Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were used to summarize results. All analyses were descriptive for procedures and ages with small strata; sex differences tested using Fisher's exact test. Results: Early postoperative fever developed in 32 of 98 patients (32.7%; 95% CI 24.2–42.4). Fever occurred in 16 of 54 male patients (29.6%, 95% CI 19.1–42.8) and in 16 of 44 female patients (36·4%,95% CI23.8–51.1; oddsratio 1•36,95%CI0•58–3•17; Fisher'sexactp=0·52). Fever after orthopedic procedures occurred in a maximum of 6/15 (40.0%) procedure groups, the corresponding estimates being: caesarean section 12/31 (38.7%), appendectomy 4/14 (28.6%), cholecystectomy 2/7 (28.6%); hernia repair 3/14 (21.4%); and other procedures; both [0/10] [0%). The confidence intervals were generally wide, reflecting a large degree of imprecision. Conclusions: About one third of the patients developed fever in 48 h after surgery. The differences across procedures were exploratory and equivocal, and the study did not identify independent predictors of fever. Recommendations for local diagnostic or management algorithms will need further evidence from larger procedure-specific studies that have used standardized temperature measurement and collected perioperative confounders. title: Individualizing Diagnosis and Management of Stress Urinary Incontinence in Neurogenic Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI), defined as involuntary leakage with effort, exertion, sneezing, or coughing, remains a significant cause of morbidity. While well characterized in the general population, SUI in the setting of neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction (NLUTD) poses unique diagnostic and management challenges. This review outlines sex-specific epidemiology, diagnostic strategies, and evolving management approaches for SUI in NLUTD, emphasizing individualized and mechanism-based care. RECENT FINDINGS: Incontinence prevalence varies by neurologic diagnosis, with estimates ranging from 23.6% in patients who suffered from stroke to over 50% in patients with spinal cord injury (SCI) and multiple sclerosis (MS). The underlying pathophysiology is highly variable, with neurologic disease influencing detrusor and sphincter function in unpredictable ways. Urodynamic studies have proven especially valuable in this population for distinguishing between sphincteric incompetence and detrusor-driven incontinence, guiding treatment decisions that help safeguard renal function. Noninvasive strategies, including pelvic floor therapy, mechanical devices, and limited pharmacologic options, offer modest benefit and often are constrained by neurologic deficits. Surgical interventions, such as urethral slings, artificial urinary sphincters (AUS), and, in select salvage cases, bladder neck closure, remain central for refractory disease. Recent multicenter studies highlight variable outcomes, with AUS demonstrating durable efficacy, while urethral slings remain appropriate in carefully selected patients with variable anatomy.
authors: Amir A. Feinberg; George E. Koch; Hiren V. Patel; Courtenay Kathryn Moore; Iryna M. Crescenze

title: Inguinoscrotal Herniation of the Urinary Bladder Presenting With Obstructive Uropathy: A Rare but Important Diagnostic Consideration
abstract: Bladder involvement within an inguinal hernia is rare, present in fewer than 4% of cases, and is seldom recognised before operation. When the herniated segment is large it can produce serious morbidity, including obstructive uropathy and deteriorating renal function, so timely recognition is important both to avoid intraoperative bladder injury and to reverse renal compromise. We report a 71-year-old man with a longstanding right scrotal swelling, nocturnal urinary leakage, an obligatory seated voiding posture, and rapidly worsening renal function. Ultrasound demonstrated a large pelvic fluid collection extending into the scrotum, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) confirmed a right inguinoscrotal hernia containing most of the urinary bladder with bilateral ureteric compression at the vesicoureteric junctions and consequent hydronephrosis. The estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) fell from 78 to 48 mL/min/1.73 m² with a corresponding rise in serum creatinine, indicating acute kidney injury. Urethral catheterisation drained a large residual volume, produced immediate decompression and a striking reduction in scrotal swelling, and served as a useful early diagnostic sign. The patient underwent urgent open right inguinal hernia repair; operative findings showed coexisting direct and indirect components, with the bladder lying within the direct defect. The bladder was reduced without resection, the posterior wall reconstructed, and a polypropylene mesh placed, with intraoperative cystography confirming bladder integrity. Recovery was uneventful and renal function had normalised by eight months with no recurrence. This case is instructive because it links a frequently overlooked anatomical problem to a reversible cause of renal failure, and it reinforces the value of CT in delineating hernia contents and protecting the bladder during repair. The principal learning points are to suspect bladder herniation in elderly, obese men with large inguinal hernias and atypical urinary symptoms such as positional voiding, to obtain CT when urinary features accompany a groin hernia, and to recognise that prompt decompression and repair can restore both urinary and renal function.

title: Intelligent Hydrogel Sensors for Health Monitoring and Therapeutic Intervention: From Material Design to Integrated Diagnosis and Treatment
abstract: Intelligent hydrogel sensors are integrated sensing devices employing stimuli-responsive hydrogels as the core functional sensing layers. Featuring tissue-mimetic mechanical flexibility, superior biocompatibility, and dynamic stimulus responsiveness, they fundamentally resolve the mechanical and biological interfacial mismatch between traditional rigid electronics and soft living tissues, providing new avenues for in situ, real-time, and in vivo physiological monitoring and precise biomedical intervention. This review systematically elaborates the full-scale design logic, multifunctional integration strategies, and cutting-edge biomedical applications of engineered intelligent hydrogel sensors. The material selection principles covering natural, synthetic, and hybrid polymer systems, multi-mode crosslinking strategies for three-dimensional network construction, and functional modification approaches for conductivity, biological recognition, self-healing, adhesion, and antifouling performance are comprehensively summarized. The sensing mechanisms that convert physical deformation and biochemical variations into quantifiable electrical or optical signals are classified and analyzed, including resistive/capacitive, piezoelectric, electrochemical, and optical transduction modes. This review strictly focuses on hydrogel-dominant sensing platforms and discusses their versatile applications in wearable physiological monitoring, implantable in vivo sensing, and in vitro biochemical diagnosis. Particular emphasis is placed on the core role of intelligent hydrogels in constructing "perception-feedback-treatment" closed-loop theranostic systems, which enable autonomous on-demand drug release or physical stimulation in response to pathological signal changes, achieving integrated diagnosis and therapy. Despite substantial laboratory progress, the clinical translation of intelligent hydrogel sensors still faces critical challenges, including insufficient long-term in vivo stability, biological contamination, uncontrollable immune responses, large-scale manufacturing difficulties, and poor performance consistency. This review further outlines future development directions based on artificial intelligence-assisted material design, biomimetic structural engineering, advanced 3D/4D printing manufacturing, and interdisciplinary integration. It is anticipated that intelligent hydrogel sensors will evolve into highly integrated, personalized, and autonomous intelligent healthcare units, promoting the paradigm shift from passive universal treatment to proactive, personalized, and predictive precision medicine.
authors: Di Chu; Qi Hou; Mingxin Li; Yuan Dong

title: Interactive Demonstration of Active Bed-Frame Vibration Sensing for Respiratory Airflow Monitoring
abstract: Respiratory airflow waveform monitoring is a crucial physiological signal for sleep disorders and critical care monitoring. However, current clinical approaches often require cumbersome instrumentation, which limits their practicality for everyday use. We present a non-invasive system that reconstructs an airflow-correlated respiratory waveform across unconstrained sleep postures. Our system injects an imperceptible single-tone vibration into an ordinary bed frame and measures how respiration-induced body-load redistribution modulates the frame’s structural vibration response. A co-designed L-shaped sensor bracket and resonance-aligned excitation enhance sensitivity to these subtle respiratory effects, while a real-time signal-processing pipeline demodulates the measured response into a continuous respiratory waveform.
authors: Jiale Zhang; Shufeng Yin; Lingxiao Yang; Daniel Vena; Pei Zhang; Yiyue Luo; Junyi Zhu

title: Isolated anterior talofibular ligament stabilization versus combined anterior talofibular and calcaneofibular ligament stabilization for chronic lateral ankle instability: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Isolated anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) stabilization is the most common surgical treatment for chronic lateral ankle instability (CLAI), but whether adding calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) repair improves outcomes is unresolved. PURPOSE: The study's objective was to systematically review and meta-analyze functional and radiographic outcomes in isolated ATFL stabilization versus combined ATFL + CFL stabilization for CLAI. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Guidelines to compare isolated ATFL vs ATFL + CFL surgeries, including stabilization and reconstruction, in CLAI. Primary outcomes included the Karlsson score, anterior talar translation (ATT), and talar tilt angle (TTA). All meta-analyses were conducted using Stata® 19.5 (StataCorp LLC, College Station, TX). RESULTS: A total of 353 patients were included: of these, 179 (50.7%) received isolated ATFL stabilization and 174 (49.3%) underwent combined stabilization. Karlsson Ankle Function Score were comparable between groups (p = 0.940). Combined ATFL + CFL stabilization was associated with a significantly lower risk of recurrent instability (OR = 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14 to 0.82; p = 0.002). ATT did not significantly differ between groups (MD = -1.05; p = 0.146), while TTA was significantly reduced in the combined stabilization cohort (MD = -1.52; p = 0.008). CONCLUSION: Combined stabilization is associated with significantly lower recurrence rates and improved radiographic stability. These findings support the use of combined ATFL + CFL stabilization to enhance mechanical stability, particularly in patients at higher risk of persistent instability.

title: Lamas and Doctors: Coexisting Systems of Life Governance in the Ganzi Tibetan Region
abstract: Modern medicine has become an important knowledge system for understanding diseases, treating the body, and determining death. However, in the Ganzi Tibetan region of Sichuan, hospitals coexist with Tibetan medicine and Buddhist practices. Based on ethnographic fieldwork conducted in August 2026, this paper examines how religious and medical knowledge jointly shape understandings of illness, medical choices, and practices related to death. The study draws on participant observation and semi-structured interviews with doctors, translators, local residents and monks. It finds that modern medicine primarily addresses the physical aspects of illness, while lamas and religious practices interpret its causes, timing, meaning, and implications for the afterlife. Translation, divination, and community relations connect these knowledge systems in everyday decision-making. Rather than replacing one another, religion and medicine operate at different moments and sometimes in parallel. The governance of life and death in the Ganzi Tibetan region therefore emerges from their negotiated coexistence, challenging a simple opposition between tradition and modernity or faith and science.

title: Laparoscopic Versus Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy: Outcomes for pT3-4N0-1M0 Prostate Cancer
abstract: Purpose To compare laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (LRP) with robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) for patients having pT3–4N0–1M0 prostate cancer (PCa) in terms of efficacy and safety. Methods Between August 2021 and July 2025, 70 cases with pT3-4N0-1M0 PCa at our hospital were enrolled in this study, comprising 35 LRP cases (LRP group) and 35 RARP cases (RARP group). All patients exhibited preoperative PSA levels > 20 ng/mL and received pelvic lymph node dissection (PLND) during the operation, with subsequent androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) postoperatively. Patients were followed for 12–60 months, with comparative analysis of perioperative parameters, continence recovery and biochemical recurrence (BCR) between the two groups. Results The two groups were well matched for all preoperative baseline characteristics. The RARP had a shorter operative time compared to the LRP (p < 0.001). There were no remarkable differences in estimated blood loss (EBL), positive surgical margin (PSM) rate, complication rates, or BCR between them. However, the RARP group showed significantly better continence recovery at 1, 3, and 6 months (p < 0.05) postoperatively. By 12 months, continence was similar between them (p = 0.669). Conclusion Both LRP and RARP are effective and safe for treating pT3-4N0-1M0 PCa. RARP is associated with shorter operative time and earlier continence.

title: Laparoscopic one-stage repair of concurrent Morgagni hernia and hiatus hernia: A case report and review of literature
abstract: BACKGROUND Morgagni hernia (MH) is a rare congenital diaphragmatic defect that is extremely rare when concomitant with hiatus hernia (HH), and there are only a few cases reported in the world literature. Surgical treatment is the definitive treatment for MH, and in clinical practice, laparoscopic surgery is the first line of minimally invasive approach for diaphragmatic hernia repair. CASE SUMMARY A 73-year-old female patient, with heartburn and occasional dry cough for one year, was thought to have gastroesophageal reflux disease. Preoperative imaging and endoscopic examinations were completed in a comprehensive way, and the diagnosis of right-sided MH, sliding HH, and non-atrophic gastritis was made. She underwent laparoscopic tension-free one-stage repair of both diaphragmatic hernias combined with 270-degree Toupet fundoplication under general anesthesia. The operation went smoothly. To ensure safe gastrointestinal recovery, the patient was kept nil per os with exclusive parenteral nutrition on postoperative day one. Water was permitted on day two, followed by a liquid diet on day three, at which point parenteral nutrition was completely discontinued. She returned to a normal diet within one week. At her 12-month follow-up, she reported zero reflux symptoms, and scans showed no recurrence. CONCLUSION Concurrent Morgagni and HHs are safely resolved by single-stage laparoscopic repair using biological mesh and Toupet fundoplication.
authors: Ze-Lin Xia; Kai-Cheng Luo; Jie Tang; Liang Sun

title: Lead-free soft hybrid materials for piezoelectric sensors: A paradigm shift from toxic lead-based ceramics to sustainable electronics
abstract: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that these materials are commonly made out of lead-based ceramics, and for example, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) contains 60% of lead. Such materials entail great risks to the environment and people's health. This extensive paper elaborates on the evolution of lead-free soft hybrid piezoelectric materials with special emphasis on bismuth iodide-based organic-inorganic hybrids that can be a safe choice of the electronic sensor market of tomorrow. The latest breakthrough research demonstrates that owing to a well-planned halogen bonding between the organic and the inorganic components of the material, there occurs a slight structural instability which in turn opens the way to the improved piezoelectric performance thus making the piezoelectric coefficients comparable to those of commercial PZT with zero toxic lead content (d 3 3 =161.5 pm/V). This review connects developments in sensing mechanisms, material chemistry, crystal engineering, wearable electronics, energy harvesting, and medical implants.
authors: Shivashankar A. Huddar; Bipin S. Chikkatti; Ashok M. Sajjan; Nagaraj Ramalingayya Banapurmath

title: Learning curve and determinants of sentinel lymph node mapping outcomes in endometrial cancer: A single-center CUSUM analysis
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the learning curve of sentinel lymph node (SLN) mapping in endometrial cancer and to identify predictors of mapping failure in a single-center experience. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 59 patients with clinically early-stage endometrial cancer who underwent minimally invasive staging with SLN mapping at Cathay General Hospital between August 2021 and February 2025. Cumulative bilateral detection rates and cumulative sum (CUSUM) analyses were applied to assess the learning curve. Clinical, surgical, and pathological factors associated with mapping failure were examined by univariate analysis. RESULTS: . Endometrioid histology comprised 95% of cases, and 81% were 2023 FIGO stage I. The overall detection rate was 92.3%, with bilateral mapping in 69.5%, unilateral mapping in 23.7%, and complete failure in 6.8%. Bilateral detection improved from 65% in the early phase (cases 1-20) to 72% in the late phase (cases 21-59). CUSUM indicated proficiency after ∼38 cases, with stabilization projected at ∼65 cases. Observed mapping failures were often associated with inadequate dye migration or empty specimens. Adnexal adhesions showed a borderline association with bilateral mapping failure (p = 0.080), whereas age, BMI, histologic grade, lymphovascular invasion, and stage were not significant. CONCLUSION: SLN mapping in endometrial cancer exhibits a distinct learning curve, with proficiency achieved after approximately 40-65 cases. Adhesions encountered during surgery, particularly adnexal adhesions, may represent a key technical barrier, underscoring the importance of structured training, standardized protocols, and meticulous surgical management to optimize mapping outcomes.
authors: Wei-An Chen; Yu-Ju Tseng; Chih‐Ming Ho; Tsai-Yen Chien; Tzu-Hao Chang; Chia-Yen Huang

title: Local processors: Active dendrites and artificial intelligence
abstract: Neuroscience and artificial intelligence have been closely connected for over a century, with each field influencing the other. Modern artificial intelligence systems rely almost exclusively on the point-neuron model, where inputs are linearly summed and passed through a global activation function. Although highly successful, this architecture differs substantially from neural computation that occurs in the brain, and current leading models require massive infrastructure consuming megawatts of power, which contrasts to the brain's remarkable efficiency. One underexplored source of biologically inspired computational principles lies in the dendrites of pyramidal neurons. This review examines the electrical properties of active dendrites and how they could inform the next generation of artificial intelligence architectures. We describe how dendrites can function as semi-independent computational subunits, generating local nonlinear events that implement coincidence detection, signal amplification, and logical operations within a single neuron. We discuss how the structural segregation of different dendritic compartments provides a biologically grounded alternative to global error backpropagation through local credit assignment. We further examine how activity-dependent spine growth and pruning support continual learning without catastrophic forgetting, and how the spatiotemporal selectivity of dendritic integration gives rise to sparse, energy-efficient representations. Together, dendritic computation represents a potential blueprint for artificial intelligence architectures that are adaptive, context-aware, and energetically frugal.
authors: Yi Hu; Nicholas S. Glatz; Lucy M. Palmer

title: Low‐Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review
abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations. STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used. ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence. DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.
authors: Switinder Singh Ghotra; Cláudia Sà dos Reis; A. McGee; Jonathan P McNulty

title: METAPHORICAL CONCEPTUALIZATION IN WHY AI IS INCREDIBLY SMART AND SHOCKINGLY STUPID: A SEMANTIC ANALYSIS
abstract: This study explores how artificial intelligence (AI) is conceptualized through metaphors in Yejin Choi’s TED Talk, Why AI Is Incredibly Smart and Shockingly Stupid. Based on Conceptual Metaphor Theory, it identifies metaphorical expressions, examines their underlying conceptual mappings, and analyzes how they shape representations of AI and its relationship with human cognition. A qualitative descriptive approach was employed by repeatedly examining the complete transcript, including the question-and-answer session. Expressions whose contextual meanings differed from their basic meanings were identified and analyzed in terms of their source and target domains. The analysis revealed twelve conceptual metaphors, including Ai is a giant, AI development is warfare, common sense is dark matter, achieving common sense AI is a moonshot, and ai learning is human education. Collectively, these metaphors portray AI as powerful but imperfect, while human cognition remains the primary reference for evaluating its abilities and limitations. The findings contribute to cognitive linguistics, particularly semantics, metaphor studies, and discourse analysis, by demonstrating how complex technological concepts are communicated through familiar experiences. This study also expands research on conceptual metaphors in TED Talks, which has predominantly examined religious, legal, and educational discourse, by focusing on artificial intelligence.

title: MRI Alzheimer Disease recognition Using 2D DWT and Multi-Dimensional CNN
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects memory, cognition, and behavior, representing that leads to dementia with older adults. AD detection is performed using various deep learning models applied to magnetic resonance images (MRI). The feature vector is extracted by using 2D discrete wavelet transformation (DWT) to capture approximation, horizontal, vertical, and diagonal coefficients of each image. Then 1D, 2D, and 3D deep learning models are employed, and their performance is evaluated and compared using evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score. The 1D model included 1D convolutional neural network (CNN), while 2D CNN, CNN combined with long short-term memory (CNN+LSTM), ResNet-18, ResNet-34, and MobileNetV1 architectures are also implemented. 3D CNN and 3D CNN+LSTM are used for 3D models. Experimental results showed that the 3D-CNN model outperforms all other architectures because it uses the approximation horizontal, vertical, and diagonal components of 2D DWT as one input block, achieving an accuracy of 99.88%, precision of 99.66%, sensitivity of 99.89%, specificity of 99.86%, and an F1-score of 99.76%.
