title: Making Smart Homes Fit for Autistic Children: Family Work and Monitored Independence
abstract: General-purpose smart-home technologies are increasingly present in family life, yet how they support or disrupt autistic children and families with autistic children remains underexamined. We conducted a multi-source qualitative study drawing on five caregiver interviews, Xiaohongshu (also known internationally as RedNote) posts explicitly situated in autism contexts, and contextual posts from Xiaohongshu and Weibo. We find that families create support for autistic children by adapting environmental outputs, prompts, and interaction channels, while sensory intensity, communicative rules, and opaque operating states can turn the same technologies into barriers. Support also depends on continuing family work, including translation, configuration, modification, maintenance, and boundary-setting. Remote monitoring enables conditional independence while generating tensions among safety, privacy, and control. We contribute three concepts, including relational fit, family work as support infrastructure, and monitored independence, for understanding accessible domestic technology. We derive design implications for adjustable interaction, legible and recoverable failure, lower-burden configuration, and negotiable monitoring.
authors: Tingting Xiang; Weihan Jiang; Hrishitva Patel; Haiqi Shen; Tianzhi He; Kyrie Zhou

title: Making sense of endometriosis care: an interpretative phenomenological analysis of gender diverse people with endometriosis in the UK
abstract: Background: Gender-diverse people with endometriosis in the United Kingdom (UK) encounter prolonged diagnostic pathways and barriers to accessing appropriate healthcare. However, research examining their experiences of endometriosis care remains limited. Materials and methods: In-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted with five gender-diverse people who had accessed endometriosis care in the UK. Data were analysed using interpretative phenomenological analysis (IPA). Results: Two overarching themes were developed, each comprising two subthemes. The first, negotiating legitimacy under conditions of systemic rigidity, comprised systemic rigidity and anticipatory identity management and clinicians as gatekeepers of legitimacy and autonomy. The second, the psychological burden of navigating healthcare, comprised embodied and emotional consequences of navigating care and self-advocacy as dependent on emotional, cognitive and social resources. Participants described inflexible, cisnormative healthcare that constrained their autonomy and access to appropriate care. Previous experiences of invalidation and anticipated stigma contributed to identity concealment and heightened self-monitoring. Although diagnosis provided some participants with relief and validation, it did not guarantee that their experiences would subsequently be recognised or believed, making continued self-advocacy necessary. Conclusion: Structural and interpersonal healthcare processes may reinforce minority stress and contribute to inequities in endometriosis care for gender-diverse people. The findings support the development of more inclusive, gender-affirming and patient-centred endometriosis services.
authors: Zofia Szaprowska; Daniel Gaffiero

title: Matrix-aware 2D field-effect biosensing of cardiac troponin I using complementary ion-sensitive transduction
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for rapid, sensitive and reliable detection of cardiac injury at the point of care. Here, we develop a dual-sensor platform that combines an aptamer-functionalized molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) field-effect transistor (2D-FET) with a graphene-based ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) for the detection of cardiac troponin I (Trop-I) in complex biological matrices. The atomically thin MoS2 channel enables highly sensitive detection of Trop-I, achieving a limit of detection of 0.001 ng mL-1. However, the high ionic strength of serum substantially attenuates the field-effect response, resulting in approximately 80% degradation of the sensor response. To address this matrix effect, the ISFET is employed as a secondary sensor to characterize the ionic environment of the sample. Machine-learning-assisted integration of the 2D-FET and ISFET responses is investigated as a strategy for compensating serum-induced signal distortion and recovering key electrical figures of merit extracted from the 2D-FET transfer characteristics, including maximum on-state current (Ids_max), subthreshold slope (SS) and transconductance (gm). This dual-sensor architecture combines molecular recognition, high analytical sensitivity and matrix-aware electrical signal correction, providing a potential pathway towards more reliable FET-based biomarker detection in complex biological fluids. The approach may further enable multiplexed detection of cardiac biomarkers through incorporation of target-specific aptamers, offering potential for broader assessment of cardiac stress and myocardial injury risk.
authors: Subhabrata Das; Bharti; Babulu Pradhan; Abhishek R Nath; Kashish Sapra; Jaydeep sharma; Vijayender Bhalla; Satyaprakash Sahoo; Manish Mathew; Md. Ehesan Ali; Kaushik Ghosh

title: Mechanotransduction in breast cancer and implications for preclinical modeling
abstract: Breast cancer remains a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, representing the most frequently diagnosed new cancer of 2024. Despite overall improvements in survival, women of African ancestry experience disproportionately higher rates of aggressive subtypes and adverse outcomes, signifying persistent biological and clinical gaps. Mechanotransduction, the process by which cells sense and respond to mechanical cues, regulates mammary homeostasis, tumor progression, metastatic dissemination, and therapeutic response. However, its context-dependent and bidirectional roles remain incompletely resolved, and reproducing biomechanical environments in preclinical models remains a substantial challenge. This review synthesizes current understandings of canonical and cancer-associated mechanotransduction in breast tissue, including cell-extracellular matrix (ECM) and cell-cell adhesions, mechanosensitive ion channels, glycocalyx remodeling, cytoskeletal dynamics, nuclear force transmission, and mechanosensitive transcription. It further examines how ECM stiffness, viscoelasticity, ligand availability, collagen architecture, tensile and compressive stresses, and stromal and immune cell activity influence invasion, metastasis, and treatment resistance. Ancestry-associated stromal, molecular, and structural variations are considered as a critical motivation, but remain incompletely characterized as sources of ancestry-dependent heterogeneity. Thus, this review explores mechanotransduction as a framework for assessing proliferation and metastasis mechanisms through two-dimensional culture, three-dimensional matrices, spheroids, organoids, co-cultures, bioreactors, organ-on-a-chip systems, bioprinting, animal models, and computational approaches for their capacity to reproduce these processes. We ultimately propose an iterative design-build-validate framework that links empirically derived mechanical and molecular measurements to model selection, construction, and multilevel validation. Integrating mechanobiological heterogeneity into rigorously benchmarked models could improve understanding of metastatic progression, reveal context-dependent therapeutic resistance, and support more representative and patient-informed breast cancer research.
authors: Matthew D Harrington; Jinghui Sun; Grayson Whitten; Hai Yao; Heather W. Dunn

title: Model-Free Runtime Measurement of Task-Relevant Information
abstract: Autonomous systems increasingly monitor physical kinematics, environmental states and task completion outcomes. While existing work provides methods to plan information seeking actions and interpret acquired observations, current approaches do not monitor whether the live process of information gathering is functioning properly. Consequently, such systems can remain operationally active without resolving outstanding mission requirements. To address this limitation, we introduce Acquisition-State Telemetry (AST), a model free architecture that evaluates ongoing information acquisition from observable evidence relative to declared task requirements. Specifically, a domain interface maps raw observations into task resolution coordinates and normalized comparative representations, which are processed by a fixed causal monitor. This monitor emits two continuous real time signals that quantify (i) prospective progress across unresolved requirements and (ii) informational friction generated when recurrent evidence yields negligible informational gain. We evaluated a single, unadjusted monitor configuration across eight diverse domains including search and rescue dialogue, spatial grid exploration, hierarchical capability acquisition, continuous robotic manipulation, and probabilistic intent estimation. We show that across these domains the friction channel distinguished unproductive stagnation from purposeful exploration prior to task completion, while remaining muted during post completion activity. Furthermore, in closed loop reinforcement learning experiments under early termination constraints, we demonstrate that penalizing informational friction allowed agents to sustain high mission success, whereas unpenalized policies and baselines with matched operational costs failed to complete required tasks.
authors: Δημήτρης Παναγόπουλος; Adolfo Perrusquía; Yang Xing; Weisi Guo

title: MultiViewDx: Evidence-Linked Multi-View Clinical Diagnosis
abstract: Medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can perform well on existing medical visual question answering (MedVQA) benchmarks, but their training data often does not match clinical diagnosis. Most supervision is organized around isolated images or short QA pairs, leaving two structures weakly specified: how evidence leads to a decision, and how views, series, modalities, and patient context from the same case are linked. We introduce MultiViewDx, a partly physician-validated multimodal instruction dataset for evidence-linked multi-view medical imaging diagnosis. Multi-ViewDx uses the clinical case as the supervision unit. It links imaging studies with patient context, normalizes heterogeneous reports into an evidence-linked workflow (evidence → findings → differential discussion → diagnosis), and uses a unified image-text retriever to constrain instruction synthesis to source-supported evidence. It covers X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, histopathology, and other clinical visual sources. We fine-tune MultiViewDx-8B-AN and evaluate it on both existing MedVQA benchmarks and real-world case-based diagnostic reasoning. Across four MedVQA benchmarks, it achieves the best average accuracy among compared systems (79.0%), outperforming HuatuoGPT-Vision-34B (66.7%) and Claude3-Opus (55.7%). Beyond Med-VQA, on JAMA Clinical Challenge cases, it receives the strongest overall rating under a physician-designed rubric for key clinical points, diagnostic inference, and evidence grounding. Controlled ablations and clinician evaluation show that both case-level multi-view organization and evidence-linked reasoning targets contribute to the gain.1
authors: Junda Wang; Zonghai Yao; Yujan Ting; Eric Z. Chen; Hieu Tran; Hong Yu; Weijing Huang; Terrence Chen

title: Multiattribute noise in photogrammetric point clouds: A critical review of denoising frameworks and identified gaps
abstract: Photogrammetric point cloud reconstruction using consumer-grade devices has become a widely adopted, low-cost alternative to active sensing, enabling applications in heritage documentation, digital twins, virtual tourism, and serious games. However, the noise inherent in these pipelines remains poorly characterized and inadequately addressed by existing denoising methods. In this review, we systematically characterize photogrammetric noise as a multiattribute phenomenon, encompassing geometric displacement, surface orientation corruption, and chromatic inconsistency. This is further exacerbated by nonuniform point distribution due to occlusions and variable image coverage. These noise properties arise from three convergent sources: sensor-level optical distortions and pixel limitations, acquisition-induced instability and illumination variability, and inconsistent image overlap leading to density nonuniformity. These characteristics are especially pronounced in consumer-grade workflows and are not adequately represented by the synthetic noise models underlying most current denoising methods. Among existing approaches, filtering-based methods are valued for their conceptual simplicity, efficiency, and local applicability, making them the most practical choice for consumer-grade deployment. A structured evaluation of filtering frameworks against the identified noise profile reveals five critical gaps: attribute blindness, normal instability, operational complexity, structural rigidity, and lack of density adaptivity. Optimization-based and deep learning approaches, although conceptually distinct, are limited by data and computational requirements, reducing their suitability for consumer-grade workflows. This study is novel in systematically evaluating multiple frameworks against a photogrammetric-specific noise profile, offering a cross-framework characterization not previously reported. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental misalignment between existing denoising logic and the multiattribute, nonuniform noise of consumer-grade photogrammetric data. They establish the criteria that future denoising frameworks must satisfy to be practically deployable in passive, image-based reconstruction pipelines.
authors: Yun Sin Chong; Hui Hui Wang; Yin Chai Wang

title: Multidimensional Assessment of Structural Joint Integrity via Axis-Matched Response Correlation Enhanced by Time-Reversal Impact Focusing
abstract: The Doctoral Thesis, prepared as a set of publications, develops and experimentally validates a synchronised multidimensional diagnostic approach for structural joint integrity assessment. It integrates paired three-dimensional acceleration measurements on opposite sides of a joint, controlled multidimensional excitation based on time-reversal wave-focusing principles, synchronised excitation and sensing channels, per-axis coherence evaluation, and fusion of directional indicators into a single scalar metric, validated through bolt-torque reduction over eight stages.
authors: Viktors Kurtenoks

title: Nanozyme‑functionalized hydrogel bioinks for 3D bioprinting: Tumor microenvironment remodeling and spatiotemporally regulated cancer immunotherapy
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D)-bioprinted nanozyme-hydrogel composites bridge nanocatalytic therapeutics and biomimetic tumor engineering for advancing tumor modeling and localized cancer treatment. Nanozymes are catalytic nanomaterials that emulate enzyme-mimicking activities while overcoming the instability and high cost of natural enzymes. Since the discovery of Fe3O4 peroxidase (POD)-mimicking catalysis, nanozyme research has advanced from empirical exploration to rational structural engineering for biomedical applications. Compared with conventional delivery vehicles limited by rapid clearance and insufficient tumor accumulation, 3D bioprinting enables precise spatial integration of nanozymes within tunable hydrogel bioinks, offering programmable construction of biomimetic tumor microenvironments (TMEs) and localized therapeutic scaffolds. This review systematically summarizes nanozyme catalytic classification, structural modulation strategies, and biomedical advances, with a core emphasis on state-of-the-art 3D-bioprinted nanozyme–hydrogel composite systems for tumor modeling and cancer therapy. Rationally engineered nanozymes exhibit tunable POD-, oxidase-, catalase-, and superoxide dismutase–mimicking activities, often based on metal-centered electron transfer. Integrated into printable hydrogel matrices, nanozymes achieve sustained intratumoral retention, overcoming the drawbacks of free nanocatalytic agents. 3D bioprinting recapitulates TME heterogeneity by constructing scaffolds with customizable stiffness, redox gradients, and porous architecture, supporting high-fidelity tumor modeling and high-throughput drug screening. In therapeutic applications, printed nanozyme systems remodel immunosuppressive TMEs, trigger tumor ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death via the cGAS-STING pathway, and enable stepwise antitumor cascades to suppress tumor growth, invasion, and recurrence, synergizing with photothermal and sonodynamic therapies. Nevertheless, critical challenges persist, including inherent trade-offs among bioink printability, structural stability, and catalytic performance; insufficient lesion-specific selectivity; and a lack of standardized bioprinting protocols. Optimizing composite formulations and printing parameters will promote the clinical translation of next-generation nanozyme-based tumor theranostic platforms.
authors: Yuan Sui; Yilin Wang; Xinwen Sheng; Chengyun Li; Jiale Feng; Yan Zhang; Chun Yang

title: Navigated robotic guidance for minimally invasive bertolotti resection technical feasibility and workflow evaluation
abstract: Bertolotti syndrome is characterized by symptomatic lumbosacral transitional vertebral anatomy in which an enlarged transverse process articulates or fuses with the sacrum or ilium. Diagnosis can be difficult because transitional anatomy is common, symptoms may overlap with other spinal disorders, and the pain generator may arise from the pseudoarticulation, adjacent disc or facet, instability, or nerve compression. When targeted nonoperative treatment fails, surgical options include resection, nerve decompression, or fusion depending on anatomy and the dominant pain mechanism. Published evidence supports image guidance for localization and confirmation of resection and describes early robotic assistance for trajectory and incision planning; however, evidence specific to robotic Bertolotti resection remains limited. This article evaluates the feasibility of a preoperatively planned, navigated robotic workflow for minimally invasive Bertolotti resection. A framework is presented for preoperative computed-tomography planning, convergent access through a minimally invasive incision, trajectory-controlled drilling of bone-cut trajectories across the transverse processes and pseudoarticulations, navigated osteotomy, fragment removal and verification of complete decompression or resection. Feasibility was assessed by completion of planned robotic and navigated steps, intraoperative confirmation of registration and resection, and review of technical, perioperative, and imaging outcomes. These concepts may improve reproducibility and reduce challenges related to limited visualization and complex three-dimensional anatomy, but do not prove superior outcomes. This paper outlines a novel technique; however, further comparative studies using standardized measures of pain, disability, operative time, blood loss, radiation exposure, navigation accuracy, resection quality, and reoperation rate are needed before the clinical value of robotic guidance is established.
authors: Zachary R. Good; Christopher R. Good

title: Navigating Without a Compass: Chinese Medical Students’ Perspectives on AI in Clinical Training
abstract: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming clinical practice, yet its integration into medical education remains largely unstructured. In China, where AI adoption is accelerating, little is known about how medical students perceive AI’s role or what guidance they expect from educators. This study explores Chinese medical students’ perspectives on AI in clinical training and their preferences for faculty engagement. Methods: Using educational cultural hegemony as a theoretical framework, the research team conducted in-depth, semi-structured interviews with 13 medical students across all five years of training at a medical school in China. Interviews addressed three sensitizing scenarios involving AI for clinical documentation, diagnostic assistance, and learning support. Transcripts were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Four themes were identified: Learning in the Shadows describes how students use AI covertly due to uncertain policies; Trust but Verify captures students’ nuanced stance on AI reliability; The Human Element reveals concerns that AI may erode clinical reasoning and patient-physician relationships within China’s high-volume healthcare system; and Educator as Compass describes students’ desire for faculty who proactively teach AI literacy and model appropriate use. Conclusion: Chinese medical students navigate AI use without formal guidance in an ambiguous space between enthusiasm and caution. They seek educators who acknowledge AI’s presence and preserve humanistic medicine. Findings underscore the urgent need for curricular integration of AI literacy and faculty development, particularly within hierarchical educational contexts. These findings carry implications beyond China’s borders, suggesting that when institutions fail to acknowledge emerging technologies, students adapt independently but not necessarily safely or equitably.
authors: Kezheng Chen; Yubei Wu; Yiling Hu

title: Nursing management for patients with minor papilla stent placement after failed endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography cannulation: Two case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is the standard intervention for pancreatic ductal drainage. Selective cannulation of the main pancreatic duct via the major papilla fails in 5%-10% of cases due to anatomic variants, particularly suspected pancreas divisum, and cannulation often occurs via the minor papilla. CASE SUMMARY This case report describes two patients (a 37-year-old female and a 71-year-old female) who presented with pancreatic ductal dilation and underwent ERCP for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. In both cases, selective cannulation of the main pancreatic duct via the major papilla failed after repeated attempts; however successful minor papilla cannulation and pancreatic stent placement were achieved without intraprocedural or postprocedural complications, including post-ERCP pancreatitis, bleeding, or perforation at the 1-month follow-up. This report emphasizes the critical role of comprehensive nursing interventions throughout the perioperative period. CONCLUSION Preoperatively, nurses contributed to risk identification by thoroughly reviewing imaging and anatomical variations. Intraoperatively, they ensure seamless instrument preparation, timely device exchange, and steady guidewire stabilization, which are pivotal for procedural success. Postoperatively, a standardized “fasting-enzyme inhibition-fluid resuscitation” protocol was strictly implemented to enable early detection and prompt management of potential complications. These nursing strategies optimize outcomes in this high-risk population, offering a forward-looking nursing perspective for minor papillary cannulation, and proposing a nursing framework for such complex procedures.
authors: Hui-Bing Jin; Jin-Hong Huang; Sen-Shi Wang; Shi-Xue Dai; Yue Li; Liang-Fang Li

title: Octopus-Inspired Implants for Rapid Deployment and Active Localization of Biochemical Abnormalities
abstract: Timely identification of localized biochemical abnormalities within internal organs remains challenging, as conventional diagnostic approaches often involve multistep procedures, while implantable sensors are typically restricted to predetermined monitoring sites. Here, we present an octopus-inspired, battery-free implantable sensing platform, termed the Tentacle Wireless Sensor (TWS), that integrates rapid minimally invasive deployment, high-performance wireless electrochemical sensing, and active biochemical exploration. By coupling an ultrathin, magnetically navigable electrochemical interface to a spatially separated wireless resonant module, TWS minimizes the dimensions of the deep-tissue sensing probe while preserving wireless readout functionality. The flexible interface can be deployed through a miniature puncture-based access route within 87 s, enabling immediate wireless biochemical interrogation without additional subcutaneous implantation. The system achieves a stationary pH resolution of 0.1 units and a complete response within 0.609 s to a large pH transition. We demonstrate magnetically guided navigation and spatially distributed electrochemical sensing in abdominal and intracranial environments, including active localization of leakage-associated pH abnormalities and oxidation-potential sensing. This platform establishes a strategy for rapidly deployable, spatially adaptive implantable bioelectronics, offering opportunities for timely localization and on-demand assessment of biochemical abnormalities.
authors: Jing Zhao; Zhongyi Li; Lifeng Wu; Yiqi Yin; Zhejian Feng; Guozhen Shen; La Li

title: Office‐Based Transoral Ultrasonography in the Diagnostic Workup of Oropharyngeal Cancer
abstract: This article demonstrates how to perform and interpret transoral ultrasound of the palatine and lingual tonsils in patients with suspected oropharyngeal cancer. This technique offers a reliable adjunct to conventional assessment but requires substantial operator experience and patient cooperation.
authors: Amalie Hartvig Pall; Martin Garset‐Zamani; Tobias Todsen

title: Outcomes in the treatment of carotid body tumor, 20 years of experience
abstract: Objective: To present the results of the treatment of a series of cases of Carotid Body Tumors (CBT).Material and methods: Retrospective study in which the cases of CBT of patients treated for 20 years were analyzed.The frequency of presentation was analyzed according to the Shamblin classification, the type of treatment used, complications, as well as the results obtained.Results: 55 patients with 62 CBT were included.According to the Shamblin category, we found 4 cases (6.5%) type I, 44 cases (71%) type II and 14 cases (22.6%) type III.Surgery was performed in 64.5% of tumors.The median intraoperative bleeding was 350 ml, while operative time was 120 min.There were 3 postoperative complications (7.5%), which included one Horner syndrome, one superior laryngeal nerve lesion and one stroke.In the rest of the patients, treatment was with External Beam Radiation Therapy (EBRT) or surveillance.Conclusions: Surgery is the best treatment option for CBT, especially in Shamblin I and II.Preoperative embolization was not essential for resection of these tumors.EBRT appears to be the best treatment for Shamblin III tumors.
authors: Arturo Pabel Miranda-Aguirre; Hector Gurrola-Luna; Héctor Gurrola-Machuca

title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with early and locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer
abstract: The European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with early and locally advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were published in August 2025 and were adapted in November 2025 according to previously established standard methodology to produce the Pan-Asian adapted ESMO consensus guidelines for the management of Asian patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC. The adapted guidelines presented in this article represent the consensus opinions reached by a panel of Asian experts on the treatment of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC representing the oncological societies of China (Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology), Indonesia (Indonesian Society of Hematology and Medical Oncology), India (Indian Society of Medical and Paediatric Oncology), Japan [Japanese Society of Medical Oncology (JSMO)], South Korea (Korean Society of Medical Oncology), Malaysia (Malaysian Oncological Society), the Philippines (Philippine Society of Medical Oncology), Singapore (Singapore Society of Oncology), Taiwan (Taiwan Oncology Society) and Thailand (Thai Society of Clinical Oncology), coordinated by ESMO and JSMO. The voting was based on scientific evidence and was independent of the current treatment practices, drug access restrictions and reimbursement decisions in the different regions of Asia. The latter are discussed separately in the article. The aim is to provide guidance for the optimisation and harmonisation of the management of patients with early and locally advanced NSCLC across the different countries of Asia, drawing on the evidence provided by both Western and Asian trials. Attention is drawn to the disparity in the drug approvals and reimbursement strategies among the different regions.

title: Paradoxical pain localization and mirror-image laparoscopic cholecystectomy in situs inversus totalis: a case report and literature review
abstract: Background: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital anomaly characterized by complete mirror-image transposition of the thoracic and abdominal organs. Although laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the standard treatment for symptomatic gallstone disease, reversed anatomy creates unique diagnostic and technical challenges for both surgeons and radiologists. An even less common phenomenon is paradoxical right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain despite a left-sided gallbladder, which may delay diagnosis by masking biliary disease behind an apparently normal pain pattern. Case presentation: A 48-year-old Persian woman presented with a 2-day history of progressively worsening RUQ pain. Physical examination demonstrated localized tenderness without generalized peritonitis. Routine electrocardiography unexpectedly revealed dextrocardia, prompting further radiologic investigation. Abdominal ultrasonography demonstrated multiple gallstones within a left-sided gallbladder, while contrast-enhanced computed tomography confirmed complete SIT. After comprehensive preoperative cardiologic and anesthetic assessment, laparoscopic cholecystectomy was successfully performed using a mirror-image operating room configuration and reversed trocar placement. Despite altered anatomical orientation and ergonomic challenges, the critical view of safety was achieved before clipping and division of the cystic duct and artery. Histopathological examination confirmed chronic calculous cholecystitis. Recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained symptom-free at 6-month follow-up. Conclusion: This case highlights that the principal challenge in SIT extends beyond mirror-image anatomy to include paradoxical symptom localization and altered operative ergonomics. Recognition of laterality disorders, comprehensive preoperative imaging, and meticulous ergonomic adaptation allow laparoscopic cholecystectomy to be performed safely while maintaining the same fundamental surgical principles applied to patients with normal anatomy.
authors: Setareh Mahmoodi; Mehra Fekri; Koosha Sami; Milad Dodangeh

title: Passive Smartphone-Microphone Phonocardiography for Joint Maternal-Fetal Cardiac Well-Being Monitoring: A Longitudinal Self-Recorded Case Study in Late Pregnancy
abstract: Maternal and perinatal deaths are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, where routine fetal monitoring is largely inaccessible. With the prevalence of smartphone as personal assistive gadget, we ask whether a phone's built-in microphone, with no extra hardware or emitted signal, can serve as a software-only maternal-fetal cardiac screening aid when moved from the chest to the lower abdomen? We report a longitudinal, self-recorded case study of a single subject (Z) over the last five weeks of a singleton pregnancy, later delivered at term without complications: 28 short, uncontrolled recordings (rest, morning, post-exercise). Lacking maternal/fetal ground truth, we exploit the prior that maternal and fetal heart rates occupy largely disjoint frequency bands, blindly decomposing a Shannon-energy envelope into two candidate-rate bands, and additionally probe a slower breathing-rate band as a rest/exercise discriminator. A fast, regular, fetal-plausible rhythm was recovered from most recordings and remained essentially unchanged across maternal activity states, consistent with normal fetal cardiac autonomy; a slower, noisier maternal-plausible rhythm was recovered less reliably. Beat-to-beat variability proved largely noise-dominated at our short window lengths, and the breathing-rate probe did not significantly separate rest from exercise; both are reported as negative findings. We position the work within AI for global health: a low-cost screening aid for remote and underserved communities, pending reference-validated follow-up, not a replacement for clinical monitoring.
authors: Muhammad Mahboob Ur Rahman

title: Peroxidase-mimicking Nanozymes for Redox Monitoring and Regulation in Cancer Theranostics
abstract: Cancer progression is closely associated with dysregulated redox homeostasis, including altered hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) metabolism and adaptive antioxidant responses within the tumour microenvironment (TME). These biochemical changes provide opportunities for redox-responsive cancer diagnosis and therapeutic intervention. Peroxidase-mimicking nanozymes have emerged as engineered catalytic materials capable of exploiting H₂O₂-dependent reactions for signal amplification and modulation of oxidative stress. This review critically examines their catalytic mechanisms, structural determinants, and applications in cancer theranostics, with particular emphasis on the relationship between interfacial redox chemistry and biological function. Unlike natural peroxidases with structurally defined catalytic sites, many nanozymes mediate peroxide-dependent reactions through surface-associated redox centres involving electron transfer and reactive intermediate formation. Their tunable composition, morphology, and surface chemistry offer opportunities to tailor catalytic performance for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. By exploiting tumour-associated H₂O₂ availability and local acidity, appropriately designed nanozyme systems may facilitate preferential catalytic activation and amplified diagnostic signals. Therapeutically, peroxidase-like activity can promote oxidative damage in cancer cells, while multifunctional nanozyme platforms may incorporate complementary mechanisms to modulate hypoxia, antioxidant defences, and tumour-associated immune responses. However, catalytic performance and tumour selectivity are strongly influenced by biological matrix effects, tumour heterogeneity, catalyst stability, and potential contributions from dissolved metal species. Distinguishing sustained heterogeneous catalysis from consumptive redox reactions, together with establishing in vivo efficacy, safety, and reproducibility, remains essential for clinical translation. Future developments should therefore prioritise mechanistically validated nanozyme platforms that integrate reliable redox monitoring with controllable therapeutic activity, supporting the development of more effective cancer theranostic strategies.
authors: Cynthia Ezeaniekwe; Natasha Logan; Xiaotong Liu; Cuong Cao

title: Person-centered identification of experimental learning profiles among preservice physics teachers
abstract: School experiments are central to physics education, but preparing future teachers for experimental instruction requires more than procedural laboratory skill; it also involves self-regulation, inquiry orientation, motivation, collaboration, and pedagogical reasoning. Because these dimensions may combine differently within individual preservice teachers, this study used a person-centered approach to identify learning profiles among 218 preservice physics teachers enrolled in a Techniques of School Experimentation course at a Kazakhstani university. Using multidimensional survey data and K-means cluster analysis, four profiles emerged: highly engaged and competent experimenters, steady and competent experimenters, developing experimenters, and low-engagement or struggling experimenters. The profiles reflected a clear engagement–competence continuum, with higher-profile students reporting stronger planning, inquiry, reflection, collaboration, mastery orientation, and ability to connect experiments to future physics teaching. Cluster membership was associated with year of study, expected course performance, and intention to teach physics, but not with gender, prior high-school physics background, or prior experiment experience. These findings indicate that preservice physics teachers in the same methods course differ substantially in their readiness for experimental instruction. The study contributes an empirically grounded diagnostic framework for understanding experimental readiness as a coordinated engagement–competence continuum among preservice physics teachers.
authors: Akmaral K. Sugirbekova; Фарида Наметкулова; Alma E. Abylkassymova

title: Perspective Chapter: Transforming Primary Care – The Role of Physicians in the AI-Driven Healthcare Era
abstract: The progression of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare from narrow diagnostic tools and clinical decision support to large language models and agentic systems has implications beyond technology for the structure of medical practice. This chapter examines the evolving relationship between AI capability and physician function. First, it maps current AI performance against core physician tasks, distinguishing functions with high potential for task-level automation from those that remain physician-led and currently require human participation. Second, it examines the functions that only the physician can fulfill, according to current evidence. Third, drawing on direct clinical and operational experience in primary care, it describes where AI has its most sustained and measurable impact: chronic disease management. Continuous AI-augmented monitoring of diabetes, hypertension, and obesity is enabling a transition from episodic, snapshot-based care to proactive, longitudinal intervention at scale. The chapter presents the AI-native clinic operations and chronic care as an emerging practice and care model and reports early operational and clinical results, with their limitations. The chapter concludes that the physician of the AI era combines three roles: a clinical expert who can supervise and correct AI outputs, an emotionally intelligent relational anchor who can reach what AI cannot, and a practice entrepreneur who can deploy AI platforms strategically to expand care access and improve patient outcomes. It proposes that AI shifts the physician’s role rather than removing it, toward functions that deployed AI systems cannot currently perform; whether physician-led AI integration will reshape primary care remains to be demonstrated.
authors: Li Wang; Dawei Zheng; Cheng He; Xin-Nong Li

title: Photoluminescence-Driven Quasi-BICs in Photonic Nanomembranes for Active Refractometric Sensing
abstract: Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.
authors: Ya‐Lun Ho; Hsin-Chang Lin; Wei-Che Chang; S.-H. Huang; Yen‐Ju Wu; Jui‐Han Fu; Vincent Tung; Yang‐Chun Lee; Kuniaki Konishi; Masanobu Iwanaga; Chun‐Hao Chiang

title: Physical AI for Health and Wellness Management
abstract: As global healthcare faces rising costs and chronic disease, Physical AI emerges as a transformative solution. This book addresses a critical gap in literature, moving beyond high-level theory to provide a comprehensive roadmap for integration. By exploring the why, what, and how of Physical AI, we offer a strategic blueprint to achieve superior clinical outcomes, economic sustainability, and enhanced patient satisfaction in an increasingly complex post-pandemic world. This book first delivers a multidimensional look at the why, what, and how of the field. It examines historical evolution and cross-industry success to establish a solid foundation before exploring the current landscape of digital convergence and practical implementation. Second, the author focuses on economic and clinical sustainability. Unlike existing texts that dwell on abstract theory, this work prioritizes the healthcare value proposition. Readers will learn how to leverage AI to reduce workflow bottlenecks and improve patient access while maintaining a model that is financially viable and scalable for any environment. Finally, this book provides a blueprint for co-design and research. We identify critical success factors necessary to develop suitable AI, empowering readers to upskill in health informatics. This feature provides the tools to adapt relevant theories into high-quality research outcomes that stand up to the demands of a maturing digital health domain, ensuring that technology serves the user rather than complicating the care process. This book is designed to benefit graduate and senior-level undergraduate students, non-traditional community-college learners, and certificate-seeking health informatics and public health students. Healthcare stakeholders, including physicians, medical administrators, CEOs, CIOs, consultants, and IT practitioners, will find guidance on designing effective systems. Additionally, governing bodies in Australia, the EU, and the United States can leverage its strategies to advance computerized medical records and e-health agendas effectively.
authors: Nilmini Wickramasinghe

title: Phyto engineered Ag decorated ZrO2 nanohybrid: A sustainable strategy for sensitive and reliable electrochemical sensing of dopamine
abstract: The detection of dopamine (DA) is of considerable importance because of its essential role in neurological functions and its association with various physiological and neurological disorders. Although several analytical approaches have been developed for DA determination, enzyme-free electrochemical sensors have attracted increasing attention owing to their rapid response, operational simplicity, reliability, and high sensitivity. In this study, ZrO 2 and Ag-decorated ZrO 2 (Zr@Ag) nanostructures were synthesized using an eco-friendly green approach using Ficus religiosa bark extract and employed as electrode modifiers for dopamine sensing. The structural, morphological, optical, and surface properties of the synthesized materials were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and complementary characterization techniques. The Zr@Ag nanocomposite exhibited an optical band gap of 2.3 eV, a zeta potential of −113 mV, and a particle size of approximately 80.1 nm, indicating favorable surface and physicochemical characteristics for electrochemical sensing. The Zr@Ag nanocomposite was integrated onto a screen-printed gold electrode (SPGE) to fabricate an enzyme-free Zr@Ag/SPGE sensing platform. Compared with ZrO 2 /SPGE, the Zr@Ag/SPGE exhibited markedly enhanced electrochemical performance, delivering sensitivities of 80.97 and 1735.63 μA mM -1 cm -2 and detection limits of 0.005 μM (5 nM) and 0.003 μM (3 nM) (S/N = 3), respectively. The improved sensing performance of Zr@Ag/SPGE can be attributed to the synergistic interaction between ZrO 2 and Ag, which promotes efficient electron transfer and enhances the electrochemically active surface characteristics of the electrode. Furthermore, the practical applicability of the developed sensor was evaluated using goat serum (GS), sheep serum (SS), and fetal bovine serum (FBS), yielding satisfactory dopamine recoveries of 98–101%. The consistent dopamine responses obtained in these biological matrices further demonstrate the reliability of the sensor for real-sample analysis. Overall, the green-synthesized Zr@Ag/SPGE provides a sensitive, selective, enzyme-free, and cost-effective platform for dopamine detection, with promising potential for practical applications in biological and clinical analysis.
authors: Lasina Jarajana; Naveen Kumar Kalagatur; Ushakiranmayi Mangamuri; Venkateswara Rao Kalagadda; P. Sudhakar

title: Plasmonic Mediated Atomically Thin Aluminum Quasicrystal for Dopamine Sensing
abstract: Dopamine levels are linked to neurological illnesses like Parkinson's and Alzheimer's. Thus, reliable and sensitive detection of dopamine is crucial for early diagnosis and surveillance of neurodegenerative diseases. Non‐noble‐metal‐based nanomaterials are ideal for light‐mediated sensing of organic molecules. Among these, two‐dimensional (2D) quasicrystal (QC) structures consisting of five elements ( Al 70 Co 10 Fe 5 Ni 10 Cu 5 (2D Al QC)) provide active sites due to their high surface‐to‐volume ratio, making them excellent for organic chemical sensing. Here, we propose a simple, label‐free, spatial self‐phase‐modulation (SSPM)‐based sensing method in liquid form. SSPM‐based time evolution of the diffraction pattern for varied mixing levels of a 1100 ppb dopamine solution shows a shift in the SPR‐activated 2D Al QC nanostructure solution. The 1100 ppb solution shows a different dN / dI value, indicating a change in sensitivity to the nonlinear refractive index and time constant. SSPM is used to demonstrate dopamine‐sensing methods and to perform qualitative and quantitative evaluations. The SSPM‐based sensing has been further compared with other optical sensing methods, such as Raman Spectroscopy, UV‐vis Spectroscopy, and FTIR Spectroscopy. The experimental observations are also explained using DFTB‐based simulations.The current SSPM method can be used for rapid, large‐scale medical diagnostics.
authors: Saswata Goswami; Guilherme S. L. Fabris; Diganta Mondal; Raphael Benjamim de Oliveira; Anyesha Chakraborty; Thakur Prasad Yadav; N.K. Mukhopadhyay; Samit K. Ray; Douglas Soares Galvao; Chandra Sekhar Tiwary

title: Port-Site Fascial Closure in Laparoscopic Surgery: Current Practices, Evidence and Outcomes
abstract: Port-site hernia (PSH) is an infrequent but clinically relevant complication of laparoscopic surgery, occasionally resulting in bowel incarceration, intestinal obstruction, or emergency intervention. Fascial closure is widely advocated for larger trocar defects, although uncertainty persists regarding the optimal diameter threshold, the influence of trocar design and anatomical location, and the benefits of routine versus selective closure. Reported PSH rates vary considerably across studies because of differences in patient characteristics, surgical techniques, follow-up duration, and diagnostic methods. The 2022 European and American Hernia Societies guideline suggests closing fascial defects measuring at least 10 mm, particularly at umbilical and single-incision access sites, while acknowledging the very low certainty of the supporting evidence. More recent comparative evidence has demonstrated a reduction in relative PSH risk following fascial closure, although the estimated absolute benefit remains small and statistically uncertain. This chapter critically examines the anatomical and technical factors contributing to PSH, evaluates contemporary evidence regarding closure and non-closure, reviews available closure techniques and associated complications, and presents a practical framework for intraoperative decision-making. Particular emphasis is placed on integrating the final fascial defect size, port location, procedural manipulation, and patient-related considerations into an individualized approach to port-site management.
authors: Younis Al-Mufargi; Mohammed Al Sibani; Mohammed Al Subhi

title: Portable GMR biosensing with Fe 3 O 4 /PVA–GOx functionalization and machine learning for quantitative glucose detection
abstract: A portable giant magnetoresistance (GMR) biosensing platform integrating an Fe 3 O 4 /PVA–glucose oxidase functional layer, dual-coil magnetic excitation, embedded signal acquisition, and machine-learning-assisted prediction was developed for quantitative glucose sensing. The system exhibited stable concentration-dependent GMR responses over 0.02–0.15 mg ml − 1 . Linear Regression (LR) and support vector regression with a radial basis function kernel (SVR-RBF) were evaluated using development-set analysis, leave-one-concentration-out validation, independent external testing, and prepared-saliva samples. On an independent 10-concentration dataset, SVR-RBF achieved R 2 , MAE = 0.0029 mg ml − 1 , and RMSE = 0.0040 mg ml − 1 , outperforming LR ( R 2 , MAE = 0.0048 mg ml − 1 , RMSE = 0.0059 mg ml − 1 ). In prepared saliva, the fixed SVR-RBF model maintained low prediction errors (MAE = 0.0043 mg ml − 1 ; RMSE = 0.0050 mg ml − 1 ). These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining magnetic GMR transduction, functional magnetic nanomaterials, and nonlinear regression within a compact platform for quantitative glucose sensing, while further validation in authentic biological samples remains necessary.
authors: W. S. Mada Sanjaya; Hasniah Aliah; Edi Suharyadi; Julia Angel; Vandri Ahmad Isnaini; Dyah Anggraeni; Gilang Pratama Putra Siswanto; Rindra Yusianto; Agung Wijaya Temiesela

title: Predictive Structure and Realized Forecast Gain in Nonlinear Fields
abstract: We measure forecast accuracy recovered by changing the readout of an unchanged representation. In a controlled known-mode Brusselator ensemble, replacing affine with quadratic readout lowers mean future-field relative L2 error by 26.83% on 720 new initial states generated after method freezing. The prespecified paired bootstrap interval is positive, conditional on three fixed encoders trained with affine decoding heads. A secondary control retains a 26.69% reduction within the same training-derived four-dimensional output space. This measures a realized deficit of the selected affine reader, rather than the code's optimal decodable risk or total retained information. Physical-component diagnostics locate most of the squared-loss reduction in uniform and remaining-field components. Under this same controlled generation law, a richer known-mode quadratic dictionary has lower mean relative L2 but less accurate critical amplitudes; prior and parameter budgets differ. In a complementary driven lattice, frozen sensor codes and predictors are evaluated on new conditional futures. Conservative lower bounds certify additional information at four ages and fixed-predictor score gains at two, although all four score means are positive. This difference describes certificate resolution at the allocated continuation budget, not an information--utility separation. The contribution is a prospective fixed-code readout intervention, common-output-space control and physical localization of the recovered accuracy.
authors: Rongzhen Dai

title: Primary rectal malignant melanoma: a rare case report
abstract: Primary malignant melanoma of the rectum is a rare and highly aggressive malignant tumor. Its clinical manifestations lack specificity and it is often misdiagnosed as hemorrhoids or rectal polyps, with a very poor prognosis. This article reported a case of a 71-year-old Asian female who presented with changes in bowel habits and hematochezia. Colonoscopic biopsy and immunohistochemistry confirmed the diagnosis of primary malignant melanoma of the rectum, with no primary lesions found on the skin. Imaging suggested a lesion in the lower rectum, and postoperative pathology and immunohistochemistry showed positivity for Melan A, HMB45, and SOX10, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of approximately 45%, consistent with characteristics of malignant melanoma. The patient underwent robot-assisted laparoscopic abdominoperineal resection (Miles operation) and did not receive postoperative immunotherapy; during a 6-month follow-up, no recurrence or metastasis was observed. Literature review indicates that the diagnosis of rectal malignant melanoma relies on immunohistochemistry, the choice of surgical approach remains controversial, and immune checkpoint inhibitors have shown good efficacy in advanced patients. This case highlights the need to raise clinical awareness of this disease to achieve early diagnosis and individualized treatment selection, which may improve patient prognosis.
authors: Yang Xiao; MingWang Li; Xia Ye; Ming Nie

title: Printable inks for flexible healthcare sensors: From materials to device insights
abstract: Printable inks have been widely used in wearable healthcare sensors, and their functions go beyond simply creating conductive or sensing layers. Ink formulation controls printability, film formation, electrical path creation, adhesion to flexible substrates and stability of the process under mechanical strain such as bending and stretching. This review highlights recent advances in printable inks used in wearable healthcare sensing devices including metal-based, carbon-based, polymeric, and biofunctional ink systems. Their merits as well as limitations including high curing temperature, poor dispersion stability, limited conductivity, poor substrate adhesion, and difficulty of biological functionalization will be discussed. This review focuses mostly on the relationship between ink formulation, rheology, printing, printed microstructure, and sensor performance. The existing research usually studies them separately, therefore, making it difficult for comparison between different ink systems and prediction of the performance of devices in real-life situations. Rheology has been studied usually only as a limitation in printing process although it affects pattern resolution, film homogeneity, formation of conductive paths, and repeatability. The commonly used printing methods, particularly inkjet, screen printing, and flexographic printing, are also compared in terms of resolution, material compatibility, throughput, and scalability. Although wearable healthcare sensors have developed considerably, several challenges still limit their use beyond laboratory demonstrations. These include material-related limitations, poor long-term stability, mechanical degradation, biofouling, and reduction in sensor performance over time. Overall, this review highlights the importance of understanding the process-structure-performance relationships of printable inks for developing reliable, scalable, and real-time wearable sensors.
authors: Naveen Bokka; Ankammarao Padamurthy; Tata Rao Lanka; Abhishesh Pal; Prasanth Kumar Enaganti

title: Procedural Compliance and Relational Legitimacy in Sensitive Health-Data Governance: A Case Study of GDPR Alignment in Albania
abstract: Purpose: This study examines whether and under what conditions procedural compliance in sensitive personal-data governance becomes legitimacy-relevant during periods of regulatory transition. Focusing on Albania’s regulatory convergence with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) through Law No. 124/2024 “On Personal Data Protection” (Republic of Albania, 2024), the paper develops a mechanism-based explanation of how consent practices come to carry legitimacy within an organisational setting. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a qualitative case study design using process tracing and analytic generalisation (George and Bennett, 2005; Yin, 2018). A structured governance audit of consent and documentation artefacts is conducted across three analytically defined phases (pre-GDPR, transition, GDPR-aligned). Operational clinic records (N = 29; 2022–2025) are incorporated exclusively for descriptive contextualisation to illustrate the limitations of behavioural indicators within a sensitive and potentially stigmatised service environment. No statistical inference is undertaken in the present study; these records are used descriptively only, and analyses reported in Imeri and Prifti (2026) are not relied upon here. Findings: Documentation structures exhibited increased legal specification, standardisation, and traceability across successive phases, consistent with strengthened procedural legitimacy. Observable variation relevant to legitimacy formation, however, is primarily associated with records that also captured interactional detail, such as documented patient questions, clarification exchanges, and reassurance about confidentiality, rather than with template completeness alone. These patterns are interpreted through Relational Communication and Engagement Capacity (RCEC), proposed as a mediating mechanism linking compliance infrastructures with relational legitimacy. Originality/value: The study proposes a refinement of the Ethics → Compliance → Trust (ECT) framework by further developing RCEC as a candidate mediating mechanism. The findings aim to inform governance and public administration scholarship by illustrating how compliance reforms may translate into legitimacy dynamics under conditions of regulatory convergence. authors: Brixhilda Imeri; Migena Prifti

title: Profiling Autism Through Language: Lexicogrammar, neurocognition, and machine learning
abstract: Existing accounts of language in autism have tended to focus on English and have rarely progressed beyond broad characterizations of pragmatic difficulty. This volume changes both. Drawing on a clinically defined corpus of Japanese-speaking individuals with ASD and combining Systemic Functional Linguistics with machine learning, it identifies 46 lexicogrammatical discriminators of ASD and non-ASD discourse, with 80% classification accuracy. Thirty-eight of these discriminators are interpreted across twelve cognitive-functional domains, including weak central coherence, joint attention, predictive processing, executive function, and working memory, revealing how recurrent grammatical choices relate to neurocognitive profiles. Analyses span a broad range of lexicogrammatical categories, including clause complexes, process types, appraisal, modality, evidentiality, negotiating particles, and sound-symbolic expression. The result is the first book-length, empirically grounded account of lexicogrammatical variability in ASD, opening new directions for diagnostic assessment and language intervention. Essential reading for researchers and clinicians in autism studies, human neuroscience, clinical linguistics, and neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Psychoanalysis and School Psychology: Toward a Psychoanalytically Informed Framework for Educational Practice
abstract: Although the relationship between psychoanalysis and education has long been marked by tension—not least because the two fields approach the human subject from different epistemological and institutional positions—both have much to offer to each other by deepening understanding of students, learning, and educational life. Moreover, contemporary school psychology has developed into a prevention‐oriented, systems‐based profession with strong commitments to assessment, intervention, consultation, and evidence‐based practice. Yet this development has also left comparatively less room for sustained attention to unconscious communication, defensive processes, emotional meaning, and the affective life of educational institutions. This paper argues that psychoanalytic thinking offers school psychology a distinctive reflective framework for understanding educational difficulties as unconscious, relational, and institutional phenomena. Drawing on key psychoanalytic and group‐analytic traditions, the paper examines how concepts such as transference, countertransference, containment, holding, symbolization, and social defense can deepen understanding of classroom life, teacher–student relationships, school culture, and family–school work. It further proposes that a psychoanalytically informed school psychologist does not function as a clinician within the school, but as a reflective practitioner who can collaborate with school communities in thinking more deeply about behavior, anxiety, conflict, exclusion, and the emotional meanings attached to learning. The paper also considers the limits and risks of this perspective, including time pressures, accountability demands, institutional resistance, and the danger of overinterpretation. It concludes that psychoanalysis does not replace school psychology; rather, it expands its interpretive and ethical capacities by restoring attention to the emotional and unconscious dimensions of educational practice.
authors: Panayiotis Lianos
venue: International Journal of Applied Psychoanalytic Studies

title: Pulmonary nodules: classification, biomarkers, signaling pathways, diseases, early diagnosis and management
abstract: Pulmonary nodules are increasingly detected by thoracic imaging and low-dose computed tomography-based lung cancer screening, but most are benign, transient, or indolent. Clinically, the key task is to distinguish nodules that require timely cancer-directed evaluation from those that can be safely observed. This review summarizes the classification, disease spectrum, risk assessment, early diagnosis, biomarkers, signaling mechanisms, translational models, and management of pulmonary nodules. We first distinguish imaging phenotypes and disease entities, then differentiate the individual-level models used to select candidates for lung cancer screening from the nodule-level models and structured reporting systems used after nodule detection. Low-dose computed tomography remains the foundation of screening and surveillance approaches, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), positron emission tomography combined with computed tomography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography, nonsurgical biopsy, surgical diagnosis, and local therapies play more selective roles depending on the probability of malignancy and patient fitness. Noninvasive biomarkers, including circulating cellular, nucleic acid, methylation, protein, autoantibody, extracellular vesicle, and metabolic analytes, are most likely to serve as adjuncts to imaging and clinical risk assessment rather than as stand-alone diagnostic tests. Artificial intelligence may support detection, workflow efficiency, malignancy risk reclassification, invasiveness assessment, and multimodal integration, but its value depends on external validation, calibration, implementation, and prospective evidence of management benefit. Mechanistic studies of adenocarcinoma spectrum subsolid nodules have implicated the involvement of early oncogenic signaling, genomic instability, immune escape, stromal and vascular remodeling, and adaptive survival pathways. Translational models can support mechanistic and procedural research, but do not replicate real-world nodule management in patients. Overall, care for pulmonary nodules should be risk-adapted, longitudinal, multidisciplinary, and patient-centered.
authors: Zhuomiao Ye; Lijun Li; Minghui Zhang; Wei Su; Xin Li; Shoaib Anwaar; Mingyu Xiang; Yulong Yin; Mei Liu; Mingzhu Yin

title: QGenAI: A Web-Based System for Competitive Examination Practice, Difficulty-Stratified Analytics, and Mistake-Driven AI Tutoring
abstract: Preparing for national competitive examinations such as the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE), the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), and the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) requires regular multiple-choice question (MCQ) practice, reliable answer verification, and systematic mistake revision. When aspirants rely on disconnected textbooks, static question portals, and standalone chat tools, practice records become fragmented and conversational assistance lacks awareness of a learner’s actual errors. This paper presents QGenAI, an authenticated web-based practice, difficulty analysis, and personalized tutoring platform built for JEE, NEET, and GATE preparation. Learners configure custom practice sessions by selecting an examination profile, subject, topic, difficulty tier (Easy, Medium, or Hard), and question count (1, 5, 10, 15, or 20). The application retrieves active MCQs from a structured question bank while withholding answer keys from client payloads to preserve assessment integrity. Submitted responses are graded server-side, persisted with idempotent retry logic, and aggregated into account-scoped analytics covering session completion, difficulty-wise accuracy, seven-day activity, and topiclevel mistake queues. Furthermore, an integrated AI Tutor module connects to external large language model (LLM) providers (Groq, Gemini, OpenAI, or Mistral) to deliver both general topic lessons and targeted remediation grounded in up to five of the learner’s most recent incorrect attempts. The system is implemented using React, Vite, Python FastAPI, and Supabase PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security (RLS). We detail the four-tier architecture, relational schema, REST interface, evaluation formulation, and a worked empirical example across 28 completed sessions.
authors: Abishek M P; Dinesh E; SHANKARA GOWTHAM; Mohana Preetha S
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Quad-Band Terahertz Metamaterial Sensor Based on Dual Near-Perfect Absorption for Fingerprint Identification of Cancer Cells
abstract: Early and accurate cancer diagnosis remains a critical challenge in clinical oncology due to the limitations of traditional, destructive labeling methods. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel, label-free quad-band terahertz (THz) metamaterial biosensor designed for high-precision fingerprint identification of cancer cell lines. Utilizing a classic tri-layer sandwich architecture with a top patterned geometry of dual rings, numerical simulations were systematically performed via CST Studio Suite 2024 to evaluate the sensor’s electromagnetic performance. The proposed sensor established four distinct resonance channels at 2.274, 2.349, 2.552, and 2.615 THz, achieving ultra-deep absorption profiles down to −40.36 dB. When numerically investigated against six distinct biological lineages (Basal, HeLa, Jurkat, MCF-7, MDA-MB-231, and PC-12), the sensor successfully converted minor intracellular refractive index fluctuations into highly resolved, non-overlapping spectral displacements. Performance evaluations revealed an exceptional maximum optical sensitivity of 9642.8 GHz/RIU alongside a monumental Figure of Merit (FOM) of 1928.56 RIU−1 for breast cancer cells (MCF-7), while demonstrating a peak Quality factor (Q-factor) of 870.33 for leukemia cells (Jurkat) and a high sensitivity of 6600.0 GHz/RIU for skin cancer cells (Basal). Ultimately, these decoupled multi-channel fingerprint outputs provide strong diagnostic redundancy, confirming the designed metamaterial absorber as a highly promising tool for next-generation, non-invasive early cancer diagnostic applications.
authors: Aykut Coşkun; Ahmet Özmen

title: Reframing the lived experience of persistent dizziness: insights from active inference
abstract: We present an active inference account of persistent dizziness predicated on models of enactivism and ecological psychology; including first-hand accounts of the patient's lived experience. Mechanistically, we consider persistent dizziness to reflect an initial failure of sensory attenuation of vestibular and other sensory prediction errors. This failure becomes self-maintaining if the patient infers-or learns-that unattenuated prediction errors cannot be resolved through action. The ensuing formulation provides an integrative account of the pathophysiology of dizziness and how it underwrites-and is maintained by-affective inference and an altered sense of agency that shapes the experience of the person with dizziness. We foreground the holistic person-centered approach on offer from a clinical perspective, and consider complementary levels of therapeutic intervention under this theoretical framework.
authors: Marc A. Broberg; Mick Thacker; Karl John Friston; Jorge Eduardo Esteves

title: Rehabilitation Potential as a Social Judgement
abstract: 'Rehabilitation potential' is among the quieter categories of contemporary clinical practice. It appears in referral criteria, admission decisions and discharge planning as a technical estimate of how much function a patient might regain. This article argues that, applied to older people, it operates instead as a social judgement, and that the judgement long predates the vocabulary in which it is now expressed. Reading rehabilitation through the critical medical humanities, we trace practices directed at restoring function in later life from Greco-Roman antiquity, Ayurvedic Jara Chikitsa, Chinese tonification regimens and the Islamic bimaristan, through the medieval European almshouse and the Enlightenment hospital, to the geriatric units of the post-war welfare state. Across these settings the material provision of care varied enormously; the mechanism governing access did not. Societies restored older bodies to the extent that they judged those bodies worth restoring, and expressed that judgement in whichever idiom was locally authoritative, humoral, theological, actuarial and now diagnostic. We identify three properties that allow the judgement to pass as a measurement: it is comparative, it is prospective, and it is self-confirming, since withholding rehabilitation produces the deterioration that retrospectively justifies the refusal. Naming these properties has consequences for practice. It shows why better prognostic instruments cannot correct the category from within, and why access to later-life rehabilitation requires the rights-based footing now taking shape in international law.
authors: Damian Sendrowski; Martyna Kaja Sendrowska; Dariusz Kozłowski

title: Resistance to technological innovation: the case of teleconsultation before and during COVID-19
abstract: Purpose This study analyzes resistance to technological innovation in the healthcare field, focusing on the formal, long-term adoption of teleconsultation in medical practice, which became established during the COVID-19 pandemic. Different institutional studies on resistance to change were analyzed to evaluate their capacity to explain the phenomenon. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative interpretive research was conducted involving documentary research and interviews with professionals from public and private domains, including health regulation organizations and individual practitioners, to capture their understandings of the issue. Findings The results showed that the primary hindering factors were the need for physical examination, the risk of deteriorating remuneration conditions for doctors, and insufficient undergraduate training in telemedicine. Research limitations/implications Thus, the study infers that institutional logics of the same order can coexist, accommodating contradictions between them. Medical autonomy, a principle of democratic logic upheld by part of the professional community and the imperative of public health emergencies, characteristic of professional logic, provoked a rapid response, constituting the driving pressures for the adoption of teleconsultation. Originality/value Technological innovation tends to face resistance during implementation, but under favorable conditions, it becomes consolidated alongside the previous practice. Traditional professional logic resisted the introduction of the new logic represented by teleconsultation until confronted by the pandemic, when it was compelled to adapt to the circumstances.
authors: Hosana Rodrigues; Arnaldo Luiz Ryngelblum; Ernesto Michelângelo Giglio

title: Resource-matched acquisition of functional assessment data for dementia progression forecasting
abstract: Additional functional information may improve dementia progression forecasts, but it is uncertain which visits should receive it under a limited assessment quota. We compared five visit-ranking policies using the same core predictor and its 11-variable functional-block-expanded version in longitudinal National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center data. The endpoint was a next-visit increase of at least 1.0 point in the Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes score (CDR-SB). Models were fitted using training participants; routing quantities were estimated on separate validation participants and frozen before testing. Each policy selected 3,366 (14%) or 4,809 (20%) of 24,043 held-out transitions from 5,905 participants. Core area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.6790. Validation-utility routing achieved AUPRC 0.6809 at 14% (difference +0.0019; participant-clustered 95% confidence interval (CI) −0.0002 to +0.0041) and 0.6835 at 20% (+0.0045; +0.0016 to +0.0075); risk-only routing had the highest AUPRC among the five policies at both quotas. Supplementary analyses included ten participant-level refits of histogram gradient boosting (HGB), calibration diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, and a ten-initialization adaptation of discriminative mutual information estimation (DIME). The results show small, objective-dependent retrospective changes; they do not establish clinical benefit, an optimal assessment budget, or a basis for autonomous ordering.
authors: Chih Mao Tsai; Jiann-Der Lee

title: Retrocaval Ureter Detected on CT Urography: A Case Report
abstract: Retrocaval ureter is a rare congenital anomaly resulting from abnormal embryological development of the inferior vena cava rather than a primary abnormality of the ureter. Although congenital, patients often present in adulthood with symptoms related to upper urinary tract obstruction. A 47-year-old man presented with recurrent intermittent right flank pain, typically precipitated by consuming a large volume of alcohol. Physical examination and laboratory investigations were unremarkable. Ultrasonography demonstrated mild right hydronephrosis and proximal hydroureter without an identifiable cause. Contrast-enhanced CT urography with threedimensional reconstruction revealed a Type I retrocaval ureter, demonstrating the characteristic fish-hook deformity with the proximal ureter coursing posterior to the inferior vena cava. The patient underwent open ureteroureterostomy with double-J stenting and had complete resolution of symptoms and hydronephrosis on follow-up.This case highlights the importance of considering retrocaval ureter in adults presenting with recurrent unilateral flank pain and unexplained hydronephrosis. CT urography with multiplanar and three-dimensional reconstructions is the imaging modality of choice for accurate diagnosis, anatomical assessment, and preoperative planning. The case also illustrates the close relationship between embryological development, anatomical variation, and radiological anatomy.
authors: Shirom Rajeev Siriwardana; K. A. P. S. Keragala; S. W. Dissanayake

title: Richter’s Hernia: Clinical Presentation, Diagnostic Challenges, and Emergency Management-Updated Review
abstract: Background: Richter’s hernia is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening type of abdominal wall hernia characterized by incarceration of only a portion of the intestinal circumference, usually the antimesenteric border. Unlike conventional incarcerated hernias, it may progress to intestinal ischemia and necrosis without causing complete bowel obstruction, frequently delaying diagnosis and increasing the risk of serious complications. Aim: This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of Richter’s hernia, emphasizing its etiology, epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, treatment, complications, prognosis, and patient education. Methods: A narrative review approach was used to synthesize available literature addressing the anatomical mechanisms, clinical characteristics, diagnostic challenges, and contemporary management of Richter’s hernia. Particular attention was given to emergency recognition, assessment of bowel viability, surgical approaches, postoperative care, and recurrence prevention. Results: Richter’s hernia most commonly affects the small intestine and is associated with femoral and inguinal hernias, incisional defects, and previous minimally invasive surgical procedures. Its distinctive pathophysiology allows intestinal contents to pass despite progressive vascular compromise of the entrapped bowel wall. Clinical manifestations range from localized pain and tenderness to intestinal necrosis, perforation, peritonitis, and sepsis. Ultrasonography and computed tomography support diagnosis, although negative imaging findings do not exclude the condition. Management requires prompt surgical assessment, appropriate resuscitation, antimicrobial therapy when indicated, and timely operative intervention. Bowel resection may be necessary when irreversible ischemia or necrosis is identified. Conclusion: Early recognition, individualized surgical management, and appropriate postoperative surveillance are essential to minimize complications and improve outcomes.
