title: Data analytics capabilities and organisational performance at an emerging economy’s local government assembly: the roles of top-management support and data driven decision making
abstract: This study examines the impact of Data Analytics Capability on organisational performance within an emerging economy’s local government assembly, with particular focus on the mediating role of Data-Driven Decision Making and the influence of Top Management Support. Grounded in the Organisational Information Processing Theory and the Upper Echelons Theory, the study adopts a cross-sectional survey explanatory design. Data was collected from 127 employees of the local assembly through structured online questionnaire and analysed using Partial Least Squares Structured Equation Modelling. The results reveal that DAC has no significant direct effect on organisational performance but exerts a strong positive effect on DDDM. In turn, DDDM significantly enhances organisational performance and mediates the relationship between DAC and performance. Additionally, TMS support significantly and directly influences organisational performance, although it does not moderate the DAC-performance relationship. The study concludes that DAC alone do not guarantee improved performance, rather, their value is realized through integration into decision-making processes. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study is among the first to provide empirical evidence from an emerging economy’s local government context demonstrating that DDDM is the critical pathway through which DAC translate into performance outcomes, while TMS operates as a direct driver rather than a conditional enhancer. This study contributes theoretically by refining the application of the OIPT and the UET in public sector analytics contexts and offers practical insights that performance improvements depend more on the use of data in decision-making than on the mere possession of analytics infrastructure.
authors: Alfred Nana Kissi Andoh; Michael Fudzi; Boniface Baada; Emmanuel Ekow Asmah; Joshua Addo; Emmanuel Attobrah

title: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults
abstract: Dual-task performance requires coordination between cognitive control and motor systems. This study examined how deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (DTMS) influences cortical responses and computational performance during dual-task processing. In a randomized crossover study, 19 healthy adults underwent DTMS targeting the bilateral prefrontal cortex and anterior cingulate cortex and sham stimulation in separate sessions, with functional near-infrared spectroscopy and dual-task assessments performed before and after each intervention. Compared with sham stimulation, DTMS increased task-related cortical activation in regions involved in cognitive-motor processing and improved computation number without affecting accuracy. Activation changes involving the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, secondary motor cortex, and language-related regions were associated with dual-task performance. These findings suggest that DTMS may modulate distributed cortical dynamics supporting cognitive-motor coordination and inform its potential application in populations with cognitive-motor impairments.
authors: Baoyao Zeng; Weining Wang; Zhengran Ding; Chen Wang; Ce Li; Runzhe Yuan; Bao Zhou; Yulian Zhu

title: Design and Rehabilitation Applications of Lower-Limb Exoskeleton Robots for Children with Cerebral Palsy
abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is a major cause of walking impairment in children. Children with CP commonly experience abnormal muscle tone, impaired selective motor control, postural instability, pathological gait and increased walking energy expenditure. Lower-limb exoskeletons robots can make gait training in children with CP more task-oriented and quantifiable. Grounded in the clinical needs of lower-limb rehabilitation for children with CP, this review examined five types of exoskeleton architectures and associated assistive approaches: single-joint flexible, single-joint rigid, multi-joint flexible, multi-joint rigid, and exoskeleton-wheeled walker hybrid systems. Their rehabilitation evidence and limitations in pediatric settings were discussed. We also reviewed sensing and assist-as-needed control strategies; individualized adaptations for different CP subtypes; . the effects of audiovisual feedback, virtual reality and gamified interaction on active participation; and rehabilitation outcome assessment. Key challenges include limited pediatric-specific evidence, fit and comfort issues that limit long-term use, and inadequate adaptation of control algorithms to the complexity of pathological gait in children with CP. Future directions are discussed to provide a theoretical basis and practical reference for the structural optimization, control refinement, and clinical rehabilitation evaluation of lower-limb exoskeletons robots for children with CP. Current evidence is derived primarily from studies of spastic CP. Clinical translation still requires coordinated advances in lightweight pediatric design, individualized prescriptions, algorithmic safety, therapist control and long-term follow-up evidence.
authors: Junyi Yang; 曹武警

title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation
abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. This work addresses these challenges by integrating soft robotics with computer vision. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.
authors: Charbel Tawk; George Saab; George Abdallah; Jason El Khoury; Reynald Aouad

title: Designing optimal perturbation inputs for system identification in neuroscience
abstract: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms, such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.
authors: Mikito Ogino; Daiki Sekizawa; Jun Kitazono; Masafumi Oizumi

title: Determinants of Organizational Sustainability Using Toe Model in Engineering, Electrical and Information Technology Industry: The Mediating Effect of AI Adoption
abstract: This study examines the determinants of organizational sustainability in Jordan's engineering, electrical, and information technology sectors. It explores how technological, organizational, and environmental factors influence organizational sustainability, and how AI adoption is a mediating variable in this regard. The research method used was a quantitative method, surveying 396 participants. The data were analyzed with SPSS and SmartPLS 4, which employs PLS-SEM. The results show that organizational and environmental aspects have the highest impact on sustainability. The factors with the most direct impact on sustainability are AI complexity (no impact) and AI compatibility, top management support, culture of innovation, regulatory pressure, and competitive pressure (all with an effect). Most relationships are mediated by AI, accentuating its importance in promoting organizational sustainability in emerging economies.
authors: Ahmad Ziad Abdalkareem Alzghool; Amar Hisham Bin Jaaffar; Mohd Rizuan Abdul Kadir

title: Developing an Industry-Aligned TVET Curriculum Framework and Authentic Assessment Blueprint for Automotive Checking Fixture Fabrication
abstract: Modern automotive manufacturing depends on precise quality control, yet traditional Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) curricula fall short. Conventional programs rely heavily on passive lectures and isolated 3D CAD exercises, an approach that leaves graduates ill-prepared for real-world Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T), workholding mechanics, and shop-floor metrology. To address this gap, we developed and validated a 14-week project-based TVET framework and assessment blueprint centered on automotive checking fixture fabrication. Guided by Design-Based Research (DBR) and the Conceive-Design-Implement-Operate (CDIO) lifecycle, our approach integrates parametric CAD modeling, CNC machining, FDM 3D printing, and Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) verification with Measurement System Analysis (MSA). An expert panel of twenty industrial quality managers and TVET educators evaluated the framework, establishing strong content and construct validity with Item-Objective Congruence (IOC) scores above 0.80. The resulting 90-contact-hour curriculum features an authentic assessment rubric that ties 70% of the total grade directly to physical fabrication accuracy and metrological compliance (GRR < 30%). This model provides TVET institutions with an expert-validated, practical roadmap to align academic instruction with modern industrial quality standards
authors: Widodo W.S.; Sulaiman S.N.
venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science

title: Digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance in Vietnamese commercial banks: Empirical evidence from accountants and managers
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the relationships among digital accounting implementation, financial reporting quality, usefulness of accounting information, top management support, and perceived operational performance in commercial banks. Data were collected from 562 accountants and managers working at 27 commercial banks in Vietnam, an emerging Asian economy. The study evaluated the proposed model using a two-stage Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling approach. The findings indicate that digital accounting implementation is positively associated with perceived operational performance. In addition, digital accounting implementation is indirectly associated with perceived operational performance through statistically significant indirect paths involving financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information. Financial reporting quality is also positively associated with the usefulness of accounting information. Furthermore, the positive associations between digital accounting implementation and both financial reporting quality and usefulness of accounting information were stronger at higher levels of perceived top management support, whereas the interaction between digital accounting implementation and perceived operational performance was not statistically significant. Collectively, the findings suggest that perceptions of digital accounting implementation are closely related to perceptions of information quality, information usefulness, managerial support, and perceived operational performance. This study contributes empirical evidence on the interrelationships among these perceived organizational constructs in the context of banking digital transformation in an emerging economy.
authors: Cuong Bui Manh; Hải Phan Thanh; Cường Nguyễn Thành

title: Digital multimodal vocabulary projects in Indonesian EFL higher education: Design, assessment, and students’ perceptions
abstract: Vocabulary assessment in Indonesian EFL higher education remains predominantly focused on discrete-item tests, prioritizing individual receptive knowledge. To address limitations of such tests, this study examined collaborative, digital, multimodal vocabulary projects in a pre-service teacher class in Indonesia and explored students’ perceptions. This study is an exploratory, single-case qualitative study conducted with a class of 30 third-semester EFL teacher-education students. They collaboratively created two digitally mediated multimodal projects: a Quizizz-based vocabulary quiz set and an idiom-based conversation video. The project artefacts, rubric notes, the lecturer’s reflection notes, and semi-structured interview scripts were analyzed thematically. The study revealed that students experienced gains in creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, digital skills, and enjoyment throughout the process. However, they reported time constraints, communication challenges, and performance anxiety. Group-based digital projects were evident to make vocabulary use in context observable, and multimodal assessment was found to support vocabulary learning and learning-oriented assessment. The research contributes empirical evidence on multimodal assessment for vocabulary learning in Indonesian EFL higher education, a context that remains underrepresented in the literature. It is recommended that collaborative, multimodal task design be integrated into pre-service teacher education to scaffold digital literacy, collaboration, culturally relevant development, and contextually grounded vocabulary assessment practices.
authors: Nurmala Hendrawaty; Zulfa Sakhiyya; Sri Wahyuni; Yuliati Yuliati
venue: International Journal of English Language and Literature Studies

title: Digital sovereignty in professional translation workflows: a case study of migrating from Windows to Linux
abstract: This study examines digital sovereignty in professional translation through a screening of computer-assisted translation tools and translation management systems, and a case study of migrating a translator's workstation from Windows to Linux. The framework combines three principles - Control, Continuity and Exit - with three practical requirements: native Linux operation, independence from mandatory external services, and independent access to essential data and resources. Drawing on documentary evidence and the limited number of responses received from providers, the ecosystem screening distinguishes Linux accessibility from operational independence: browser-based platforms may remain dependent on provider-controlled infrastructure. The migration case demonstrates the feasibility of reconstructing one professional workflow around a locally operable Linux core, using LoopCAT, LibreOffice and locally run TranslateGemma, alongside tools for optical character recognition, communication, credential management and backup. Selected cloud services remained available where needed. The findings suggest that digital sovereignty depends on how workflow dependencies are organized, rather than on individual applications or operating systems. It does not require technological isolation, but meaningful control over essential components, continuity of work and practical exit options. The framework is tailored to the case examined here and may require adaptation to other professional workflows.
authors: Michael Farrell

title: Disparity in Coronal Deformity Measurements: Standing Radiographs Versus Navigation in Varus Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: This study aimed to ascertain whether a discrepancy exists between coronal deformity measurements obtained from radiographs and those from computer navigation, and to explore potential reasons for such discrepancy. This study assessed 621 primary navigated TKAs performed on varus arthritic knees. Preoperative and postoperative hip-knee-ankle angle (HKA), mechanical lateral distal femoral angle (LDFA), medial proximal tibial angle (MPTA), and joint congruence angle (JCA) were measured using scanograms. Initial coronal deformity after arthrotomy and prior to performing releases or bone cuts was recorded during navigation using a proven dynamic method. The difference between radiographic and navigation measurements of initial deformity was calculated. The mean preoperative HKA was 12.6º (SD ± 6.11, range 0.8º to 40.9º), while the mean initial alignment on navigation was 14° (SD ± 5.96, range 2º to 42º). The mean difference between these values of-1.42º was highly significant (SD ± 3.04, range -17º to 10.5º, P < 0.001 on t test,), with a correlation of r = 0.873 (P < 0.001). This difference exceeded ± 2º in over half of the knees (n = 314, 50.6%). There was a progressively increasing difference between the two measurements with an increase in mean initial HKA, LDFA, and JCA, and a decrease in mean MPTA (ANOVA, P < 0.001). Surgeons performing TKA surgery using navigation or robots should be aware of the potential discrepancies between coronal deformity measurements. Factors such as increased coronal deformity, medial bone deficiency, and lateral laxity may contribute to this discrepancy.
authors: Anand Kumar Gupta; Arun Mullaji

title: Disrupting the Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus Increases ‘Social Brain’ Activity During Emotion Recognition
abstract: Neuroimaging studies have identified a specialised social brain network that supports emotion recognition and social cognition. This network performs a range of functions that include facial expression recognition and inferring the mental states of others. Studies of neuropsychological patients report that damage to the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), the top-down control area in this network, impairs facial expression recognition. To investigate how transient disruption of the right IFG affects the wider social brain we combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Participants ( n =20) were scanned across two sessions while performing a delayed match-to-sample emotion recognition task in which happy or fearful expressions were preceded by a congruent or incongruent word cue. Prior to each scan, thetaburst TMS was delivered over the right IFG or over the vertex control site (session order was balanced across participants). A group whole-brain analysis revealed that TMS to the IFG increased neural activity in multiple regions of the social brain network. These included the bilateral temporal pole, precuneus and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). This pattern of results shows that the disruption of top-down control mechanisms localised in the IFG alters the neural processing in remote nodes of the social brain network. Our findings are discussed within the wider context of how we recognise and understand the emotions of other people.
authors: Emel Küçük; Hannah Gofton; Cameron Smith; DANIEL H. KAISER; David Pitcher

title: Disrupting the semantic network shifts activity to domain-general brain regions
abstract: Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus-a core lexico-semantic region-was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain's capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.
authors: Anna‐Lisa Schuler; Andrea Bruera; Gesa Hartwigsen

title: Distinct motor profiles in neuromodulation-induced prehabilitation before brain tumor surgery: a resting-state fMRI study of motor performance
abstract: Introduction: Brain tumor surgery near motor areas requires balancing maximal resection with functional preservation. Neuromodulation-induced prehabilitation (NIP) may support preoperative functional reorganization, but individual motor and neural responses remain poorly characterized. Methods: = 16) underwent a 1-3-week NIP protocol comprising at least 10 sessions, with twice-daily sessions when necessary, combining low-frequency transcranial magnetic stimulation and/or multichannel transcranial direct current stimulation with intensive motor training. Participants were stratified using Fuzzy C-Means clustering based on pre-post changes (ΔPOST-PRE) in performance components, specifically dexterity (Simple/Choice Reaction Time, 9-Hole Peg Test) and strength (Handgrip). Pre-post changes in resting-state functional connectivity and motor performance relationships were analyzed within the identified profiles. Results: Clustering revealed two distinct functional profiles: Strength and Dexterity groups (strength-dominant vs. dexterity-dominant, respectively). While overall performance remained stable, profile-specific performance and neural reorganizations emerged. The Dexterity group showed improved Simple Reaction Time and a significant decrease in Frontal Pole (FP)-Middle Frontal Gyrus (MFG) connectivity. Conversely, the Strength group exhibited a significant increase in Precentral Gyrus-Supplementary Motor Area and FP-MFG connectivity. Remarkably, in the Strength group, an increase in FP-MFG connectivity was correlated with improved manual dexterity. Discussion: This exploratory study addresses an emerging area of preoperative neurorehabilitation. Behavioral profiling identified distinct motor-change patterns and connectivity trajectories during NIP, suggesting different neurobiological pathways of prehabilitation. Although preliminary, these findings provide a framework for understanding individual variability in preoperative functional reorganization and support functional profiling as a promising approach to guide individualized neuromodulation and motor training before tumor surgery.
authors: Selma Delgado‐Gallén; Roger Bragulat; María Redondo‐Camós; Nuria Brault-Boixader; Alba Roca‐Ventura; Edgar Buloz-Osorio; Ruben Perellón‐Alfonso; Leonardo Boccuni; David Bartrés‐Faz; Álvaro Pascual‐Leone; Josep M. Tormos Muñoz; Kilian Abellaneda‐Pérez

title: Dose-response relationship between isokinetic strength training intensity and lower limb spasticity improvement in stroke patients: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Post-stroke spasticity (PSS) significantly impairs motor function recovery and quality of life in stroke survivors. While isokinetic strength training has demonstrated efficacy in neurological rehabilitation, the optimal training intensity for spasticity management remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationship between different isokinetic training intensities and lower limb spasticity improvement in stroke patients. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed medical-record data from 392 stroke patients with lower limb spasticity who received rehabilitation therapy at our institution between January 2021 and December 2023. Patients were categorized into four groups based on isokinetic training intensity: control (standard rehabilitation only, n = 98), low-intensity (30% maximal voluntary contraction [MVC], n = 98), moderate-intensity (50% MVC, n = 98), and high-intensity (70% MVC, n = 98). The primary outcome was change in Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) scores at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included Fugl-Meyer Assessment Lower Extremity (FMA-LE), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), and isokinetic peak torque measurements. Covariate-adjusted and sensitivity analyses were performed to address confounding by indication. Results At 8 weeks, all groups demonstrated significant improvements from baseline (all P < 0.001). The high-intensity group achieved the greatest MAS reduction (1.07 ± 0.36 points), followed by moderate-intensity (1.02 ± 0.29), low-intensity (0.69 ± 0.48), and control (0.20 ± 0.45) groups (F = 95.789, P < 0.001, η 2 = 0.425). These associations remained significant after adjustment for baseline covariates (all adjusted P < 0.001). The difference in MAS reduction between the moderate- and high-intensity groups was not statistically significant (1.02 versus 1.07 points, P = 0.813). Linear dose-response relationships were observed for all outcomes (all R 2 > 0.40, P < 0.001). Between-group comparisons revealed significant differences between all training intensities for FMA-LE improvement (high: 7.23 ± 1.92; moderate: 5.64 ± 1.89; low: 3.48 ± 1.92; control: 1.27 ± 1.72 points; P < 0.001). Conclusions This study demonstrates a significant dose-response relationship between isokinetic strength training intensity and lower limb spasticity improvement in stroke patients. Higher training intensities (50%–70% MVC) were associated with superior outcomes across all measures, although no additional antispasticity benefit was demonstrated at 70% versus 50% MVC, suggesting that structured progressive resistance training may be incorporated into comprehensive post-stroke rehabilitation programs.
authors: Yang Zhang; Weigui Zhu

title: Drivers and Barriers to Artificial Intelligence Adoption in the Banking Sector: Evidence from Cambodia
abstract: Driven by the Fourth and Fifth Industrial Revolutions, global financial institutions are aggressively deploying artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to optimize operations, risk management, and customer engagement. However, empirical investigation into AI adoption dynamics within emerging economies remains critically sparse, as established technology acceptance frameworks predominantly reflect advanced or industrialized environments. This study investigates the primary determinants—encompassing both technological, organizational, and environmental drivers and barriers—influencing AI adoption across the banking sector in Cambodia, evaluating 25 hypotheses to establish an integrated conceptual model tailored to emerging financial settings. A mixed-methods design with concurrent triangulation was executed. Quantitative data were gathered via a survey of 83 banking institutions and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Qualitative insights were extracted via content analysis on 17 semi-structured interviews. As a result, PLS-SEM path modeling confirmed 17 of 25 hypotheses as statistically significant drivers. Primary drivers include top management’s innovativeness, business scope, top management’s support, familiarity with innovation, and relative advantage. Surprisingly, traditional economic and structural inhibitors—technical complexity, cost, centralization, formalization, organization size, slack, government policies, and geographical settings—were statistically unsupported as firm-level barriers in the quantitative model. Nonetheless, qualitative content analysis supported 24 of 25 factors, exposing a profound perception-reality gap where operational friction is overridden by top-down executive mandates and competitive survival pressures. AI adoption in emerging banking markets operates under a Strategic Survival Mandate, wherein banking institutions bypass cost and complexity constraints to maintain market relevance. Policy interventions are critical to promoting sound adoption.
authors: Soklay Ky
venue: International Journal of Management and Economics Invention

title: ER–mitochondria contacts orchestrate mitochondrial transport via C19orf12
abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–mitochondria contact sites facilitate lipid transfer, calcium signaling, and mitochondrial division; however, their role in mitochondrial transport remains unclear. Here, we identify hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP)-associated protein C19orf12 as an ER-anchored regulator of mitochondrial trafficking. The loss of C19orf12 leads to perinuclear mitochondrial clustering in cells, impaired anterograde transport in neurons, and progressive locomotor dysfunction in mice that recapitulates key features of HSP in humans. Mechanistically, C19orf12 forms a discrete complex with the mitochondrial Rho GTPase Miro1 and the Kinesin-1 motor Kif5b, thereby providing a molecular link between ER–mitochondria contacts and microtubule-based anterograde transport. Ca 2+ also modulated C19orf12–Miro1 behavior in vitro and showed a biphasic association with mitochondrial motility in live cells. Therefore, our findings establish ER‒mitochondria contact sites as logistical hubs for Kinesin-1 motor loading and highlight the importance of the Ca 2+ -tunable C19orf12 scaffold in sustaining directional mitochondrial transport, providing a mechanistic framework for how C19orf12 loss may contribute to neurodegeneration.
authors: Xiayuhe Pei; Shuqian Zhang; Peiyang Li; Yutong Wu; Yiru Cheng; Xia Feng; Yue Wu; Xiaoshuai Huang; Ning Huang; Bei Liu; Junlin Teng; Jie Chen; Craig D. Blackstone; Pengli Zheng

title: EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF SUPPLY CHAIN QUALITY ON SUPPLIER PERFORMANCE: A FIELD STUDY AT THE GENERAL COMPANY FOR ELECTRICAL INDUSTRIES, BAGHDAD
abstract: This study examined the impact of supply chain quality on supplier performance at the General Company for Electrical and Electronic Industries in Baghdad. Supply chain quality was measured through five dimensions: top management support, supplier relationships, total quality management, information integration, and continuous improvement. Supplier performance was assessed through quality, delivery, flexibility, and cost. The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The population comprised 245 employees from relevant departments, from which a purposive sample of 150 employees was selected. A total of 127 valid questionnaires were collected and analyzed. Data were collected using a questionnaire whose validity and reliability were established. The overall Cronbach’s alpha coefficient was 0.947. Data analysis was conducted using SPSS version 26.The findings indicated moderate levels of both supply chain quality and supplier performance, with mean scores of 3.60 and 3.51, respectively. Total quality management recorded the highest mean among supply chain quality dimensions, while cost was the highest supplier performance dimension. The results also revealed a statistically significant positive relationship between supply chain quality and supplier performance. The combined dimensions of supply chain quality significantly explained 65.9% of the variance in supplier performance. Supplier relationships emerged as the most influential dimension.The study recommends strengthening long-term strategic supplier relationships, investing in digital infrastructure and information-sharing systems, establishing a specialized supplier development unit, adopting continuous improvement practices, and implementing supplier performance evaluation systems based on measurable indicators.
authors: Nawfal Kadhim Abd Oun

title: Early Survivorship and Clinical Outcomes Following Cementless Robotic-Assisted Restricted Kinematic Alignment Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstract: Background and objective: Kinematic alignment (KA) has gained interest in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) because of its potential to restore native knee anatomy and improve patient outcomes. Robotic-assisted TKA has been adopted to enhance the precision and reproducibility of component positioning. The purpose of this study was to evaluate early survivorship and clinical outcomes following cementless robotic-assisted restricted KA TKA. Methods: A retrospective review was performed of consecutive patients undergoing primary cementless robotic-assisted KA TKA by a single fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon between May 2024 and June 2025. Patients with a minimum one-year follow-up were included. A restricted KA philosophy with predefined alignment boundaries was utilized. The primary outcome was survivorship free from aseptic revision. Secondary outcomes included all-cause revision, reoperations, manipulation under anesthesia (MUA), patient-reported outcomes, and radiographic alignment distribution. Results: A total of 100 cementless robotic-assisted KA TKAs were included. Survivorship free from aseptic revision was 100% at a mean follow-up of 22.8±3.2 months, with no cases of aseptic loosening. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) physical function increased by 8.0±9.1 points, PROMIS pain interference decreased by 11.5±10.9 points, and PROMIS mobility increased by 9.8±8.8 points from baseline. The mean postoperative Forgotten Joint Score (FJS) was 66.0±26.7, and patient satisfaction was 3.6 ± 0.6 on a four-point Likert scale. The MUA was performed in 6% of knees. Postoperative radiographs demonstrated a broad coronal and sagittal alignment distribution consistent with KA principles. Conclusions: Cementless robotic-assisted KA TKA demonstrated excellent early survivorship and favorable patient-reported outcomes at short-term follow-up. Robotic assistance facilitated consistent execution of KA principles while achieving patient-specific alignment targets, supporting the early compatibility of restricted KA with contemporary cementless fixation.
authors: Alex M. Hollenberg; Lane H. McCoy; Nicholas M Brown; Andrew M. Schneider

title: Early visual cortex is not functionally necessary for temporal attention: A TMS study
abstract: Temporal attention enhances the selective processing of information at a specific point in time and improves perception. Previous neuroimaging studies investigating its neural mechanisms have either conflated temporal attention with temporal expectation or provided correlational evidence. Thus, whether early visual cortex is functionally necessary for temporal attention remains unknown. Here, we combined psychophysics with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to examine whether V1/V2 are functionally necessary and play a causal role in temporal attention. Observers performed an orientation-discrimination task in which two consecutive stimuli, T1 and T2, were presented in the periphery, preceded by a precue providing either valid or neutral temporal information. Double-pulse TMS was delivered under four conditions: at T1 (T1-TMS), at T2 (T2-TMS), at both T1 and T2 (both-TMS), or not at all (none-TMS), to assess its effects on temporal attention and the efficacy of the stimulation was verified by pupil size analysis. Behavioral results revealed robust temporal attention benefits on d′ , reaction time, and the Balanced Integration Score (BIS) across all four TMS conditions, indicating that the benefits of temporal attention were unaffected by occipital TMS. Furthermore, pupil dilation was largest in the both-TMS condition, followed by the T1-TMS and T2-TMS conditions, and smallest in the none-TMS condition, providing physiological verification of the stimulation protocol. Together, these findings reveal the first causal evidence that the early visual cortex is not functionally necessary for endogenous temporal attention. Significance Temporal attention prioritizes sensory information at specific moments, yet its underlying neural mechanisms remain poorly understood due to a lack of direct causal evidence. Neuroimaging studies have implicated multiple areas, including early visual and higher-order cortical regions. Here, using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to disrupt neural activity in the early visual cortex, we found that behavioral benefits of temporal attention remained intact. These findings reveal that the early visual cortex is not functionally necessary for temporal attention. Critically, this study provides the first causal evidence that selectively and voluntarily attending to specific time points operates independently of early visual areas, suggesting that higher-order regions–such as the fronto-cingulate network–play a primary role.
authors: Hsing-Hao Lee; Marisa Carrasco

title: Effect of Early Mid-Range Functional Training for Upper Limb in Improving Upper Limb Function and Quality of Life Among Patients with Acute Stroke
abstract: Stroke ranks among the leading causes of death and disability worldwide, and impaired upper-limb function after stroke severely disrupts daily activities and wellbeing. Acute-phase rehabilitation may exploit enhanced neuroplasticity. Objective: To assess the feasibility, safety and preliminary effect of early mid-range functional training with sling suspension therapy on upper-limb function, spasticity and stroke-specific quality of life in acute stroke patients. In a prospective single-group pre-post pilot study, 45 consecutively enrolled acute stroke patients (aged 50–75 years; ischaemic and haemorrhagic) underwent a 12-week programme of mid-range functional training with sling suspension therapy in gravity-eliminated positions, twice daily, 6 days weekly, 45 minutes per session. Upper-limb function (DASH; primary outcome), stroke-specific quality of life (SSQOL) and spasticity (Modified Ashworth Scale, MAS; secondary outcomes) were measured at baseline (Day 1), mid-intervention (Day 45) and follow-up (Day 90), using repeated-measures analysis with Bonferroni-corrected comparisons, effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). All 45 participants finished the protocol (0% attrition). DASH fell from 76.0 to 36.0 (95% CI 30.8–49.2; d = 1.31); SSQOL rose from 114.5 to 172.5 (95% CI 49.3–66.7; d = 2.00); MAS declined from 2.55 to 0.95 (95% CI 1.09–2.11; d = 0.94); all p < 0.0001. FThis uncontrolled pilot study suggests early mid-range functional training with sling suspension therapy is feasible, well tolerated and linked to better function, quality of life and reduced spasticity; spontaneous recovery cannot be excluded, so findings warrant a randomised controlled trial.
authors: Rajkumar Salem Krishnan; Anandan Duraisamy; Arunachalam Ramachandran; A. Shanmugam; Mohana Chinnasamy
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Effect of functional electrical stimulation combined with kinesiotaping or anterior rafting strap binding on motor and gait outcomes in chronic middle cerebral artery stroke survivors: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke survivors frequently experience persistent lower-limb motor impairment, spasticity, and gait dysfunction, all of which substantially limit functional independence. Alongside routine rehabilitation, adjunctive non-invasive interventions such as taping and functional electrical stimulation (FES) may facilitate neuromuscular activation and biomechanical control during gait. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of FES combined with either kinesiotaping (KT) or anterior rafting strap binding, in addition to conventional physiotherapy, on motor and gait outcomes in individuals with chronic MCA stroke. METHODS: In this prospective, assessor-blinded randomized controlled trial, 57 chronic MCA stroke survivors were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to: (1) the FES group, (2) the FES + KT group, or (3) the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group. All participants received standardized conventional physiotherapy, including task-oriented gait training. Lower Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA-LE), gait speed measured with the 10-Meter Walk Test (10MWT), walking endurance measured with the 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT), functional mobility measured with the Timed Up and Go (TUG), and ankle plantarflexor spasticity measured with the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks post-intervention. Descriptive statistics, ANOVA, and ANCOVA adjusting for baseline values, age, and stroke chronicity were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: The FES + KT group and the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group demonstrated significant improvements in motor and gait outcomes compared with the FES group (p < 0.05). Direct unadjusted post-hoc comparisons between the FES + anterior rafting strap binding and FES + KT groups were not statistically significant for FMA-LE, 10MWT, 6MWT, or TUG (p > 0.05). The adjusted ANCOVA estimates favoured the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group across the assessed outcomes; however, these adjusted findings should be distinguished from the unadjusted post-hoc comparisons. For plantarflexor spasticity, the direct post-hoc comparisons demonstrated a significantly greater reduction in the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group than in the FES + KT group (adjusted p = 0.039). CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group may improve lower-limb motor recovery, gait performance, functional mobility, and plantarflexor spasticity in chronic MCA stroke survivors. However, direct unadjusted post-hoc comparisons between the FES + anterior rafting strap binding group and the FES + KT group were not statistically significant for FMA-LE, 10MWT, 6MWT, or TUG. These findings support the integration of biomechanical alignment strategies with neuromuscular stimulation to optimize gait rehabilitation in chronic stroke.
authors: Hariharasudhan Ravichandran; Kshama Susheel Shetty; Nupuresh Murali; Dhaneesh Damodaran; Amratha G. Shetty; Rachana Purushotham; Debadutta Patra

title: Effect of glenosphere lateralization or inferiorization and humeral offset on range of motion after reverse total shoulder arthroplasty: A robotic assessment
abstract: Background The use of preoperative three-dimensional (3D) planning, augmented baseplates and patient-specific instrumentation (PSI) for reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) has gained in popularity allowing more accurate positioning of glenoid and humeral components. There exists a paucity of data on the influence of component selection on postoperative range of motion (ROM). The purpose of the present study was to evaluate the effect of glenosphere lateralization or inferiorization and humeral offset on postoperative ROM using a 6-degrees- of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic arm. Methods Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty implantation was planned in twelve cadaveric shoulders using three-dimensional computed tomography based preoperative planning. Each shoulder was dissected of all soft tissue and rTSA (Univers Revers TM , Arthrex Inc.) implantation was performed using PSI. Each specimen was mounted to a 6-DOF robotic arm and tested with 3 different glenospheres (standard, +4 mm lateralized or +2.5 mm inferiorized) and non-constrained humeral liners (+3, +6 or +9 mm offset) for a total of 9 configurations. Robotic assessment consisted of ROM testing in abduction, flexion and adduction under 5 Nm torque. To match the repeated measures design, a 2-factor linear mixed effect model was created for each test whereby the choice of the glenosphere was a categorical factor and humeral offset was a continuous factor. Results Lateralizing the glenosphere by 4.0 mm or inferiorizing it by 2.5 mm significantly improved abduction ROM (+3.6° and +3.5°, p < 0.001, respectively), flexion ROM (+1.7° [p = 0.015] and +4.0° [p < 0.001], respectively) and adduction ROM (+4.0° and +4.9°, p < 0.001, respectively) when compared with the standard glenosphere. Glenosphere inferiorization was associated with an increase in flexion ROM by 2.3° (p < 0.001) when compared with the lateralized glenosphere. Increasing humeral offset beyond 3mm significantly reduced abduction (-0.5°/mm, p < 0.001) and flexion ROM (-0.9°/mm, p < 0.001), but did not significantly affect adduction ROM. Conclusions The implant configuration that was associated with the most favorable ROM was a +2.5 mm inferiorized glenosphere, which led to significant improvements in all three ROM, and a +3 mm humeral liner, which was associated with improved abduction and flexion ROM.

title: Effect of robotic assistance on upper-limb sensorimotor recovery: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Introduction: Robot-assisted upper-limb neurorehabilitation enables several beneficial therapy components, including repetitive task-specific practice, high training intensity, real-time feedback, gamification, and continuous physical interaction with the patient's limb. However, conventional comparisons of robot-assisted and therapist-delivered rehabilitation cannot determine whether the physical assistance provided by the robot contributes independently to recovery. This systematic review and meta-analysis, therefore, focused specifically on randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of upper-limb rehabilitation in which experimental and comparator interventions were designed to be similar except for the presence, or level, or mode of robotic assistance. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched through November 2025 for eligible studies. Study screening and filtration were performed using Covidence software. Thirteen studies met the eligibility criteria for qualitative synthesis, and nine studies involving 272 stroke survivors provided Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA) data for quantitative synthesis. The standardized mean difference (SMD) between the control and the experimental group for change in pre-to-post intervention FMA score was calculated to perform meta-analysis. Heterogeneity computation, sensitivity analysis, risk of bias, publication bias, and certainty of evidence evaluation were also performed. Results: The main meta-analysis pooled effect (SMD = 0.425) favored the experimental robot-assisted condition across disease stages, assistance levels, and targeted limb segments. However, this overall effect was imprecise (95% CI: [-0.007, 0.858]) and showed substantial heterogeneity (62.62%). In studies restricted to chronic stroke, the pooled effect was larger (SMD = 0.53), although imprecision [0.067, 0.992] and heterogeneity (60.72%) remained similar. Estimates for shoulder-elbow and hand-focused interventions were small and imprecise too. Sensitivity analyses showed that the direction of the pooled effect was stable across various considerations. The certainty of evidence was judged to be low, primarily because of risk of bias concerns (mainly lack of double-blinding), inconsistency, and imprecision. Exploratory meta-regression did not identify clear study-level moderators of between-study heterogeneity. In addition, no significant publication bias was identified. Discussion: Although this study provides preliminary evidence suggesting a positive independent influence of the robotic assistance on upper-limb recovery, the limited number of studies with their small sample sizes and substantial heterogeneity preclude a firm conclusion. Larger, adequately powered RCTs that isolate robotic physical assistance while standardizing other intervention components are needed to establish its independent causal contribution to upper-limb sensorimotor recovery.

title: Effectiveness of Video Observed Procedural Skills (VOPS) versus Directly Observed Procedural Skills (DOPS) among post graduate residents of Gynae/Obs: a comparative study
abstract: Introduction: Assessment is an important constituent of the medical curriculum for health professional1 during training period. It is defined as process of collecting, interpreting, keeping the record of the information of learner’s answers to the curricular task.1 Assessment drives learning and aims to enhance and boost the capability of all learners and health professionals.3, 4 . Directly observed procedural skills assessment was traditionally used for many years. Recently video observed procedural skills assessment has evolved in various specialities of medicine. Both methods are work place-based assessment methods. Our study compared both methods to determine effectiveness of the effectiveness of these methods among postgraduate students of Gynae and Obstetrics. Objective: To determine the effectiveness of DOPS versus VOPS for assessing episiotomy repairs in obstetrics. To compare difference in resident’s performance in terms of rating scores assessed separately using between DOPS and VOPS. Study design: Comparative analytical study Duration: 6 months, commencing from 8th July 2024 till 25th Dec 2024, and was conducted within 4 Obs and Gynae departments within the public healthcare sector in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. Results: A total of 41 residents participated in the study, and their procedural skills were assessed using the Australian Medical Council (AMC) Workplace-Based Assessment (WBA) framework. Out of 41 residents, most of them were from 1st year and 3rd year i.e 87.79% while 12.19% were from 3rd year residency. VOPS has positive predictive value=58.1% (TP/ (TP+FP=18/31) and negative predictive value of 90% (TN/(TN+FN=9/10). Overall accuracy is 65.9% (TP+TN/total=27/41). VOPS can identify two-thirds of the participants. Conclusion: VOPS is good screening test for competency with high sensitivity, low specificity and higher negative predictive value.

title: Effectiveness of the SEFT teaching model on the clinical practice competence of surgical residents: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the SEFT teaching model in improving surgical residents’ clinical practice competencies, so as to provide a basis for optimizing training strategies.Methods This single-center, non-randomized retrospective cohort study included 38 residents. The 2019 cohort (n = 19) was the control group, receiving traditional demonstration and practice-based training, while the 2020 cohort (n = 19) was the intervention group, trained via the SEFT teaching model. Scores across five core competencies were compared using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test.Results The intervention group scored significantly higher than the control group across all five assessment domains (all p < 0.05): medical history taking (90.43 ± 3.83 vs. 84.29 ± 10.63, p = 0.039), physical examination (91.20 ± 4.88 vs. 83.76 ± 11.51, p = 0.017), initial medical record documentation (90.61 ± 4.98 vs. 84.20 ± 4.97, p < 0.001), and clinical reasoning and decision-making (87.00 ± 3.64 vs. 80.76 ± 9.24, p = 0.039).Discussion The SEFT teaching model, with its closed-loop structure and targeted feedback, showed promising potential to enhance surgical residents’ clinical practice competencies.

title: Effects of Robotic-based Combined Cervical Traction-Extension Intervention on Pain, Muscle Tone, Range of Motion, and Disability in Patients with Chronic Neck Pain
abstract: Purpose: This study compared the effects of a robot-based combined traction-extension intervention with those of conventional cervical traction on pain, cervical range of motion, functional disability, and muscle tone in patients with chronic neck pain. Methods: Twenty-four adults with chronic neck pain were assigned randomly to a robot traction group (n=12) or a conventional traction group (n=12). Both groups received 10-minute sessions three times per week for four weeks, for a total of 12 sessions. The robot group received traction while maintaining 65° of trunk recline and 10° of cervical extension. Pain was measured using a visual analog scale, cervical range of motion with a digital goniometer, functional disability with the neck disability index, and sternocleidomastoid muscle tone with a hand-held myotonometer. Paired t-tests were used for the within-group comparisons and independent t-tests for the between-group comparisons. Results: Both groups showed significant improvements in pain and functional disability after the intervention (p<0.001). Flexion and extension range of motion also increased significantly in both groups. The muscle tone increased in the robot group and decreased in the conventional group. The between-group comparison revealed a significant difference only in the extension range of motion, which was greater in the conventional group (p=0.003). Conclusion: Both interventions effectively reduced pain and disability and improved cervical mobility. The robot-based method was advantageous for flexion recovery and postural stabilization, whereas conventional traction was more effective for extension mobility and muscle relaxation, suggesting that the two approaches may serve complementary roles.

title: Effects of non-invasive brain stimulation on upper-limb motor dysfunction in chronic stroke patients: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
abstract: Background Patients with chronic stroke often experience upper limb motor dysfunction. Non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) has been extensively studied for promoting motor function recovery; however, the efficacy of different stimulation parameters and combined therapies remains controversial, and long-term follow-up evidence is still insufficient. Objectives Comparison of the efficacy of different NIBS protocols in treating upper limb motor dysfunction in patients with chronic stroke. Methods This systematic review and network meta-analysis adhered to the PRISMA guidelines. PROSPERO registration number: CRD420261482727. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, WoS, CENTRAL, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure for randomized controlled trials published between 2010 and 2024 regarding the use of NIBS in treating upper limb motor dysfunction in patients with chronic stroke. The NIBS intervention strategies encompass transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) tailored to various target sites and stimulation parameters, as well as diversified rehabilitation approaches combining these techniques with behavioral rehabilitation therapy (BRT), functional electrical stimulation (FES), and smart rehabilitation therapy (SRT). The standardized mean difference (SMD) was used as the effect size for a network meta-analysis conducted using Stata 18 software. And summarize the long-term follow-up results. Results After screening, a total of 36 studies were included, involving 1,052 patients with upper limb motor dysfunction following chronic stroke. Using the Fugl-Meyer Upper Extremity Assessment Scale (FMA-UE) as the primary endpoint, the intervention regimens comprising NIBS and BRT demonstrated superior efficacy compared to the control group (SMD = 0.831; 95% CI: 0.322–1.340), with a SUCRA score of 92.5%. In contrast, the remaining 11 intervention regimens showed no statistically significant differences. Among the secondary outcome measures, the Wolf Motor Function Test (WMFT) score showed significant efficacy only in the high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (HF-rTMS) group (SMD = 0.995; 95% CI: 0.271–1.719; SUCRA = 92.5%); however, no significant differences were observed between the intervention and control groups for the remaining outcome measures (all p > 0.05). Conclusion Combining NIBS with BRT may help improve upper-limb motor dysfunction in patients with chronic stroke. However, the internal components of this combined intervention exhibit considerable heterogeneity, and the associated benefits require further research for confirmation. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261482727 , Identifier: CRD420261482727.
authors: MS Huiwen Li; Haijun Lai; Peishan Chen; Xiaoyun Zhuang; Yin Qin

title: Effekte der cerebellären transkraniellen Gleichstromstimulation (ctDCS) auf die cerebello-corticale Inhibition (CBI) bei ehemals sehr frühgeborenen jungen Erwachsenen
abstract: Die cerebelläre transkranielle Gleichstromstimulation (ctDCS) hat in den letzten Jahren zunehmendes Interesse für die Untersuchung von Kleinhirnfunktionen und zur Behandlung von Erkrankungen des Kleinhirns erlangt. Zu diesen Erkrankungen gehören beispielsweise Ataxien, der essenzielle Tremor oder Dystonien. Die Effekte der ctDCS können mit der Untersuchung der cerebello-corticalen Inhibition (CBI), welche durch transkranielle Magnetstimulation (TMS) hervorgerufen wird, quantifiziert werden. Eine Frühgeburtlichkeit kann die Entwicklung des Kleinhirns beeinträchtigen und zu langfristigen entwicklungsneurologischen Defiziten führen. Das ist am besten für Frühgeborene verstanden, die fokale Veränderungen wie z.B. Blutungen des Kleinhirns erlitten haben, während die Folgen bei fehlenden fokalen Kleinhirnpathologien weniger gut verstanden sind. Ziel der vorliegenden Promotionsarbeit war zu klären, ob sich die CBI zwischen ehemaligen Frühgeborenen und Kontrollen signifikant unterscheidet und, sofern dies der Fall ist, ob diese Differenz durch ctDCS beeinflusst werden kann. Dafür wurden 40 Probanden, 20 ehemals sehr frühgeborene (≤ 32. SSW) und 20 ehemals reifgeborene (≥ 37. SSW) junge Erwachsene im Alter von 18-30 Jahren untersucht. Alle Probanden erhielten an jeweils drei verschiedenen Terminen in einem zeitlichen Abstand von mindestens 7 Tagen eine 15-minütige ctDCS des Kleinhirns mit einer Stärke von 2 mA. An jedem Termin wurde doppelt verblindet entweder mit kathodaler oder anodaler Polarität stimuliert und gegen eine Scheinstimulation verglichen. Zur Quantifizierung der Effekte der ctDCS wurde pre- und bis zu zwei Stunden post-ctDCS die CBI bestimmt. Zur Bestimmung der CBI wurde mittels transkranieller Magnetstimulation (TMS) ein konditionierter Stimulus (CS) über der Kleinhirnhemisphäre und 5-7 ms später ein Teststimulus (TS) über dem kontralateralen primär motorischen Kortex appliziert. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass es zum Zeitpunkt der Baseline keine Unterschiede in der CBI zwischen der Frühgeborenengruppe und der Kontrollgruppe gab. Die Effekte der ctDCS zeigten keine signifikanten Unterschiede in beiden Gruppen. Die CBI wurde sowohl durch die anodale als auch durch die kathodale Stimulation in beiden untersuchten Gruppen vermindert, während sie bei der Scheinstimulation unverändert blieb. Die Ergebnisse eines fehlenden Einflusses der ctDCS auf die CBI bei ehemals sehr Frühgeborenen sollten in größeren Kohorten in zukünftigen Studien bestätigt werden.
authors: Paula Agnes Steinhoff

title: Electromyography biofeedback therapy for spinal cord injury rehabilitation: a systematic review
abstract: Background: Electromyographic biofeedback (EMG-BF) is being increasingly used as an adjunct to rehabilitation after spinal cord injury (SCI), but the available evidence is limited by the small sample size, heterogeneous comparators, and variable outcome reporting. We aimed to systematically identify and narratively synthesize the evidence on the effects of EMG-BF in SCI rehabilitation. Methods: We searched the PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP and other databases from inception to 8 January 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity and inconsistent outcome-data types, we did not pool effect estimates; instead, we performed a structured synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM) and graded the certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Ten randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 537 participants were included. All 10 studies reported a favorable direction of effect for EMG-BF, but the evidence for every outcome was of low or very low certainty. Across the five RCTs reporting surface electromyography (sEMG), all reported larger signal amplitudes in the EMG-BF arm, although the outcome data types varied (means vs. medians) and the muscle sites and comparators differed. Two RCTs reported greater lower-limb muscle strength with EMG-BF. One RCT reported a higher functional independence measure score, and two reported higher ASIA motor scores with the use of the EMG-BF. Four RCTs reported reduced spasticity (modified Ashworth scale, MAS), but MAS was reported inconsistently as ordinal grade distributions or as grade-derived scores, precluding any pooled estimate. Three RCTs reported higher Berg balance scale scores with the use of the EMG-BF. Only one pilot RCT reported pain, and it permitted only within-group comparisons. Conclusion: Low- to very-low-certainty evidence suggests that EMG-BF may improve sEMG signals, lower-limb muscle strength, functional independence, ASIA motor scores, spasticity and balance in patients with SCI, but these findings are preliminary. Large, well-designed RCTs with allocation concealment, blinding of outcome assessors, standardized comparators and prospective registration are needed. Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261282923, Identifier: [CRD420261282923].
authors: Mingwei Liu; Zhong-yuan Liu; Bing-can Zhang; Shu-ji Gao; Hui-de Peng

title: Engineering Topological Phases in Two‐Dimensional Materials: A Path from Preparation to Device Applications
abstract: Owing to their topologically protected edge or surface states, rapid electronic transport, and highly tunable physical properties, two-dimensional topological materials (2D TMs) have garnered significant attention in condensed matter physics and materials science, and are regarded as potential candidates for quantum computing. Since the first observation of the quantum Hall effect, fundamental research on the physics of TMs has made remarkable progress. To better utilize the unique properties of TMs, the importance of material fabrication and phase engineering of topological states has become increasingly prominent. This review systematically discusses phase engineering in 2D TMs, from their growth to device applications. First, various topological phases and related 2D materials are introduced briefly. Next, the growth methods for 2D TMs are summarized. It then discusses progress and limitations in growth, driven by the requirements of characterization and application. Furthermore, the general approaches for modulating topological phases are reviewed, alongside the current applications in electronic devices. Finally, the review outlines future directions and challenges in phase engineering of 2D topological materials, aiming to promote the transition of 2D TMs from fundamental physics research to phase-engineered material platforms.
authors: Yuanming Ye; Hongwei Zhu

title: Enhancing anesthesiology medication safety and security through implementation of an automated dispensing system in a multihospital health system
abstract: PURPOSE: This quality improvement project describes the implementation of 150 Automated Dispensing Cabinets (ADCs) across a large multihospital health system's surgical and procedural areas to enhance medication safety and security in anesthesiology practice by addressing vulnerabilities in controlled substance handling, medication documentation, and diversion risk. SUMMARY: An internal audit identified significant opportunity for greater adherence to American Society of Health-System Pharmacists recommendations regarding controlled substance dispensing, medication labeling, and barcode scanning. In response, over 150 ADCs were deployed across the enterprise to provide point-of-care dispensing, electronic tracking, and automated label generation. A multidisciplinary team conducted comprehensive planning including physical assessments, medication inventories with particular attention to look-alike/sound-alike medication separation, inventory management protocols, and extensive staff training. Following full implementation which began in 2022, the system processed 737,906 total annual medication vends across the health system with closed loop tracking for controlled substances. Electronic monitoring replaced manual audits, enabling comprehensive insight into transactions, and supporting more efficient identification of workflow variances. CONCLUSION: Implementation of ADCs fundamentally transformed perioperative medication administration by providing real-time surveillance, eliminating large quantities of pre-dispensed controlled substance practices, and enabling comprehensive waste tracking with the ability for 100% testing capability. The transition from paper-based to electronic systems substantially improved accountability, documentation accuracy, and security measures against diversion. This multidisciplinary approach demonstrates that systematic innovation in medication management significantly enhances patient safety while creating more efficient and sustainable clinical workflows.
authors: Brent A. Dunworth; Amanda B Dickert; Ashley Houser; Molly Knostman; Patrick Ford; Susie Aboulhosn; Jordan C Simpson

title: Enhancing working memories using repetitive TMS
abstract: SUMMARY Working memory, the ability to retain and manipulate information no longer present in the environment, is fundamental for goal-directed behavior (Baddeley, 2012; Baddeley & Hitch, 1974; D’Esposito, 2007; D’Esposito & Postle, 2015). Alpha oscillations (∼8–12 Hz) have two apparently contradictory roles in working memory. Alpha activity gates irrelevant information through inhibition, a role causally supported by rhythmic transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) of parietal cortex at alpha frequency when a retrospective cue renders a memory item irrelevant (Bonnefond & Jensen, 2012; Riddle et al., 2020). Yet alpha activity also tracks the content of memory and binds the features of memorized objects during maintenance (Foster et al., 2016; Pagnotta et al., 2026). Whether alpha oscillations causally support the fidelity of memory representations during maintenance is untested. Here, 24 participants received short trains of repetitive TMS (rTMS) at theta (6 Hz) or alpha frequency (10 Hz), or in an arrhythmic control pattern, during the second half of the delay of a color working memory task, over the left posterior inferior frontal sulcus or the left intraparietal sulcus. A mixture model separated memory precision from swap errors and guesses. Alpha stimulation of the intraparietal sulcus specifically increased memory precision, whereas rhythmic stimulation of either site reduced response error, guesses and swaps irrespective of frequency. These results provide causal evidence that alpha oscillations support the fidelity of working memory representations during maintenance, and show that rhythmic stimulation at the appropriate frequency, site and time can enhance human working memory.
authors: Mattia F. Pagnotta; Mark D’Esposito

title: Esophageal Achalasia: Peroral endoscopic myotomy and the risk of postprocedural reflux
abstract: Peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) has expanded the treatment options for esophageal achalasia by allowing tailored division of the esophagogastric junction muscle through a submucosal tunnel. Its clinical effectiveness must, however, be considered alongside the possibility of gastroesophageal reflux after myotomy. This critical narrative review examines the comparative effectiveness of POEM, the mechanisms and measurement of postprocedural reflux, and the implications for prevention and follow-up. PubMed/MEDLINE and the websites of gastroenterology and surgical societies were consulted in 2026, prioritizing randomized trials, their long-term extensions, practice guidelines, expert consensus statements, and relevant observational cohorts. Randomized evidence supports substantial symptom improvement after POEM, with a particular therapeutic advantage in spastic type III achalasia, but demonstrates more reflux esophagitis or abnormal acid exposure than after pneumatic dilation or Heller myotomy with fundoplication. Symptoms alone substantially underestimate objective reflux, whereas retained food and fermentation can complicate pH interpretation. Acid suppression, endoscopic evaluation, and selective reflux monitoring therefore form part of responsible post-POEM care. The choice of treatment should balance durable relief of obstruction against the burden of reflux prevention and surveillance, acknowledging that the very long-term clinical consequences remain incompletely defined.

title: Evaluating canine hip analysis: NANet model for norberg angle prediction
abstract: The Norberg angle (NA) plays a crucial role in evaluating hip joint conformation in canines by quantifying femoral head subluxation within the hip joint. It is a key metric for assessing hip joint quality and diagnosing canine hip dysplasia (CHD), a multifactorial orthopedic disease influenced by both genetic and environmental factors. While contemporary tools offer automated NA quantification, they still rely on substantial manual labeling and verification by trained veterinarians. Rather than focusing on workflow efficiency, the objective of this study is to develop a fully automated system capable of predicting the NA directly from radiographs, thereby reducing dependence on manual annotation and enabling consistent and reproducible assessment. To address the limited availability of diverse, high-quality annotated radiographs, our previous work incorporated diffusion-based generative models to augment the training dataset from 1,168 images to 2,693 images. Training with this expanded dataset resulted in substantial performance gains, with an average improvement of 35.3% across evaluation metrics. Our proposed NANet model outperformed state-of-the-art alternatives, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy. In particular, the predicted Norberg angle fell within 5 degrees of the reference measurement in 81.30% of test cases, approaching or surpassing the consistency observed among human annotators.
