title: Purely Mechanical Muscle Length Feedback Enables Embodied Reflexive Control in Musculoskeletal Robots
abstract: Reflexes are a fundamental principle of biological movement; however, their application in musculoskeletal robots has been limited due to reliance on complex electronic sensing and control systems. This study presents the first implementation of the muscle length feedback reflex and establishes a minimal sensorimotor unit based on mechanical intelligence. Specifically, the proposed reflex module integrates sensing, computation, and actuation within its physical architecture, enabling autonomous contraction when muscle length exceeds a threshold, entirely without electronic components. Additionally, a muscle spindle‐inspired mechanism allows for adaptive modulation of this threshold. When incorporated into musculoskeletal robots, the module reproduced the patellar tendon reflex. Furthermore, by integrating this mechanical reflex with high‐level phase‐dependent threshold modulation control, bipedal locomotion was generated as an emergent behavior. These findings demonstrate that essential local sensorimotor control can be physically realized within mechanical systems, providing a minimal, robust, and scalable design principle for musculoskeletal robotics and advancing embodied intelligence beyond traditional control architectures.
authors: Shunsuke Koseki; Mitsuhiro Hayashibe; Dai Owaki

title: Real-time noise cancellation for EEG monitoring and brain–computer interfaces
abstract: Raw electroencephalography (EEG) data suffer from a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Effective real-time cleaning of EEG would improve the robustness of EEG monitoring, brain–computer interfaces, and brain-state-dependent stimulation applications in both laboratory and real-life environments. Here, we present a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm (rtSOUND) for EEG noise suppression. We adapted the established offline SOUND algorithm for real-time use and implemented it into an open-source EEG-processing software. Instead of using conventional temporal filtering, SOUND operates the data with a spatial filter. This makes it particularly suitable for real-time applications, since each streamed data sample can be cleaned separately in near real-time. Unlike temporal filtering methods, SOUND does not make assumptions about the frequency content of noise and brain signals but assumes that the noise topographies differ from those generated by brain activity. With an EEG forward model, rtSOUND cross-validates the EEG time series and estimates the spatial distribution of noise, resulting in a data-cleaning linear spatial filter. Each streamed EEG sample is processed synchronously, and the filter is periodically updated in an asynchronous parallel process. The algorithm rapidly updates the spatial filter in response to changes in the data, ensuring that noise reduction is both immediate and accurately adapted to the current EEG state. rtSOUND was validated with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)–EEG and resting-state EEG datasets measured from 25 healthy subjects. SNR of both TMS-evoked potentials and resting-state data consistently improved across various metrics. rtSOUND particularly benefitted channels with poor SNR, while retaining the waveforms in high-quality channels. The algorithm was fast enough to process data streamed at 5 kHz. rtSOUND improves the SNR of EEG in real time, providing a robust method to improve signal quality for brain-state-monitoring applications.
authors: Matilda Makkonen; Olli‐Pekka Kahilakoski; Johanna Metsomaa; Pantelis Lioumis; Risto Juhani Ilmoniemi; Tuomas P. Mutanen

title: Real-time posterior probabilistic TMS motor mapping with robust individualized stopping criteria
abstract: Background: Electric-field-informed regression provides high-resolution transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) motor maps, but conventional nonlinear fitting is too slow to update the map during acquisition, so sessions rely on predefined stimulation budgets, despite substantial inter-individual variability in the data required for stable localization. Objective: To develop a real-time analysis updating a posterior probability map between pulses and compare its hotspots with finger-tapping functional MRI (fMRI). Methods: We analyzed two independent cohorts (12 and 13 participants, one newly collected); each hand muscle was analyzed independently. We replaced the conventional per-element sigmoid fit with Spearman's rank correlation coefficient and transformed the resulting score map into a posterior probability map using Bayesian evidence. Acquisition stopped once posterior mass within 5 mm of the hotspot passed a preset confidence level. Results: The Spearman and linear scores updated the region of interest within milliseconds, versus tens of seconds for sigmoid fitting. Spearman more closely matched the full-data sigmoid hotspot in recorded sessions and converged faster and more precisely to the true source in virtual subjects. Across both fast scores, at a confidence level of 0.85 the stopping criterion was met after a median of 74-159 pulses. FDI hotspots lay 8.3 ± 4.3 mm from the fMRI center of gravity, in the precentral hand region. Conclusions: Rank correlation reduces computation time without loss of accuracy relative to sigmoid fitting. The resulting posterior probability map provides a session-specific stopping criterion in place of a fixed pulse budget.
authors: Renxiang Qiu; Zi‐Jian Feng; Ole Numssen; Yu‐Feng Zang; Florian Wilhelmy; Erdem Güresir; Thomas R. Knösche; Konstantin Weise

title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
abstract: Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.
authors: Patryk Klochowicz; Ahmad F. Kassir; Chandrakanta Parida; Jarosław M. Granda

title: Reorienting TMS treatments for fear memories and posttraumatic stress disorder. The emerging potential of the anterior prefrontal cortex.
abstract: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is characterized by re-experiencing trauma through vivid and involuntary intrusions, avoidance of cues that could trigger traumatic memories, and alterations in mood and cognition. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) offers a promising approach to modulating activity and functional coupling within neural circuits underlying these processes. To date, TMS studies in fear-conditioning research and PTSD have mainly focused on dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) and ventromedial (vmPFC)-connected or broader medial-prefrontal (mPFC) targets, yielding encouraging but heterogeneous effects on posttraumatic symptoms. In parallel, emerging evidence has implicated the anterior prefrontal cortex (aPFC; Brodmann area 10) in threat- and trauma-related processes, including memory retrieval, higher-order control of defensive responding, adaptive strategy selection, and resilience. Whereas the dlPFC and vmPFC have been incorporated into mechanistic models of fear regulation, the aPFC has received limited attention in theoretical frameworks of fear and PTSD. Here, we review TMS studies organized around dlPFC, vmPFC-connected or mPFC, and aPFC neuroanatomical targets, integrating evidence from experimental and clinical research. Based on the hierarchical model of prefrontal organization, we argue that these regions represent potential TMS targets or circuit nodes, but likely act on partially distinct mechanisms. The vmPFC appears primarily involved in early automatic downregulation of defensive responses; the dlPFC may support cognitive control strategies such as reappraisal; and the aPFC may enable a supraordinate influence over higher-order representations and avoidance-related circuitry, as well as flexible selection of emotion-regulation strategies. We conclude that integrating the aPFC into this framework may guide next-generation, mechanistically-informed TMS treatments for PTSD.
authors: Alba Chiara La Pastina; Eugenio Manassero; Benedetto Sacchetti

title: Repeated Head Impacts May Compromise White Matter Integrity and Bimanual Coordination in American Football Players
abstract: Background: Repeated head impacts (RHI) in American Football may contribute to subtle white matter (WM) abnormalities and functional deficits even in the absence of clinically diagnosed concussion. Hypothesis: Contact athletes would demonstrate tract-specific differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) compared with noncontact controls, and high-exposure (HE) athletes would show greater within-season diffusion change, worse bimanual coordination, and greater symptom burden than low-exposure (LE) athletes. Study Design: Prospective cohort study. Level of Evidence: Level 3. Methods: Twenty-two male varsity American Football players and 13 male noncontact controls underwent preseason diffusion tensor imaging. Football athletes were monitored over a single season using helmet-mounted accelerometers and stratified into HE and LE groups. Tract-specific FA and MD were derived using probabilistic tractography. Pre-post SCAT3 symptom and severity checklist data were collected from all football athletes, and pre-post Kinarm Ball-on-Bar (BOB) bimanual coordination data were available for 12 athletes. Results: At preseason, contact athletes demonstrated higher FA in 15 of 16 tracts compared with noncontact controls, with lower FA in the forceps minor. MD was lower in 10 of 16 tracts, higher in the bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculus, and similar in the corticospinal tract and superior thalamic radiation. Over the season, HE athletes sustained more impacts ( P < 0.001) and greater cumulative g -force ( P = 0.001) than LE athletes. On the BOB task, LE athletes showed modest improvement, whereas HE athletes worsened, yielding a between-group difference in change of 0.59 (95% CI, 0.22-0.96; P = 0.005). Generalized estimating equation models accounting for within-athlete tract correlations did not detect HE-versus-LE differences in FA change (Wald χ²(1) = 0.14; P = 0.71) or MD change (Wald χ²(1) < 0.01; P > 0.99), and SCAT3 symptom and severity scores remained low with no meaningful between-group differences. Conclusion: In 22 contact athletes, repeated head-impact exposure was associated with preseason WM differences and worsening bimanual coordination across a single season, while longitudinal tract-level DTI and symptom-based clinical measures showed limited between-group change. Clinical Relevance: Objective motor assessment and advanced neuroimaging may help characterize subtle consequences of RHIs that are missed by routine symptom-based tools.
authors: Sebastian D’Amario; Blaire T. Magee; Allen A. Champagne; M Wilson; Gabriel Ramirez‐Garcia; Nicole S. Coverdale; Douglas J. Cook

title: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation paired with a 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis for ankle-foot dysfunction among older adults following subacute stroke: clinical findings and exploratory neurophysiological analyses
abstract: Objective This work evaluated clinical effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) plus custom-made 3D-printed ankle-foot orthosis (AFO) for older adults living with post-stroke ankle-foot impairment. Neurophysiological assessments were also carried out for exploratory purposes, drawing exclusively on indirect physiological readouts. Materials and methods Sixty older participants with ankle-foot dysfunction after subacute stroke were randomized into three parallel groups: conventional-only rehabilitation, 3D-printed AFO therapy, and combined rTMS-AFO intervention ( n = 20 per group). Evaluations including ankle active range-of-motion (AROM), resting motor threshold (RMT), integrated surface electromyography (iEMG), Clinical Spasticity Index (CSI), Fugl-Meyer Assessment of the Lower Extremity (FMA-LE), Berg Balance Scale (BBS), and 10-Metre Walking Test (10MWT) were performed at baseline and four-week post-intervention time-point. Results Noticeable within-group functional improvements emerged in all three study arms upon completion of treatment ( p < 0.001). Participants assigned to combined therapy achieved greater functional improvements compared with those receiving standalone 3D-printed-AFO or conventional rehabilitation ( p < 0.05). The conventional rehabilitation group produced the weakest magnitude of functional recovery across measured endpoints. Conclusion Compared with single-modality rehabilitation approaches, adding rTMS to 3D-printed AFO therapy brought measurable improvements in ankle mobility, muscle recruitment, balance and walking performance. These clinical benefits occurred alongside elevated excitability within the ipsilesional corticospinal tract. Explanations regarding sensorimotor integration and afferent-efferent circuit regulation should be regarded as exploratory hypotheses because direct neural measurements were not obtained in this investigation. Further independent research is needed to test these mechanistic assumptions.
authors: Yuting Zhang; Hehe Chen; Rui Xu; Lingyu Zhu; Siyuan Song; Weixin Zhu

title: Resource-aware device-level control of air-conditioning load clusters for load shaping
abstract: Aggregated air-conditioning (AC) loads can support load shaping, but cluster requests must be translated into discrete device actions as resources and thermal margins change. We present a resource-aware device-level control method with two mechanisms: online resource-aware admissible-target correction, which filters the request using predicted and online resources and aggregate stress; and paced device-level setpoint dispatch, which uses action budgets, safeguards, and thermal-laxity ordering for 0.5 \(^{\circ }\) C updates. We evaluated 1004 residential AC units over 28 days in 1-min closed-loop simulations. Nominally, E4 achieved mean peak reduction and peak-valley-difference (PVD) improvement of 3.154% and 3.521%, with 9.266 actions per device and 0.347% control-induced thermal violation. A representative constrained MPC-QP achieved higher mean peak reduction and PVD improvement (3.590% and 3.967%) with fewer actions (3.669 per device), but had a 2.415% control-induced thermal-violation rate. This comparison revealed load-shaping–execution–thermal-risk operating points. Parameter sensitivity and degradation under four uncertainty models were evaluated. Under an uncompensated 5-min actuation delay, E4’s PVD improvement fell to 0.715% and actions rose to 74.770 per device. Conclusions are limited to the simulated population and load-shaping metrics; field operation and feeder-level power flow were not evaluated.
authors: ZhiYong Zhang; HaiYun Wang; Sizhe Yan; Zhuang Zhao; ZiBin Wang

title: Resource-based competencies and digital maturity: a synergistic approach to enhancing SME operational efficiency in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Although digital maturity offers transformative potential for SMEs, many in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) fail to realise proportional efficiency gains due to weak internal competencies. This study examines how resource-based and dynamic capabilities interact with digital maturity to enhance operational efficiency. Guided by an integrative theoretical framework that combines the Resource-Based View (RBV), Dynamic Capabilities Theory (DCT), the Technology–Organisation–Environment (TOE) framework, and complementary behavioural and institutional perspectives, the study employs a predictive cross-sectional design using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Data were collected from 9,826 SMEs across thirteen SSA countries. The findings reveal that digital maturity significantly improves operational efficiency, with innovation capability and strategic alignment as mediators. Agility and institutional pressure amplify the digital–efficiency relationship. The study offers a contextualised, empirically validated model for SME digital transformation in resource-constrained environments. Though internal competencies and top-management support do not significantly moderate the digital-performance nexus, agility and institutional pressures amplify the transformative impact of digital maturity. SME digital strategies should prioritise capability development alongside technology deployment. Policymakers should design supportive regulatory and capacity-building frameworks, while technology vendors and financial institutions align products with firms’ absorptive capacities and agility levels. This study offers a novel, empirically validated model of SME digital transformation tailored to low-resource, high-uncertainty environments. By conceptualising digital maturity as a dynamic, capability-driven process, it advances theory and provides actionable insights for strategic capability building in digitally evolving SMEs. JEL Classification: L25, L26, M25, O31, O33
authors: Deodat E. Adenutsi

title: Reticulospinal hyperexcitability after stroke: Associations with impairment severity and no evidence of functional advantage in severe cases
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Reticulospinal tract (RST) excitability increases after stroke. Although animal studies suggest that this hyperexcitability may compensate for corticospinal tract damage, its role in motor function in persons with stroke (PwS) remains debated. This study aimed to replicate RST hyperexcitability in PwS using the StartReact paradigm, examine associations with motor impairment, and explore whether heightened responses were associated with functional benefit in a subgroup with severe upper-limb impairment. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 46 PwS and 37 healthy controls completed a StartReact paradigm. Upper-limb impairment was assessed using the Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer, Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), grip strength, and Modified Ashworth Scale. PwS were classified as having high or typical StartReact effects based on the control 90th percentile. Severe impairment was defined as ARAT ≤10. RESULTS: PwS showed greater StartReact effects than controls (median: 15.00 vs. 5.21 ms; U = 667.5, p = 0.047, rank-biserial correlation = 0.22). StartReact effects were negatively correlated with ARAT (r = -0.44, p < 0.01), Fugl-Meyer (r = -0.51, p < 0.01), and grip strength (r = -0.36, p = 0.01). The high StartReact subgroup showed poorer upper-limb function, weaker grip strength, and greater biceps spasticity (U = 266, p = 0.02). Within the severe impairment subgroup, high StartReact effects were not associated with greater grip strength. CONCLUSIONS: StartReact-derived RST hyperexcitability was associated with greater post-stroke upper-limb motor impairment. In the severe subgroup, heightened responses were not associated with greater grip strength. These findings cannot establish that RST hyperexcitability supports functional recovery.
authors: Adi Lorber-Haddad; Noy Goldhamer; Tamar Mizrahi; Shirley Handelzalts; Lior Shmuelof

title: Robot-Induced Bias in Movement Smoothness Metrics for Rehabilitation: Quantification and Correction in Simulation
abstract: Robot mechanics can bias kinematic measures of recovery and limit comparisons across rehabilitation devices. We developed a closed-loop human-robot simulation calibrated to published healthy and stroke group kinematics. Paired runs held motor-control parameters and movement plans fixed to quantify bias in seven metrics relative to a low-impedance reference, normalized using external repeatability benchmarks. Within a subset informed by published device specifications, median log dimensionless jerk (LDLJ) bias was 0.93 and 1.79 benchmark units for stroke and healthy profiles, respectively. Sobol analysis identified Coulomb friction and apparent mass as leading contributors; LDLJ bias persisted across 11 robustness variants. LDLJ bias increased as simulated movements became less fragmented. If recovery similarly reduces fragmentation, this effect could partly mask improvement in measured smoothness. Correction combining identified robot dynamics and observed metrics with gradient-boosted trees reduced median normalized absolute error from 0.77 to 0.10 for LDLJ and from 0.24 to 0.08 for spectral arc length (SPARC) in the device-informed subset of a random 20% hold-out. Median smoothness residuals remained at or below 0.15 benchmark units across four separately held-out parameter regions. Under an alternative controller, LDLJ error decreased from 1.60 to 0.17 without retraining, although transfer varied across metrics. These simulation results support mechanical characterization and movement-dependent correction toward more comparable robotic assessments, motivating validation in patients.
authors: David Regev; Alex Scherbakov; Eran Bamani

title: Robotic Assessment of Thumb Proprioception after Stroke: Reliability, Validity, and Sensitivity.
abstract:
Objective

Despite the thumb's critical role in dexterity and its dense sensory innervation, thumb proprioceptive deficits after stroke remain limited due to the limited nature of clinical assessments. This study evaluated the reliability, validity, and sensitivity of a novel robotic assessment of thumb proprioception, SomatoCircleJump (SCJ), in individuals with chronic stroke.

Design

Cross-sectional psychometric study evaluating the reliability, validity and sensitivity of SCJ using baseline data from a clinical trial, with assessments conducted twice 5-10 days apart. In SCJ, a robot moved the visually occluded thumb, and participants indicated when the thumb passed a visual target.

Setting

University-based rehabilitation research laboratory.

Participants

Thirty-five stroke survivors with residual unilateral hand weakness and 24 healthy age-matched controls.

Interventions

Not applicable.

Main outcome measures

SCJ proprioceptive error, defined as the angular difference between actual thumb position and the visually presented target. Test-retest reliability was assessed with Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). Validity and sensitivity were evaluated by comparing SCJ with the Fugl-Meyer Assessment Sensory Scale for the upper extremity (FMA-S) thumb position item, and two robotic proprioception tests, one for the thumb (ThumbSense) and one for the fingers (Crisscross).

Results

SCJ demonstrated good test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.82, 95% CI [0.72-0.87]). SCJ error correlated significantly with FMA-S (ρ = -0.56, p < 0.001), ThumbSense accuracy (ρ = -0.62, p < 0.001), and Crisscross error (ρ = 0.61, p < 0.001). Using a 2SD criterion relative to controls, SCJ identified thumb proprioceptive impairment in 61% of stroke participants, compared with 23% identified by FMA-S.

Conclusions

SCJ is a reliable, valid, and sensitive assessment of dynamic thumb proprioception after stroke. It revealed that thumb proprioceptive deficits are common and related to finger proprioception deficits, supporting its use in future studies of sensory impairment and rehabilitation outcomes.
authors: Garcia-Fernandez L, Farrens AJ, Chan V, Rojas RD, Wolbrecht ET, Perry JC, Do AH, Cramer SC, Reinkensmeyer DJ.

title: Robotic Exoskeleton-Assisted Training for Upper Limb Recovery After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
abstract: Upper limb motor impairment is among the most common and most persistent consequences of stroke. Robotic exoskeletons may deliver the high-intensity, repetitive, task-specific practice that drives motor recovery, but their efficacy as a distinct device class remains undetermined, since previous syntheses pooled them with end-effector devices. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Embase from inception until July 3, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing upper limb exoskeleton training with conventional therapist-mediated therapy in adults with stroke. We included 11 trials randomizing 371 patients and analyzing 338. Exoskeleton training produced greater improvement in total Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) score (mean difference 2.45, 95% CI 0.88 to 4.01, p = 0.002). Subgroup analysis by stroke phase showed a significant difference between strata (p = 0.011), with a large effect in subacute stroke (mean difference 5.31, 95% CI 2.73 to 7.89, p < 0.0001) and no significant effect in chronic stroke (mean difference 1.46, 95% CI 0.00 to 2.93, p = 0.05). Exoskeleton training also improved the proximal FMA-UE subscore (p < 0.0001), the Action Research Arm Test (p = 0.0003), and the distal FMA-UE subscore (p = 0.02), but did not affect spasticity measured by the Modified Ashworth Scale. Robotic exoskeleton training confers a statistically significant but modest advantage for upper limb motor impairment after stroke. The benefit is concentrated in the subacute phase and is greater proximally than distally, supporting its use.
authors: Malek Sager; Ali Abusbaeh; Marwan Tantoush; Abdelrahman Najaim; Hasan Almgherbi; Bahaeddin Ben Hamida; Allaeddin Abusbaeh; Mohammed Alhamadi; Ayoub Tantush; Mohamad Alemam; Moaaz Shaded; Nada G Madkour

title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
abstract: In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions. This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states. In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback. We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies. Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning. Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments. We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.
authors: Chaoyu Zhang; Guangshen Ma; Mark Draelos

title: Robotic Palpation for Spatiotemporal Arterial Pulse Quantification and Mapping Using Multilevel Microdome-Based Soft Pressure Sensors.
abstract: Humanoid robots have advanced capabilities through physical and physiological examinations, but their reliance on visual information limits biological-object assessment, underscoring the need for tactile perception. Current tactile systems primarily detect basic contact using a limited number of sensors, hindering accurate soft-object localization and physiological signal acquisition. This study introduces a robotic palpation strategy by utilizing a fully soft-tactile-sensor-integrated humanoid hand for real-time spatiotemporal arterial pulse diagnosis. A facile fabrication technique produces an artificial pressure-sensitive layer with multilevel microscale dome-on-dome (DoD) structures using eutectic gallium-indium, achieving high-density (>72 500 ea/cm2) and large-area (wafer-scale >98% yield) fabrication. The DoD-integrated pressure sensor exhibits a 7.5 × enhanced dynamic response compared with a single-level sensing layer, enabling the simultaneous detection of subtle vibrations under high-pressure conditions. The artificial skin is integrated into a humanoid hand, featuring 81 sensors on the fingertip and a total of 801 sensors on the hand, allowing real-time spatiotemporal arterial pulse quantification and mapping.

title: Robotic assessment of spasticity in neurological conditions: measurement properties and clinical applications. A scoping review protocol
abstract: This scoping review maps robotic and motorized systems used to assess spasticity and passive hyper-resistance in neurological clinical populations. It examines populations, devices, perturbation protocols, measured constructs, measurement properties and clinical interpretation. The review follows JBI scoping review methodology, with PRISMA-ScR and PRISMA-S reporting. This registration documents an ongoing review after search activity, evidence charting and manuscript development have begun.
authors: Salvatore Facciorusso; Stefania Spina

title: Robotic-assisted knee arthroplasty methods provide insight into Homo neanderthalensis gait and the evolutionary origins of modern human knee variation
abstract: Lower-limb alignment is central to human bipedal locomotion and a key determinant of joint kinematics and osteoarthritis risk in modern clinical practice. However, its significance in hominins, and therefore its evolutionary implications, remain poorly understood. Advances in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) provide highly precise measurements of lower-limb alignment, joint morphology and soft-tissue balance that can elucidate these understudied aspects of hominin functional morphology. Here, we perform a proof-of-concept robotic-assisted TKA on an anatomically accurate model of the Spy II Neandertal. Using a robotic-assistance system, we registered bony morphology and replicated soft-tissue laxity extrapolated from a modern patient with a comparable alignment phenotype. We confirmed a pronounced constitutional varus alignment, classifying Spy II as a CPAK type I knee. This phenotype resembles that of modern athletes engaged in significant weight-bearing sports or intense physical activity during growth. The demonstration of constitutional varus in a hominin fossil thus suggests a deep evolutionary origin for this alignment pattern in modern humans, contextualizing normal knee variation and supporting an individualized alignment approach to modern TKA.
authors: Hendrik Pott; Peter Savov; Ricarda D. Stauss; Lara Watson; Ottmar Kullmer; Max Ettinger; Nicole M. Webb; Tara Chapman

title: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty demonstrates superior early functional outcomes compared with conventional total knee arthroplasty: a quasi-randomised controlled trial
abstract: BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has gained popularity over the last decade, with claimed advantages in implant positioning accuracy and soft-tissue balance. Whether these technical advantages translate into better clinical outcomes for patients remains debated. This investigation compared 1-year patient-reported outcomes between robotic-assisted and conventional TKA performed within the same institution but following structurally different surgical workflows. METHODS: This quasi-randomised controlled trial enrolled patients who underwent primary TKA at the Department of Orthopaedic and Trauam Surgery of the Eifelklink St. Brigida (Simmerath, Germany) between 2022 and 2025. Group allocation was determined by surgeon assignment through the institutional digital scheduling system. All patients received the same implant (Smith & Nephew Legion Genesis II, posterior-stabilised). Robotic-assisted procedures were performed using the CORI Robotic System (Smith & Nephew, UK) following a four-dimensional personalised alignment workflow (coronal, sagittal, transversal and balancing) guided intraoperatively by the Knee Balancing Score (KBS). Conventional procedures followed a femur-first technique with adjusted mechanical alignment. Outcomes included WOMAC total and subscores, visual analogue scale (VAS), Tegner activity score and a dedicated functional questionnaire, all assessed at 1-year follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 845 patients were included (robotic-assisted: n = 390; conventional: n = 455). At 1-year, 383 and 445 patients completed follow-up, respectively. The two groups were comparable at baseline. The robotic-assisted cohort showed significantly better results across WOMAC and related subscales (P < 0.001), VAS (P < 0.001), Tegner (P < 0.001), functional and satisfaction items, including walking distance and knee stability. No difference was found in the use of walking aids. CONCLUSIONS: Robotic-assisted TKA was associated with superior functional and patient-reported outcomes at the 1-year follow-up. The clinical benefit observed is likely not attributable to robotic precision alone, but reflects the structured, personalised intraoperative workflow that robotic assistance enables. Trial Registry German Registry of Clinical Trials (ID DRKS00030614).
authors: Filippo Migliorini; Luise Schäfer; Andrea Maria Nobili; Daniel Kämmer; Jens Schneider; Andreas Bell

title: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: a narrative review of resection accuracy and individualized soft-tissue balance.
abstract: Robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (RA-TKA) was introduced to reduce variability in bone resection and component positioning. Contemporary platforms do much more than that: they combine three-dimensional planning, intraoperative registration, objective gap assessment and virtual component adjustment. As a result, the question has shifted from whether a robot can reproduce a planned resection to whether robotic data can be used to individualize alignment and soft-tissue balance. This review follows that shift and examines the clinical evidence behind it. This narrative review examined the relationship between robotic resection accuracy, individualized soft-tissue balancing, and clinical outcomes. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language peer-reviewed studies published between January 2010 and September 2026, using combinations of the terms ("robotics" OR "robotic" OR "robot-assisted" OR "robotic-assisted" OR "robot arm" OR "robotic arm") AND ("arthroplasty, replacement, knee" OR "total knee arthroplasty" OR "total knee replacement" OR "knee arthroplasty" OR "knee replacement"). Reference lists of key reviews and primary studies were hand-searched. Priority was given to randomized trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, large comparative cohorts, long-term studies, and studies that quantified intraoperative gap or laxity behavior. The most reproducible advantage of RA-TKA is still execution accuracy, with fewer limb- and component-alignment outliers than conventional instrumentation. The newer value proposition is more complex. Depending on the platform and workflow, robotic systems can quantify compartment gaps and support virtual component adjustments, while force-controlled assessment is available in selected systems. These capabilities may reduce soft-tissue releases, but their clinical value depends on the balancing strategy and target definitions. Contemporary functional and patient-specific workflows often achieve high rates of predefined gap balance while keeping joint-line orientation within guardrails. Clinical superiority, however, is inconsistent. In recent randomized trials, functional alignment markedly reduced soft-tissue release, but patient-reported outcomes were not consistently superior to mechanical alignment at 2 years. Long-term survivorship data remain limited and conflicting, and economic value depends heavily on procedural volume, platform costs and downstream resource use. RA-TKA improves execution accuracy and can facilitate quantitative soft-tissue assessment and individualized planning. These capabilities have not established consistent superiority in patient-reported outcomes or survivorship. Further evidence is needed to validate alignment and laxity targets and determine the long-term clinical and economic value of specific workflows.
authors: Lei Shen; Chenjun Zhai; Tao Jiang; Yong Wang

title: Screening novel cathode materials from the Energy-GNoME database using foundation machine learning force fields and DFT
abstract: The development of new cathodes is essential for enabling next generation energy storage technologies. Here, we introduce a multi-fidelity workflow that bridges AI-based candidate identification and density functional theory refinement for accelerated discovery of cathode materials. Starting from the Energy-graph networks for materials exploration (GNoME) database, we use foundation machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) as an intermediate-fidelity layer to screen Li-, Na-, K-, Mg-, and Ca-ion intercalation cathodes. We assess dynamical stability and simulate intercalation voltage profiles to determine the average operating voltage and specific energy. The surviving candidates are further prioritized using experimentally motivated filters based on space-group prevalence, elemental availability, and cost, followed by DFT+U refinement of the most promising structures. Finally, combined MLFF and DFT nudged elastic band calculations are used to assess ion-migration kinetics and identify candidates with the potential for good rate capability. The workflow reduces 615 high-confidence Energy-GNoME cathodes to 10 prioritized candidates with favorable electrochemical properties and manageable volume changes. In addition to delivering a shortlist of promising candidates, this work benchmarks the consistency of Energy-GNoME, ML interatomic potential, and DFT predictions and demonstrates how MLFFs can transform AI-prioritized materials databases into physics-grounded discovery pipelines.
authors: Nada M. Alghamdi; Paolo De Angelis; Pietro Asinari; Eliodoro Chiavazzo

title: Shared Leadership and Team Performance: A Systematic Literature Review of Mechanisms and Contextual Conditions
abstract: The increasing complexity, digitalization, and uncertainty of contemporary organizations have heightened the need for leadership approaches that facilitate the integration of distributed knowledge and expertise. Shared leadership has therefore gained increasing scholarly attention as an alternative to traditional vertical leadership. However, existing research remains fragmented in explaining how and under what conditions shared leadership contributes to team performance. This study conducts a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to examine the evolution of shared leadership research, the theoretical mechanisms underlying its relationship with team performance, and the contextual conditions shaping its effectiveness. The findings reveal three major shifts in the literature: from direct relationships to underlying mechanisms, from variable-based approaches to relational and network-oriented perspectives, and from viewing context as a research characteristic to recognizing contextual configurations as determinants of effectiveness. Four complementary mechanisms are identified: relational capability, collective cognition, collective coordination and knowledge integration, and adaptive capability. These mechanisms are explained through complementary theoretical perspectives, including Social Exchange Theory, Social Identity Theory, the Input–Mediator–Output–Input framework, Transactive Memory System, and Complexity Leadership Theory. The findings further indicate that effectiveness depends on organizational, team, task, and environmental configurations, particularly collaborative culture, task interdependence, competency diversity, task complexity, digitalization, virtuality, and environmental uncertainty. Based on these findings, an Integrative Framework is proposed that repositions shared leadership as an organizational capability enabler that transforms distributed knowledge into collective capability and coordinated action, thereby enhancing team performance.
authors: Muhammad Fajrul Islam F; Muh Alim Fasieh; Gd Pandya Wicaksana Gara; Jemmy Regri Ferdianto; Ni Wayan Mega Sari Apri Yani; Theresia Dirda Rosari Widyadara

title: Short-term outcomes of robotic-assisted direct anterior THA in patients with generalised ligamentous laxity: a propensity-matched study.
abstract:
Background

Generalised ligamentous laxity (GLL) has been linked to instability and implant failure in primary total hip arthroplasty (THA). This study assessed outcomes of GLL patients undergoing robotic-assisted direct anterior approach (DAA) THA.

Methods

Retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from patients who had robotic-assisted primary DAA THA between August 2013 and October 2022, with a minimum 2-year follow-up. Eligible patients completed at least one patient-reported outcome measure (PROMs): modified Harris Hip Score (mHHS), Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (HOOS-JR), Forgotten Joint Score (FJS), visual analogue scale (VAS), and satisfaction. Patients with GLL (Beighton ⩾4) were matched 1:2 to controls (Beighton ⩽3) by age, sex, BMI, and follow-up. Outcomes included PROMs changes, achievement of MCID/PASS, complications, and revisions.

Results

Of 126 patients, 42 had GLL and 84 were controls. Both groups showed significant improvements in PROMs, high satisfaction, and similar achievement of MCID and PASS. Revision rates were comparable (p > 0.05): 1 GLL patient (2.4%) for infection and 1 control (1.2%) for aseptic loosening. No dislocations occurred.

Conclusions

GLL patients undergoing robotic-assisted DAA THA achieved favorable outcomes and survivorship comparable to controls, with no dislocations at minimum 2-year follow-up. Larger multicentre studies are needed to confirm whether this approach truly mitigates the higher dislocation and revision risk in the GLL populations.
authors: Quesada-Jimenez R, Reyes-Cordova A, Patel DH, Kuhns BD, Kahana-Rojkind AH, Domb BG.

title: Signal to signature: transcranial magnetic stimulation as a biomarker of drug-induced cortical modulation in early-phase development
abstract: This research focuses on the use of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) as a biomarker to measure the effects of drugs on the brain at an early stage. An important objective in the development of new treatments for neurological and psychiatric disorders is to determine whether a drug truly affects the balance between excitatory and inhibitory processes in the brain. Reliable methods for measuring such effects are therefore needed. This thesis investigated whether TMS can detect changes in brain activity following the administration of both established and experimental drugs. By combining measurements of brain activity (EEG) and muscle responses (EMG), insights were obtained into cortical excitability. The results demonstrate that TMS can capture subtle but consistent drug-induced effects. Effects of anti-epileptic drugs, antidepressants, and novel investigational compounds were detected, and TMS proved capable of distinguishing between different mechanisms of action. Furthermore, the studies showed that findings in healthy volunteers largely correspond with results observed in patients with epilepsy, supporting the translation of early-phase research findings into clinical practice. Although further standardization and methodological refinement are required, the findings suggest that TMS has the potential to become a valuable tool in early drug development and could contribute to the more efficient development of new treatments for disorders of the central nervous system.

title: Simulation-based optimization of look up tables for TMS ASM operation at the Large Binocular Telescope
abstract: Gravity and temperature induced deformations in extremely large telescopes are commonly compensated using look up tables (LUTs). At the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT), the existing LUTs were derived from focal plane aberration minimization and do not explicitly enforce geometric constraints required for metrology operation. They also do not account for rapid environmental variations or long-term structural evolution. We present a simulation-based framework that integrates the Telescope Metrology System into the control strategy to redesign the LUTs. A sequential optical model of the LBT was used to reproduce the active optics loop and to evaluate the sensitivity of wavefront error and pointing to Adaptive Secondary Mirror rigid body motions. The optimized LUTs will be validated through dedicated on sky tests to assess their suitability for routine operation.
authors: Byeongjoon Jeong; Luca Rosignoli; Heejoo Choi; John M. Hill; Brandon Mechtley; Olga Kühn; Gabriele Rodeghiero; C. Veillet; J. Chu

title: Simulation-pretrained autoencoders versus PCA for compressing multimode fibre transmission matrices
abstract: Multimode optical fibres can image through a thin, flexible probe once their transmission matrix (TM) has been measured, but a TM is large and must be re-measured whenever the fibre moves. A compact model of feasible TMs would make storing and re-estimating them cheaper, so we ask how compactly TMs can be represented, and from how few measured TMs. Here we benchmark a permutation-equivariant autoencoder, pretrained on simulated fibres and adapted to measured TMs, against principal component analysis (PCA). At 62x compression, adapting the pretrained autoencoder with just two measured TMs reconstructs the TM of a 50um fibre well enough to focus light at 98% of the ideal enhancement, and it stays accurate when the TMs are shifted by 25 pixels or zoomed by 10%, which quickly degrades a linear basis. It is not, however, a better compressor: PCA is about ten times more accurate when fitted on all 163 real TMs (1.1% against 11.9% error on held-out TMs) and is already more accurate from ten. The autoencoder's value is as a prior when few or no real TMs exist: with none it reaches 29% error, against 91% for PCA fitted on the same simulation. Transfer to a different fibre is only partial. The most important extension, not yet tested, is to recover pixel-basis TMs from fewer measurements than a full TM, which would turn the pretrained prior from a compressor into a measurement-saving tool.
authors: Callum Wilson; Terry Wright; Qing Yang; Zhong Wen; Michael P. Pound; George S. D. Gordon

title: Social Media Engagement and SME Sustainability in Bangladesh: An Integrated TOE and TAM Framework
abstract: Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) are the vibrant and dynamic sector of world economy. SMEs employ social media (SM) to develop brand awareness, connect with consumers, and make sales at a nominal cost. This stakeholder interaction enables access to information. Sharing this information supports decision-making, which is key to SMEs’ performance and sustainability. The objective of the study is to explore the factors of social media adoption that impact the SMEs’ sustainability considering the TOE framework and TAM model in developing countries like Bangladesh. This study involved the TOE framework and TAM model as SM adoption factors that impact the sustainability of the SMEs. For the empirical examination, a closed-ended questionnaire has been used. A Google form questionnaire was used to gather information through an online survey. The respondents were selected randomly from Bangladeshi SMEs. A sample size of 231 respondents has been collected from SMEs’ proprietors and officials. The findings of the research indicate a positive and significant relationship between relative advantage and compatibility of technological factors, top management support and cost effectiveness of organizational factors with SMEs’ sustainability. This research helps SME firms identify the benefits of social media adoption and states the justification behind a firm’s investment in social media. It develops an empirical, multidimensional hypothesized model, including several determinants that may influence social media adoption. This study includes various recommendations for decisionmakers of SMEs, policymakers in the country context, and SME interested scholars.
authors: Raj Moulick; Md. Sumon Hossain; Mst. Banu; Shamalia Haque

title: Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: 2026 Expert Consensus
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neuroinflammatory disease that significantly impairs quality of life. Spasticity is one of the most frequent and highly disabling features of MS, often accompanied by cramps, pain, bladder dysfunction, sleep disturbances, fatigue, and tremor. Recently, the concept of 'spasticity-plus syndrome' (SPS) has emerged to reflect the interplay among these symptoms. This work aims to update the Spanish clinical guideline for managing MS-related spasticity (MSS) by adopting this evolving concept. METHODS: of MSS management. Building on the previous guideline, the panel formulated updated recommendations with the scientific endorsement of the Spanish Society of Neurology (SEN). To support a structured and transparent development process, an adapted GRADE-informed framework was used to guide the appraisal of the evidence and formulation of recommendations. RESULTS: A total of nine publications addressing the SPS concept were identified. Based on the evidence and expert consensus, the panel developed 13 recommendations covering triggering and aggravating factors, the diagnosis and evaluation of spasticity, and therapeutic strategies for patient management. In addition, a comprehensive treatment algorithm was proposed to guide therapeutic decision-making according to patients' clinical profiles. CONCLUSIONS: This work provides updated recommendations for the management of patients with MSS, integrating the SPS concept into clinical practice. The panel highlights the importance of a symptom-oriented approach that considers the full spectrum of clinical manifestations to individualize treatment, simplify the therapeutic approach, and minimize the risk of polypharmacy.

title: State-Dependent Modulation of Corticospinal and Cortical Responses by Closed-Loop Paired-pulse TMS.
abstract: Brain oscillations shape cortical excitability in a phase-dependent manner. Cortical excitability reflects the net output of intracortical circuits, including inhibitory and facilitatory pathways. However, whether the phase of ongoing brain rhythms differentially modulates inhibitory and facilitatory responses remains unknown. Paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation (ppTMS) can selectively engage these circuits, providing a unique tool to dissociate their contributions. We combined real-time EEG-guided closed-loop TMS with single- and paired-pulse TMS in 24 healthy adults (13 female) to probe how sensorimotor mu (8-13 Hz) and beta (14-30 Hz) oscillatory phase shapes responses associated with intracortical inhibitory and facilitatory processes. Single-pulse TMS (spTMS), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI), and intracortical facilitation (ICF) were delivered at four phases (peak, falling, trough, rising). Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) and TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs) were recorded to assess corticospinal and cortical responses, respectively. We found that MEP amplitude was phase-dependent across all three stimulation types, with spTMS-evoked and ICF-conditioned MEPs showing the largest amplitudes at the rising phase, whereas SICI-conditioned MEPs were largest at the peak phase of the mu oscillation. TEP P60-N100 amplitude was modulated by oscillatory phase across all stimulation types, with maximal responses at the trough phase. SICI showed opposing phase patterns between the two measures, revealing a dissociation between cortical and corticospinal responses. MEP and TEP preferred phases were correlated across participants only in the ICF condition. These findings extend phase-dependent spTMS effects to paired-pulse stimulation and show that ongoing mu phase differentially shapes responses to SICI and ICF across cortical and corticospinal levels.Significance Statement Ongoing brain oscillations are known to shape cortical excitability across their phase cycle. However, whether this effect differentially influences inhibitory and facilitatory responses has remained unresolved. Here, using closed-loop EEG-guided transcranial magnetic stimulation in healthy adults, we probed how SICI- and ICF-conditioned responses vary across different phases of the sensorimotor mu and beta rhythms. We show that corticospinal and cortical responses to inhibitory and facilitatory paired-pulse protocols exhibit distinct phase-dependent patterns in the sensorimotor mu rhythm. These findings extend phase-dependent stimulation effects beyond single-pulse TMS and reveal that the relationship between cortical state and stimulation response differs across paired-pulse protocols.
authors: Choi DS, Güth MR, Ma M, Harmon M, Wischnewski M, Park J, Blenker A, Lee S, Opitz A.

title: Stimulation parameters of epidural spinal cord stimulation for functional recovery after spinal cord injury: a narrative review
abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) causes persistent motor, sensory, and autonomic deficits that conventional rehabilitation only partly mitigates. Epidural spinal cord stimulation (EES) can re-enable standing, walking, upper-limb control, and autonomic regulation, yet clinical translation is constrained by pronounced heterogeneity in stimulation parameters and by a weakly controlled evidence base. This narrative review maps stimulation parameters-electrode placement, frequency, intensity, pulse width, waveform, and stimulation mode-onto functional targets after SCI, critically appraises the supporting evidence, and maps scenario-specific parameter considerations onto a descriptive evidence hierarchy. Evidence was identified through targeted, non-systematic searches of PubMed/MEDLINE and citation tracking of key primary studies and reviews through 30 June 2026; human epidural-stimulation studies in SCI reporting parameters or functional outcomes were prioritized, with preclinical studies retained for mechanistic synthesis, transcutaneous trials used only as contextual evidence, and preprints labeled as such. Because no systematic search was performed, the review is presented as a narrative review: evidence is appraised using a design-based hierarchy, human, animal, and preprint findings are explicitly distinguished, and all parameter-level considerations are offered as preliminary observations rather than graded recommendations. Two reproducible motor parameter philosophies emerge-tonic, individually titrated lumbosacral stimulation embedded in intensive activity-based training, and programmed biomimetic (spatiotemporal, dual-mode, closed-loop) approaches-whereas hemodynamic management now has the most standardized parameter set. Evidence for upper-limb, bladder, spasticity, and pain indications remains case-level, and for neuropathic pain no SCI-specific parameter evidence exists. Mechanistic evidence derives predominantly from animal models, and clinical reports are dominated by small uncontrolled series in which stimulation is delivered as one component of a combined stimulation-plus-training intervention. Parameter-level conclusions are therefore preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than practice-defining; standardized parameter reporting, physiology-based stratification, and adequately powered controlled trials are the priorities for converting EES from individualized experimentation into evidence-based neurorehabilitation.
authors: Jingkai Wang; Yermike Bieshanbieke; He Wang; JiChao Yang; Shanfeng Ji; Yulong Li; HaoYuan Gu; Yongli Lou

title: Strategic Orientation, Dynamic Capabilities, and Business Model Innovation: The Emergent Role of Top Management Support
abstract: Background: As connectivity becomes commoditized amid over-the-top (OTT) competition and stagnant average revenue per user (ARPU), business model innovation, rather than network expansion, has become a primary determinant of incumbent telecommunications operators’ continued relevance. Objective: This study examines how strategic orientation translates into business model innovation (BMI) through dynamic capabilities (DC) and under what conditions top management support (TMS) influences this relationship among incumbent telecommunications firms in Indonesia. Methods: This study tests direct and DC-mediated effects of SO on BMI, with TMS as a potential boundary condition moderating the DC–BMI relationship. Analysis uses two-stage partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) applied to survey data from 130 executive respondents. Results: SO positively influences DC (β = 0.610, p < .001) and exerts both a significant direct effect on BMI (β = 0.377, p < .001) and a significant indirect effect through DC (β = 0.125, p = .025), indicating partial rather than full mediation. TMS does not significantly moderate the DC–BMI relationship (p = .313) but emerges as a significant direct predictor of BMI (β = 0.324, p = .001), with an effect larger than that of DC itself. Eliminating the reconfiguring dimension of DC on discriminant validity grounds left sensing and seizing as the final indicators of DC. Conclusion: Findings suggest a shift in the interpretation of TMS’s role, from a boundary condition consistent with upper echelons theory toward a direct antecedent consistent with dynamic managerial capabilities theory.
authors: Topaz Malik Aziz; Luqman Satria Manggala; Ervina Priyanti; Mira Maulida

title: Supply Chain Digitalization and Supply Chain Resilience in Manufacturing SMES in Italy
abstract: Introduction: Digitalization offers manufacturing SMEs several supply-chain management capabilities that may enhance resilience. This study explores the relationship between IoT adoption, data analytics capability, and cloud integration and supply chain visibility and supply chain resilience, with supply chain visibility as a mediator and top management support as a moderator. Methodology: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 344 employees from Italian manufacturing SMEs. The data were analyzed by PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Results: IoT adoption, data analytics capability, and cloud integration were positively associated with supply chain visibility, which in turn was positively associated with supply chain resilience. All three relationships were partially mediated by visibility, and the highest mediation was found for analytics. Top management support did not significantly moderate the visibility–resilience relationship. Conclusion: Results suggest that digital capabilities should be treated as separate information functions instead of being seen as a homogeneous tool. The study offers a comprehensive picture of digital capability, visibility, and resilience within Italian manufacturing SMEs.
authors: Jiyad Shaikh

title: Synchromodal Network Transport Management System Adaptability for Inland Navigation. Lessons from Po River, Italy
abstract: Inland navigation is one of the most environmentally friendly modes of freight transport, utilizing existing or human-made infrastructure and consuming only a fraction of the energy required by other modes, giving it significant potential to contribute towards the pressing CO 2 emissions goals set by the EU through the Green Deal. However, a further shift of cargo to inland navigation requires a reliable and resilient Inland Waterway Transport (IWT) system of adequate capacity with aligned standards and regulations. Climate change impacts on rivers, operational issues arising from aging infrastructure and low digitalization, make it difficult for vessel operators to maintain competitiveness. This paper explores the potential contribution of Corridor Management Systems (CMS) adapted to river particularities and enabling the concept of synchromodality to build resilient and attractive IWT systems. Stakeholder consultations indicated unanimous agreement that such a system would improve continuity of operations within the logistics network, with over 75% also indicating that it would enhance navigability of inland waterways. The analysis focuses on core functionalities of such systems and implementation challenges, with particular focus to the Po River in Italy.
authors: Orestis Tsolakis; Georgia Ayfantopoulou; Sofoklis Dais; Edwin van Hassel; Luca Crose; Luca Zanetta; Iolanta Conte; Aneta I. Oniszczuk-Jastrząbek; Ernest Czermański

title: Synthesis of ADP‐Ribose Mimetics as Potent Inhibitors for the Coronavirus Hydrolase Mac1
abstract: We describe the design and synthesis of α‐azido‐4‐thioribose and α‐epoxycarbaribose‐based adenosine diphosphate ribose (ADP‐ribose) analogs as potent inhibitors of the SARS‐CoV‐2 macrodomain Mac1. The α‐epoxycarbaribose was designed to emulate the structure of the distal ribose of ADPr, which adopts an E 3 conformation during hydrolysis and release from the target protein. In addition, a sulfonyl carbamate linker and the remdesivir‐inspired nucleobase GS‐441524 were incorporated into our designs to increase inhibitor lipophilicity and potency, respectively. The α‐epoxycarbaribose GS‐441524 pyrophosphate was identified as the most potent Mac1 inhibitor to date, exhibiting low‐nanomolar affinity. Replacing pyrophosphate with the less polar sulfonyl carbamate linker yielded an inhibitor with an IC50 of 19 nM. Analysis of co‐crystal structures of Mac1 and its inhibitors showed that the epoxide is intact and revealed that the sulfonyl carbamate linker positions itself to mimic pyrophosphate binding.
authors: Koen J. Rijpkema; Marion Schuller; Roy Steneker; Bas van den Berg; Jerom Sman; Jeroen D. C. Codée; Ivan Ahel; Dmitri V. Filippov

title: Systematic Literatur Review: Implementation of Risk-Based Internal Audit (RBIA) in Hospitals
abstract: Risk-Based Internal Audit (RBIA) is an internal audit approach that focuses audit activities on areas with the highest level of risk to provide strategic added value to the organization. In the hospital context, RBIA plays a crucial role due to the high complexity of clinical, operational, financial, legal, and reputational risks, which directly impact patient safety and organizational sustainability. This paper aims to develop a systematic review of RBIA implementation in hospitals. The method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with the PRISMA approach to data collection. A literature search was conducted through the Scopus database between 2010 and 2025, with 12 selected articles that met the criteria. The synthesis results reveal that RBIA implementation is significantly influenced by top management support, the role of the board of directors and audit committee, the competence of internal auditors, and the level of risk management maturity. Risk maturity is proven to play a role as a structural foundation and a mediator, determining the effectiveness of RBIA in improving internal audit effectiveness, hospital governance, and patient safety.

title: TACTUS: A Robotic Palpation System for Spatially Heterogeneous Hardness Mapping of Woody Breast Myopathy
abstract: Woody breast (WB) myopathy is a spatially heterogeneous fibro-degenerative condition of the broiler Pectoralis major muscle. Existing mechanical reference methods rely on single-point or sequential compression measurements, limiting characterization of spatial hardness variability. This study presents TACTUS (Tactile Adaptive Conformal 3D Uniform Sensing), an automated tactile array that generates thickness-normalized, three-dimensional hardness maps at 20 anatomically distributed locations within approximately 30 s. TACTUS integrates 20 independently motorized tactuators with force-sensing resistors and encoder-driven linear actuators, alongside a LiDAR depth camera for surface profiling and adaptive compression. The system was evaluated using 100 broiler breast fillets across four WB severity classes (Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe). TACTUS identified significant force differences among severity classes (ANOVA, p < 0.001), with the strongest differentiation in the cranial region and a significant caudal effect not detected by texture-analyzer measurements. Fillet-level TACTUS force showed moderate but significant correlation with texture-analyzer measurements (Pearson r = 0.441, p < 0.001). Semivariogram, local change entropy, and heterogeneity analyses revealed increasing and anatomically structured hardness variability with WB severity. These findings demonstrate TACTUS as an automated, operator-independent platform for spatially resolved mechanical characterization and ground-truth generation to support hyperspectral and near-infrared spectroscopy-based WB classification systems.

title: THE ROLE OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN MANAGEMENT ACCOUNTING: FROM TRADITIONAL COST CONTROL TO DATA-DRIVEN DECISION-MAKING
abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping management accounting from a function primarily concerned with retrospective cost control into a forward-looking capability for data-driven decision-making. This study examines how the existing literature explains this transition, the mechanisms through which digital technologies influence managerial decisions, and the organizational conditions that enable or constrain the process. A structured narrative literature review was conducted using studies identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and SSRN. The review applies thematic analysis to a corpus described in the manuscript as comprising twelve sources, covering empirical, conceptual, and review contributions. The synthesis identifies three interconnected dimensions of change: the adoption of digital technologies, including big data analytics, artificial intelligence, business intelligence, and cloud-based accounting; the integration of established cost management techniques into broader analytical systems; and the repositioning of management accounting systems as mechanisms that translate digital information into strategic decisions. Across the reviewed studies, digital transformation is associated with improved accounting information quality, decision-making quality, operational efficiency, and organizational performance. However, these benefits are not automatic. Digital leadership, top management support, organizational data culture, analytical maturity, and appropriate governance emerge as important enabling conditions. The review concludes that digital transformation does not replace traditional cost-control practices; rather, it embeds them within real-time and predictive decision-support systems. The study contributes an integrative, stage-based account of this transition and highlights the need for longitudinal and context-sensitive research to clarify its mechanisms and boundary conditions.
authors: Armiani; Baiq Desthania Prathama; Elvina Setiawati; Dwi Arini Nursansiwi

title: THE TRANSFORMATION OF MANAGEMENT CONTROL IN THE AGE OF BUSINESS INTELLIGENCE AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY IN MOROCCO.
abstract: Intelligence (BI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools is associated with the value-creation mechanisms of the management controller within organisations. Methodology: Grounded in a theoretical framework drawing on Anthony (1965), Lambert and Sponem (2009), Moll and Yigitbasioglu (2019), Davenport and Harris (2007), and Bhimani and Willcocks (2014), the study adopts a hypothetico-deductive approach and a quantitative methodology, with a cross-sectional design and a non-probability convenience sample. A structured questionnaire was administered to 80 professionals in management control, internal audit, and financial management, primarily based in Morocco and France. The primary field of study is Company X, a large multinational group operating in Morocco. Findings: The statistical analysis provides support for all four research hypotheses (p < 0.001). Analytical BI Maturity is significantly and positively associated with the value creation of the management controller's role, in particular as reflected in the quality of managerial information (H1: r = 0.610; α = 0.917); Operational AI Integration is also positively associated with value creation, in particular as reflected in the controller's evolution towards a business-partner role (H2: r = 0.621; α = 0.847); and Cognitive AI Capabilities are likewise positively associated with value creation, in particular as reflected in the strengthening of forward-looking performance-management capabilities (H3: r = 0.571; α = 0.791). In addition, Digital Organizational Maturity – encompassing digital competencies, top-management support, and data quality – is itself positively and significantly related to value creation (H4: r = 0.754; α = 0.871). These findings suggest that value creation in management control is associated with both the maturity of BI/AI tools and the organisational maturity required for their effective integration and use. As the design is cross-sectional and correlational, these results indicate statistical associations rather than causal effects. Originality/Value: This research provides original empirical evidence by quantifying, in an under-explored predominantly Moroccan context, the strength of the association between Digital Organizational Maturity and value creation through BI/AI tools. Research Limitations/Implications: the study is based on small, non-probability sample (N=80) wich limits generalizability of findings. The cross-sectional design and bivariate correlations preclude causal inference and assessment of each explanatory variable's unique contribution. Future research could use larger samples, longitudinal designs, cross-country comparisons, multivariate analyses, while investigating the potential moderating role of organizational digital maturity. Practical Implications: The findings suggest that BI/AI investment alone may not be sufficient for value creation, and the results are consistent with the view that parallel investment in digital competencies, managerial sponsorship, and data governance is also relevant. Prioritised operational recommendations are proposed as prospective suggestions by the authors for Company X and, more broadly, for organisations undergoing digital transformation of their management-control function, to be interpreted with caution given the sample size and the correlational design. Keywords: Business Intelligence; Artificial Intelligence; Management Control; Value Creation; Business Partner.
